title: Press Taylor: 'We're going to give all these guys an opportunity to grow' | Press Conference
text: Tre has talked about how the continuity of the coaching staff leads him to believe that there will be a chance to be more sophisticated in a lot of ways. How do you see that from from your your perch? >> Yeah, I I would agree with that just from the sense that we've all heard it now. You know, we're really getting coach Sudsville up to speed with what we've got going on. Will Long adding the staff, but they had the whole offseason and we can kind of help them along the way where last year we were all everybody was probably in JT and L's office all all the time trying to get clarity on what what we went through, what we installed, what we talked about and trying to get answers and then things come up through the course of the season that you you learn from that maybe they had answers for in the past or we have our own answer for. So now I mean it we're in second grade essentially. We've moved on from first grade. We're able to to kind of pick up where we left off but move forward with it and then evolve. we've had time to think about what fit us, what fit our people, you know, who we're integrating into the offense now, and how we're going to utilize those people. So, I do think there's just a natural progression for things of where we're going to go. Um, you've kind of gone through the early simple portions of answering certain questions for players and they know it too. We have a really smart group that they're able to kind of evolve as well with us. Going off that, when you're in the quarterback room and you see that JT is still there and Caleb and Tyson and Case, how do you see that continuity show show up when you're in those meetings? >> Yeah, it that's a lot of fun in there. And those guys have seen so much football and let alone they've all been together here. So, we all have, hey, remember week seven last year when this came up and we did this? Are we still doing that or do we want to do something different? Because week 13, we got the same thing. We changed it based on whatever we want. You know, you have shared experience to pull from and be able to communicate through. So, we get going a lot faster. We spend a lot less time going through what the formations are and what these motions are called. And now, when do we want this snapped? How can we use our cadence in this particular play? How can we make things look even more similar? How can you use your cadence or your pre- snap operation to fold the defense in a way that really isn't putting us in a bind in any sort of way? So, they're all taking the next step, and that's having those guys be on the same page and be moving forward together is really special for us, I think. With >> that in mind, predicted big things for Luther Bergen. How much easier is being a second year wide receiver versus being a rookie wide receiver. >> I think I mean, you know, Caleb made the reference he was drowning last year. I think I think that's what being a rookie in this league kind of feels like or being the first year in a system really feels like. So those guys I mean I don't think they've ever had the volume of offense that we have. So you're asking a guy come through, let alone Luther got hurt early on, missed all off season pretty much and then was working his way through in training camp. So you saw in the spring he was one of those guys that you really saw the skill set flourish. Now he's not thinking quite as much. He's able to just go out, react, play, not worry about where I'm standing, where I'm supposed to be when the ball snaps, who I'm targeting to, my depths on routes, and you're just seeing him play. And Luther's college tape was as good as anybody we've seen. So being able to see that skill set come out is a lot of fun. Uh he put in a lot of work through the off coming back in the offseason, then this summer as well. He was here all the time this summer working, trying to get his body right, trying to be in shape, you know, fighting to get guys to come throw to him all the time. and he he was here so he's hungry and ready to go and we'll see what that means for his training camp right here. >> Successful as you guys were running the ball last year, how how can you build off of it? How can you how can you run the ball even better this season with mostly the same personnel? >> Yeah, I mean we do have a lot of the same people. You know, obviously the change at center getting getting Garrett up to speed with the expectation, the communication, which so far has been very good from him. uh getting Logan in there as well, working those guys into it because they're kind of the ones driving the ship. They're responsible for setting the initial point and then we go from there based on what the defense does or what the play calls for. So that's a big part of it. Um you know that it doesn't necessarily carry over. Now we we certainly feel like we established a little bit of identity in the way we want to play and things that we feel like we're good at and now we're trying to take that to the next level as well. Um, it's going to take a lot of work to be able to run the ball successfully. And we understand that because it's unlike passing game, I think at times it it it's really all 11 on the exact same page. The quarterback is very involved in the run game from the way we run the ball at least. Um, whether that's our kills, our audible communication system, or what he's responsible for, holding the backside, defensive end, something like that. So, there's a lot of growth there that we think, you know, we went back and watched a lot of the tape and there's runs that hit and there's runs that we feel like could have hit for more. There's runs that maybe didn't quite take off that we think there's something there that we want to dive into. So, that's something we can probably get into a little bit earlier. You know, it took us probably four games to get going last year. So, hopefully we can get started a little quicker this season. >> What do you think of the slim down quarterback? >> He looks good, doesn't he? He looks fast. So, we'll see. We hear a lot about the the dynamic between Ben and Caleb, both from them and from others around the building, how how like-minded they are. What examples do you see of that from your perspective of the the connection they have together? >> Um, you know, being in the quarterback room, seeing the way Ben communicates with all the quarterbacks, Caleb as well. Um, there's a certain intensity, there's a level of demanding, but it takes a lot to be great in this league. It takes a lot to to operate the system at the level we expect. So, I think I think what everybody appreciates though from Ben is everybody knows it's coming from a place of what's best for the Bears. What's going to help us win? Okay. And and holding everybody accountable to the standard we all set and we all agree on. I mean, everybody understands what it is. And if you if you don't want to achieve that level or if you don't want to work to that standard, then you're not going to be in this building. And so, I think everybody understands that. Everybody understands that his mission is just to win championships. And this is what it's going to take to get there. And he can show you the tape. He can explain it. You can see it. And it's easy to get on board with it at that point. So, if that's what you really want, you're willing to take any level of coaching you can get. And so, that that's the beauty of the guys we have in the room right now is we can all be demanding. They're they're holding us accountable as well. You guys said this, now it's this. What do you want me to do? And we have to have a clear a crystal clear answer for them. And so, I think that's just the the standard in the building right now at this point. So, it's really cool to see from uh the quarterback room, but obviously everybody across the board. >> Rome talked about last obviously frustrations last year not being healthy. Have you noticed that he's comfortable now? Looks more comfortable in his body with his normal with his foot and everything. >> Yeah, I think you know one day in he's everybody's kind of excited. It's the first day of school so you see a lot of that but there's a lot of great energy yesterday. He looks like he's moving around really well. Um I think if he hadn't said anything I don't know that you necessarily would have noticed through the spring the way he was moving because he looks like he's moving really well. Um and we're excited to see what Rome does through this training camp. >> Chris, you you were here last season. What's the transition been for you from last year to this year with the change in role? >> Well, it's obviously ideal to have a year in the building, kind of see what the expectations are, the offense coordinator, what everything looks like, you know, being in Declan's hit pocket last year and being able to hear all the communication that was going on between him and Ben or him and the coaches, what every meeting looks like, being able to keep detailed notes on that. So, we're we're really kind of operating at the same standard or the same speed we were last year, maybe even more because everybody in the room has heard it before. We all know what the expectations. We all know what meeting is coming up, what we're going to cover, what we need to talk about, how we want certain drills to look. So, I think from that standpoint, it's helped. My time's probably a little bit different just ter terms of scripting. I may pull myself out of a few more meetings just to be able to make sure we're staying ahead and that the operations flowing pretty smoothly throughout training camp. Did you think when when Declan left that you should be the choice? Were you expecting to get that call? >> No, I I was excited for Declan. I was talking to Declan throughout the the process, I think, and was excited for the opportunity for him and I told my wife like she asked, you know, do you think you're going to be the coordinator? Like, I don't know. The only thing I knew just having been around Ben for a year that Ben was going to do whatever he felt was best for the organization. So, I knew that if Ben brought somebody else in from the outside or promoted somebody else to this role, that's what he felt was best for the Bears and I was all on board with that because ultimately we're all trying to win. And if he sees me being able to move this operation along in this position, then great. I'm going to do that to the best of my ability alongside him to make sure we're fulfilling his vision. >> Is there anything specific on game days that the role you were in last year that you feel like will will help you what your communication will be like with Ben during games this year? >> Yeah, again in the I was in the box and sat right next to Declan. So I kind of understand what communication Ben likes. You know, we we try to pair down our communication as much as possible. So there's not a ton of voices. You know, typically um Declan, Kyle Dean, Declan, Harry Freed were kind of the voices that would talk when it mattered. You know, everybody kind of understood when he needs me to give information right now at this time. So being able to to operate in that role, understand what that expectation is, we would assume that's going to help our game day communication as well. >> Harris has described Ben as a different guy on game day. How would you paint that picture of what changes? I >> I don't talk to Ben on game day, so I don't really know. I just kind of steer clear. Um you see a certain intensity. You know, we don't see him much in in the locker room pregame, especially us that go to the box. We go to the box early, so you don't see him address the team necessarily before, but when he steps on the field, there's a certain look in his eyes. It's kind of like, all right. And you get excited because we get excited on our side because we have Ben. Like that's part of the process of why do you think you're going to we have Ben? Like that's a big part of it. and you just kind of see it in the way he operates and you stay out of his way and let him do his thing and communicate when he asks you to communicate. >> To that point, Caleb has talked a lot about the evolution of his relationship with Coach Johnson, getting used to the intensity, the high standards as a coach working with him. Um, what's that process been like for you and where is it at now? >> It's awesome. It's the same thing. I mean, he holds the entire coaching staff accountable and to achieve a certain standard. I mean, this this is what he expects. This is what he expects the way he coaches players. He expects us to coach players. he at the same time everybody's got to do it your own way. You know, I think the one thing is if you're not authentic to yourself, players are going to see through that. They're not you're not going to be able to get the most out of people. Um, so that's a big part of it, but the way we communicate, the detail that we communicate with, the the urgency that we operate with, I mean, that that's all something that comes from Ben. That's a standard throughout the building. Now, >> what is the realistic expectations for a rookie like Logan Jones? So, do you have to tap the brakes a little bit on what you can expect from him? Um, I think the really the only expectation we have for Logan is that he gets better every single day. And we'll see where that takes us by the time week one rolls around. By the time week 10 rolls around, we'll see where we're at. But every single day, we expect Logan and every rookie we have in this building to get better and to to just continue to grow in their their process and the operation and the understanding of NFL football and our schemes as well. >> What's impressed you most with where Caleb was last year at this time to where he is at right now? I think kind of like we were just talking about, you've seen growth every day and and it comes out, you know, we were able to do a little bit more in the offseason just in the way we operated, the tempo we operated with. You know, if we had 15 plays and a 10-minute walkthrough, we were probably getting nine plays by the time we had to repeat everything. Now, I think yesterday we got to 13. We didn't quite get to 15 yet, but we got to 13 and we're able to move a little bit quicker. Uh, and that's not just necessarily Caleb, but that's everybody in the offense. the way we operate, the way we communicate, the urgency we have, and that's that's a big thing in this building. You just feel urgency every single day. >> You talked about the benefit of being in year two. Is that any different as a second year head coach than a first year head coach? >> Um, >> and in what ways, I guess. >> Yeah, that's a good question. Um, I'm sure he is. Part of it is just just understanding, you know, I think we all kind of understand what the flow of everything looks like, what a meeting looks like, what the day looks like. Our training camp schedule hasn't changed too much. Now it will at certain times we'll we'll bounce around a little bit in terms of when we practice just because it's more a reflection of what the season is up ahead of us. Um, so so there's a little bit of that. I think there's a little bit more of we don't need to be walked through everything quite as much as we were in the past because we didn't understand what his vision was for everything. Now we've all been through it for a year. Now we have tape to reference and hey, this is what we did last year. We got to take it up. Here's how we're going to take it up. Here's the expectation from now. So I think and the coaching staff does a great job taking initiative and we all understand what he's expecting or what he told us he wanted it to be and how can we take that up a step ourselves without him even getting involved. So that's that's been a big process as far as the coaching staff moving forward. >> Last one I heard. Coach, with Zavon's skill set, how wide of a package might you all give him throughout training camp or is there a caution to maybe not overload his plate >> there? There's always a fine line of that. Um I think just one year in we've kind of operated in just the fire hose method of let's throw a ton at him and see what he can handle and see how they bounce back from, you know, maybe mistakes, whether it's mental errors or physical errors throughout the day, how they're going to bounce back the next day and what they can handle because we're okay with guys failing through practice like that. That's a big part of this thing. We have plenty of reps. We have plenty of walkthroughs throughout the course of it that we'll get it corrected and then you'll get your opportunity at the, you know, the next goaround to see if you've responded from it, learned from it, what you can handle. And again, nobody's going to be a finished product by the end of training camp. We expect these guys just, you look at Coloulston, Luther, some of the rookies, Aussie, the rookies that contributed to us last year, and it it it didn't take off week one. It didn't take off necessarily week seven. Then by the end of the year, you see where these guys are at. So, we're going to give all these guys an opportunity to

text: How do you kind of approach a rookie like Chase who obviously is a a relatively high pick, but you want to give him his room to grow? Like how do you kind of approach looking at him? >> Yeah, but then in the question that you answered a little bit like the room to grow, right? Um lineman, first year, second year, even the third years you get going like it's just it's appearances at the plate. Like, you know, baseball you see pitches, you get more acclimated to it. Football is the same, you know, um and then the teaching progression of cuz we you get these kids from college, right? And obviously I [clears throat] saw background in that and knowing that everybody's developed or given a different book of work. And so getting them the the language, the technique, the understanding of the why, um I think's really important for any young guy. Obviously with Chase, you know, yeah, then you got the label where they're picked, uh the anticipation, the you know, what they expect out of that. You've got to kind of block out all the noise um with those guys. And he's done a great job with that, you know, him um coming in obviously great program, had a lot of success, you know, high-level guy. Um you're still starting anew because you are at the bottom of the totem pole. You haven't seen the speed at those reps, things maybe that you got away with in the past because of strength or you're just you're just better than those teams. You know, it's different now because you're playing against guys that are everybody, you know, and so I think this you know, as young guys you got to take that same approach. I mean, I I had literis a funny stat, but like, you know, some of you guys probably know like a sports broadcasting journalism guy, right? Like in so I got into it. So I go back to Ernie Pyle Hall at in Bloomington like the the lead or the open for and as you that's your guys' world and your business, right? Then nobody's reading the article, right? Now, I know it's more online and we got the clickbait with the cool pictures like that, but like at the end of the day, right? Like how you hooking me into that? How you just starting the newscast was like, "Wow, we've got great footage tonight of this." And then well, that's great if you're just showing my fat butt walking around the sideline. No one cares about you getting to chase Besana in the story. So, you know, saying that to like back to it of how do you slow it down to that? Right, we're in drop back protection. You're on the slide side. You've got to block this play. How are we getting so that you can go block the play and not just you know, like I said, any position. Carson, I throw it to the open guy. Well, yeah, they throw touchdowns. You know, young Jeremiah and these guys are Well, that's just run touchdowns. Run the ball. Well, there's a lot more to it. Um and so you have to understand that as a coach, but you also have to get that into the kids' mind like you'll be the guy again. And how fast do we get you back to that because there's a process to that, you know? Um and I like what he's doing. I like what Jayden's doing. I like all those young guys. I mean, you can KD's coming in and those those those three young guys that we brought in like you know, it's it's trigonometry start. You know, I've said that before. Well, let's get you to learn relearn the abacus and then precalc and then calc and then get to the real stuff. Um and when you do that with a high talented guy, the faster that growth will be as long as you coach them to be comfortable in who they really are and don't stifle that growth or don't create the paralysis by analysis because you're giving them too much because Chase is not Isaac. Chase is not Yelda. Doesn't mean he's not as talented as those inside guys, right? But he's not those guys right now. So, how fast do we get him there? >> How does that background with Chase and your relationship with Steve, how does that kind of help you guys connect now that you're >> Yeah, I mean I they just the coaching the individual player itself it's still I mean college football is the number one business in the world. I mean it's a multi-billion dollar business. But our product as coaches is still the people. And so a connection of having that is good. So, the speed up of maybe knowing what buttons to push, maybe knowing in a certain temperament. This is a coachable moment in dialect or this is a coachable moment in volume and intensity. Right? And so you can hear my voice is hoarse. Like you've got to select those two as a coach with each individual player. Um but no matter what you know, said all time to my guys like it's third and seven though. I'm not out there setting I'm not out there making the calls. So, however you get each individual to that I think helps. So, you know, back to your question there like yeah, it it's helped a lot because I've the learning curve of who he is as a person and what drives him as a player. I got a little better book of work starting with him than maybe some kid that you just it's blind and it's the first time for, you know, so. >> Is that mental adjustment from college that you're talking about? Is that a steeper learning curve now because of all the complex things that defenses are doing in the world's game? >> You're saying from in the college level or the pro level? >> adjustment from college to NFL >> Yeah, I mean everything just ratchets up. So, how do you learn in a meeting and take the meeting to a field and then you see it on tape or you can slow it down and you can pull the PFF cut up and watch the four-man pressures and like oh yeah, the nickel and the and the mic are coming. The nickel and the mic are coming. But the speed of that and then as they add the complexities, yes, it's totally different. And I think that's too like that's, you know, back to you know, the questionnaire like what system are they coming from? What is their background? Like what's your starting point? What's the what's the Rosetta Stone for those guys to understand it? But no matter where they came from, yeah, there's there's definitely some complexities of things and added tools and protections or things that at this level we have time to get into or two you have to get into because that's the only way to get it where you know, you might be just better than some teams at that level down. It's like, well, yeah, we know he's free but the quarterback's going to see it and get it out. Well, you're not letting your multi-million dollar quarterback just get it out if you don't have to, you know, that's got to be the answer sometimes, but getting us to the right guys to the five known rushers, to the where's the adjustment in those things? There there is a lot to that. And so that's why I said circling back to it like, but you can't throw all of that like that's version F. How do we get from A to B to C to D and you climb to that, you know, and so that's the that's why camp and for us having the extra weeks I mean, it's still not even August yet, right? We're in camp mode, but we're still in July, right? So like we we every day's critical. You can't let one get away, but you can't try to cram 10,000 in a 5-lb bag either, you know. >> Can't you explain the role of >> [snorts] >> the running game struggling last year? So outside of the Pearsons and the Yeldons of the room, what if anything are you focused on this year when it comes to the depth of the room so that maybe there's not so much of a a drop-off? >> Yeah, I mean, I I I think it it's always, you know, injuries are part of the game, you know, to the extremity and even the stuff that we lost to guys that weren't necessarily injuries, but just the freak situations that kind of happened. You know, you can't go in saying, well, in week 12 this is what's going to happen. So you have to continue to develop the underbelly and you got to make sure you got the right people in the room and all those things and um so that's part of it. Um you know, but the the the the breath of fresh air I guess would be for our guys with the ones that are carryover and then the new guys. Like we started from square one. And so emphasizing the operation in and out of the huddle and setting your feet so that the skill guys can get set so that we can trade shift and motion whatever that is. That has to be core to the DNA so you can use cadence, you can use tempo and then that gives you your schematic advantage to be able to run the ball. You know, and so the when you line up and you know that all you know, all 22 know you're running it and all section 222 knows you're running it then you got to go operate that way. Um I think that plays into it more from the top down but still trying to develop that like I said the underbelly and those next step guys watching the tape with them, making sure that when you're talking to the ones that are maybe watching the tape, the backup guard or tackle whoever it is you're also talking to him because he's literally one snap away and you know that's what we saw last year, obviously. >> What you seen out of Isaiah so far and what's the next steps in his growth? >> I like how is the is mindset coming in to camp um with the new operation, with the new calls. Um there was like a re-bite with him. It was kind of like understanding of like not that veteran season guy like oh yeah, I've done that, I've seen that, I'm back to it but all this is new, this is important. Taking the note, working to it. Um I'd say his confidence right now like he's doing some really good things right now that he's never done because of the technique and the things that is carryover. Those will be coming more habitual. And so just as we said and we were talking about Chaser like building up to that and now he's had you know, for him really year and a half of really playing those are valuable reps and then now when you get into practice and you're going, you know you like you know, our guys inside I mean LJ's playing well, Walter's come out playing well like those interior guys, Royce stepped in here and like we're getting some really good looks on the inside and so you won the rep, why did you win the rep? How can you enhance it? You lost the rep, why did you lose the rep? It it seldom is like why you just you just got your butt kicked, you know. It's I gave it to him and why did you give it to him? Maybe it was you thinking something else. Maybe the technique was sloppy. He's self-diagnosing that a little better right now. And so the the correction of the mistake, one's not turning into two when he's on the field. Or things that used to be issues, he's seen enough now and it triggers. Oh, this is that look. There's my profile. Here's what I'm going to go do. Um you know, and so I think that's what's shown with him the most right now. And I'm really happy with honestly the steps that he's taken and what he's done. You know, we've only had Padgett for a couple days, but just through everything. Like there's a there's a certain speed and comfort to him that's shown up that's he's not really it's flashed. We've all seen it on tape, right? Everybody watches tape too. Like you saw, "Ooh, okay." Um it's less of a flash and more of starting to be the main way right now for him, which is good. >> With Isaiah, um so you guys sign up Isaac, so it's pretty obvious he's probably going to have one of those roles. So when you draft Chase, it feels it it if I'm Isaiah, I'm thinking, "Okay, this is the guy that I'm going to have to really battle with." Do you do you see a change in a guy when something like that happens and a guy might get drafted and it seems very targeted towards maybe where you're playing already? >> Yeah, I mean I think just in general, not just with Zay and and with that, but like you would that's the hopes. Right? I mean competition's the best thing about our game and really for up front. So um as you're getting pushed and you can't that way you can't go into cruise control. So I think it really shows kind of the the core of a guy when okay, you think this or this may be the case, watch what I'm going to do. And so if that elevates his game, then it elevates the team. And so now you're getting into it, you know, back to the question here. Like, "Okay, now you've got six to seven, maybe your eighth guy now are like, you know what? These are all the game ready guys and they're not you're not hoping and wishing that it's controlled there, but as guys, you know, push each other that way. So um like the response. Um and it's on the back end too. like back to a guy like Chase and like I said with Jaden and all these young guys, like if you see a guy in front of you accelerating, if you really want to be there someday or you want that to be you at some point, then you've got to accelerate your growth. And so that hopefully that sparks as a competitive catalyst and not a woe is me, like, well, cuz then you get your answer that way, too, you know? And then we've had the right response with the whole unit really right now of that. >> This will be the last question. Go ahead. >> You mentioned Jaden a few times. It's kind of unusual to see a seventh-round rookie already working with the twos. What What has impressed you about him? >> Um, I mean, there's a lot of things, but I think just, you know, back to the young guy. Um, the strain, you know, like we'll clean up the technique and stuff, but he's not playing as slow as some guys may early on. Um, and then just the way that we're working the rotations to try to develop the depth, find out, you know, who's the next guy, who could be a rotational guy, who could step in. You know, the competition component to it where it's, you know, you don't really know till lights are on. Obviously not played a game, but like it hasn't seemed too big for him right now, the speed of the game, whereas he's still getting beat, but oh man, yeah, coach, you know, he'll turn around and tell me what the answer is before we have to give it to him after, you know, we got the jumbotrons running now, so um, I just like, you know, like I said, I like the the the growth mindset of all those young guys, and that's that's what he's been into, so and then it's hard sometimes. We've had him last week he was at right, this week he's at left. Same thing we did same thing with Josh Pryor last year, right? Undrafted guy, played right, he played left, he played some tight end stuff, like you have to be able to put that on him a little bit early once they're in it to see what they can handle. And then once you got him in a good groove where it's functional, then how do you enhance that? And so I think he's he's just adapted really well to like learning and then playing hard while he's learning and not slowing down to try try figure it out that way. So, happy happy with all those young guys as they've come along that way so far.

title: Teryl Austin Press Conference 7.30.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: T.A. you uh you were talking this summer a little bit about kind of the role you wanted to take and kind of take a step back at practice and stuff. Like, could you talk a little bit about what your process is when you're at practice and what you're looking for and how you're trying to approach it? >> Uh right now at practice uh you know, as I watch practice, I always kind of watch away from our bench side uh because you you know, I can give guys on that side instant feedback or coaches on that side instant feedback of of what I see, but the process is really I've been looking at you know, how we're doing things um if there's things that we can do better uh procedurally, if there's things we can do better schematically, all that stuff. So, I just kind of sit back and take that. I take notes. Uh and then usually when we get back, if there's anything that's uh that's pressing, I'll handle it on the field uh with the coaches or whatever. Or if it's not pressing, then we talk about it when we get back to meetings. I'll maybe bring it up to, you know, position coaches um you know, things I may have for Nick or whatever uh or even Mike at that point. Uh but just kind of what I seen and and then they take it from there. >> In all your in all your different stops, you've obviously had a lot of different roles throughout the defense. Just how different is this role for you? >> Uh this is really different because uh you know, obviously when you're coaching a position, you have your guys that you're dealing with daily and you got relationships that you build, you know, cuz you're in that room all the time. Or if you're coordinating, you're leading a group of men and all that different thing and all those different things. There, it's kind of like you're you're floating in limbo. I'm you know, I'm with them, but I'm not really leading them. Uh I'm not really, you know, in the rooms with them every day, uh so to speak. Uh so, it's a little bit different getting used to that way. Uh but you know, my my job is to try to be helpful for the for the guys. Uh and that means all the guys, coaches and players and and and see where if I see something that I think may help them uh to give them uh a little bit of of share with them a little bit and then see if that helps. And and that's really kind of where my where I'm at right now with that, which is is bit different. >> What are the challenges with that to adjust your view from a that narrow focus to kind of that broad lens? >> It is. It's a little bit It is. It's different. Uh it takes a little getting used to. I actually called a friend of mine, Bill Sheridan, who's at uh Jacksonville. Uh Bill and I've worked together at a couple places. Um and I asked him cuz he's in a similar role. And so, we kind of discussed the the pros and cons, what are good, you know, where where you kind of fit in and and those things and what would be what he thought was helpful uh because he did that uh at Jacksonville and he's still there. So, uh talked to him about it and and the different role and how that is. You're You're not narrow focused now. You've got to widen out. You've got to see you know, it's more big picture, big things. Um you know, uh not just, "Hey, how do I get this group ready to play?" >> There's a Go ahead, Darren. >> Uh I was going to say, there's there's a been a lot of talk about developing the young players here. There's been a lot of draft picks on the defensive side the last few years. A lot of that, I'm assuming, is going to come from the position coaches being in that room. >> Mhm. >> How can you help in that regard in terms of developing younger talent? >> Um I can just help in terms of what I've seen in development of young players and uh you know, offering advice. Again, I don't tell them to do anything. I offer, "Hey, man, you might want to do this with with player X. Uh this may help him. Uh you know, maybe this guy needs a little bit more film study. Maybe pull him aside and try to talk to him about these things." Or, "Hey, if he did things a certain way, maybe this would give him some success." So, that's really you know, how done it. >> In what areas has has Nick leaned on you and and where do you feel like your experience helps him as a as a play caller and coordinator? >> Uh I think where he's kind of uh leaned on me, it's not not the scheme part of it, but uh you know, maybe in terms of process, maybe how you handle some different things uh that occur. How do you do it with uh cuz you know, we weren't a big uh in terms of a lot of scheme and different different things. When we were at Pittsburgh, we were more, "Hey, listen, we're going to do this. We're going to do this really well. We'll add some wrinkles into it." And, you know, you know, just in terms of how we approach that process of it. You know, because again, it's it's always a different thing when you come from somewhere else. And And so, I think he's kind of, you know, kind of asked me, "Hey, how do we do these certain things?" And And see if it kind of meshes up with some some things that he likes. That That's kind of the the process with Nick and I. >> You know, are you helping guys with foot position like tweak it like this or is it more like, "Here's a scheme. Here's a bigger picture stuff." Like are you or are you doing a little bit of >> I I do a little a little bit of both is what I'll do. You know, there's there's certain times I'll say, "Hey, you know, you got to be lined up here." Certain times, you know, you know, there's just so many different things that go into to helping. And I think that's why I said it's kind of a weird situation in the sense of I don't really have the like in terms of I'm not in that room all the time. I'm not really coaching those guys, but how can I help them without stepping on the coaches' toes? Because I think that's really a real thing. I I want you know, all these coaches here to be empowered to teach their guys and not feel like I'm coming in trying to tell their guys what to do. It's their It's their room. The guys have, you know, so far what I've seen the guys do a really good job. And my job is to try to enhance what they do, not contradict what they do, and and make the players feel like, "Hey, wait, what's he saying this? He's saying that." >> How do you balance >> Absolutely. >> You were You were here during some heady times, the team making the Super Bowl, Larry Fitzgerald kind of hitting his peak. Like what was it like coming back? Like what has that been like for you coming back in the building, coming back to the stadium, all those things? >> It's It's been good. You know, I really uh you know, I got to thank Mike and Monty for, you know, cuz this this role I'm doing is new. It's They just brought it up. They made it up cuz they thought I could help and I you know, I got to thank them for giving me an opportunity to come in at um And and so it's it's been good getting back. It was different getting back in the building. It's like it's like the same building but I don't remember my way around. And and but it it but it was good. There were some new things in the building and all that stuff but it's been great. Um You know, you get back in you know, and then you just get into a rhythm and a routine of you know, the bottom line is what's your job here. My job is to try to help us become a better football team, help the players develop as players and and and people and and get them to reach their potential cuz if you do that stuff then I think success follows. And I think that's kind of when you know, we came here the first time it was really that. You know, people didn't give us much of anything and you know, we just tried to take the guys we had. We tried to develop them and and and and do those things and I thought we had you know, a good run at it. >> Speaking of that, you were a Pitt guy. You know, what you like you know, you talked about you know, Larry Fitzgerald when you were here and coaching against him, coaching with him and then seeing a a fellow Pitt Panther go to the Hall of Fame. What what you like to kind of see him grow? >> Yeah, it's it's it's awesome. I mean, you know, Hail to Pitt. >> [laughter] >> But you know, being in the watching Larry grow, it was kind of neat because when Larry came in the league, I was actually at Seattle. And so you know, I had Larry you know, he had Larry and Anquan. So it was like okay, how do you defend that? You know, and I talked to how we used to coach against him and then when I got here, I would say you know, Larry was great because he always wanted to know you know, that's that's one of the things that well, I think Larry is such a great player. He always wanted to know, hey, how did you guys play me? What did you think? What you know, and and so he was always searching for information because in his mind if he had information, he could beat it. He could he could use it to his advantage. And so it was cool watching him and then going you know, leaving and then coaching against him in different places. I was reading I got on the website the other day and I was reading like all all landmarks he had and I'm like, boy, I was there for a lot of that, good and bad on both sides, you know. It's But that, you know, that's really just a testament to his longevity and and how he was and as a player. And and obviously, he's probably even a better person. >> With this new role, how far back do you all relationships with Monty and Mike go that you were the name that came to mind? >> Well, I'm not sure with Monty, because I really know Monty just from being around. You know, you're around a circuit, you know guys, you've talked to guys, say hello to guys. But obviously, uh I've seen uh Michael obviously since I was here. Um when I left, I've done some seminars with uh where Michael was involved. And so, I got an opportunity, you know, throughout the course of the of my travels to stay in touch with Michael and see him and talk to him and all those things. So, um you know, I probably see Michael more than than anybody. Uh uh >> Uh before >> Uh Michael Floor didn't know. Which is uh is is kind of neat. And uh you know, so when that when it was all happening, um you know, the biggest thing when when Mike and I talked, he said, you know, "Hey, listen, he's got a lot of guys that he knows, he's worked with uh that have worked with me." And he thought, uh "based on a lot of that stuff that that I was a guy that he should talk to uh about this role." And so, that's how that came about. And uh so, it's been you know, it's been good. >> Kind of a random one, but we've seen you guys have the video boards up in practice with the replays. What are the benefits of that for for coordinators and position coaches to have that during practice? >> Instant feedback. It is instant feedback. Uh so, as you do, um when you're watching that, uh we used to have that at practice uh when I was with the Steelers for the last 7 years. So, the minute you guys would come off, you had an opportunity to look at it, uh watch it, make corrections. So, that way the same mistakes don't continue to happen over and over in practice. You have instant feedback. You can get things corrected and fixed uh immediately. And so, that's where the benefit is, cuz you'll see a lot of it. I do this I do it now like plays over while they're waiting for the next play. I'm going to look up and I'm going to see if what I thought I saw I saw. And and I think it's helpful for the players, too. So when you're coaching them, you can talk to them and they can actually see it right there and it's not like, "Hey, I did this." And no, no, this is what happened to you. I think it really helps. It is the instant feedback, I think, is the key part of it. >> You've been a part of defenses that have had very impressive defensive linemen. Last at night, Clelin, Dexter, Christian, all those guys. What are your early impressions of Walter Nolen? >> Uh my early impressions of Walter, he's damn good. Uh really like the way he moves. Um you know, he's got all the physical attributes, all that different stuff. But I think what I what I what I like most about him is I think he has a really good feel for just the game itself in football. Um you know, there's a lot of guys that are talented and and sometimes it takes them a while to pick things up and do that stuff. You just watch the way he moves and the way he does things. I think his his uh his football sense is is really really really high and I think that's good that always helps guys become better players. >> Other than staying healthy, where does he have to develop? >> Well, he's he's like all young players. I'm not saying he's a perfect player. What I'm saying is he has a lot of talent to to he has a high a very high ceiling. And so he's like a lot of players. He's you know, he's like you got to work on your stance, you got to work on your get-off, you got to work on your hand placement. That is that is the never-ending battle that all players face. Uh that you know, you have to continue to to really do well with the small things to continue to improve your craft. And I think that's you know, what he has to do. And if he does that, all the other stuff I think will take care of itself. >> How does extra time at camp week early with an extra game, first game What advantages are there really to any of that for this team? >> I think anytime when you have a new coaching staff, the more opportunities you have to get together, it allows everybody to, you know, obviously you're talking systems and all the different things you put in, but also to learn people. Because at the end of the day it's a people game and how you relate and get with people and get the most out of people, I think a lot of times deals with how you relate to them and how you can get your message across to them. And I think it gives you extra time to do that and I think that's important. >> With this schedule as it is, you don't have meetings after practice. You don't you can't put practice to bed till the next day. Having that instant replay, does that kind of help that a little bit address some of the things that are happening then instead of having to wait till the next day? >> It does. But I also think that from what I've seen there's a a group of players that come in and watch it on your own because you know, you have access to it on the iPad. So there'll be some as we're meeting at night, they'll come in and they'll be in the back of the room while you know, they'll come in and and and then maybe meet with the coaches extra if they want to. And other guys I'm sure will take it and watch it in their rooms. And so they'll have that. Coaches always enter feedback. So by the time you know, it gets to be 8:00 or 9:00, there's feedback written in the computer. So as they they watch it, they'll be able to get feedback from notes that the coaches have left for them in that in the iPads. >> You mentioned Go Danny, you go you good. >> In in your new role as you just kind of learn how you want to get things done, previous stops for you where you've been a coordinator, have you ever had someone in a similar role to what you're doing now? >> I have not. I have not. I've had I think one of the things when I first when I got my first coordinator job in the league, one of the things Jim Caldwell did that was obviously very helpful was on my defensive staff hired two guys who had been coordinators. And so they helped me and it would be very similar you know, to to maybe what I'm doing in terms of help except they coached the position. But they but they had experience in the job. They sat in the seat. They knew the things that you know, some of the things I could maybe help me or some of the things maybe to look out for. And so, that was that was valuable. >> You mentioned uh Walter, but is there anybody else that's really stood out to you so far in this camp? >> Well, I think there's, you know, there's been such a lot. We just put the pads on the other day. Uh I think there's some young guys. I think uh Bug has stood out. Uh you know, I just you watch his play temperament. Like, it's fun. Like, you know, Buddha is Buddha. I mean, I was wherever I was in the league, it was always fun to watch Buddha, you know? Uh but, I think there's some there's some guys that are starting to, you know, feel it and get going. But, uh I I think it's been good. I don't The best thing I could say is I don't think there's anybody that's really disappointed uh because I think I've seen growth from most guys. And I think that's really the key right now is you're seeing growth from guys uh and guys not going backwards. >> You've been around the league a very long time. You've worked with a bunch of different >> Don't make it sound like that, okay? [laughter] I mean, come on, man. >> It's you've you've been around a a lot of different head coaches and just the coaching styles and just whatever it might be. I know it's very early, but do you have any standing thoughts on Mike Vrabel as a first-time head coach? You've been What What do you think of the job that he's doing? >> You know, I think he's doing a good job. I I love the energy he comes in with every day. He's really consistent in what he does and how he does it. And I think when you're trying to set a a groundwork for what you want to do, I think that's important. Uh you can't ride a roller coaster. You can't be up and, you know, if practice isn't how you, you know, if it's great, you're up, and then when it's not so great, you're down and you're mad. No, I think you know, so far early, he's been uh I think he's been really good and and he's shown what you see some of the really good coaches around the league have, and that's really a consistency uh in terms of the demeanor, consistency in terms of message. And, you know, now it just, you know, as we get going in the games, that'll really tell the that'll really tell the tale.

title: Jack Strand, Drake London and other Atlanta Falcons speak post-practice at AT&T Training Camp
text: So, how's the acclimation process been, Jack? >> Uh, it's been good. I think, uh, just kind of taking it day by day and getting used to, you know, playing playing in a new offense and a new system and getting to play with a whole bunch of new guys. But, it's been a lot of fun and just kind of through meetings and stuff, getting getting more used to to playing in this in this system and, uh, you know, taking more reps and everything. But, it's been going good so far. >> What's the hardest part about is it the speed? Is it the playbook? I would say just the the playbook and the terminology probably just learning how to how to piece all the play calls together and uh you know figure out where where certain guys are going on certain plays and different shifts and everything. I think that's probably been the been the biggest thing and then just reciting the play in the huddle I think that's been another thing I've been working on that a lot too talking to my girlfriend at night having to read me the play so I can get used to saying them. >> Baptism by fire a little bit for you but how beneficial is it to have guys like Michael Penn Jr. and Tua in this quarterback room? Oh, those guys are awesome and they've been they've been so welcoming to me and any questions that I have, I know I can go to them and and they'll help me out and uh you know, they've just they've kind of yeah, they've been welcoming me since since my first day here in the spring and um really just it hasn't felt like you know, I'm uh you know, lower down in the QB room or anything. They've kind of they've just welcomed me in and uh they're treating me like any other QB. But it's it's been awesome to get a chance to work with work with those guys and watch them at practice and and just get a chance to learn from them. Well, yesterday morning as a quarterback, >> I'm sorry. What do you feel like your strengths are as a quarterback? >> I think uh I think I got a good arm for sure. I can kind of I can get the ball into tight windows and kind of just understanding where windows are and being able to put the ball there and uh I think uh another thing I just I like learning the offense and stuff. Um he's he's doing great. >> Going back to the venables defense thing for a second, you talked about how much he threw at you guys. It was it was set in stone and this is how we're going to run the defense and if you're able to do it, you're going to do it. So that um you know, we installed a lot of defensive and it helped me at the end of the year. you know, when you're the season is over, you look back and it's like, damn, we running a lot of stuff. If I wouldn't have came if I would have came out a year ago and not went to coach Rene's defense, I wouldn't have I wouldn't have been ready.

Um certainly this is a team that understands or has expectations of playing in the postseason uh and yet there's there's still that journey that starts again. So um and and look this messaging it's not every day it can come once every four days there's a topic yesterday you know with the initial team meeting it was hitting some of those bullet points that um can can play against these odds for instance of so many one-score games you know where are the areas that we really got to look ourselves you know look at ourselves and say we can improve here. You made it clear on how you're going to handle everything, >> but when you read what the resurre >> Yeah, I've read all of it. And I listen, I I don't have any comment on the specifics because I think um yeah, I think when it's finally finished, um we'll all have a better feel. So, um you know, it's unfair fair for me to answer any of those questions right now without having the the totality of it finalized and I I think it'll come sooner than later. >> When you were offering suggestions to Greg and Jerry about this new building, what were kind of the musthaves that you knew this thing? I don't that I mean I think look Greg and Carrie had a chance to go see like eight you know the newer ones and it's interesting cuz I haven't you know in other words I've not seen a lot of the new facilities and I think they saw most of the new ones and so they were beginning to formulate like what they might have liked with one of them or may not have liked with the other and So I mean these companies do this for you know so I didn't walk over and say hey we need you know that I can't recall um it was really more just functionality and and I think everyone in the process felt you know bigger is not always better and and I wouldn't describe it as like this massive I mean you know in other words you're actually you're actually closer to a lot of the items or so first floor lays out kind you know, in a similar way. Second floor and then obviously with the addition of the third floor. It happened in that that Giant game you know that catch to Sutton that went out of bound. It didn't go out of bounds actually. We kicked the field goal late. That was a Saturday ad that we saw late relative to a certain coverage. So when when something like that happens to you, um I'm not like a real big believer of the haze in the barn on f, you know, I just think that you're looking still to not and sometimes it can be to a fault, but you're still looking at something maybe that can change the outcome of a game. And so, um, yeah, and look, he did a good job writing about it. And then like there's five things in there you completely like forget about, you know, in other words, they they just they went somewhere and so it was interesting just reading something that seemed far away and yet it was just last, you know, last spring or last season. So, um, >> was it an accurate portrayal of what you went through? >> Um, yeah, I thought it was it was pretty real. Okay. >> What's the thought behind giving someone that kind of unique access? I think it was just as you're as you're I wanted to know like all right are you are you talking about just being here for the practices or are you talking about you know and so it's hard for anyone to really do that. Um so I I can't recall when I just said to him all right we'll we'll do it. Um and he hung in there you know. Um >> you had a comment a couple years ago.
