title: Jesse Minter on Ja’Kobi Lane’s Day 2 Training Camp Performance | Baltimore Ravens
text: Start off today by uh thanking our fans. Um you know, we have a great setup for training camp where we can get, you know, people out here. It creates an unbelievable environment for us, for our players uh to to you know, bring juice and energy to practice. So, really appreciate the fans and all the setup. And with that, we'll open it up. >> I know it's kind of early in camp, but we saw some potential with Jacoby Lane making a couple of catches today. How much does that kind of help with a young player going forward when he starts making those tough catches? >> Yeah, I mean, it's all about like what you do out here and I think Jacoby's a confident player and I think a lot of the guys that are picked are confident players. The confidence has to come to do it day after day, period after period. And then, the teammates gain confidence in them when they do that. So, a lot of times, man, the young guys, they got a lot of confidence. They've been really good players, but it ultimately comes down to, you know, Lamar trusting him and the other the other offensive players and the defense players trusting him to to be out there and uh make plays for us. So, that's the way it's always been. I think uh those guys will have a ton of opportunities to gain trust of of the coaches and the players. And you know, he made a couple nice plays today. >> How much does he rely on the tight ends hitting and blocking and getting involved in the offense today? >> Yeah, it's the same concept. I mean, you know, you draft guys and you know they're going to have the opportunity to help the football team. Um and then they got to go out there and again, do it day after day, rep after rep, gain trust, learn from their mistakes, you know, and learn day by day. And man, it's it's anytime those young guys are out there early making plays, it's a it's a good sign. >> On the side of the ball, rookie as well, Zaire Young, no pass, but kind of looked like he was in the backfield quite a bit today. Just What do you like to see when you see his intensity level where it is right now? >> Yeah, he's um sometimes you got to dial him back, you know, and especially in these situations. Uh Love the way that guy goes about his business, his physicality, his toughness. I think he's a good rusher, too. I think that's Sometimes guys look at like these big, tough, rugged edge defenders. He's a really good pass rusher, too, and he's going to be able to rush in a lot of different spots. Got a lot of confidence that Again, not right now, but as it goes that that he'll gain confidence with the other guys out there and you know, hopefully develop a role for himself. >> Jesse, with Hamilton and in particular with the interception today, it looked like a good read and he was in a spot where you might normally see a dime back playing. And I'm just wondering a player like that who has a good special teams year like he did last year, do you look to get him more opportunities on defense in different places? >> Yeah, I mean, when you when you start putting a puzzle together, um but particularly like right now we got 90 players, so it's easy to say we got three deep at all these different positions. The reality is guys have to be able to fill multiple roles and a guy like that with the skill sets that he has, I think he learned a lot his rookie year and he's a guy that's, you know, similar to a lot of these safeties throughout the league now that can play nickel, that can play dime, that can do a lot of different things for you and excited to see him grow in those roles throughout training camp. >> Kyle Hamilton yesterday and he obviously he's played for a few defensive coordinators now and he said he felt like the communication at this point in camp was really, really high. I know that's something you and Weaver are looking for. How have you guys kind of tried to stress those guys how important communicating especially at this time is and what are you seeing as you watch them? >> That's a great point. I think you know, we've actually thrown a lot at him, I would say, for 2 days just from various coverages and alignments and different things and it's intentional, you know, to kind of force them to be really locked in and dialed in, force them to study, force them to know what they're doing and also really force them to communicate pre-snap so that we're in the right situation. Again, Kyle's like the the pied piper for us. Him and Roquan, I mean, those guys, the way they drive the ship out there, when you have guys like that, it gives you the ability to do it. And so, that's a credit to them. Uh, it's a credit to the defensive coaches teaching stuff. Um, and I look forward to just that that being our standard of how we operate. Yeah, both those guys, I I mean, really really Um, you know, first week towards the end of that first week of August, I feel like you'll start to really see them getting the mix. They're working through a couple things. Right now, they're also getting like acclimated just to be ready when they do get uh, when they are ready. So, uh, look forward to having both those guys. Feel confident that they'll have enough time to get themselves ready for week one. Yeah, he's got a great, I mean, he's got a great competitive spirit about him. Um, he he plays in the slot really well, you know, and a lot of times, you know, it's different nowadays. Like it it's not always like the small slot receiver anymore. People move different types of players in there. Uh, but he has a good feel playing in there, playing zone and man. It's an instinctual position to be able to do that. He got some he got his feet wet last year. Uh, and he's always kind of let got that underdog chip on his shoulder mentality uh, from from having made it the way that he made it. Um, so, it's a credit to him. Um, and man, just like enjoy enjoy being out here with him. He makes everybody better with the energy and the consistency that he tries to bring. Yeah, I think Zay has unbelievable leadership skills. Um, and sometimes like leadership skills can be different. You know, some guys are the guy that, you know, you want to always sit everybody down and talk like the way he goes about his business is leadership because he approaches everything. He works really, really hard at his craft. He studies. He goes that's being a leader, you know, and just how you operate. And then he's he's got a really infectious positive personality, um, which I love. You know, it's it's it's just, um, very I mean, it's the type of guy you want to you want him to walk in the room. When he walks in the room, you're going to feel better uh when he starts talking and he's around. So, love Zay. Uh, super excited for him. Um, and he just needs to again keep being himself because he's growing into that just as he gets more experience and, uh, you know, the guys continue to see how what type of player he really is. >> Just curious what was the message of the staff to Lamar in terms of like what you wanted to him to improve on going in from the spring to the summer. >> You know, I think like when you're learning a new offense, that's the majority of it. Uh, he's got an unbelievable skill set we've all talked about. So, when you new offense, you tie in like new footwork, new timing, um, obviously reads, different cadences, all those types of things. I would say that like where he's at right now and where he was at maybe when we in the part of OTAs, like he is unbelievably further ahead. So, obviously he put in time, looked at stuff. The coaches have done a great job with him. Um, and so, man, those types of things when you be when you get those things down, then your natural ability can take over. That's what we want for Lamar. >> Just with Derek, what was the first Derek Henry what was the first thing that kind of really struck you when you first got in the building? And secondly, you know, obviously with 32, he showed no signs of slowing down, but but do you is that even a conversation about having to kind of manage any of that stuff in the >> You know, I think like the thing that strikes me the most about him is just his intent like every day. Um, he the success that he's had is a combination of, you know, being being gifted and having some tools, but like one of the craziest work ethics um and just work demeanors that I've been around. How he goes about his business. you know, I do think like like like all the players, you know, we're going to have to be really smart to get him through the long season. Uh I don't I don't look at that from like, oh, he's slowing down standpoint, but just that's our job. Um and so there'll be a lot of those guys that throughout camp, you know, he may get a less team reps in a day. He may get a day where he's not doing as much. See that with some of the guys. But again, man, that the way that guy goes about his business is really impressive. And then, you know, you play against him and you think you realize like how big he really is. And then he walks into your office and like, man, for that dude to be playing running back with the size and skillset that he have is uh definitely one of a kind. There That's a great question. I really appreciate that. Um it's something I think you think I think about every second of the day. Uh I think it's a it's a little similar to, you know, whether or not guys need real reps in the preseason. Like there's some guys that you can do enough with them without actually doing it that they'll be ready to do it. And then there's guys that haven't played as much that they're going to have to need to tackle. And so I think again as a team, it'll probably be a little bit individual based. There'll be some groups that tackle in practice occasionally and there may be be some guys that you see out of out of those periods. Yeah, that I mean, he's a great player. He can thrive at any area of the field. you know, it it's there's so many variables and circumstances that lead to plays whether they end up in touchdowns or not. I know the type of player that he is that he that he's working to be. I expect him to be really productive for us no matter where the ball is at on the field. >> All right, thanks coach. >> Thank you. >> Guys, the the the players that are at the podium are still signing.

title: Zay Flowers: ‘I Took It to Another Level’ | Baltimore Ravens
text: Uh the the new guy, D'Onta Foreman out there. >> Oh, I love him. He, you know, he he work every day. He willing to listen. Um and, you know, he he he take keys from everybody and then he apply them. So, he's learning fast. He learning fast and he keeping up with the tempo, so that's good to see. >> Jay, what's the vibe here, man? I mean, it's a brand new start. You've been through the OTAs and all that. And it's still early, though. What's it like? >> I mean, everybody excited to play. Everybody flying around the first few days, you know. Everybody get a fresh start. So, like it's good to see everybody back excited. Everybody, you know, ready to go. >> As far as the offense, though, still learning it? >> Uh we still learning it, but we got a jump in OTAs cuz we got a few weeks here early. So, that's been helping. That's definitely been helping a lot. Now, we just trying to detail it out and stay as clean as possible. >> In this offense, what's what's sort of the balance of Decklin Doyle, using you as you have in the past, and where you've been good in the past, and trying new things, and and putting you in positions where maybe you weren't used in the past? >> Uh he going to use his playmakers. That's what I'll say. He going He going to make sure his playmakers is touching the ball and um contributing to the game. So, whoever the playmakers is, that's who going to be, I feel like, touching the ball and getting the job done and helping us get it done. It's a lot It's a lot more um time in camp where we can bring a lot more people along and, you know, add them in the offense. So, it'll be a it'll be It's going to be fun. It's going to be a lot of people touching the ball. >> Do you think the usage that he's kind of ushering you towards is going to make you, you know, get to the end zone more this year? >> Um I hope so. I hope so, but um you know, it's been great, though. It's been Everybody been touching the ball. Everybody been everywhere. Everybody getting used to every position. So, you can't Everybody's positionless. Everybody You can play every spot, inside, outside. Uh sometimes the the receivers playing the tight end position. So, you never know. >> You know you've always been a hard worker. Lamar was telling us how you would call him at 5:00 a.m. Get him out for workouts and whatnot. Did you take it to an even other level this off season and if so, why? >> Um I'll say I'll say I took it to another level, definitely, cuz you know, you got to make an impression. New coaches, new coaches staff, something new. Like I got the last system we was in, you know, you can you can get used to something and then when you get used to it, you know, you can kind of find your ways around it and do stuff. But this one I just want to make a good impression, um be back in shape, top tier, and you know, and put it on the field. >> Last year you said one of the things you wanted to be able to show more of your game was the down the field catching ability. Do you feel like this offense allows you to do that? >> Uh this offense allowed me to do everything. Um deep balls, um short routes, mid routes, everything. Everything. Touch the ball coming out the back like everything. So it allowed me to show everything I need to show. >> Along those lines, it just seems like there's a lot of possibility for your role and the impact you could have going into the season. What are your expectations for what you'll be able to accomplish here? >> Um I just want to get better every year. I want to get I want to do better than I did last year and prove it in every part of my game. Route running, catching, uh contested catches, everything. So like I I just want to get better, man. That's That's what I'm here for and these coaches are going to help me do it. >> You obviously have a really good connection with Lamar Jackson. Have you given any tips to the young receivers, the rookies on how to kind of be his receiver and be quarterback friendly for his specific style of play? >> Uh if I'm being honest, Lamar can adjust to everybody. So he knows everybody different, everybody play style is different. Um like Jacoby, he know Jacoby can go make tough catches like middle of the field throw today. He threw it high. He knew Jacoby was going to get it, so you kind of kind of adjust to you, but at the same time you can help him by just running. That's all you got to That's all you got to do. Just run. >> Zay, speaking of Lamar, why do you think you guys have such a good chemistry on the field the last few years or so? I don't know. I think we just play football. Like if the play break down, we turn it to backyard football. Something we used to. And you know, I try to get open as much as I can and create as much space as possible to have him throw clean throws. So I think that's why it work cuz we understand if the play break down, go get open. The play not done. >> There were there were some debate in the off-season about whether people thought you were a true one receiver and Lamar, you know, was throwing that obviously. What's What did you think of that? What What's your reaction when you heard that talk? >> I don't pay attention to that. I just try to get better. Get better every week. That's my goal. >> Zay, did you hear about it? >> Yeah, um little bit. >> Zay, Kyle Hamilton said that despite playing different defensive coordinators in the past, they're really learning new stuff. I guess from your perspective so far, what feels like some of the more significant differences in Jesse Minter's defense? >> Um I feel like they everywhere. Like cuz sometimes you don't really know what's going on in the back end. Then you watch film and sometimes it look like it'll be a sack. You know what I mean? So like the the the back end is I feel like they everywhere. Kyle's moving all around. Um like he moved all around all the time, but now he's covering a lot. He's covering a lot. He's doing a little bit more of everything. Malakai and um Hawk, they're doing great jobs back there. So everybody's just taking on their role and Nate is stepping up to be in that number one. >> Zay, what is the Zay, what was your reaction when the team keeping Coach Beanie and what and then Coach Harbaugh brought you to the team? Coach P, that's my guy. Coach P he he like it's like he kind of like a player as in like, okay, this how you win. He They teach us how to win. And they also teach us the plays in ways that we could just take it from the classroom and put it on the field. So, I'd say they made our job easier in the classroom and on the field by just saying, "Play your game. Everybody move different." Like, Jacoby is not going to move as quick as I am, or I'm not going to high point the ball as high as Jacoby is, you know what I mean? So, they just let you play your game and try to add to it. >> This is the first new system you've had to learn since you've been in the league. Was it a little bit easier the second time, or is it back to square one with the new system? >> No, it's back to square one. It's It's a It's a whole lot different. Um in terms of the calling of the plays, the name of the plays, um remembering, it's a lot different. Everybody's system is a little bit different, but it's It's a little similarities in some of some plays, you know what I mean? Cuz there's only a a certain amount of stuff you can really run in football, you know what I mean? >> So, the Ravens have made it clear like they want to have you here for the long term. Is that You said you'd like to be here for the long term. >> With the contract stuff, is that something you prefer to get out of the way before football? Once the season starts, is that something you kind of need to do in the off season? >> Oh, man. Honestly, I'm just I'm just working right now. I'm trying to get better. I leave that to my agent and my representation. Right now, I'm trying to learn this offense, get closer to my teammates and my play my coaches, and just keep getting ready for the season. >> Speaking of the defense >> Uh I think we in a great spot. Everybody know the standard. Everybody know we got to come out here and work, and everybody know what we working towards. >> So, speaking of the new system, why do you think Lamar is able to pick up the new system so fast this his rookie year? >> I don't know. If I'm being honest, I don't know how he be able Like, I don't know how he pick up on the system so fast. Like, it's crazy. Cuz like I got to study a lot. I just did with this one. I don't know. He just pick it up quick. Like, I don't know. I don't I really I honestly don't know. >> Do you ever Lamar each other talk to you know try to help each other learning? >> Not really. Not really. I try to draw out the plays as much as I can cuz writing down help me remember. >> So as far as training camp from like the way it was going to be before to now and mornings little brisker, what do you think's the biggest way you like it? >> I love it. I love um practicing in the morning. You can get it out of the way then hit the the classrooms and learn a little bit more. >> All right, appreciate it man. >> Yep. Thank you.

title: Roquan Smith: ‘Trey Hendrickson’s Track Record Speaks for Itself’ | Baltimore Ravens
text: So, I know it's still early in camp, but >> is there is there any major differences do you think under Jesse compared to what you've been dealing with with John? Uh how would you kind of compare so far camp? >> Yeah, I think this is the uh what? The second day of camp. Uh and obviously every human being is always different. So, you know, like just like all 32 teams, things are going to be different. Jesse has his unique way of doing things. John had his unique way of doing things. And I'm enjoying it. Uh out here with the guys getting better and just controlling what I can control. And that's just my attitude and effort day in and day out. >> And you know in this off season, Jesse talked about you really taking ownership of the defense as the middle linebacker. How important was it for you kind of throughout this whole process to try to take ownership of the defense and be the leader of this group? >> Yeah, absolutely. I think uh leadership, that's a strong word, you know? Um and I don't I don't take that lightly. But first and foremost, I have to make sure myself is in the position I need to be in before you try to lead anyone at the end of the day. And like first you got to lead by example and be vocal when you need to. But I think those things all take care of themselves when you're doing your job the right way. And when you got a great group of guys around you, like whoever is out there with me or whoever I'm out there with, um we all know the mission at hand and what we have to handle. And it's about doing that day in and day out, practice in and practice out. And then that's just going to echo throughout the season. >> On the topic of taking care of yourself and then obviously getting a little older, you had some sort of nagging injuries last season. Did this offense or off season, sorry, look different for you at all in in any demonstrable way? Is there any way you're kind of concentrating on either shape or just injury prevention that's different from last season? >> Yeah, absolutely. I think um every year you're either getting better or you're getting worse. And I uh definitely had to attack some things uh with the body, soft tissue, and things of that nature. Uh and I feel really good. So, it'll just echo uh throughout the season cuz you know, a lot of people can talk, but it's more so about your actions and what you do on the field. So, I'm not in the talking business. I'm more so in the result business. So, you know, but it's a lead up to that and I'm just getting myself there just like each and every person out here. So, I'm excited for the journey and you know, the journey is always the best when it's the way it's supposed to be. >> You're at a different dynamic this year with which is Weave as the coordinator but Jesse's going to be calling the defense. What have you seen so far about how they kind of engage engage with each other and how do you anticipate kind of relating to each one of them? >> Yeah, I think it's a it's a beautiful dynamic and it's a beautiful situation like knowing Weave from in the past and I think he's a tremendous person first and foremost. Think he's a tremendous coach as well and just like having him here and then obviously Jesse um track record speaks for itself and I think when you tie two beautiful minds like that together, it just brings out the best in everyone cuz two minds, two great minds is a lot better than one. So, I'm excited for the journey with those guys and I know a lot of other guys can attest to that in the locker room as well as on the defensive side of the ball. So, we're definitely excited about those two and I know it's going to be pretty sweet. >> We heard Kyle talk about yesterday unlearning the way things have been done here in previous years and just the process of figuring out the way that Jesse Minter wants to do things. What's that process been like for you just trying to understand and get a sense of this defense? >> Yeah, I think you know, the things that like most human beings fear and I'm sure we all can attest to that is change and I think that's just part of life and like when things are different, people may not know how to adjust like right away and I think Jesse is a unique individual and I think he's a brilliant mind, very cerebral guy, seen a lot and obviously called a lot of great defense over the years. So, I just think what he brings to the table, who he is as a person, I think it's just going to be good for everybody and just allow everybody to really play to the best of their ability and like very calculated. So, I feel like I'm that way and I feel like with him being the leader of it all, being that way is just going to echo down throughout the groups. >> Brooke, you've been a part of what Jesse talked about how he's, you know, wants to be and have more of a dialogue with players and take your guys' input into consideration. Is there anything either on the field or off the field that like you've said to him that has been kind of enacted? >> Oh, yeah. No, absolutely. I think I think, man, he's he's true to his word and like, you know, that's what you have in this world, especially as a lady, guy, whoever or whatever uh you consider yourself to be. Like, I think when you have your word, you say something and you go about your word and to this day I feel like he's been about his word. He say something, that's what he do. He asked for feedback, give him active feedback and, you know, he reciprocates that and it goes from there. So, it's always great when you know you have someone that actually hears you out. Not necessarily mean everything is going to go the way you want it to go, but he always has to do what's best for the team. But, I think hearing you out and if it's something that he sees as best for the team, then he'll echo that through his actions and that's awesome. >> Brooke, in your case where you're the signal caller on the defensive side of the ball, what are the benefits to having a head coach who's also calling the plays on on that side? >> It's awesome, man. I think like just honestly like just having a mind like his, like actually calling the defense and then if there's little things he may see that may be if you can handle it mentally where it's like, "Hey, maybe this here may come up this play, that play, you know, be alert for this." And just those like reminders when you have that in the headset because at the end of the day, he's at the top of the food chain and like he he's seen a lot and like obviously he can see some things that I can't see, vice versa. But, yeah, just having that in the headset, man, it's knowing what type of mind he has. I'm just truly excited for it and I'm excited for it to echo throughout the defense throughout the season and obviously it started now and it's just going to continue to build. >> Brooke, you've been a of some really good pass rushing defenses here. But also, you know, the Ravens go get a big money guy like Trey Hendrickson, [clears throat] who has that real, you know, strong specialty sacking the quarterback. How different is it when the defense can kind of predicate around Trey's ability at that skill? And And do you feel sort of gravity shifting his way when you're sort of aligned in these certain schemes? >> Man, I think I think truly like having a having some elite pass rushers. And obviously, Trey's track record speaks for itself. But like, over my years like playing with guys like Khalil Mack, Robert Quinn, you know, and different guys like that. And like, when you have like elite pass rushers, and we have plenty of them, who's going to continue to show like Mike. I expect Mike to have a big year. T-Rob, whenever his number's called. Young, you know, and each and every guy that goes into that role because there's so many guys. And I think once you have that, it takes off so much stress from everyone. From the back seven, especially cuz you know the ball is actually has to come out. And like, you can truly It's not It's not a lot of patent, you know, unless unless you're doing a max protection or something like that. But then, that's like what, two, three man routes? And things of that nature. So like, yeah, once you have those type of guys, man, it just It lightens the load for everyone. So, I'm very excited about Trey obviously being here and like watching him and like It's It's pretty sweet watching him, watching Mike, T-Rob, all of those guys. So, I'm excited. I think it's going to be great. >> Ro, you've kind of seen You've gotten to see Trenton Simpson grow up in a way. How has that chemistry continue to develop between you two over the expected season? >> Yeah, man. I think Trent first and foremost, a phenomenal person. Like, he's the type you want to like If I had a daughter, he would marry your daughter or something like that. Kids, you know, like the dude is like that type of guy like off the field and on the field, man. He's one of those guys that's eager to learn about any and everything he Anything you put down, he want to He want to pick it up. And he he's like a sponge and like honestly this is like the best and I'm not just saying this like because it's media or whatever but like this is probably the best I've seen him. Obviously he's in peak physical shape. His physique is like no other and like but what he's doing mentally right now not making the same mistakes twice and things of that nature. I'm just excited for him to show what he's about and like what he's everything he's been holding in and like make no mistake about it. He knows what this year is. This is last year on this contract and it's about like going out and showing proving to himself first and foremost and then showing it to the world because I already believe in him and everyone else in the building believe in him as well and it's just about going out and showing that game in and game out but it's starting right now throughout practice and I think I obviously too having coach Santucci back like I think he's a phenomenal teacher, a phenomenal leader and able to truly break things down and where is Trent is like I thought about it. The guy's never had the same a same position coach more than one year. So when you just truly think about it and when you're being taught different philosophies, different things that can be a lot on your plate like for anyone. So like and then switching and coming playing linebacker truly for the first time in NFL like you when you think about it it's like the highest level of the highest levels and like a lot of pressure was on him early on but like I think he can handle it and he has handled it to the best of his ability and like he's always chin up, chest out, never drop his head and like come in the same person day in and day out and like you can't do anything but respect a guy like that. >> What are some of the battles that you went through with Teddy last year? What's stood out and impressed you about how he's attacked this year? >> Yeah man, Teddy like it's kind of crazy like some of the stuff I I I can't like discuss with training room stuff or whatever like that but like the way that guy's looking and what he's been doing man I'm I'm like whoo I wish I could do some of the stuff he's doing and like you would never know he's had that type of injury or whatever like that but he's the type of guy just put his head down and grind, and he know what he wants for himself, very mature beyond his years. I've said that many times before, and like I think that just echo and like a little adversity. Like he's not letting that phase him one bit. He's like, "Hey, it happened. So what? Now what?" And that's what he's going to do. He's just going to continue to prove doubters wrong starting at what? Small school ball out in Cal transferring. So he's always had the odds against him in a sense and um yeah, he's just going to continue to do that, and I'm just excited for his journey as well. And I think whenever he gets back, it's going to be a great addition for all of us. >> One more question. >> Speaking of uh peak physical shape, Derrick Henry, you went against him once in Chicago about 6 years ago. Do you remember that game? And you look at what he's, you know, still continuing to do, what kind of goes through your mind when you when you see that? >> Yeah, no, absolutely. Yeah, I remember like we was going down there to Tennessee. It was a nice warm day. Uh and the king, you know, that's all every week. Like, "Hey, hey, you know, 6-3, 6-4, 260, whatever he weighs." He's like, "Greek god." You know, all that. So like, yeah, you was definitely going down and making sure, you know, you got your chin strap maybe a little tight, a little extra air in your air in your helmet and everything like that. But like, yeah, what this guy's been able to do like, hey, make no bone about it. Like we all know like first ballot, who he is as a person, never complain, never seen a guy complain, come in day in, day out, grind, you know, never take the easy route. And like I'm just truly happy to have him on my team now and not have to worry about going against him cuz even up in London um when I was here, like we knew like, "Hey, you stop him, you got a chance to win every time." And like just pairing him with Lamar and the rest of the guys on the offense, man, it's it's truly special. >> All right, thank you, Ronnie. >> Yeah. >> That's it for today. Thank you all.

title: The Ravens Had Pocic in Their Back Pocket
text: Pocic signing and where he factors into what now will be perceived as a competition but perhaps is is nothing more than just a shoe-in at this point. >> Yeah, they had Pocic in their back pocket for lack of better word for a while and not to say a deal was done, but they kind of knew he was an option and he wasn't an option getting talked about a whole lot, at least among us and other people. I don't you know Dude, this is an Achilles injury from December. So, you just don't know. But, to go back a little bit, we discussed it plenty, Bobby. They wanted a young center. They wanted to get their center in the draft. There's two guys they liked, Slaughter and Jones. They both got taken. So, once that happened, they started exploring their other options. The other options were trades and the free agent option, the guy that they liked was uh uh Pocic. And, you know, they brought him in, which nobody wrote and I didn't know at the time. I just learned it last week. They brought him in for a physical 5 days after the draft to sort of meet with him, see where he's at in his recovery, get a feel for who he is as a person, all that stuff. Just to sort of, you know, that's that was part of their exploratory lining up our options and it seemed pretty clear it was going to be either him or a trade. They've been in dialogue with different trades. Bradberry's a guy that, you know, we've mentioned on here that was a potential option. Um while they've been doing this, they've been monitoring uh Pocic's recovery uh from his injury and pretty much how it worked out was, "Look, we could wait here. We could keep waiting. But, teams just aren't weren't willing to make a trade and trade a starting-caliber center before training camp. Teams want to get to training camp. They want to see how the roster's shaking out. They want to see how their young guy looks. So, I think if they were going to pull off a trade for a legitimate starting caliber center, Bobby, there's not a lot out there. We talk all about all the time. Teams just don't willingly trade uh quality offensive lineman. I think it was going to have to be later this summer, right? When teams sort of got in that roster crunch and might be willing. And I don't think the Ravens were willing to wait. I think they wanted a guy to come in and learn the offense, start working on developing a rapport with Lamar Jackson, uh get to know Dwyane Ledford. Obviously, if it was Bradberry, he played for Ledford at NC State, so that wouldn't have been as big of an issue. But, they wanted they wanted a guy. They wanted to have their guy in there. Um so, and you know, when when Posic got cleared earlier than they expected, that sort of accelerated the process as, "Hey, he's ready to sign. He's gotten cleared. Uh let's do this. It's right here in front of us. It's a very He's not making much more money than Danny Pinter is at this point, Bobby. It's a very modest one-year deal for starting offensive lineman. I think they think it's a good fit. He's a really big guy. Um I think they think he's very comparable as the other veteran options on the trade market. Um you know, I I you know, the he's not a upper echelon center, but I think we knew that. I think, you know, they needed to get a solid option in there and they feel like uh the one if he didn't have the injury and kind of the recent injury history here, he you know, I was talking to our uh you know, somebody out in Cleveland, they said, "You know what? He played really well at times. The issue was late-season injury sort of slowed him down." And here he is coming off an Achilles in December. That I I feel comfortable saying that and but I do think if if they have to give him a couple extra weeks, they'd be fine going with Danny Pinter for a couple weeks. He's been in the building, he had a solid offseason, he's already started that process with with Lamar and all that. So, this just makes them deeper at another position at the position and uh uh you know, we'll see how it develops, but I think they're feeling pretty good about their offensive line depths and when you look at it, the big priority there's two big priorities this year, Bobby, right? It was pass rush and it was solidify the offensive line and um you're going to see three new starters on the offensive line, that's one thing, but I think what what's even better is the depth. They've added some depth. I mean, you know, we can't forget a Jovon Gwyn who was a guy that Dwayne Ledford really liked and made sure the Falcons kept him on board and he made sure the Ravens added him and you know, obviously Emry Jones the Ravens view him as a future starter and Carson Vincent uh DeCosta sort of raved about him this off season. I get that, but you know, in a salary cap league you only had so many assets you can put towards it and I think they feel pretty good where they're at right now. >> Well, at the very least you're getting a guy that has experience unlike the rest of that group that was you know, perceived to be competing for starting center. I mean, Pinter was the only one with career starts under his belt with 10. Gwyn and Bullock as you know, zero combined and now you're getting a guy that's three games shy as a starter of 100 throughout his career and he's and he's had you know, service time dating back to to 2017 when he was drafted in the second round out of LSU by Seattle. That's where he spent the first four years of his career. The next four were in Cleveland, as you alluded to, and now he comes to Baltimore. I don't understand how it didn't get on there. I kind of looked back, and I didn't see it, um, but I did get it confirmed from a couple people, and I think people paused a little bit when they said we've agreed to terms pending a physical, and like, this a here we go again but it does worth mentioning that he did take a physical in May the first week of May when they brought him in just to see where he was at with the Achilles and all that so obviously they'll take another one and they'll have to make a roster move here they need to get a spot to add him is this where you can say we can't carry five quarter quarterbacks anymore is this where you say we can't carry two punters anymore does they does he subtract from an offensive lineman that they already have and say okay we got more than enough interior guys so we'll see but I can't see that being a hugely significant move it'll be a back end guy probably going off to accommodate him. >> All right he'll turn 31 in a couple weeks and that's your point 66320 and given what Cincinnati presents and the rest of that AFC North Ethan's going to need every single ounce of all that he brings to table physically as it pertains to the game

title: Josh Allen: "There's A Lot Of Love On This Team" | Buffalo Bills
text: All right, back here on One Bills Live, Chris Brown, Steve Tasker and our annual camp with one Josh Allen. So, Josh, thanks for stopping by. I appreciate it here. Couple of soggy days, but getting good experience with a wet football. You got to throw that around in the fall at some point in time, right? So, why not get the work in now? Um Joe Brady has a new title, but so do you. Uh for the second straight training camp, you added husband to your title list last year at training camp. Now you've added dad to your uh title list here. So, congrats on that. >> Um I'm sure you're enjoying the heck out of it. Uh just by some of the reactions we've seen in some interviews you've had already. Um are you just you're beaming. You're beaming. You're glowing as a dad. It's it it you wear it well. >> Well, thank you. Yeah, I'm I mean, it's once you're dad, as you guys know, it's you're always a dad. You know, at some point you stop being a football player. At some point you stop doing what you're doing like you'll never not be a dad anymore. So, um something that I've always looked forward to and and always wanted kids and me and my wife were very fortunate to to have our daughter the the way we did and she's she's our little uh our little angel. She's awesome. >> Good for you. That's and uh it makes it a little bit different in training camp. You got to you you got to make you know, you carve out that every >> Carve out some time. >> Oh, yeah, you got to now you got to yeah, you got to every minute of off time. Yeah, you're you're making calls and making sure that you can see and it it's different than being obviously there, but um you do what you got to do. >> What else is different about this training camp? >> Um I mean, new schedule. Uh I would really say everything. The way that we're going about things. Um a lot of new faces in the building. You know, that's staff, that's players included. Um so, yeah, we're we're coming out here. We're flying around right now. We're we're competing against each other. Um had a really good day that it's first time I think since I've been here where the weather looks really bad. >> Yeah. >> Like it's been it's been pretty good here. It's been hot uh really last 8 years. Um we we'd have a day or two of rain here or there, but you know, it looks like there's going to be a lot of rain on the forecast which hey, it's we know we play in Buffalo and that's something that you're going to have to deal with. >> You mentioned new faces and I'm just curious from a process standpoint Josh because every year you have to do this to some degree getting new wide receivers on board. I think fans would really like to see and I'm not looking for state secrets here but like how you take it upon yourself to on board guys. What are those initial conversations like do you sit in a film room and talk through things with new receivers? How do you get them acclimated and on board? >> Yeah, sitting in film room in OTAs and in training camp will all sit together and just talk about body language within routes depths just mindset of of when to expect the ball when when to give me eyes and it takes a while sometimes for new receivers and but you're the good ones it doesn't take that much time right? Like with DJ it it feels like we're like this pretty good the first couple of days but honestly I think it's the off the field stuff being able to hang out being able to sit down and talk and just like one another's company and I think that relationship off the field off the field pays dividends down the field. >> Yeah, it's a conversation you can explain it to people who are listening that when you're a veteran like DJ Moore knows the score when you come in the coaches put in these plays and you come in and you come together as an offense you go over and you watch them on film and all that and you run the plays but but when it comes back and they start running it back when you're running the plays and you're learning the players don't talk to the they talk to you. I mean like the like DJ Moore's going to Josh what do you see you know, what do I what do I do here and what you're you tell me >> be taught a different way and it's like hey for do it like it that do what what makes makes it right for you. >> it as a wide I I don't care how the coach wants it run. I don't know how that guy wants it run. How do you want it run? >> But for someone like DJ right? There's not a concept here that he hasn't run in his NFL career. He understands it now again there are little nuances and hey, this is what worked for me in the past. After looking at what some of stuff that that worked for you, like, let's marry those up, let's put it on field, and see how it works for us. >> The other new people are two in your room, Pete Carmichael, Beau Hardegree, and obviously you guys have had a few months now together in that room. You know, physically, they're they came back in great shape, and now you're just kind of itching to get the pads on to where we can truly evaluate it against a great offensive line, a great scheme, you know, as far especially in the run game with what uh with what we do here at the Bills. So, uh I'm excited about that. They They test me every day. You know. of >> How much of a transition is it going to be for Bradley Chubb to go from a four-three defensive end to an outside stand-up linebacker? I mean, is there more to it than we think, or is there less to it for him to be able to transition to that that role? >> I mean, I think the number one thing was to try to show him how much carries over, right? From what he's done his whole life, you know, the the roles he's been asked to do, how much carries over, and then get him to understand the differences, and how do we like bridge that gap. And he's done it a good job of of understanding what we're trying to do. We think it's going to allow him to get to his length a little bit better than he it has in the past. There's times he's gotten jammed up um just with limited space, and and obviously he's a unique athlete. With his size, with his length, we're really excited to to get him in a little bit more space, right? We're not trying to go crazy, but get him a little bit more space uh to allow him to have a little bit more vision, see what's going on, and then be able to get to that length, whether it's the run or the pass game. >> Jim, how much have you seen Bradley Chubb's leadership kind of rub off on some of the younger guys that are up front? >> Yeah, that's really cool. I mean, you you go through the free agency process, and you talk to guys, and you know, they can make their spiel. You you talk to different people around the league, and and you get their input about it, and from day one, it's just it's natural. Like he doesn't have to try, it's who he is. He's a natural leader. Guys want to follow him, you know, great professional habits. You name it, like he's knocked that out of the park. So, um on top of being a great player. You know, he knows the system. He's played in in a very similar system, right? It's kind of what he grew up in in Denver. So, um excited for the on-the-field leadership he can provide. You know, that was the biggest thing we had to sell him, like you you talked about the leadership and how you can help young guys grow around you, but number one, just be you. Be a player. Like be a great football player for us, and uh it's always great when guys can handle both and and not blink, and he's one of those people. >> Jim, for a player like Cole Cole Bishop who had a a kind of breakout year last year, how do you improve upon that and how does he actually go about making that improvement happen? >> Um >> Jim, how hard is it to improve and how does he go about making it happen? >> Yeah, I think for a guy like Cole when you have that breakout and the system changes, right? Sometimes you you panic a little bit early and that you know, having him a little bit limited in the off season, I think was good. We're able to have a lot more one-on-one conversations with him and and teach the scheme and show him how he fits rather than just being thrown into the fire of trying to compete and and execute every single day and that was the number one thing I tried, trying to turn the situation that we had in the off season into a a really positive one that way. Um this will free him up. Just like Ed, you know, you talk about Ed up front and the different things we can do with him. Uh the safety group, I see the same way. You know, I was always a Swiss Army knife that kind of did a lot of different things and that's what I like my safety group to be. Uh there's going to be a lot of different roles and a lot of different positions and techniques they're asked to do. Um and that's that fits Cole Bishop's play style and and his personality very well. >> Jim, there's a natural breaking period in any host defensive scheme. How do you square the vision that you have with this defensive scheme knowing that it may take a little bit more time? >> Yeah, my job, you know, being a professional is to try to make that breaking period as short as possible, right? There always is one because you're learning new players. They're learning me, right? They're getting We're getting comfortable with each other. Um over communicating is probably the number one thing that I can do. Trying to let them get in my brain, right? Like what am I thinking? How do I see this playing out? Being uh being very open, which sometimes I don't want to be, but that's the fastest way, right? If you if you get that communication and trust back and forth with your coaches and players, that's going to give them the best chance to get there faster. >> In what way do you not do you not play it open? And what do you mean by that? >> That's just not my personality. I'm I'm more reserved. I like to sit back and just take it all in. Read people, you know, read the room, that type of stuff. But um in a new situation like this, like I have to talk. Like I have to get into these the different different rooms and groups and um just kind of see where their head is at, what they're thinking, what's what's easy, what's hard, you know, like I have to ask more questions and and not just sit back and uh assume anything. >> Where are you in that process? >> Hairston skill set fit and what do you need to see out of Max? >> Yeah, Max is a man corner. Like he can run, he can challenge, you know, anytime you have that speed and quickness um at an elite level, you know, it it allows you to play a a lot of man coverage. But the number one thing that I noticed coming out of college, he could take the ball away. Right? He can take the ball away. So with a guy like Max, it's the the ability to mix and match playing man coverage, challenging receivers, but having vision on the quarterback to take the ball away cuz that's one of his biggest things and obviously it's the the number one stat in defense, right? Take taking the ball away. >> To play off that question, how concerned are you kind of with the the youth you have at especially boundary corner? You've got a rookie, a second year guy who didn't play a whole lot. Is that at all a concern as you as you get going here? >> Yeah, there's a number of of depth concerns, right? I think that's you're always looking to make that roster better, right? Whether it's at corner, um just not a ton of experience past the first group, right? That's going to be a heated battle among many during camp. So definitely one we have our eyes on. We like who we have. We we like the talent. We like where they're at currently. There's a lot to be determined on that field and they're going to get the opportunity to go compete and and win roles. Um also why I love the safety group and the versatility. You know, they've done a great job here in the past with kind of that tweener safety nickel body type and uh you know, we're going to continue to build off that and find roles for those guys. >> Can you talk about >> How do you guys learn them with the short amount of time in training camp and they they don't hit as much as the old days or the two-a-days before you can find these guys teach these guys how to textbook tackle like that tackle the guy for Denver made against Cook in the playoff. I hadn't seen a textbook. I mean, that was just a perfect hit that caught and it actually caused a fumble in that in the playoff game. How do you get a chance to to teach these guys the proper way to tackle? >> Yeah, that's To me, that's one of the biggest separators in the NFL, right? Is is who can tackle and who can't tackle, right? And there's a a natural element, right? If guys don't bite coming out of college, it it's hard to to turn them into great tacklers, but as a coaching staff, like you have to emphasize it. You have to find ways to be creative um to create the finish part of a tackle because that's not happening, right? There's so much where you have to protect your guys and protect the team with the length of the season, but I think that is ultimately one of the biggest separators in the NFL is can you turn the tape on and you see a team that tackles really well or a team that's inconsistent? So, it's a huge focus of ours. >> Do you feel they need to be more physical in in practices and in for tackling and going live in in camp? >> You're talking You're talking to a guy who broke his leg in practice being physical. So, um you know, there's there's a give and take, right? You have to get guys to understand there's only one way to play the game, right? Like you have to play it with a certain intensity. Um does not mean you have to take guys to the ground, right? I mean, you you can teach a lot of a lot of things in the in the settings that we do. You just have to be you have to be careful you're not teaching bad habits um indirectly, right? As far as pad level and finish and that type of stuff. So, I think how we emphasize things in the meetings and in some of the drill work we do early in practice has to be correct in order to to continue to build. >> Given that this is your first time with your coaching style, just like listening, asking questions, learning about the group that you have, what's the biggest thing that you've learned since you stepped foot in this building? >> To me, I was just blown away professional habits in the meeting room, right? There's obviously been a good foundation uh with this group of guys in you know, you start putting on film and you're talking over calls and they're communicating within the group. They're making close calls, right? They're making coverage calls. They're making adjustments and alerts. And this was the first day like we're installing a new call that they didn't know, right? So, just to see kind of what the habits within a meeting room setting and then how you can take that to the field like very interactive and very few places I've been had that. Like when you walk in the door, right? You're always trying to create it and build it, but from day one to have that, you know you can coach to a certain level because like you're going to get response, right? You're not looking at chairs where they're just going just just tell me what I need to know and and I'll figure it out later. So, to me, that kind of ends up changing your your teaching style, right? Because you know you're going to have those interactions. You're going to be able to fire questions and make the meetings more fun, right? It's It's more engaging for the players and and I think that helps them learn. >> Is there a guy in particular that you walked in that meeting and like he he just gets it? >> No, it it was a group. I I almost jumped back because so many guys start talking that fast and it's like oh like do I stop this? Like I still got some things I want to say. Like I don't know if you understand this the way that I want, but um again, it just makes you go back and re-evaluate kind of how you're going to interact with the players in that setting and you know, anytime you have that, like you just you're so far ahead. Like you're so far ahead because it's not like they're waiting to get on the field to have that interaction and communication, right? Our DBs are on the front and the backers are behind them. So, you're seeing DBs turn around and actually make eye contact and like that's going to carry over. There's no way that doesn't carry over to the field. >> Johnson is a different personality than a lot of the guys that we see out here. Your personality talking about listening and how you go about it, what have you seen from him and how does that mesh with you? >> He's the opposite. He's speaking first. >> I think every team needs a little bit of an edge, right? The biggest thing about CJ is his his heart, man. He's got a huge heart. He means well and he loves football. He loves to compete, right? Some of the other stuff, yeah, he he's going to walk the line. He's going to cross the line and you're going to have to have those conversations with him. Um it's important when you have a big strong personality like that that the group understands who he is and where he's coming from, right? Deep down, what does he believe? What's he all about? So, as we get through camp, like that's a big piece um with the players, with me of getting guys to understand, you know, why why you play the game, right? Why why are you the way you are? Like how did we get here? So, we'll we'll go through some things where just building that trust and communication, but anytime you have those strong personalities and guys that want to speak out, they want to be in front of the group, like you just have to get the people around them to understand who they are, where they're coming from and and then you get you get buying. You don't always get people who agree with it, right? But you at least get an understanding of of where people come from and the passion that they have, right? What drives them to what what motivates them and he's a winner, right? He's a competitor, he's a winner, he's been productive on the field and uh that's going to help our defense as well. >> Hey Jay, is it a bit surreal for you to be back here specifically at Fisher in a much much different role? >> Yeah, obviously it in some ways it feels a little full circle. You know, remember being in these dorms was they weren't quite as nice and um obviously there's been a ton of upgrades. It was always a great place to go to camp because as a team you do become closer, right? You're you're isolated and it's a great setup. Not every team has this type of setting to to have practice. The the weather obviously here is is a little bit better than some places where you're dealing with some of the heat issues, but um training camps were always a little bit special, um nerve-racking, right? Cuz cuz you're you're high stress and you're trying to make a team especially being undrafted. Um but it is a little bit of a a strange feeling walking around here kind of feeling like you know it, but at the same time it's it's a totally different field just with the role I'm in. >> Jim, beyond the talk about Caleb specifically, but just how do you view that competition at inside linebacker with Dorian coming back and just the group as a whole? >> Yeah, really excited to see how the beginning of camp starts to play out when um when guys are getting on the field and just the different combinations, right? Like how we can play guys off of each other and how many snaps, you know, there's there's a number of guys that are going to have roles on special teams, right? So the depth at that position I think is extremely important as we go forward and um some unique and different skill sets, right? Within within the top part of that group. So um can't wait till the pads come on. You know, for a linebackers it's it's hard to get a true evaluation um until the pads come on and and and you start getting into different situations, but um early reviews are great, man. I love the way that they're they're playing and functioning within the defense. >> Jim, beyond the details of individual roles, kind of high level, what what's the the most important concept players have to grasp and understand who played in the old defense that are going to be successful in yours? I think to me there's there's probably going to be a little bit more volume than they've had and to me getting them to understand the reasoning behind it, right? Not it's not volume just to to have a lot to carry a lot of things and to put a lot of things on tape, right? It's still in my mind like we're doing things for a reason, right? We're not going to be reckless. Uh the game planning behind it, there's going to be reasons and that's where training camp to me gets hard because you're installing to just put things on tape, right? So, as a coach at you have to over-communicate. All right, this is a situation, right? Maybe this is the the skill set of the tight end and that's the only reason we'd run this pressure. Like, there's certain things you have to communicate on within game planning how you actually want to call this versus an off-season or a training camp when you're just trying to get things installed and get things wrapped. Um you know, there's something plenty of things that we would not want to do against our offense, you know, with that style of offense. And I think there's there's that fine balance of getting guys to understand like I want to dictate what offenses do and the more we can carry into a game, we have options. We have adjustments that we can get to, but at the same time I I told them my my very first thing is is play speed and confidence. Like if play speed or confidence start to go down, we're doing too much, we're not coaching it correctly. We have to make adjustments as a staff um to put them in better positions to win. >> Jim, talking to different players about switching from a 4-3 to 3-4, it seems like a lot of players are really excited about the possibilities and opportunities. [clears throat] What do you see from the model [cough] from the players overall [clears throat] so far about switching? >> I think overall it's it's you you look at the front, right? You look at the D-line, the outside backers, the the linebackers. From a a DB perspective, you know, they might act like they're excited, but there's not a lot that changes in their world, right? But, I think from a front standpoint, they understand the differences. You know, they understand from a blocking scheme standpoint like what you force offenses to do, the the one-on-ones that you you create, the angles that you can create in the run game. I think we have a smart group that understands um the differences of that and and how it can help them, right? How it can help free them up, um isolate offensive lineman, which is what you want to do in the NFL, man. You you want to take some of the double teams off and make a little bit harder for those guys up front. So, um we have a smart group that understands what that's all about and they're excited to to have the opportunity to go make plays. >> Jim Nantz will go off top and just a bit. Um the AP is doing a thing on the 25th anniversary of the extreme heat deaths. You were a freshman at Wisconsin at the time in 2001. Did Did in any way did that you remember that or did it influence you um in any way if you recall? >> Uh I just obviously shocking, right? It was the first time that I really had seen something like that happen and and obviously we we grew up in a era where where you you got [snorts] after it, right? Workouts like designed to be very hard and and in a number of cases like they want people to fail, right? Not necessarily your whole team, but like and I think it just made everyone kind of step back and re-evaluate. Is that the right way? You have the heat issues. Like what's What's the right way to be smart about this? You want to push your players. You want to push your team. Going through hard things as a team brings you together, right? Like there's a lot of good behind um running a training camp a certain way or a conditioning session a certain way and I think it just made everyone from coaches, players, medical staff kind of step back and and re-evaluate. Is this the right way to do things? But I mean, being young as a player, it was just kind of one of those like we're not invisi- invincible things, right? That was kind of the biggest piece you took from it was like, "Oh man, I like we better take care of ourselves and take care of each other um when you see things start to happen as far as uh guys getting in trouble with with whether it was heat or just just a hard work load for the day. Yeah, number one, we we communicated with him. We have some great experience vets around. You learn like learn how to be a professional, uh learn the position. Um he did a great job. You know, he went down to Florida with Chub. Like from day one, he's he's really turned into a you know, just puppy dog to some of those older guys. Like just follow him around, learn from him. Um he's got a chip on his shoulder. He's still, you know, it's funny. You get guys that they're drafted in a certain spot. Like he still feels like he slighted, right? Like man, I'm better than what where I came out. Um we're glad we got him. You know, we're really glad we got him. He did an amazing job kind of transitioning his body over the last 6 weeks, um putting himself in a in a great position here to to put his best foot forward in camp. But he took everything we we taught him in the spring and just soaked it all up. It's kind of drinking from a fire hose as a rookie because you you have no break, right? You start your college season and you just go. So, um this last six six weeks, you can tell just from the way he's carrying himself right now that he handled it the right way.

title: DJ Moore Addresses Media for the First Time at Buffalo Bills Training Camp!
text: What do you think things are little progress report between you and Josh so far? >> Um, I want to say they're on the ups. Um, the first two days have been really good. So, we just got to keep building on that and uh go from there. >> What did you do? I don't know. Did you guys meet at all in that 6-week gap? And if not, how do you continue to build on that even if not doing reps on the field? >> Uh, constant communication. Um, he was in LA. I was moving from moving houses and selling houses. So, uh just the communication-wise and just getting out here earlier and just going back and forth like we are uh today. Uh, constant communication on the field uh between the two days and we just going to keep building. >> Now that you've been in the building for a couple months, what's it been like to see Joe Brady in this setting as running his whole operation compared to like, you know, your experience with him back in Carolina? >> Uh when he was in Carolina, he was on people a lot. Uh now that he's in this major role as being the head coach, uh I feel like he's made it more of a made it more known that this is the details and how we're going about things and uh with specific guys he's counting on uh so, you got to have a like you got to wear a hard hat every day with him and then um he wants the best out of everybody. >> Gabe, how do you approach this as as a fresh start and new start or just the opportunity that presents itself? >> Uh, it's definitely a new start. A new team. Being here in Buffalo is definitely like a new start. Uh, especially with Josh and and all the guys that have been here the longest and um I'm the new guy coming in. So, I got to catch up. But, I think I'm doing pretty good at doing that and uh we're hitting the ground running. >> Gabe, what's what's been just your impression so far of your fellow wide receivers and the guys in that room? >> Uh, they all like they all are What can I say? They're funny and they all are themselves. Um, you never see somebody uh not being themself. Uh, they're always asking questions and and want to go out there and have fun doing what they doing. >> You've already been involved in the community a bunch over the summer. Just why was that important to you and what's it like getting to know the people around here in the Buffalo area? >> Uh, one to show my kids, uh, the right way to do things and then my wife makes me, uh, figure out different ways to, you know, give back and come up with new ways to be in the community. So, with that, we have more to life and then we just go around the community not just in one certain area, but like throughout the throughout the cities that that are around us and give back. >> What are some of your initial thoughts on getting away from training camp and coming here and having your family? Like what is this experience been like so >> Uh, we did this before in Carolina. So, being in the dorm room again is like second nature and then being being away from them is fine for right now, but, uh, they're not too far away, so I'm good with that. >> Not sure how well you knew Ian Weiler when you guys were in Chicago together, but he he joined the team recently. Just what's it like having a familiar face like Ian back around? >> Uh, it was funny. We was watching Ian on TV and then, I guess when the season ended for them, uh, in the UFL, we picked them up and I was like, "Dang, I already know Ian." And Ian's a good football player. He's fast. He's intelligent. He just going to hit the ground running. >> How do you deal with the ex- How do you deal with the expectations that are put on you? Um, you may have your own expectations, but are you aware of the outside expectations of your arrival? >> I don't really worry about expectations for real. I just go out there and be me, uh, each and every day to try to get better and better and and be on the upside of things around here. Don't mind them. >> He started it. >> Okay. >> [laughter] >> Um, you talked about the guys in your room. What have been your impressions of Keon, the football player? >> Keon is very smart. I mean, he's always giving a different viewpoint on on how the plays can be ran and and stuff like that. And you know, he always he always talking. So, some of the things he he says you be like, "Okay." But then you be like, "Dang, that was really might be a a good way to put things." >> Do you enjoy a role of maybe being a mentor for younger players? >> Uh, I wouldn't say a mentor. I just just go out there, be myself, lead by example. And they they so far they just been following and we've been having a good time.

Uh, so I did think that there there there's got to be a little bit more injury potential when it's raining than when it's not, especially day one and when you're trying to get acclimated. To the point about the fan experience, I feel bad uh for the kids. Uh think of the kids who will never, and that's not to say you can't go to your local memorabilia place and just buy one, but how often in your life or as a kid or a Bills fan, are you going to get a chance to meet Josh Allen? And for some of those kids, the one and only time happened either Wednesday or Thursday, and they get a chance to have Josh Allen sign what? Their wet helmet, the wet football, the wet piece of paper, the whatever. I see kids dropping their stuff into the into the grass or onto the the, you know, onto the ground. And it's I'm like, "Oh my god, those kids are going to have this keepsake that they're going to look at for the rest of their lives and say, "God damn it, the rain." Or else I'd have this perfect Josh Allen signature uh or this thing that I can even I'm not even talking about the resale value. I'm just talking about the moment and just to have have it be raining. Yeah, the rain it hasn't rained hard enough to really ruin the experience and it seemed to let up enough post practice that Josh Awen was still out there signing autographs. >> Yeah, but it it today it let up by the time practice ended. I think yesterday it got a little bit uh clear around the end of practice. Maybe not, but it hasn't stopped the autograph signings.
