Um not really a part of it like a bunch of special teams right now, but just even just being in the meetings and listening, uh I like his his motive and like what he bringing to the table for sure. Um he's a wiry guy. Um a little different than Rich. Rich was more old school and kind of demanding. He's more uh open and listening, so I I I like that aspect in him. Um yeah. I miss Rich though, but >> He he went to your rival though, right? Clemson is is a rival of South Carolina. >> I texted Rich this morning and gave him the middle finger sign. >> [laughter] >> He'll be He'll be okay. >> At what point do you start to feel free and confident with Gannon's new installs in the defense? >> Uh I was free in OTAs, honestly. Um it uh really helps my skill set. Um, it allowed me to make plays at corner. Um, I like it. I like what we're doing. I think the other guys at the safeties like what they're doing. It's a little different. Um, they we use like a three safety thing. That's kind of new. Um, but that put everybody on the field, you know? >> Did Rich respond to your text? >> Who, Rich? >> Yeah, did he respond to the middle finger text? >> course. >> What did he respond with? >> Sent me one back. >> Is that a usual occurrence? Do you guys usually [snorts] send a finger to each other? >> Always. >> Since uh since 2019. Actually before that, Rich even ran my pro day when I came out of college and uh yeah, he's been trying to be up under me ever since. >> So, your text string is just a it's just middle finger after middle finger? >> Middle fingers and pictures, that's it. >> Yeah, he likes to send old pictures of me and him. He needs to let it go. He left us. >> You had told us how much it helped to have, you know, a year of outside corner on your belt approaching this off season. Now that you got time to reflect on it, how much has that helped and how, you know, better will that make you at the position? >> I think it helped a lot. Um, just going over the film and just watching the mistakes I made and just, you know, uh some of the dumb penalties that I I gave up, just just not knowing and understanding what, you know, the levels of it, how what it takes, but you know, I feel like I had a really strong year to start it, but definitely ready to prove myself again this year, for sure. >> What do you think you guys have in that room depth-wise? Do you like what you have? >> Uh corner or just the defense? >> corner. >> Uh yeah, I like it. Uh CV, CV. Um, I've been with CV his whole career. Every playoff game I've ever played in, CV was on the other side of me. So, you can't take that away from him. Um, Ceedy Ceedy's a great addition. Young guy, love football. Um, really athletic. I like what he I see him about I kind of knew it already. I've worked out with him since he was in college. And then uh Saint-Juste, too. Really big kid. Play a lot of football. Um, high IQ guy, smart guy. He's from Canada. He likes to tell everybody that. Nobody really cares, but you know, >> he he's a he's good football player, too. I I like the depth we got right now. Uh there's a lot of competition going on. Um but we just got to end the camp healthy. I think that's the biggest goal is to be healthy coming in the season and get through the season healthy. >> How important is it to have a strong defense for the first four plus weeks that Mike is not on the field? >> Um it's just like I always say in the NFL, everybody got to step up. If a If the top guy goes down, somebody got to play. Um it was like that when Jair got hurt for me and I had to come up and play, so you learn how to step up to the plate. Somebody will play. Um there's a lot of people. People got to step up. I think Van Ness is going to take a big leap this year. Um Uh Terrell's been playing really good in camp. Well, OTAs since camp has been 2 days, but I think everybody's ready to play. Uh we lost Quay in free agency, but Z has been a great addition. Um he's played a lot of football, got all-pros and accolades, too, so I think we're ready to play as a defense. Um offense is going to be the offense. We're out of our control, you know. We just got to get ready to play football. We're going to get to Minnesota. We'll be in Minnesota. It's going to get cracking, for sure. >> For you and your game, I guess in terms of trying to take that next step continually even build on what you did last year, you know, what does that look like for you? What do you want to do on the field in terms of, you know, taking that next step and kind of showing the world? >> I just want to compete. Um take a step from last year, you know. Um not all just worry about PBUs and just pass breakups in my stats, you know. I want to play complete football. Um of course limit the penalties and stuff like that, but that's growing pains. I feel like uh it's just another step that I can take and I think we have the athleticism to do it, so just put it together.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Hey, Hey. Heat. Heat. Hello. Nat. Good morning. When did uh Kan get hurt since he was on the field? >> Well, he just um was feeling a little tightness and just like most guys, we're going to be cautious. Get a scan and make sure he's good to go, but he should be out there today. >> Yeah, same thing. he felt something um in individual and so we're just being cautious with him and we'll have a little bit better idea once he goes through the testing today but he will not be out there. >> Matt, what happened exactly when Musgrave went down this this spring? Do do you remember the play or just exactly kind of what happened there? Yeah, it was he was just doing a a basic individual drill and felt something and so obviously we investigated further and we're just hoping that it'll subside over time. >> I know it's still early, but how have you seen Zier and Cooper's skill sets mesh and kind of them build their chemistry as they got? >> Well, yeah, Z's played a ton of football and I think you can feel his presence and his veteran leadership. uh not only in the linebacker room or on defense, but amongst the team. So, I think he'll be a great guy for everybody in that room to kind of lean on in terms of his experience and what he's what he's seen in this league. >> Does he maybe allow you to do a little bit more with not that quite wasn't an experienced guy, but does all that Zyra's done, does that maybe allow you to do a little bit more with Cooper? >> Um, I I don't know. I I would think like right now we're just we're all focused on learning a new system and and there's a natural evolution I would say in our game every year with an idea of what you think it's going to look like and where it goes to and I think we're kind of working through that process right now. >> Talked about how he had wanted to get Zier for a while. What have your interactions been like with >> Really positive I think from day one just when we got him. um sitting down with him and trying to get to know the guy. Uh but it's not a secret as to why he's had so much success. I mean, you can see it just his approach when he when he enters the building, how how um engaged he is in meetings. Um and then the guy loves to practice and you can't have enough of those guys. >> What does it mean to get, you know, Isaiah extended too because we talked so much about Cooper and Frank everything, but having him >> McDuffy is a glue guy. I mean, he is the epitome of what we want everybody to be in this program. I mean, he's from day one, he loves football. He he's a great teammate. Um, and I just think it speaks to his character. So, to, you know, you just can't have enough guys like that. >> Matt, what do you what do you think Scott Moore can potentially bring to your team this year? Well, I think you saw a little bit of flashes yesterday and granted we're still early in the process, but certainly um he's proven it as a returner, but I do think there's more out there for him um on the offensive side of the ball. So, we'll see where it goes. >> Looked like he had a lot of cat and mouse at the line of scrimmage yesterday right off the bat with Jordan making calls and kind of switching the plays and whatever. How did you think the offense reacted to some of the pressure looks? They're dropping out. They're coming. Was did they pick up where they left off from this off? >> Yeah, I think there was a lot of learning that transpired over the course of the offseason. I think JG does such a great job of giving you, we talked about it today, just some of the disguises like you can't tell are they coming, are they not coming? Um, and that's only going to get amped up the further we move along into training camp. I mean, obviously day one you're you've got a very limited menu. Um, that'll that'll pick up today and as we transition in some of those, you know, past situations, some of those looks can get pretty exotic. >> Do you need to do a little bit more of that since you open against Flores? >> You can't get enough of it when you're going against a guy like that that is can throw anything at you. So, yeah, I definitely think that that'll help us, you know, early on in the season. We have a long snapper today. >> Excuse me. >> Will you have a long snapper today? >> Um, I know that we're working out some guys. >> Matt Tucker Craft's improvement as a player has been obvious, but he also seems like he's become a really confident guy without also being kind of a jerk about it. >> Oh, what did you want to say, Rob? >> You should have just said it. you know, >> if this wasn't live, I would. But the the evolution of him as a sort of a leader and a confident guy in that room. Um, where do you think that comes from? And how do you how do you see that develop? >> Yeah, I think just um I think it comes from the work that he puts in and he I think I said it yesterday, he doesn't shy away from the work. Um, and I think, you know, just over time he he's he's got more comfortable, I think, and has matured. And um there's a reason he was voted a captain last year and cuz everybody sees it, what he does, how he treats others in the building. Um you know, he he's right along the lines of Isaiah McDuffy. >> What you think of that pass by Jones yesterday and what do you think ultimately in the long run with some development you might be able to get there? Uh well, it was an extremely athletic play to escape the pocket and I mean he he threw a dime right there in the back corner of the end zone to Isaiah Na uh who made a great catch, but um you know I think there he's got a big learning curve in front of him. So I don't want to I don't want to put it too far out there. Certainly he's a talented guy, but he's he's going to have to prove it every day. >> Brandon Cece took a lot of the first team reps yesterday. What have you seen from him that you like? >> [snorts] >> uh a lot. He's first of all the skill set. I think we can all see that. But uh he's a guy that's hungry for for a young guy. He's a pretty mature mature kid. Um but yeah, he he loves football. That's the best way to put it. And he's going to get better and better and better the more reps he gets. >> How do you feel like Keshan Nixon has grown this off season now having a full year under his belt at outside corner? Yeah, I thought he he's he's played some really good football for us. So, um it'll be it'll be great to get him back out there today. >> What's the value of having someone like that back in the room today out there on the field rather than just being off? >> Well, he's he's got a ton of experience under his belt and certainly knows how we want to do things around here. Um and so excited to see him out there competing today. >> You said you're learning a new defense. You've obviously had experience with that a couple of other times in your tenure. How do you streamline the process or accelerate the process or is that it just takes the time it takes? >> Yeah, I would say it just it takes reps just like anything else in life. And um you know it's there there's a lot of learning going on, but I thought our guys did a really nice job from a coaching standpoint and the players were receptive to it in terms of just the foundation we laid in the offseason. And I think that's one of the key benefits to an offseason program is to just so it's not the first time they're hearing it when they come to training camp. >> Zavon Williams playing in the receiver room this season. >> He's going to compete to get as many reps as he can. Um I thought he had a good first day, but you know, you got to you got to do it consistently. Certainly. He's a guy that we are high on um coming out in the draft. I thought he had some flashes last year of some some really key and big plays, most notably in that Giants game. He caught a huge third down jump ball type situation. Um, so it's fun. It's going to be fun to see his growth throughout the course of the preseason. >> Guys, you will try to develop on the offensive line at one position, and I'm talking about backups. I know you have your five and they're going to play there, but do you want to still just shuffle them around like crazy this this? >> No, I don't I don't think you ever want that, but it's just the nature of it. And certainly if you're not entrenched in one of those starting roles, um the more you can do, it makes you more valuable. So, I would say it's going to be pretty fluid in regards to how we rotate those guys along the front. >> What you've done in the past? Uh uh yeah, dependent upon what each guy can handle. >> During the practices when the pads aren't on, what are you looking for from the edge rusher group as you evaluate their play >> to work an edge and not to go through the offensive lineman? I mean, that's been some lengthy discussions. There's been a lot of examples shown and I get it. It's football. Stuff happens. But we we don't want to see any bull rush out there. It's it's just hard to do when when you don't have pads on. And there were a couple instances yesterday where guys were in that position, but I thought they did a good job of that point and sort of just continuing to drive the offensive line into the lap of the quarterback. They pulled off and that's that's kind of what we're looking for. >> I know that you do extensive research into who you want as your defensive coordinator, but what what do you think was most surprised you about this time with Ganon that maybe you didn't realize during the hiring process? >> I wouldn't say anything surprised me. I mean, I had a pretty good idea of um the man we were getting when when we got him. Um but he's got he's got he understands football. He understands offensive football, which I think is I mean it's imperative when you're in one of those roles. You better know the other side of the ball. Um and he understands the importance of trying to give similar looks and have different things off of that. So, I think he does a great job. He's a great communicator. Um he holds these guys to a high standard now. Um it's it's the tape's the tape. It is what it is. And um yeah, he's not afraid to just hold it to that. >> Matt, the Guardian Caps have a new look to them this year. Is there any new science behind it? Do you like the way they look better than last year? >> I don't really That's That's none of my concern. Not to like dismiss your question, but like that's the least of my worries. What's next for Jordan Love? What's the next step in his evolution if there is that next step? >> I just think, you know, I think all every player can get can improve in some facet. I think one of the things that he's been really focused and conscious of throughout the course of the off season and um you know on his own in the summer is just trying to play with as much balance in the pocket as he can and knowing that there's going to be times where you get moved off the spot. But um when it's when you can can you can you maintain that balance because I think that one thing you see from I'd say majority of quarterbacks in the league when they are balanced in the pocket they're going to be more consistent and more accurate over time. >> Swoon's question about the offensive line from a few minutes ago. You back when you had Berry here you had Rasheed be the backup then you had Jordan Morgan to be the backup the last few years. What what are you looking for in a backup left tackle? Would you like to have a pure tackle to stick in there or would you be comfortable moving player A over there and kind of shifting things around or different preference? >> You guys know what I'm going to say, right? >> I know the best. >> Well, I But that is the reality of it. It's just like you try to get the best 11 out there on the field. Um, we're trying to put our best players who can help us play winning football. And so, um, in terms of what, like, I guess I don't really totally understand your question in terms of what you look for in a a backup left tackle. I mean, obviously if if your backup has starter ability, that's what that's what you want. And so, you train those guys and hopefully they can go out there and perform at a at a starter level. >> Yeah. poorly question, poorly asked, but I guess would you prefer to have like a Brandt Banks a guy you can just have be that guy as opposed to moving your starting bright guard over there and then was there something that you'd rather do than the other or is it purely whoever gives you the best chance to win? >> You answered the question. Um, I I would just say, yeah, like you're going to put your most talented players in out out on the field to to hopefully give you the best chance to win. >> Talk about, you know, some guys stepping up at bigger roles this year. One of them probably will be Matthew. Just what excites you about, you know, what he's taking that next step to maybe take that next step in the offense and he's talked about that he's ready to take that next leap. just what what excites you about year two and maybe the playbook, you know, kind of slowing down for him, too. >> Yeah, I think that you said it right there. I think just the experience. He's been in big big moments. Um he's had some big big- time plays in big moments. Um and just can hopefully can can continue to build upon what he did, especially in that Chicago game. I thought he he went out there and he balled out and he played with the play style. That's one thing that we always talk about with no matter what position group you're you're playing at is is it the the style of play and I think that there were some moments where you know we were looking for better but I think he's responded to those challenges and early indications. I mean, there was a there was a play yesterday um where we ran a keeper, dumped the ball off in the flat and he's running a low cross and how he transitions to a blocker. I think that says a lot about you as a as a player. What do you do when you don't have the football and I think he's he's early indications are are promising. >> When you were talking about balance with love, are you are you talking about having your feet on the ground and and >> Yeah, all of the above. Yeah, absolutely. >> It's as you're moving around trying to regain your balance or not. >> Yeah, that's part of it, too. When you get moved out the spot, can you can you if if allowed, I mean, if the pocket allows you to, you know, can you set back up abruptly um and and get back to a balanced position? Thanks, guys. title: Exclusive Interview with Grant Delpit
text: Welcome back to Cleveland Browns Daily, brought to you by Bally Bet, official sports betting partner of your Cleveland Browns. And for the second day in a row, I get to talk to one of my favorite guys with great news around him. Grant Delpit signing a 3-year extension that will keep you here with the Cleveland Browns through 2029. Make it to the third contract, something that's very difficult to do in the NFL. How do you feel, man? You've worked so hard to get to this point and to have it pay off, it's got to be awesome. >> It's awesome. Uh, Browns organization believing in me, the fans, uh, teammates, coaches, everybody. So, it's good to be be that, you know, that steady leader, that steady player that people can rely on. And look, look like we here for the long haul, man. >> Yeah, and we're all happy about that, you know. When you think about on the back end now, you and Denzel both through 2029. You got some young guys in there and I was joking with him and he did not like it very much, but I'm like, you're kind of the veteran now. And it's got to be crazy. I mean, I'm sure you remember being out here your first training camp. Obviously, that one didn't go the way you wanted, but to think about where you are now, incredible testament to your work and what you've done. But, how's it kind of being in that role now where you look around and you're the vet. >> Yeah, a whole lot of new faces, whole lot of new coaches. Team full of young guys, man. Team full of Bronies and we the Browns, you know, [laughter] so, you know, I think Denzel is actually like OG. I feel like I'm still in that big bro kind of range, but Denzel is he's kicking up there to that OG. >> Okay. What's it like kind of for you, you know, you wanted to get this done. We know that it it kind of impacted the way that you approached the earlier portion of the off season as you guys got it done. But, to just get it done and now be all about football and getting ready here for this 2026 season. >> Yeah, I mean, that's what's most important, training camp. Uh, we take this time to train. You know, let's let's let's get what we got to do, let's get it done. You know, of course, leave that to my agency and people who control those things, but can't say enough good things about AB and and the Browns and how they handled, you know, getting us ready for the situation and and ultimately, uh, down to the wire, but I was able to practice yesterday, so that felt good. >> Well, I was talking to you at lunch and and you said I they're working on it right now. And maybe my eyes deceive me, but it felt like at some point yesterday AB came over and said, "Yes, it is actually done." Is that how it happened and what did he say to you? >> Yeah, he came running on the field. He said, "You know, it's done." He said he said we're going to I know you haven't signed yet, but we'll honor your your contract, your deal, and you know, if you want to practice, you can practice." I said, "Come on, give me my helmet." >> That's great. That had to be a good feeling. You get goosebumps when he when he came out and said that? >> Yeah, I mean, it's hard to take it at the moment cuz you know, you really just want to practice, so I think after practice when everybody, you know, hit me up and and and doing those all those kind of things. You know, you check your phone, it's a thousand messages and [laughter] this and whatnot, but it's like we've been doing this for years now, so it's kind of it is what it is. >> Now, your mom is obviously your biggest fan, travels everywhere for all of the games. This had to be an incredible moment for you to be able to share with her as well. I know you've been having too much time to to dive into it, but how's that been to have, you know, be able to to reward your hard work and and everything that your mom's done to raise you and support you over this time? >> No doubt, you know, my family's done a great job of having a support system for us, and if y'all haven't seen my mom, she's a she's Browns number She's She's my number [laughter] one fan, but she becomes, you know, team mom and team number one fan as well, so I think that that's very important in life is just having a great support system. >> Yep. >> Uh you know, upbringing like we did, um my sisters and everybody, cousins, everybody that's just been around me is is cool to see this this growth that we have as as a as a family, so hopefully we keep it going. >> It's awesome. All right, speaking of keeping it going, that means let's getting on this field and and winning some games this year. A change at defensive coordinator, Mike Rutenberg comes in and you can feel his energy just being out here seeing him. What's it been like working with him and and how is, you know, without giving away the secrets, but you know, a lot's going to stay the same, but there are going to be some fun new wrinkles. >> A lot of new wrinkles, a lot of confusion for the offense. >> Mhm. >> Um obviously, if it's confusion for the offense, that means that we're switching up some looks and we doing this, that, and the third. So, we're getting it right right now. Uh if we're moving around a lot, you know, it's going to be a couple mistakes here and there. Uh that's what we do right now. We get it cleaned up. And we just demand our respect from the offense. >> When you have a new defensive coordinator, often then that would mean that everybody's different. But in this case, they kept your position coach, Coach Bando, who's one of the best in the league, an opportunity maybe to be a defensive coordinator himself, certainly soon got interviews this year. But how's that helped having that continuity of you yourself, obviously, Rocket, and then Donovan's been here, Chris has been here, some of those guys in that room. But to be able to have Yeah, there's some new stuff, but there's still a lot of continuity in terms of who the main guy in your room is. >> Yeah, I think that first of all, Bando, you know, what can I say, man? He's a He's a ultimate players coach. Cares about you, cares about how your family's doing. And I think that makes the players want to, you know, go just the extra mile for him. And I think that's why he has so much success with players, uh with any relationship with coaches, anybody. So, when you have a coach like that, it's easy to play for. Uh Rudy, I don't even know, man. It's like >> [laughter] >> It's uh it's a roller coaster, Rudy, man. Just always bring emotion. Yep. Like his defense literally portrays what he has a is as a person. You know, it's it's very exotic and very like uh I don't know. It's just a deep It's a fun defense to play in. And he exemplifies that. So, it's it's contagious. It spreads. >> For you guys, it's really kind of the first time in a while that you're going against, at least at its core, a new type of an offensive scheme. What have you kind of seen from the offense as you've gone through? And you've been able to do it on the field a little bit, but also through film. And, you know, obviously, they've made a lot of investment in the young skill talent there. So, I think it's going to be kind of a fun camp to see you guys battle it out. >> Yeah, like like I said, I don't know all the intricate details of what they got going on. I know that Monken's got them under control. And and it's is is a different look, different feel to it, but at the same time as a defender like I like to control the pace. I like to I like to dictate what the what the offense is going to do, so I'm going to continue doing that and hopefully, you know, iron sharpens iron. >> What do you think about your experience with coach Monk so far? I mean, just the directness, the the passion is got to be awesome. >> Yeah, yeah. I think it's you know, that's what you get with top-tier coaches like him. Been around the game for so long, finally getting his chance as an NFL head coach, so I know he has a lot to prove and I think, you know, so it's a lot on the on the table for him, but you know, he can handle it, so let's do it. >> Absolutely. Well, we'll wrap it up. Congratulations again, man. Grant, always a pleasure. Let's go Browns, baby. >> Go Browns, all power.

title: Andrew Berry Press Conference | July 30th, 2026
text: Morning, everyone. We good to get going? All right. Uh excited to start the 2026 training camp. Uh we can't wait to get ramped up and going. Um part of the reason we're really excited is because we expect this to be a very competitive camp from top to bottom on the roster. Uh obviously, over the last, you know, two off seasons, uh we made some difficult decisions in order to set up the franchise for sustained success, but we're really excited about the young core that we have in place on um you know, both sides of the ball and are looking forward to see them grow and develop over the next um you know, several weeks. I also want to just mention um you know, Todd and his staff, they did a fantastic job running a great off-season program and we're all looking forward to seeing their vision come to life on the grass here as we begin training camp. You know, last thing before I open it up for questions, I wanted to just take a few moments to acknowledge Chris Powell and Scotty Springer. Um you know, they are uh they've had a fantastic Browns Cleveland Browns career. Uh Chris was our longest-tenured employee. Scotty was our third-longest tenured employee and between them, they have five decades of experience overseeing and running, you know, the grounds crew. Um those two individuals, they embody everything that you want from an employee. Servant leadership, um excellence in their role and ultimate humility. Um you know, they did not have glamour positions, you know, in the organization, but all they did was excel and treat people with with with kindness and decency throughout. So, it's bittersweet for us um because while we're happy to celebrate such long and excellent careers, we're really, really sad to see both those two go. So, with that, I'll open up for questions. >> Can you maybe first address getting Denzel and Grant both wrapped up long-term? How do you feel about that? >> Yeah, really excited. Those guys are um you know, they're they're core members of our team. I was I was joking with with Peter. I was like, "Okay, well, Denzel's 29 and Grant, he's 27, soon to turn 28 and you know, they're the elder statesman, you know, of the team. Um but really excited to have those guys. Um they're they're what we want in the organization. We were with Chubb when we were finalizing his uh his deal. I guess it was what, 20 2, 21, something along those lines. I think you've all seen De Wain's new smell, you know, uh, you know, physique, that type of thing, and he's done a really great job with that. You get that month and a half off to digest everything, and you come back, and you're just ready to work. >> Do you already feel like part of the team going through spring? >> Yeah, no, I felt like part of the team the first day here. You know, the guys were understanding of the circumstances. They gave me my little bit of time to, you know, remorse and everything like that. But, I feel like I'm like I'm a brother. I feel like I've been with these dudes all year, all OTAs. >> Did you during Did you during the offseason did you try to find a way to like connect with some guys like Alex or Isaiah or guys in the room? >> Yeah, no, I got some training with a couple of the guys. Uh me and Q had ended up going to a wedding together. I got to see A-Wright and a couple of the other guys while I was on a little vacation. No, I got to spend some good time with everybody. >> You've had a couple of teammates long with Kendal Wright and Greg Robinson, but just seeing them get those extensions, how how excited were you for not only them, but what it says about the defense and the level you guys are trying to compete at? >> Yeah, no, no doubt about it. You can tell they're very humble. You know, they get in the locker room and everybody, you know, they get paid. You know how guys are, "Oh, yeah, you got paid." You know, they they were real humble and everything like that. They tried to like downplay it. Man, that's big money, and I'm very happy for them and their families. You know, they're able to, you know, rejoice in all that. But, they came back the next day just ready to work. It wasn't anything about the money or anything like that. They're ready to move on. >> Is this different than your first two camps with the 49ers >> Oh, well, but no, no, you're good. You're good. No, it don't it don't feel no different. At the end of the day, football is just football. You just work. You know, obviously, it's a different area, different, you know, vibe, different playbook. And I'm I'm ready for all of that. >> Jared, sacks are everything. We all know that. What do you think the next evolution of your sack game >> I mean, it's it's just finishing. I mean, when you look at the numbers and everything like that, no, I'm a big stat guy, big number guy, but to be translucent with it and talk about the statistics of it all, I'm one of the highest pressure rates, but pressures don't mean anything if you can't finish. Getting to the quarterback means nothing if you can't finish. Yeah, those them off a little bit and messes with his head, but you know, sacks is what puts them back a little bit and that's just, you know, finishing is just my biggest part. A hundred or thousand, yeah. I want to finish as many times as possible. As many times I get back there, I want to finish. Yeah, you know, I mean, Clowney is obviously one of the best rushers I've ever, you know, watched, you know, watching his film from college and everything like that. That's one of the biggest reasons I even ever played D-end. So, you know, having that dude in the room would be, you know, like, you know, monumental for me. But, I will say, you know, having that vet presence is probably even bigger than just, you know, my own personal honor of him. Having that vet presence, someone that's been around the game, someone that can teach you things like that. That's why I went to the sack summit to be around, you know, Von Miller, Maxx Crosby, you know, all these, you know, high-end rushers cuz you can learn so much from them. No, I didn't even get to see him. I I heard about it word of mouth. >> When you talk about finishing, what do you think is that next step for you? How do you go about finishing? >> I think it's just, you know, working on grip strength and everything like that. You can get your hands on them, you can throw them around and everything like that, but that with the game, the way it's evolving, quarterbacks are getting stronger, they're being able to move a little bit faster, everything like that. So, if you get your hands on them, you might not get another chance to do that. You just got to handle it right then and there. Yeah, I mean, I feel very confident that if I go out of the game, you know, somebody can come up right behind me and handle that. That's not something I've always been used to. You know, sometimes I got to go into the game, I got to go seven, eight, nine, 10 plays, get off a play, and then go back in. Like, and having those people behind you that, you know, you can trust to go in and help hold things down for a play or two while I get my little breath out, maybe three, then let me come back in and just dominate, you know, having that, you know, that second that, you know, that second string there, a little bit of depth is is monumental. >> There's been a lot said about your character ability and your willingness to come in and immediately in the spring and start being a vocal leader. It's almost like you've been here for 10 years. Well, where did you maybe develop that in the course of your life and is that something that you have felt close to doing in the same >> Yeah, I mean, that's just honestly from my dad. My dad's always been a vocal person. He's always, you know, something just go wrong, if something's not the way that he would like it up to his standards, he's going to voice it. And that's something I've just carried with my whole life from when I was in college, high school, everything like that. Just going all the way up to the league. That's something I did with the Rams and I got in trouble with it at a couple times at the Rams being too vocal, but that's just something that's the way I am. I just want everybody to I hold everybody to a high standard cuz I hold myself to a high standard. >> Okay, and what about the team leads? They said you were being too vocal. What did they say? >> No, it was Sean. >> I believe that's something you mentioned that you learned how to develop different moves. >> Yeah, yeah, definitely. I mean, we watched a bunch of different players' tapes and everything like that. When my tape came up, you know, Von and Maxx and Cam Jordan, they were quick to, you know, announce, "Hey, your power, best power in the league. You're like, you can walk anybody back. Once you work work a move off that, you you'll be unstoppable. You'll go from, you know, seven, eight, nine sacks to 20, you know, go going into those higher numbers." And he was like, "That's just what it takes." And, you know, we're not only just talking about it when we got out to the field, they was able to tell me, "Hey, try this." You know, Von took me aside for a good 10, 15, 20 minutes. It was really giving me that vet presence of like, "Hey, here's what you got to do. Try this move, try this move. It doesn't work for me, but this might work for you or this works really well for me. Try this." >> When and where was that? >> It was in Vegas on July, it was before the wedding, so I think it was July 10th. >> So, so that's your kind of thing through this camp, first and foremost, to develop your moves? >> Yeah, I think right now is the time to try out things and, you know, figure out what works for you. Obviously, I tried so many things during the off season, you know, on bags and on air, but trying to get against, you know, finally, you know, against these actual, you know, legit tackles that can actually really work and show you know, they're trying to get better also and they're trying to see these new moves, too. It will help me figure out what uh what I can add to the game. >> Do you think it would be unfair if fans compare you to Miles Garrett? >> I mean, I think it's a Bottom line, don't compare me to anyone. I'm not Miles, I'm not this guy, I'm not that guy, I'm Jerry. I'm going to put a whole standard to what D end should be like and that's going to put me against like what D end should be like. Don't put me against a specific player. I'm going to raise the standard of any defensive player, period. >> Do you think that signing him today could help you with his two signs here with your array of talent? >> 100%. I mean, obviously, we were signing him, you know, to help on the field, you know, to help, you know, the team develop as a whole, but I think me personally, selfishly, I think it would be very, you know, helpful to have that vet presence around me. >> Do you need to prove in Do you need to prove in training camp that you've got those counter moves before you sign any game or is that something you already feel like if it's week one, you can go try those counters to figure out your >> No, I mean, you got you got to try every day. You can't just pull anything out in game cuz you pull something out in game and you look dumb, you're going to be all over social media looking stupid. No, you got you got to try that in practice and that goes for anything in life. You got to practice it 100 times, 1,000 times till you can't get it wrong. You can't just try it one time practice it works and try it in game cuz when you go up against these Trent Williams, you know, these Deion Dawkins, these real legit tackles, they're going to mess you up doing that. >> So, just along the lines of trying out all these moves, I guess when people talk about you as a pass rusher, they obviously bring up your power first. Is there any part of your game that you either think is underrated or is like you think really have room to grow in terms of your how you're getting to the quarterback? >> Yeah, I mean, I don't care about too much what people think about my game like if it's underrated or overrated or anything like that. I have a lot of things I want to grow. I mean, even you ask me about anything, I want to grow my power even more. Like I just want to become a better at every aspect of the game constantly whether it's the run, whether it's speed moves, counter moves, going inside, going outside, anything. I just want to become better. >> Jerry, do you feel like comparing yourself to someone on the Steelers offensive line in general? >> I just want to elevate everyone around me. Obviously, I want to be the best player I can possibly be, get all the sacks, you know, get the defensive player of the year, go to the Super Bowl, win the Super Bowl. I don't obviously want to win all that. The biggest thing I care about is just what's happening today, and that's just to make my teammates better out there in any aspect I possibly can. Yeah, I mean, especially, you know, when you talk about the Bills, I'm very excited just because Dion's someone I'm very, you know, I love to go up against somebody I love to work against. I'm very excited for that to try out some moves against, you know, a different type of tackle. You know, obviously, they're going to learn my habits out here very quickly after a couple weeks of going up against each other every day. Everybody's going to That's just how it naturally goes. But, when you go up against somebody you see maybe once a year, cuz I've only seen them 2 years ago, it's going to be a lot different. So, I'm excited, you know, whether we play in the preseason, whether we don't, I'm just ready to work. Yeah, now, he definitely got that old school vibe, like that real nitty-gritty, "Hey, let's get to work. Let's not play around." Everything like that. Off the field, he's the nicest dude. He's a conversation, everything like that. On the field, you kind of like lean away from him, like he's he's kind of like, "All right, cool. I got you, coach." But, now, that's just, you know, I I think it's very good to have a coach like that, you know, someone that can, you know, differentiate, you know, fun and, you know, real work. >> Last one. >> Yeah, I mean obviously you know he's one of the best ever do it. As a Florida State guy, you know, I've always watched him. I was idolizing him, you know, watching you know, going around the facility you see his picture on every other wall. Like it's crazy. But I'm just ready to, you know, talk to him, get to dissect his brain a little bit about the game. Obviously we play different positions, but you still take a lot away from him. I would go one more. >> All right. Yes, I think that first of all that the trust that the Browns organization has in me teammates, coaches it it says a lot to make it to this third contract and to be locked in for the long haul. The city of Cleveland behind me, you know, it's an amazing feeling. So you know, I can't say can't really put it into words, but it's just such a blessing to have that and you know, I'll definitely take advantage of it. Yeah, you know I think y'all knew what was kind of going on and they were working on it. So I know it could probably happen at any moment, but you know, AB came jogging on the field and and told me it was done and you know, that if I wanted to practice, you know, they'll honor my my deal and since I hadn't signed yet. So um you know, can't say enough good things about AB too, you know, getting it done and and you know, my team going back and forth and getting it done. So Yeah, so he said I could practice and I said, all right, give me my helmet, let's go. Yeah, I mean, listen, Miles is a generational player. It hurts to lose him. Like I I downplay that at all. So, of course trying to figure out like what exactly the organization was trying to do in that move. But, it's not up to me. Um we got V8. He's an amazing player. We got a new defense defense coordinator. Everything going pretty smooth right now. Uh so, like I said, we're going to miss Miles. Great, you know, great like generational player. But, you know, we control we control and can't do much about that. So, move on. >> So, what is the next step for this defense? >> Well, Jeff, the next step for the defense would probably just be you know, I think that this exotic defense that that Rudy has it's it's a lot of communication. It's a lot of disguise. It's a lot of, you know, confusion for the offense. So, once we square away what we can square away, uh limit the mistakes on our side, I think it's going to make the offense so much better. So, I think we just got to iron sharpen iron mentality and be the best we can be in this camp. >> Green, going back to your sophomore year, sophomore year you said you expect more of yourself. >> Yeah. >> Are you still in that mindset and what's more left for you to give? >> Yeah, I think that everything's about winning, right? So, no matter how good you do, how bad you do, like it doesn't matter we won three games this season. You know what I'm saying? So, I think that I have so much more so much more left in the tank. Uh the guys feel the same way. You know, we worked so hard this off season, training camp and and we haven't got the results the past 2 years past past couple years. So, you know, like I'm never satisfied with losing. You know, it's it's nothing that to get used to and it's it's sickening. It's like a disease, you know, it spreads. So, let's get the medicine, right? >> Green, going back to, you know, how long you've been in this you know, this organization as you've kind of grown in it off the field, how much have you sort of tried to grab more and more, you know, of becoming kind of a leader in the locker room, you know, whether it's by example or by vocal and how have you seen that kind of How have you seen yourself grow in that in this capacity? >> No, I think it happens naturally over the years, but you know, you got to accept that, you know, I am that guy. You know, anything you do is under a microscope. People is going to follow you. People are going to do what you do. So, do it the right way. And you know, it's not like you just wake up one day and and do that. It's from playing time. It's from experience, plays you make, and relationship with the guys. So, you know, I've always accepted that role and and and taking the defense, you know, on my hands and I know a couple of other guys have done the same thing. So, it's time to go. Yeah. I'm saying it's like we got a lot of Bronnys on the team. A lot of Bronnys. You know, me and we the we the Bronzes, I feel like. We the Bronze to the Bronnys, you know. Uh it's a young team, man. And I feel like I'm not old. You know, I just been here for a little while, like. So, just them young guys, they have so much energy, man. We want to use that in a positive way. So, it's like, you know, just trying to show them the path, guide them guide them on the right way, but at the same time still still be who they are, still still cuz that's why you're here. Mhm. >> Oh, yeah? Yeah, I didn't get a chance to see him yesterday. I heard he was in the building, but I know I'm going to laugh. The dude is the funniest dude ever. As y'all might know, like he got jokes for days. You know, [snorts] and of course he has experience for days as well, so Like I said, like you know when he was here, the run-stopping ability, first of all, uh violent, relentless pursuit to the ball in the pass game. So, I think it it it comes all the way. I know he's aged a little bit, too, so he's got that wisdom on him now and all that, so I can uh if they sign him, it's good. Giselle is old. Yeah, I mean I wouldn't look at it as a burden or anything like that. I think it's a blessing to to be able to have been here for so long and to show the guys the way. They said I was like the third or second most tenured Brown now and stuff like that, so it's it's it's kind of crazy to hear that. But you know, let let's keep it, you know, real like the rookies come into Cleveland, don't know what to expect, you know, they don't think there's a lot to do in Cleveland, it's that and the third, so it's cool to show them that how what the city can offer and what we can offer to the city as well. Yeah. yeah, how good do you think he'll be? I I swear I didn't even know he was in his third year, you know, the way he carries himself, the way he's vocal about things, you know, being the natural leader that he is already. So, listen, it's not an easy situation to to handle way he handled. I think he's handling it as well as he can. Um you know, you you really wouldn't even tell that he wasn't on this team beforehand, so that's saying a lot in just with the situation he's been through. You know, I can't wait to see what he does this year. >> Since you've been here since putting in the defensive Oh. >> So, I'm wondering how encouraged are you that this team changed? You talked about winning. >> Mhm. >> It's going to take points to win. >> Yeah, listen, we know it's a offensive league and listen, we know that we can make our offense better and we know that our offense has a whole new look this year. So, it starts or been started already, OTAs, and doing whatnot, but as a defensive player, I can only worry about what I can do. You know, I can't worry about what the offense has going on. All I can worry about is being the best we can be cuz if we start wavering, it's uh we let up 40 30 points a game, it's they have no chance. So, we can do what do what we do. >> Gronk was here. Yeah, Sanders is here today. And obviously being a defensive guy, >> how excited you guys are to maybe get a chance to talk to him a little bit and pick his brain about this year? I'm in the man camp. >> So, yeah, I'm in the man If it happens, it happens, but I'm at practice, you know, we doing what we do. I know he's out here supporting this kid and and doing what he do as a dad, so you know, I I I'm not too worried about that. >> Groot, when people talk about Groot, the secondary knowledge that he has and the experience and kind of practice he has at that level of defense always comes up, I guess. Not to give away any secrets, but are there things that you've never gotten to do before? Is there something you're particularly excited about in this system that you guys have to work with right now? >> Yeah, I mean, listen, it's a lot of me if you watch Atlanta's defense from last year. So, it's a lot of crossover stuff, obviously. Um but trying to mix it into what we do well as well. Don't want to switch it up too much. But it's going to be different, man. It's going to It's a lot of new calls. It's a lot of new terms. It's a lot more communication, a lot more disguise. So, you know, I know our offense is hating it right now. So, that's a good sign for us. >> When you saw him drafted >> When you were drafted, what were your first impressions of him? >> Oh, you know, raw talent. Think this He don't say a lot, but his play do the talking. He play at a thousand miles per hour. So, I'm excited when we put the pads on to see how he is. Uh I know he's going to get around that ball as well. So, but he's just open ears, man, learning. You know, I'm doing everything I can to to, you know, get him on track. But I feel like he ahead of me because he's been here for so long doing his doing his thing with this new defense. So, um you know, we're just making each other better and and getting to that point of where he step on the field, man, he got full confidence. >> When you were drafted, did you ever take any time to reflect on it? >> Yes. Yes. Thank you. >> Congratulations.

title: Andrew Berry Press Conference | July 30th, 2026
text: Part of the reason we're really excited is because we expect this to be a very competitive camp from top to bottom on the roster. Uh, obviously, over the last, you know, two offseasons, uh, we made some difficult decisions in order to set up the franchise for sustained success, but we're really excited about the young core that we have in place on, um, you know, both sides of the ball and are looking forward to see them grow and develop over the next, um, you know, several weeks. I also want to just mention, um, you know, Todd and his staff, they did a fantastic job running a great offseason program and we're all looking forward to seeing their vision come to life on the grass here as we begin training camp. You know, last thing before I, uh, open it up for questions, I wanted to just take a few moments to acknowledge Chris Powell and Scottie Springer. Um, you know, they are, uh, they've had a fantastic Browns, Cleveland Browns career. Uh, Chris was our longest-tenured employee, Scottie was our third-longest tenured employee and between them they have five decades of experience overseeing and running, you know, the grounds crew. Um, those two individuals, they embody everything that you want from an employee, servant leadership, um, excellence in their role and ultimate humility. Um, you know, they did not have glamour positions, you know, in the organization, but all they did was excel and treat people with with with kindness and decency throughout. So, it's bittersweet for us, um, because while we're happy to celebrate such long and excellent careers, we're really, really sad to see both those two go. So, with that, I'll open it up for questions. >> Can you maybe first address getting Denzel and Grant both wrapped up long-term? How do you feel about that? >> Yeah, really excited. Those guys are, um, you know, they're they're core members of our team. I was I was joking with with Peter, I was like, "Okay, well, Denzel's 29 and Grant, he's 27, soon to turn 28 and, you know, they're the elder statesmen, [music] you know, of the team." Um, but really excited to have those guys. Um, they're they're what we want in the organization. They embody being Cleveland Browns [music] and, um, happy to have them for a long time. >> How do you think they fit with the plan if you have gotten younger over the last few years to have kind of a couple of those older guys um still hanging around for a while? >> Well, I'll tell you what, if uh if old is your mid and late 20s, then you know, I'm in I'm in I'm in tough shape here, Scott. So, but listen, they they they're they're excellent players still playing at a high level at their respective positions. Um you know, really excited to have them as contributing members of the team. >> And how important is it that for for guys like them and some of the other veterans on the team to see when you have such a young core? A lot of those veterans that were here last year aren't here this year. How much do you expect to lean on them as you guys kind of try to shape up the culture of of this current iteration of the Browns? >> Yeah, look, I think that um you know, core veterans like Let me back up. I don't think it's just for any veteran, just having veterans just have veterans, but when you have Denzel and Grant who are top-level players um and top-level people, uh they end up being kind of like temp poles, you know, within your organization and with and within your roster. Um so, it it's it's it's a luxury and incredibly valuable to have, you know, when you construct the team. And um also, both those guys are homegrown. >> How much How much does extending both of those guys, you know, I mean having third contracts with both of them with this organization kind of maybe relax anyone that might have gotten a little nervous after the Miles trade and you know, seeing that just you know, the organization showing commitment to you know, guys that have uh you know, really stepped up before. >> I'll be honest, Daryl, that really didn't have any consideration into it. Like, there are very few players in the NFL that get to third contracts. Now, maybe it's greater now that you're seeing more second contracts be 3-year terms as opposed to 5-year terms, but I think you know, since we've been here in 2020, the the third contract guys have been you know, really Joel, Miles, and then really, you know, these two. And um it's an incredible accomplishment when you can when you can get to that point. But you've got to be the, you know, obviously the right type of player, right type of person. >> Andrew, just what about the timing too and and getting those done? You avoid any potential hold-ins and just especially knowing like like you said, they're the elder statesmen and you guys have a new coordinator and all that. >> Yeah, so I'd say a couple things. Like we're always very proactive with our players. Two, candidly we don't do hold-ins here. So like, you know, our guys know that. But we're really happy to get those guys done, the business taken care of before camp. So quite honestly, I'm not sitting up here asking, you know, answering those questions from you all and you know, they can just get going and and focus on playing football as opposed to what's happened with their deal. >> Andrew, when guys have like their contract is up but yeah, I mean it is in place but there's no guarantee of money. >> Mhm. >> Does that then create a chance of open dialogue to do things? >> You know, honestly Terry, our Yeah, yeah, yeah. No, I our it's actually probably it's probably less about the lack of, you know, guaranteed money because to some degree like once we get to this point it's for a veteran it's in essence guaranteed anyway. Um so for ours, we've usually taken the policy that, you know, we will talk about any deal, you know, one or two years early. That doesn't mean that we'll complete any deal one or two years early and both those individuals fall into that category. >> And Andrew, Jadeveon Clowney came and left yesterday. >> Do you feel your need for rotational end trumps age? He's 33. He doesn't seem to fit with the youth movement. >> Yeah, you know, Tony, I think like you you can't look at the roster construction in a vacuum. Certainly we've had a bit of a youth movement here. Um but that doesn't necessarily mean like every transaction's going to be, you know, uh you know, a 24-year-old, you know, 24-year-old player or something along those lines. Um other things that come into play are certainly the role and fit, um you know, financial cost, and then like how it fits in the let's say the broader construction of either the position group or the side of the ball. >> So, where does things where do things stand with you and Osweiler? >> Uh really good visit. Um you know, things that we still have to work through. Um you know, hopeful that you know, we can add him to the team, but it's still in the balance. >> He doesn't seem like a guy that wants to toil through training with you. >> I I think that's an inaccurate uh perspective on him. Like I think um you know, he would tell you if he was standing up here, you know, his most productive years are when he has a good hearty team. Yeah. Um I think that I think that uh comment is quite honestly unfair. >> Andrew, as as you go into a season where you guys are one of or maybe the youngest teams in the league, how do you kind of judge the success of this year just beyond the simple speed of losses? >> So, you know what's funny, Dan? I didn't know you would ask the question, but I was like, I need a better response cuz I keep getting asked asked this question this spring. I I keep saying that young doesn't necessarily the implication is like young does not necessarily equal bad. Like I was looking up out of the seven teams that were the youngest last year, uh it included Green Bay who's always young. It included Philadelphia who won their division. It included Seattle who won the Super Bowl. It included Baltimore. Um so, like I don't think that like that has to be like a like a cop out for expectation or performance so to speak. Um but as we think about it, like our goal going into the season is we want to be a tough and competitive team that develops and plays its best football towards the end. We want to control and focus on the things that we can control because so many things go into factor in terms of like what happens over the course of course of the year. If we can focus on the narrow set of things that are within our control, how we prepare every day, how we organize things of that nature, then you know, we believe that we're going to be happy with what the end of the year looks like. >> Andrew, with the past quarterback competitions with this organization, there always seemed to be like a caveat that came with them. You know, piece of the roster might have been incomplete or whatever it was. Do you when you when you look at this current quarterback competition and you look at the young skill guys that you have brought in here, do you kind of feel like this might be one of the more fair, balanced, equitable quarterback competitions that you guys have been able to have in a training camp for a long time? >> You know, I don't know that I could It's a good question, Darin. I don't know that I could comment on that. I guess, you know, part of it is, truth be told, we haven't even seen the team in pads yet. So, like, you know, it's a projection in terms of what we have. We're excited about it, but, um you know, none of us really, you know, truly know. I guess the second thing I would say is quarterback's a tough position to play in the NFL. No roster is perfect. Um so, I don't I don't I understand what you're getting at. I don't know that it would be fair of me to characterize this like, okay, this is a more fair competition than than others in the past. >> Andrew, with a similar situation as last year where you have a crowded quarterback room, four guys, you know, some young quarterbacks, are you approaching it with a similar mindset as last year where you're open to taking four guys on a 53-man [clears throat] roster, but you're always, you know, open also open to, you know, potentially >> Yeah, I I mean, I am. I think you've heard me say it's the most valuable position. And like, look, they've got to earn it. We're, you know, it's not just a situation where, um you know, guys are on scholarship in terms of like a in terms of a roster spot. Um so, we'll see. Like, I don't think that you can necessarily be prescriptive at the beginning of camp because things are going to surprise you in both directions. Injuries are going to pop up. Um opportunities that you don't foresee beyond July 31st, you know, may show up on August 31st. title: The Bengals Just Got the Best Possible News on Shemar Stewart.. Training Camp Takeaways and more
