And as you just said, it's just the way that this game has kind of developed into, I don't want to say a a passing league. Um, but but it's a lot more pass than it ever ever has been. And um it's almost pass first then run. So you need a guy in there that that can slow down that star receiver when he moves inside, but yet fill the the B gap, the C gap or whatever he needs to and um hold the integrity of the defense. >> Joe Hoy, Dallas Sporting News. Shotty said that Pickkins has been dialed in during meetings and he said he's been motivated to be detail oriented because of conversations with you guys. How much does that excite you to hear that Pickkins has that mentality? >> Yeah, I mean I've seen it. Um I I mean I've watched it. I'm watching him over there take notes and talk to young guys and um yeah, be as locked in as I've as I've ever seen it and and it's already showing out there on the field. Uh it's impressive. Um he knows what this year is for him individually. He knows what this year means for the team. He wants to contribute. He's one of the best teammates I've been around. Um and just his energy, how he shows up for the team and um what he does. And so yeah, he's just taking another level and that's what you expect with a guy who who loves the game like he does. >> These talked about is the evolution of the offense taking the next step in terms of maybe getting the seam more access with Jake and some of the other tight ends. How much does that kind of play into the evolution kind of moving the ball downfield this year? >> Everything's open. Um yeah, I don't want to just, you know, give give it away. We're going to just tack the seams more than we did last year. But when you got George, you got Cida, you got Ferg, you got Flo, you got Turp, you got a run game and Javvante, Jaden, Malik, whoever it may be that comes in there. Um, Ming goes out here making plays. I mean, you name it. Um, and a bunch of young guys who are hungry, too. It is going to be tough to to to cover all 53 and a half yards of the field. And we're going to make teams do that. And so whether it's the seams, whether it's the boundaries, whether it's getting in condensed formations and um just keeping you off balance, that that's the goal of this offense. >> Hey, Patrick Walker, Dallas Cowboys.com. You being here 10 seasons, I don't think there's been a stretch of time where the Cowboys front office have made so many highlevel trades in such a short period of time from George to Quinn in got Kenny and and then made the trade to go up and get Kale DS and still Jerry Jones is saying that he's willing to trade a top pick for a player that can help maybe as early as week one. From two points of it, number one, what does that say about the sense of urgency to get things done right now? And as the franchise quarterback, how good does it feel to have a front office right now that's willing to push everything to the middle of the table? >> Yeah, it's amazing. Um, you know, it's kind of why, like I said, I'm going to wear the shirt. I'mma, you know, invite the the the the standard. I know Jerry's done the same. Um, and when you watch what the organization is doing, that that tells you that. And so I'm blessed to be, you know, obviously to be here 10 years, but to watch what's happened over the last couple years and um to see his mind and his urgency and him still wanting to do whatever he can to make this team better. Uh that that that's that's why you play and practice and make sure you give this team everything you can is because, you know, when the owner's doing is going from the top to the bottom, um why not? And you know, life's about being urgent. You know, a lot of us want to wait and want to say, "Oh, we'll do it later." But what are we really promised? you know, whether it's football or whether it's whe whether it's life. And so, um, why not now? >> Pat Dhoni, NBC Dallas. Uh, Dak, you've talked about your friendship with Jake Ferguson quite a bit. It was a big off season for him, and he was talking about just how much life has changed for him going into this season, but he's excited. And I just wondered if you would speak a little about how much he means to you as a teammate, what you expect from him this year, just in general, you and Jake Curtis. Yeah, he's the man. He's uh he's definitely a little brother. Um he's he's a guy that you enjoy hanging around. He's a guy that that makes the day better one way or another. Um he's going to make you laugh. He's going to find the the the humor in any and every situation. And uh that's what I need. Um you know, you you go through go through things in life and you know, you you create different friendships at different times. Um, and he's just been he's been a beauty all off seasonason. It was awesome to support him and be there, you know, watching him get married and just continue to take steps and grow. Um, I say he's a little brother for a reason because, um, he's young, but yet he's maturing each and every day. Uh, watching what he's done on the football field, his growth and just the way that he's taken this offseason serious and the strides he's made just within the game of football. Um, and just our connection, you know, being able to one hang outside of the the facility, but to when it's time to talk ball and when we do, whether it's in the facility or not, uh, the level of professionalism and focus that that he has um is is synonymous to me. And so, it's uh it's just it's just been fun. He's a he's a funny guy, and I know each and every one of you know that when you've asked some questions or spend spent some time with them. And so, I've just been fortunate to spend more time with him than others. Um, but he's great. Dad, Chris Hanks with Fox 4. This is for Oklahoma City folks talking about tight ends. They were asking about if you would mind comment a little bit on Jason Whitten. Did you see something early on or during your time with him that this was going to be his what you thought was his career path? >> Absolutely. Uh that that's that's who he is as a guy that that loves football. Um, you know, when I came in as a young rookie, it's all, you know, we tell any young rookie to, you know, find those veterans that you admire their career and you admire what they do and, you know, follow what they follow everything that they're doing. And that that was the guy for me, you know, being a Cowboys fan growing up, uh, watching Jason Whitten, then being able to share the locker room and share the field with him. As I've told y'all before, it was a it was a race to try to beat Whit in the morning, and I was trying to stay at the facility as long as he did. Um, you know, I tell the whole story, the old story from the patent go of him not, you know, extending his arms and telling, you know, the ball needs to be here. Uh, it's a standard that he set. It's a standard that he made everybody on not only the offense, but the team feel that you knew that the game is who he is. Uh, that there's there's a good group of us in these locker rooms that wouldn't be where we are if it wasn't for the game of football. And so, you just want to give everything you can back to it. And Jason Whitney is the epitome of that. And I know that obviously he's a was a high school coach, won a state championship and then right moving on to to to the college ranks and Oklahoma's got a great one um in him and this won't be his final stop. I expect him, you know, in this league and honestly being a head coach whether it's college or the NFL one day because um that's what the game means to him and that's how serious he takes it and more importantly that's how great he is and how great he sees the game. Michelle, >> Michelle Monte, WFPA Quinnon yesterday sat up there and said he was just so happy to be here playing with one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Uh, I know your voice carries the most, but >> how helpful is it for you, for the team to have an established like really good player >> who's also a really good leader on that side of the game? >> It's amazing. Um, yeah, he he tells me that often and so um it's cool to hear. Uh, you know, I tell him I'm thankful he was building his house in Dallas and he chose us. Uh, but it means it means everything to, you know, your best players have to practice the hardest and they have to do the things the right the most. And Q's the biggest example of that. Um, you know, not necessarily a big rahrh guy are going to talk a lot, but when he does talk, um, it's heard. Um, when and he understands that, he understands how important his voice is. And so the words he does say whether they're uplifting or whether they're serious um or whether they're just straight to the point um we we feel it and we feel it on the offensive side as well. And you know just walking and dapping guys up before the practice or before you know the team period starts him just you know kind of saying something like that again to me and just saying hey we're going to win this year. Uh, it's good to hear, but it also goes into where I was just saying the standards the standard and guys are proud to to talk about the standard is and to hold each other to it and it's refreshing as hell. >> Last one. Mike Ducey from Fox 4. You've always been a processoriented guy, but you're not shying away from the Super Bowl talk either. Is it fair to say you're you're a little less patient than you used to be in that regard as the years have gone by? Yeah, definitely less patient. However, it is still a process. Um, it's still a process and you know, as I said, it's not something you're going to I'm going to get up here and talk about every single time on the podium. You know, this is the first time me talking to you guys since training camp began and obviously since wearing the shirt and yeah, th those are the expectations. As I said, you know, when you're watching the playoffs or you're not getting to even compete for it, you know, that that that sucks. It's terrible. And so just to have everybody on the same accord, everybody having the same standard is the way that it has to start. Uh but at the end of the day, it is about getting 1% better. And you know, we're only going to get there is if we win each rep, we win each drill individually. And then that carries over into, you know, offense trying to win each play against the defense and them doing the same. And that's where the iron sharpens iron happens. And um it is a process. cuz you know, we're going to have days and hopefully we're going to have, you know, a couple days where where they get the best out of us and we can't let that, you know, um, deter our beliefs and who we are and what we're going to try to accomplish and our strengths and vice versa. You know, we've got some great guys on offense and so when we're attacking them and we're having the better days, they can't get down on themselves. You know, they got to live and learn from it. And that's the whole thing of the the whole point of this training camp is it's about not beating each other up, but uh getting the most out of each other by being physical. being physical, pushing our limits and and seeing which and what each unit can do, but more importantly, um the identity of the team that we're going to create. >> Good. Thanks everybody. >> Thank you guys. >> Uh it's actually been in my closet for a few years to be honest with you. And I think that was as much as anything like just getting dressed and I looked at it and it was like why the hell haven't I worn this, you know? And I think the only other times I even thought about wearing it may have been like traveling to a game during the season or something like that. And I'm like like that's like why would I, you know, why would I wear that week seven, you know? Um and so yeah, it's actually been in my been in my closet for a couple of years. Don't know if I purchased it. Don't know if someone got it for me, but it was a vintage um I think the brand Kith. Um right. And so they have a lot of those those kind of shirts and yeah and it just felt right. Thank you guys.

title: "Greatest Offense There Is" Cowboys Offense Reacts to Day 2 of Training Camp | Player Interviews
text: Since last year, being a part of this organization, how much has this improved your game? >> Uh I'd say a ton. I improved a lot last year, so I wouldn't say really grown. I'd just probably say just keep putting brick by brick and trying to get better and better. >> And then this off-season, all the contract stuff is behind you now cuz you're now you're you're locked in on this year. What's the mentality going into the season now on this one-year prove-it situation for you? >> Uh not really for me, just for the a lot of guys. I feel like whether you know him or not or know his name or not or know his number or not, I feel like some guys are in the same situation that I am. So for a collective, I feel like we're doing pretty good just putting one foot forward. >> Expectations are so high for the offense because you guys were so good last year. >> Mhm. >> What's the bar like in that room for you guys? >> Uh I feel like detail is one thing Kobe Bryant used to always say, detail is always going to put you at least at the same standard or better. So I feel like when we're in the meeting room, when we're out here, where we're working out, detail is definitely one of the things we've been harping on. >> Hey Chidobe. >> Trip to Park City's and it seemed like Dak has given y'all offense a new nickname. Can you can you talk about that trip and how it was with you guys and and sort of the new nickname? >> Yeah, the the Park City trip was super fun. All the receivers, some of the tight ends, just like I said, the guys when we got camaraderie and brotherhood is another thing that we've been harping on, just staying close and connected together. We're going to definitely rely on each other in the game. >> And you being Gotti? >> Comradery. >> Yeah, and then Gotti is acronym for greatest offense, you know. >> The comradery between you and CD, the trips you guys took together. Talk about this off-season you had. >> Yeah, I probably definitely say kind of like you said, the trips and that's what makes it, you know, who we are on the field just because outside of football you kind of want to keep a brotherhood, you want to know the person. So I feel like we've been doing great collectively. Defense, too. Defense, those guys are it's a new mesh of guys. I feel like that's more important than anything. Offense, we kind of had the same group, but the defense has been kind of surprised me with a mesh of new guys that's all good friends now. >> How would you describe Ryan Flournoy? >> Super good. Detail guy. That's that's what I mean by detail can put you at a high standard. When you come from position he came from you have a high detail, you end up being where he is. So, as a collective we definitely want to do that. >> Talking about the details, Shady said that you've been dialed in during meetings. Um how much is that commitment to these details for you to be dialed in during meetings? >> Uh super good. I feel like uh the collective really brought my mentality to it too. Like when we all came in, we all talked, we were already having that nuance of we want to be better. I mean you know what I mean? We want to be better which is in anything anybody else. They want to be better than what they did before, but detail is definitely one component that is always going to be there. So, we harped on that. >> What about the celebration yesterday in the end zone? That was fun. >> Yeah, that was Yeah, super fun. Uh fun for me. Uh you know, just excited uh having a little fun. >> How great can this offense be? >> It's part of the process of getting more comfortable with the contract getting taken care of. You know, as a franchise side, getting that taken care of earlier, how much does that help to say let me focus on the field stuff? >> Uh really like I said, I left it up to my agent. So, I was even when we were 9 10 months from training camp, I was already thinking about ball. I was already training. So, I kind of leave that to the people that can do that. For me, I just make catches, make plays, be a playmaker. >> We all talk about this offense a lot, but how would you describe what the ceiling of this offense could be? >> Uh I don't think there is. No, that's that's that's that's the thing. The limitations and the nuance of a limitation, you shouldn't put that on yourself. You can really do anything you want. So, I feel like as a offense, that's one thing and one mindset that we have. So, just trying to be through the roof. >> I know it's only been two practices, but has this defense been giving you guys any trouble? >> Uh just new looks. Like I said, uh not really too much trouble, but iron sharpens iron. So, plays here, they have a few plays, we have a few plays, but like I said, they surprised me the most cuz it's a group of new guys or a group of guys that we brought back and now they're all meshed together. We even got Downs, he just got in, he's meshed with seven-year vets. So, like that's one of the things that I think is super important as of right now, for real. >> What goes into sizing up new players that you have to go against? >> Uh kind of the same thing. Uh like you said, it's different schemes. So, we got a new D-coordinator, so the scheme's a little different, but the player and his tendencies could be the exact same. So, like just starting to watch what he does, if he repeats the same thing that he did the year before, the year before that, or he's the same guy since college. So, that's going to always be in that person, but the scheme is definitely new and improved. >> Jerry Jones said >> playing in Rio? What do you think it's going to be like playing in Brazil? >> Super fun. Uh I feel like that's I'm glad the league is doing that just cuz soccer and a lot of other sports are worldwide, so definitely super fun for the guys and a new experience, but detail. I feel like that's one thing that's going to get the dub in that, too. Everybody be focused on the game and if you're one guy that's like double-07 out there, you should do your job. >> How much different is year two like hitting the ground running? >> Yeah, uh not too much different uh from the like we said, Park City, when we had the camaraderie and we've been doing it for a while before we actually got out here, it's been kind of smooth. Now, my first year well, last year when I first got here, I was kind of like some of the other guys, just trying to get the groove of it, trying to know some guys while I'm getting the groove of it, while I'm trying to learn the play, so that's why I said I commend the defense cuz a lot of guys are going through that right now and they're doing super good. >> Jerry says he wants you to be a Cowboy long-term. How do you feel when you say that and how do you feel about that possibility? >> Super excited. I'm always super happy when someone thinks highly of me, so shout out to Jerry. >> All right. >> What's happening this off season for you? What's it Does it feel different out here and and what's it been like the last few months for you? >> Yeah, I getting married, best day of my life. Uh but it's been great, you know, she's been supporting me tons throughout. She's getting my meals right, the sandwiches have been great. Uh I attribute to a lot of that to my body fat percentage going down. So, uh yeah, it's been great and then coming out here with the guys playing football, it's it's nothing better than this. >> A lot easier to be healthy when you're not alone in that, that's for sure. >> that's for sure. >> Tell me about Gotti. What's What's it g o t i? Is that what it is? You know, where the idea where it came from and how that's something that you all are so focused >> Yeah, and I think that started um kind of a little bit in in OTAs, kind of a little bit at the throwing session um out there in Park City. Um we had all the guys out there, which is really special to have. Um first year that was ever ever a thing where we had everybody, rookies included. Um but you know, we know what kind of offense we can be. We know what kind of weapons we have. Um we know who's at the helm. That's four and and you know, when we're lights on, when we're fully focused, when we're we're playing our game, and we're dialed in, you know, we are we are the greatest offense there is. And um we believe that, and you know, that's just something we're striving to be every single day. Meeting room, practice, whatever may be. >> Last thing for me is just Shady's been talking about culture and leadership since he arrived. It feels like this group is full of guys who do it the right way. That's not just like a thing on the wall, right? What has it been like from your perspective in this room from from the just daily doing things the right way standard of what you've seen compared to previous years in your career? >> Yeah, it's special, and it it starts with it starts with Shady's top-down. you know, he he come in and he doesn't just talk the talk, he walks the walk. And, you know, what he says he's going to do. And that like I said, that's top-down. Um we got guys, a lot of vets, a lot of older guys who have been through stuff, who have who have seen a lot of different places. And um you know, they have great voices. But then also I I attribute a lot of that to our young guys. Um I I think today's day and age it's it's hard to find those young guys who you know, they want to be quiet and they want to work and they want to earn something. And you know, we got a lot of those guys. A lot of those young guys are hungry. A lot of those young guys are hey, I want to earn the right to speak. I want to earn the right to you know, be a leader. And that's kind of being a leader in them in that self. Um it's special. And a lot of these a lot of these young guys are are filling those roles, and you know, it just makes me more excited. >> For you, with what you have under your belt now with this team from the past, how does that help you this year with the expectation, the knowing in the system and everything? Tell me a little about it. >> Yeah, just another chip on my shoulder I got to go out and prove myself all over again. Last year was what it was, but it's a whole new year. >> For you, when you were on the field last year, this team was different. How much has that been a priority for you this off season? Doing what it takes to make sure you're there all season long for this team. And what have you done? >> Yeah, I mean we we came up short last year. I mean as good as the offense was, we didn't do enough. We didn't get where we wanted to go. So, that's definitely at the top of our list. >> Tell me about the running back group. What do you like about this group? What's standing out so far? I love everybody in the group. I feel like everybody brings something different to the table. I feel like everybody in the room could be a starter on any team that they play for. So, I mean just the competition that we got in that room is just going to make all of us better. >> What do you love about coming out here? I mean beautiful. >> [cheering] >> This is pretty nice out here. >> Yeah, I mean we got everything we wanted. All in one. We got food. We got a place to stay at. Everybody right beside each other. We just kick it, play the game, do everything. So, I can't complain. >> We've seen some explosive runs from Jayden Blue these first couple days. Where have you seen him improve the most [cheering] from last year to this year? >> Yeah, just his confidence. I mean everything that he's doing on the field is just showing that how hard he worked in the off season. So, I'm glad to see him making plays.

title: Cowboys Players Discuss Day 2 of Training Camp | Player Interviews
text: First two NFL training camps of your career, how are things coming along? Are things already starting to slow down? What's the process been like for you? >> Yeah, I feel like every day things slow down just a little bit and that's how it's supposed to be. It's a positive always to have the spring behind me, be able to learn from what I did in the spring make the adjustments that I need to and learn what I need to focus on. So, I'm excited for it and keep going from here. >> How much easier does it make to kind of put all of your off season work together now that you you know you're playing against the offense and it's more physical, you guys are flying around? >> Yeah, I mean honestly I'm a I'm a football player. Um seven-on-seven summer workouts when there when there's no pads that's that's good but I like I like the real thing. So, I'm excited for when we put pads on and do everything like that. So, so I'm looking forward to. >> Shaddy said he gave you a shoutout for your ability to you got CD B's going to play in mini camp and then they ran the same play and you clubbed him is what you said. How did you go about kind of learning that process and kind of adjusting to that against CD B? >> Yeah, I mean it's just film study the same thing that I've been doing since I was a kid just making sure that I'm watching everything that I need to watch and going from there and making sure that whenever it comes back that I make the play then. >> Caleb, what kind of how intense of a guy is Christian Parker and what kind of communicator is he because Shaddy and Jerry Jones both said his communication skills are really helping you. >> Yeah, I think as a defender and then as a defensive coach the main job is to communicate. That's the that's the biggest part of the job and to be able to say what everybody needs to learn. That's what he's done in the meeting room, that's what he does out on the field every day is just try to teach people and he does it at a high level. I mean it's the best thing for a player when a coach wants to teach you. So, I'm trying to learn as much as possible and he if he's willing to teach me then great for me. >> Shaddy said you were one of four guys who have the green dot. And now that you're trying to learn as much as possible, clearly they trust that you're a guy that can learn it and communicate it to the defense. Can you just talk about that opportunity as a rookie? >> Yeah, uh I mean I feel like uh that's something I've done at every level is communicate at a high level. Uh that's what I think makes me special. Uh just being able to understand everything and articulate everything. So, uh it's something that if that's on my plate, I'll do it at the highest level. >> Do you think it can work to your advantage? You played in two elite college systems. So, you've already adjusted once from one system to to Ohio State now just kind of adjusting to another. >> Yeah, I feel like uh making things same as same as. That's a that's a big thing playing under uh Kevin Steele, Coach Davis' defense, playing under Jim Knowles, and playing under Matt Patricia. I have a lot of defensive knowledge to bank from and I feel like that allows me to play fast out here. >> Obviously, this being the Cowboys, you're going to hear a lot of Super Bowl talk. You're hearing it from within the team meetings and you're going to hear it from the outside noise as well. Uh so, that's the obvious goal, but from an individual standpoint, what do you feel like would make this a successful rookie season for Caleb Downs to help push the team toward that? >> Uh I mean, yeah. At at the end of the day, we are all pushing to win a Super Bowl, but at the end of the day, uh somebody said it best today, we can only have the best day today. Uh so, we can't win the Super Bowl right now. We're just trying to have the best day that we can today and that's the same thing for myself. Uh I'm trying to accomplish my goals and be great in myself. Uh and today is just being about being great today. That's all I can focus on. >> Schotty said he wouldn't put expectations on you that are higher than you would put on yourself. How high are your expectations and standards for yourself? >> That's for me to know and y'all to find out. >> [laughter] >> Caleb, what are your expectations for this defense? You what do you think you guys are capable of, especially with some of the high-end talent you guys have with yourself, Winfield, and Dorance? >> Yeah, uh I think it's um to be a dominant. That's what that's what I've thought about every defense I've been on. Um and we have the talent to do it. Uh to dominate every offense that we go against, to go out in the game and know that we're prepared to make the plays that we need to make to win. So. >> Caleb, you're no stranger to competition from the offense. I mean, of course at Alabama and at at Ohio State, but going up against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Dak Prescott every single day, uh how does that one fare up to what you've been through and how do you learn from that day in and day out? >> Yeah, that's a that's a blessing for me. Uh honestly, I I thank God for the position that he put me in and the ability for me to challenge myself against the best, so I think that's a that's a big positive for my development where I want to be. And uh in terms of our team, >> Behind you, behind you. >> that pushes our defense to be better every day and then that pushes the offense cuz we're going to make the plays too and make make them better. >> We've seen a lot of you working in the slot. What is it about your skill set that works well at that specific area? >> Yeah, just being able to recognize the the schemes and the patterns that are getting put against me. I feel like that's a that's a positive for me. Uh I played slot um at Alabama and at Ohio State. Uh not full-time, but got reps at it every day, so I think it's just a a combination of everything and being able to see the game from different angles. >> What does a veteran like Jaylon Thompson bring out there? What does he do for you? >> Yeah, JT uh he's he brings that energy for me. Um you can tell he's locked in every rep and uh I appreciate him for the way he approaches the game and that's something that I've always uh even since the spring I I liked about it and the way he approached it, so um just I like the way he approaches it. Yeah. >> First time in Oxnard, huh? How did it feel out here? >> Man, it's cool. Uh you know, I train I'm 35 minutes away from here. My house is 35 minutes, so I'm right down the street. So, this this I'm right at home. >> Just being in the first cuz obviously you came here last last year after camp. Just being in the in the first camp, just talk about your excitement being here and from the beginning. >> Yeah, I mean, it's awesome. Uh just I mean, really just getting being able to compete with guys. Uh you know, I I think this is going to be one of our most you like physical camps physical camps that I've been a part of just just off the the talent that we got on the defensive line and offensive line and uh just, you know, we all great competitors, so I think it's going to be a great battle. >> Kenny, what have you learned from Quinnen Williams about him since you started working with him? >> Uh man, it's just his attention to detail. Uh just how he pass rushes. He He's really just a a complete defensive lineman. Um and, you know, something that I pride myself on is just being able to to do both, being able to to to rush and stop the run at a high level. Uh love the way he play with his hands, uh his leverage. Uh you know, he's strong at the point of attack. He understands formations and uh understands, you know, how guys are trying to block him and all that kind of stuff. And then uh when it when he gets in the pass rush game, just explosive in the pass rush. Shout out PR. >> Physically, how do you feel going into this, especially with everything that you had to go through last year going now this year physically? >> I feel pretty good. Uh, I say pretty good. Just, you know, like I said, every day is a new day. You got kinks here and there, but where my body stands right now, pretty good. I'm out there running, flying. I want to go faster. Uh, obviously I want to be stronger, but that's we're we're still in offseason. So for me, I treat every day like a stepping stone and we're not stagnant right now. This is only day two. I want to be better than I was Yes. I mean, yesterday and today and so forth. You see where I'm going. So body's good. Just want to be better. >> Obviously, you're probably one of those players that can't wait to get the pads on, but going up against uh uh David and Charlie and those tight and Aronda, those kind of tight ends. Yeah. How how interesting has it seemed to see that all three of them bring something different that >> like I said you you talking about competitors in my room. It's across the board. Uh I think it's a lot of competition going on over there on the offensive side of the ball and what you see right now is just all the guys are playing their best football physically and mentally. Me and David just was having a talk about just how we can attack each other in a different sense just coming into practice tomorrow. So, seeing how they are over there, I can't wait to to see the physicality part when we put them pads on, but also I know that they have it. I know they're going to bring it. I know that they want to level up. I know they don't want to be onedimensional. A lot of guys can be seen as a passing threat, not a blocking threat. I know all them guys over there can do both. And that's what they're trying to show. >> No, I got all of that. I got all of that. I was ready. I was ready. But I do have it. Last year you graduated to to to this leader that you come in the locker room. What other dimension do you feel like you're going to add this year to your game as you're growing as an NFL player as well? >> I think the number one thing for me is as a leader, you want to be dependable. Uh you try to gain respect. Also, you don't want to be someone who becomes complacent. So I I could have the C on all throughout practice and not have the C on in the game. It doesn't matter. I have to keep the same standard for me. That's that's what that means. I have to earn it every year. These guys have to believe that they can trust me no matter what. It's like I said, last season, last season, moving forward, I got to earn it again. And as far as the dimensions that I want to grow in this game, I just want to add more playmaking. I feel like I did that last season. If if you ask me before, I had more I had more picks, um had more sacks, but there's always more. You feel me? And I think I can do everything in the world and and triple my stats and I'll come back next season with the same exact answer for you. So obviously the dimensions I want to grow in is just being more playmaker and and have that ability to be called on even more than I was last year. >> For you as a green dot, do you have like a certain rhythm? Like is there like too much information you can get from Chris Oly? Are you a yapper on the field? Like what is your rhythm getting the calls and then relaying it to your teammates? Man, being a green dot is is kind of crazy because one thing that you realize, you have to put everyone else first and you have to be selfless in a sense. You got to make sure the communication is given across the board. There was a lot of times last season where we didn't get the message across the board. And no matter what, being selfless, being a green dot is being able to say that's my fault. No matter if the corner was too tired to get in the huddle or the safety just didn't hear you a lot of times, Tony, like you got to make sure. Yeah. What? No. What? You know what I'm saying? Love the guy, but you got to be selfless. And I'll sit there and I'll talk to every guy and no matter what happens, I sit there and I tell them that is on me and I I'll take that 10 toes. But just to answer your question, my process is pretty much making sure I hear the call, get it out so I can start to see the formation because sometimes I can lose track of the formation if I'm if my back is turned. So, we had to change the huddle. We had to change the huddle around. you'll see that we made the line face forward, never turn around, have the DBs get a little closer. So, the process is going to be a lot better for me this season. But ultimately, it's like, you know, just making sure that I keep repeating it. So, yes, I am a yapper on the field. Uh 100%. And I talk no matter what. But yeah, 100 that's like pretty much the answer to that. >> You uh obviously had a busy summer. You went down to Chiliva at Tony's camp. You have your own camp. you have a football team now that uh you're playing on. Just being that big a part of the community. Obviously, this is your community. This is where you grew up, but just how cool has that kind of been for you, >> guys? You have no idea what my summer was like for real. Uh well, someone does. Chris knows. I had a camp and I threw that for the kids obviously. And at that camp, most of the kids that I already pre like knew pretty much were like, "Hey, D uh Chase said he was going to your house after this." And I'm like, "I don't I didn't talk to no parents. I didn't talk to Chase." So, he's just telling lies. Next thing you know, I had 10 kids at my house for seven, eight days, like back to back to back, 10 kids running through my house just tearing things up. I became a uncle, brother, father figure, all for the first time in like real time. And I was just having a great a great time. It was a blast. It was very expensive. Shout out Derwin for taking a day. He he gave me one day. But he did give me a truck though. He let me drive his truck for the week. But he he gave me he gave me some financial relief when he took a day and he took him to his house and then they swam at his pool and then they came back to me and said, "This house is so much better than yours. He has so much more money than me." So, but it was it was it was a great summer just being able to have the kids around, taking care of them. Most of those kids that I try to impact come from single parent households or only have a grandparent or so. So, I pretty much do my best to show them that, you know, every it's attainable. Um, and just being in this community, being able to be here with the Chargers is something that I'm blessed to be able to have those opportunities to do. So, shout out to my my little boys, my bros. Uh, and they want to come to my house right now. They don't know that camp means I'm in a hotel. So they think they could be at my house and I'm like declining calls and sending texts like, "No, no, I can't because if they see my face and they puppy dog me, I might just say, "Yeah, yo, y'all can have my house." And I can't do that. >> Ghosting kids. >> Yeah, I can do that cuz they're not mine for real. I told them the other day, I'm going to go get some milk and they didn't get it. >> Chris, what's these first two days been like for you? >> Uh, a lot of fun, a lot of juice out there. Um it's been good to be back on the field playing football, you know, so a lot of hard work went in the offseason, the summer. Um just been exciting to get back and get going. >> What do you feel like the different team has asked in terms of understanding what you're trying to implement here? >> Feel really good about it. Um I think we're at a point that we should be in day two of fall camp, which is we understand our identity. We understand what we're chasing, what we're pursuing every day. There's a standard of excellence that's pretty clear from the coaches and the players. Um, and we've seen that the first two days, us aspiring to reach that level, and it feels uh feels like we're all on the same page. >> Does it help at all facing matching up against an offense as complex as >> 100%. 100%. You you want to be challenged in practice. Um, you want practice to be harder than games. Uh, we feel like each day we get exposed to so many different looks, plays, formations, motions. Uh we have to solve problems continuously and that's how it's going to be all season. So we're glad that it's happening now and happening early. >> Talk to you in the spring Chris about Tarke and Cam. Just how excited you were about them both making plays early on here in camp. What have you seen from them so far? >> Uh what I saw from them in the spring which is uh playmaking ability. uh their mindset's kind of shifted from just being the young guy and not trying to mess up to now being uh being a couple of our anchors on defense and really having the confidence to go play the ball uh talking out there running the show. Uh so it's been great to see them get going. >> How are you feeling about that competition in general? Feels like you had you know three guys there with target Cam and then Dante and a couple open spots on Brandon's at nickel. Just how are you sort of viewing that competition early on camp? >> Yeah, I think those three play at a high level. There's no question. um you know they're all going to make each other better and then the competition after that amongst uh the guys like Dean, Eric, Nico, all those guys. Um it's been really fun to watch and I think each day a different guy has elevated. Then the next day another guy and so we'll kind of see here the next couple weeks through the practices and then who produces in the preseason games who ends up filling out the roster there. >> About the competition of the safety room. Um, Derwin talked about it yesterday and how guys are pulling for each other, but how tight is that competition and what are you seeing >> Yeah. Uh, it's an awesome competition. I think the thing that's unique about our guys is a lot of them have been to get together for a long time for three years and and some even longer than that. And so what you see is a healthy competition, which to me is you got a group of guys chasing a standard of play. So if you got six safeties that are elite safeties, it's going to work out for all of them, however it plays out. So that's kind of their mindset. Um, so they're able to push each other, but it's not divisive and it's been a lot of fun to watch. And so for the safety room, I mean, we got a group that is uh that's really deep. And you got the young guys flashing in practice. You got the vets being consistent. Um, so it's early. It'll just be fun to see how that plays out. >> How does Genesis fit into that? You mentioned the young guys. It looks like he's making plays out there. >> Yeah, good question. um when the pads come on, I'll be able to say more um because we got to run down the alley and hit people. But as far as anticipation off the quarterback, playing the ball in the air, covering um he's been really impressive so far. >> What have you seen from from RJ? Obviously a guy you didn't get to coach directly when you were when you're position coach 24, but obviously the last few months you've gotten to know him pretty well. What What do you think of him as a player? >> Uh he I like to call him an old soul. He is uh like he operates like a vet and he thinks like the game like thinks of the game like a vet. Um, so when you see him out there, he's running the show. He's in the right spot. He's consistent. Um, what I challenge him today is take a playmakaker's mindset, right? He had a couple of interceptions last year. Uh, we want to see that in practice as well. So, a guy that's that's very consistent in the right spot, smart, um, and just challenging him to keep making more plays. >> You mentioned, what are you looking forward to next week when they come on? >> Everything. Everything. uh hitting, forcing fumbles, uh getting off blocks with more intent, more violence. Um you just find out who you are as a defense when the pads come on. You find out who certain guys are. And it's funny, like it it never fails. You watch practice without pads for four or five days and then all of a sudden they come on and somebody pops up that you maybe weren't weren't watching as intently or didn't have as high of hopes for. So, um I just think you find out your identity and who you are. describe how would you describe Khalil's value to your defense? Obviously his play, but just being a vet, being a future Hall of Famer, and being able to help the younger guys along like >> Yeah. Uh priceless. Priceless. He is uh I've said it before, but he's the flag bearer of our culture on defense. Like he uh he leads the way with his actions. Uh when it's time for him to say something, he's going to say something. Uh, and then you got a group of young edges in that room that all they're doing is watching everything he does, listen to everything he says. Um, so it's more valuable than anything I could say or do. So having him here is priceless. >> Investor, what have you seen throughout the off season? And I know it's only a couple of days at camp, but maybe be able to take advantage of extra steps to really help. >> Yeah. Uh, any exposure for those rookies and those young guys is is incredible and it's so valuable. So, um, him getting all these reps, playing different positions is going to pay off down the line. Uh, and, you know, we knew it when he got here, he operates like a pro. He's mature. Um, he's been healthy by taking care of his body. Uh, but I think what you see is just such a natural pass rush ability, the hands, the bend, the first step. Um, so that's another guy when the pads come on, it's going to be awesome to see like how does he take on the run and all those things. So, >> how do things change with two out there? Um, we keep it rolling in practice. You know, you get into a game and you spend a little bit more time game planning and figuring out how to fill that void. Uh, practice is next man up and and we kind of keep it rolling. So, we haven't felt it as much. Obviously, we miss him out there. Um, you miss his how vocal he is and the plays that he makes. Um, but for us, we're just keeping it rolling with the guys we got out there. >> Where do you feel like his head is at right now, too? Is it conversations? >> Uh, it's in a good spot. Um, I don't know the ins and outs. you know, I focus on the guys on the field and then I focus on him. If he's not, I talk to him all the time. Um, and he's in a good spot. We're in a good spot with him. We love him. Can't wait to have him back out there ready to go. >> Everyone was saying yesterday that it's a big year for Camar going into year three. You got to figure out basically >> what your talent level is. Just do you feel the same way that this is an important year for >> 100%. I've told them both like this is um in my limited experience in the NFL like this year for them is the one that propels them forward for the rest of their career. Uh and I think they both know that and I think that's a part of the reason why they're attacking it with the mindset that they are that um putting all their chips in right now and doing everything they can to have success this year. How valable is it to have a player like Derwin that can play safety, comes down into the slot, can be an ed another edge rusher, do what he does. Just how important is it to her? How special is it to have? >> Yeah, extremely special. Um, every defense coordinator is looking for a guy like that. Um, so we're blessed to have him. Um, we we're pushing to to get it done and make sure he's he's all uh signed up and ready to go for the whole off season. Um, just like Khalil, he's like the forefront of our defense. Khalil and DJ are getting off the bus first and they're leading us into the field. Like um everything he does is what you dream of a leader doing. Vocal play, uh practice habits, everything. So can't can't speak enough of how special Derwin is. >> Obviously, you were here two years ago, but have you noticed any differences going last year calling plays at this time in college and then now doing it in the first two days at a training camp? Any differences or >> um stood out to you? >> Nothing that stood out so far. Um, you know, some of the verbiage I've taken on as far as like, hey, we're going to run the the some of the calls that are maybe the same as before, we're going to keep the verbiage. Um, whatever we brought in new, maybe that's new. But like that for me has been a process of relearning some things. Um, outside of that, calling it, um, we'll figure out when we get in preseason games, the adjustment and things like that. So, nothing nothing too crazy right now. Going back to uh to Cam and target and kind of talking about year three and them knowing what's at stake and and you've mentioned aggressiveness, do you have to be careful with that? I mean, we know that that stats can dictate sometimes contract terms and things like that. Just kind of do you have to make sure their head's in the right place while being the right kind of aggressive? >> Um I think you do with some guys, but not those two. Um you know, I think they're as good as it gets as far as being team players and team guys. And um ultimately they care about the guys next to them just as much or more than they care about themselves. Um and they put that on display every day. So I don't think I have to with them. >> In the middle of the defense, just what's that process been like working with him as you know the voice in the middle. >> Yeah. Another guy like like he even came like from 24 to now. The growth and the maturity has been really impressive. Um you know he's a leader of the defense and he sees himself as that. So the way he operates day in and day out, the extra time he's spending uh with coach Spence and coach Heistand and mastering the defense, um it's been seamless for us. Like we're not pushing him to come up here and figure like he operates like he's the captain of the defense and the leader from the core of the defense and that's what he's been doing in practice. So it's been a lot of fun. >> What percentage of the defense is new stuff if you can put a number on it? >> I'm not going to put a number on it. Uh you'll find out in the season. keep trying. >> Just what have you kind I mean obviously I'm sure he's another guy that you're excited to see when the pass come on, but just what have you seen from him so far? >> Um really like from the spring to now, you kind of see when he's out there in individual and you see him in the team period, you see a little bit of twitch, you see like what's made him a really good player. His he knew he was smart, knew he had great size, but now just seeing him move, it's been it's been really exciting. He's got some twitch off the ball. Um he does have some versatility. He's great with block destruction. Um so I think he's going to be a really good valuable piece for us. >> Chris, now that you you left and came back from year one to year three of coach Harbble, what have you noticed the most about this defensive unit that may have been different from your first going on with the team? >> Um I just think it's it's a stronger unit. you know, you come in in 24 and you're taking over as a new staff. Um, you're coming off a season that didn't go the way they wanted it. So, you're trying to build a culture. And so, what you're seeing now, what I'm seeing in year three is really the result of culture building over a three-year process. And so, a team that's tough, team that cares about each other, a team that has a championship standard on defense, all of those things. Uh, Jesse and Coach Harbaugh did a great job building that for two years, and I'm stepping in year three, and we're just trying to elevate it. And so I see that that unit strength um is really in place and the culture is really taking hold.

title: Puka Nacua Reflects On Relationship With Football, High Energy at Training Camp & Consistency
text: Welcome to inside of Rams camp presented by Community America Credit Union. The star of the show, number 12, has officially arrived. Puka Nacua, I'm Cameron Irwin alongside Stu Jackson and Puka. I mean, the chance are you going? Everyone loves having you back here. It's wild to think year one we actually sat in this exact same position and you were telling me how excited you were just ahead into SoFi Stadium. What's the excitement like for year four? >> I think it it's still there. I guess uh today we had we're going up against uh number 95 and I'm lining up right next to him. I'm like, man, am I really excited to see him go out there and play in in in our blue and gold. So, I think it's going to be really exciting uh just to come back with our guys going into year two with Demarcus Robinson and just to continue that that connection I have with Matthew and to have a a young receiver come in and CJ just the the attitude and the the preparation I feel like he's been able to have as we've gone into camp has been really exciting. And then to see some some familiar faces on defense. I mean, we started off with some Huskies back at the University of Washington. Coach Lake has made his way back over here and then add Tre White Mcduffie and Jay White has been really exciting. >> What's the you know, just the energy and the atmosphere around camp been like? I mean, for anybody who hasn't been here, I mean, it's pretty easy to find you or locate you if they don't see you right off the bat just because of how many of these fans are like chanting your name and calling for you. Like, what's that like for you? >> Uh yeah, it's >> [laughter] >> it's been yeah, when we look back up I think about yeah, coming into year one and being like, man, like I was kind of like there wasn't there wasn't maybe as much excitement coming from the fans when I was being able to make plays, but the the excitement that it is now to continue to show that consistency. Coach is something that Coach McVay says all the time is consistency is the truest truest measurement of >> Oh. >> greatness. And number 17 I think is the truest >> the season. The only drop of the season. >> Yeah, we'll count that. >> But, it's been so exciting. Just that that excitement that's around here. It keeps the energy flowing and it feels like the continuity um day one. There wasn't a drop-off from like we coach talks about that phase four that time we're away and everybody being able to go and handle things on their own. And it felt like we hit the ground running at full speed. There was There was no build-up into where we want to be. We feel like we're just stacking as soon as we got here. >> In terms of your own evolution, I'm curious, too. It seems like you're able to ma- manipulate defenses and really have ownership as you head into year four. How much do you have a sense of the ownership of this offense and changing the scheme? >> I think it's been really cool. I obviously having a great connection with Matthew is a start of it, but then also having the understanding come from Coach LaFleur when we first got here of his his first time of or his time at being OC, and then having Coach Nate Scheerhaus be in our receiver room and the communication that he was giving to us practice to game to to pregame and everything that felt like. And now have him being able to be like, "Hey, this is how I'm thinking and scheming things up." And it's like, "All right, I've envisioned these pictures before. There's some of the things that we're changing in our offense that he talked about in our room." And now he's like, "All right, I get to make these changes and stuff." So, it makes it really exciting cuz I'm like, "All right, we I know we got a wideout over here." He's looking at ways for us to scheme up these defenses, and it makes it more fun. >> Speaking of that ownership, I mean, you run a pretty extensive route tree. Like you're motioned and used in so many different ways in this offense. Like, how much pride do you take not only in the diversification of those routes, but also just, you know, all the different ways that you're used by Coach McVay and the staff? >> Um I think uh from the the person that I came in and learned this position from um it's funny, I've come from Coach Yarber's coaching tree from since I got into college, but um especially learning and I think from from one of the best to do it, Cooper Kupp. Um the ability to affect the game in the pass game, playing the position wide receiver, but then also to affect the game in the run game. I think that's something that I know our entire room takes pride in, and something that's where it's like the standard that was set before me. And it I I I wear that uh that run game uh badge with pride cuz I'm like, I know that uh the guys are watching, and it if it makes our offense flow. Um the ability for somebody to be like, "Man, like I got to go put my head in this run game." And then, "Oh, we're slipping out the back door, and now we're running routes. And so that that it's a game of inches out there and so when that moment of hesitation comes from any defender, um coach McDonald finds a way to exploit that. >> Speaking of Cooper, you guys were uh you know, working out in the off season again, you, Higbee, and several other guys at uh Whitworth's gym. Just what was that experience like uh you know, getting together as a group and and doing those workouts together? >> It it's uh it's always really fun. I think uh Whit's gym is they call it the village and it definitely it takes a village. I think that's something that uh I've learned coming from from a big family but then also the football environment. And so the people that he has come in there, there's every once in a while you see Chuck Liddell in the gym and you're like, all right. I think I can I think I'm a little I'm [laughter] a physical guy and then you realize like man, I'm not that physical. So it makes it super exciting and just to go out there and compete with the guys on our team and then also go out there with Cooper. To have that connection that I I've had with him uh it goes way beyond the the lines of the football field. And so it's always fun to see him and and congratulate him on the success him and his team were able to have but then also to know that we're all going out there to compete against each other. When we're running those sprints and we're we're lifting the weights, there's also that competitive edge that everybody has so it keeps the gym very live. >> Now into year four, I'm curious, what does football mean to Puka Nacua? >> Um I think this is my this is my uh safe space. Uh it's always been uh something that my my father was my first football coach and that that moment uh of being uh playing left tackle in my first year and watching my >> Excuse me, what? >> You know, my my dad and my brother were the the coach and they threw me out there and said just go get beat up. And that's pretty much what happened to me. So now that I get to I'd say I get my turn to put some physical beating on some of the guys. It brings a lot of excitement to me but when I step out here on the football field, there can be so many things that are going on this outside world but um when I when I get to put that helmet on and I see that number 12 out there whether it has my last name on it or not, it's a it's a it's a badge and it's a it's a protective armor for me. So when I get out there and get to go, I I was blessed to to have five brothers in my family. When I go out here, I got uh 96 or 97 however many guys are out there. So it is it's a safe space. It it relaxes me. It brings me into a a mental state that I can't describe. >> Speaking of fatherhood, Coach McVay mentioned that you obviously had your son out here at one of these practices recently. Just you know, what's that experience like for you now as he gets older? And also, you you know, potentially have a future wide receiver in the making there. >> Uh it's been so exciting. My my little man Kingston just played turned 9 months last week. And he's crawling moving around. I would say he's got some paws on him. So, I'm like, I don't know. The potential to be a wide receiver is there. I think I I I've said to a couple of people that I've got to meet him on the team. I'm like, that's my that's my AD right there. I got I see him putting his hand in the dirt. He's going to be a little three-tech. He's got some He's got He's got the name. He's got the father He's like me. His His name isn't Puka, but it's pretty close. I think I think we could give him that nickname as well. So, it's been so exciting just to have that patience and just to see the the growth and development of him through the different stages. And like, man, to to be on him with FaceTime and when he was out here in practice just to like see I'm like, shoot, that's probably why I ended up catching that one-handed pass the other day. Matthew goes out there. I'm like, I got to do it for my little man. He's got to see me. He won't remember this. But I'm like, hey, you [laughter] know, your dad used to have some good catches, you know. >> So, you're telling me he's not starting at left tackle. >> Oh, no. That's >> That's my guy. Maybe. It could be close. >> Um and speaking of little ones, too, you got a chance to go out hit the road, run some youth football camps alongside Kyren Williams. You got back to Utah as well as here in Southern California. Uh what does it mean in terms of when you look at one of these young'uns that's wearing the number 12? How do you reflect on your own jersey? >> Uh I I it still feels very surreal to me. I guess when I look back and be like, man, like this is year four. And I'm I'm where I imagined myself being as a little kid in the elementary school. When the teacher said, "What do you want to be when you grow up?" I always wrote a professional football player. So, to think that's where I'm at. And these kids to come out and spend that time with me and Kyren. I think if there's anybody I think replicates my energy on the football field, it's it's 23. So, it's super exciting to go out there with him. And just to see like the level of excitement for these kids to come out here and just play the game. With the I have a younger brother and the ability for these kids to earn earn have value going into all this NIL world stuff and to see these young kids just go out here and have excitement to play the game. There's there's no rewards. I mean we did give them pizza and some snacks and they get signed cards and jerseys and stuff like that. So as a little kid I know if they give me if there was pepperoni slice of pizza right there I would have ran as fast [laughter] as I could have too. So >> Who needs NIL? >> Right exactly. I'm like pay me in pizza pizza rolls. I'm like that you sign me up right there. But a slice of pizza I'll take that too. But it's just so fun. I'm like there I there were it takes you back to just that the true excitement and just the the purest level of form of football. >> Entering year four have your individual goals changed at all? And and the only reason I ask that is like for somebody who has accomplished as much as you already have in such a short amount of time in the NFL, does that change year to year? And and if so, how does that look for you for year four? >> Um I think it definitely does change. I I what coming here and spending the the first two years of my career Cooper Kupp and then having Davante Adams come in where the the advice of man you there's got to be there's always room for improvement and there's got to be something that you're doing to develop your game in a different level in a different way. And so it's been exciting to feel like man when I watch some of the year one tape and I look back at where we were just last year and just practices that we've already had feeling more confident putting my foot in the ground the spatial awareness of where we're going out there. But I think some of that coach says the the truest measure of greatness is is consistency to go out there and continue to do it what I feel like I do at a high level and then just to continue to improve upon it. I'm like I love the physicality. I'm like land man put me on the ground over there. So it's like yeah my spatial awareness still has lacks in it. So >> there's always room to improve but it makes it more exciting cuz I'm like I know when we step out here on this football field that whether it's going to be at SoFi Stadium or we might play there's going to be guys who are going to push us to the test and to prepare for them right now with the best of the best is a really good feeling. >> Puka we appreciate you and good luck with the upcoming season. It's always a pleasure to have you in the energy here on Inside Rams Camp. >> Absolutely. Sweet. Thank you guys. >> All right. This has been an episode of Inside Rams Camp presented by Community America Credit Union.

title: Special teams coordinator Brian Mason discusses kicker battle, returners
text: So, this time of year is busy time for you, right? Cuz you're evaluating a lot of those young guys, I guess. What what are like the deep into camp yet? What what are the the surface level things you're looking for when you're looking at guys who might be able to help you >> Yeah, I would say so. We have a 90-man roster and we're trying to get everybody as prepared as possible, not knowing how things will shake out. Give everybody as many opportunities as possible and get them as prepared as possible. So, when you know, certainly we get into joint practice and preseason games, guys have an opportunity to be put in positions where they're successful and show what they can do. And we're going to try to get as many guys as possible to get reps in practice and in games. Certainly, there will be some highs and lows when you're playing that many players in practice and in games and it's just an opportunity to be able to see what certain guys can be able to do. OTAs is a really good opportunity where, you know, we don't have the pads on, so it's a huge focus on fundamentals and technique. So, now we need to take that bank of fundamentals and technique that we built through OTAs, kind of ramp it back up this week when we don't have the pads on and kind of go through the refresher of here's all the things we installed and worked in OTAs. Really identify who's got the best fundamentals and technique this week, put the pads on next week and see who can compete still using those fundamentals and technique, make good decisions and kind of be able to stack some things from there. >> What have you seen out of your kickers so far throughout spring and summer going into training >> There's not really a huge update on the kickers just being obviously that it's early in camp. Um in OTAs, I we were able to kick them the last 2 weeks of OTAs, both of them. Spencer came back from injury earlier than expected, was able to kick the second to last week of OTAs and then the last week of OTAs, um he kicked in front of you know, everybody in the media saw the last time that he kicked. Wasn't quite as consistent as he was actually the week before. We expect there to be a little bit of rust and some inconsistency since he hadn't kicked for 8 months. I think he's cleaned up some of those things throughout the summer. Um it continues to get better just kind of like he did last year. He kept getting better every single week and then performed at a really high level in August and September. So, looking for the same things from him. Um, he looks completely healthy. Leg strength looks really good. Um, those guys kicked on our own yesterday. They'll kick in front of the team tomorrow. Um, Grupe since he's been here in practice, um, in the season, in OTAs, he's been highly consistent. He's still that same guy. So, he's got to continue to be that highly consistent guy and I think it'll be a really good competition. The difficult thing is obviously we can't overkick them, but we want to give them as many opportunities as possible so we can evaluate a fair competition. So, we're going to try to get those guys the exact same number of kicks, as similar as we possibly can, kicking them three times a week and getting them in front of the team as much as we possibly can. But, certainly it's going to happen fast. It always kind of does once you get to Grand Park and before you know it we'll be in Boston. So, we're just trying to get them as many opportunities as we can, um, as evenly as we can to see how the competition goes. >> How competitive is things are things at both of the return spots? >> Yeah, I think it's extremely competitive in the return spots. Um, we have a really good within the 90-man roster pool of returners and guys that have done it both in college and the NFL to some degree or another. So, it is certainly that's another position kind of like kicker where we got to roll through as many guys as we can both in practice and games to see who can do what, um, as we continue to develop some guys. I think we have some guys that maybe don't have a bunch of experience doing it like a Deion Burks who we've talked about, who we need to get more experience to see, you know, can we use his athletic traits in a position like that in addition to the guys that have already been returners in the past. So, uh, definitely a really good pool of those guys. We got to get as many of those guys reps in preseason games. Like we know what certain guys like Josh Downs, Anthony Gould, some other guys that have done it in games can do. We need to see what some of these other guys can do and put them, um, you know, under the fire a little bit in preseason games. >> DJ again and Shaquille Griffin and it seems like between their RB2 battle especially the guys are going to be a kind of a big deal. What have you seen from them so far? I know they were out there in the in kickoff. >> Yeah, they both are guys that I think can certainly do a a number of things on special teams. They're both guys from a kickoff returner standpoint. I have high hopes for that we can develop them into being really good kickoff returners. I think in this new model, you see where running backs become even more useful as kickoff returners because it come becomes a little bit of a rugby scrum in the middle of the formation. You're looking for somebody that can run through contact and run through the smoke a little bit, which running backs can naturally do. So, I think both those guys are going to be really good in the returner competition. Both those guys have taken strides. They're both physical players in all the other phases, and I think they're going to have a really good chance um to contribute on special teams this year. >> Do you Do you think you guys found like a secret sauce or whatever that kickoff last year with like Ashton, Anthony, Ameer? Like they all kind of had really stand out years returning kickoffs. Do you like It's been changing a lot over the last few years. Do you think you guys have a really good one now? >> I think we definitely got in a really good groove last year. There's a variety of reasons why that was able to work out. Um you know, certainly the returner aspect like Ashton Dulin, unbelievable player all the way around, had a really good year as a returner. I think he's our best overall returner. Gould and Ameer both showed up and had some big returns throughout the year. But the guys up front and their our ability to utilize, we have a really, you know, unique skill set of linebackers, D-line, and tight ends and that depth with guys like Drew Ogle tree and Mo Ali-Cox and Tommy Egbuh that are really good blockers on the front line. And in the new model, you know, you can really utilize some bigger bodied guys that can block and get on body right now cuz they don't have to run back to drop like they did in the old model. And putting those guys at the point of attack and eliminating some guys really, you know, worked out well for us as well. So, it was kind of the front line and the and the returners working together, and I think we had a certainly a really good pool of guys to use that I think can be very similar to this year. Appreciate you, guys.

title: DC Lou Anarumo speaks on linebacker opportunities, cornerback competitions
