What have you seen from the first couple days from Bryce? >> Yeah, you know, good again another young guy who's is learning. Uh but um I think he is a a very intentional about what he does. He's a you know, he's you know, you hear about boxers where they're heavy-handed? He's a heavy-handed guy. When he hits you, you can feel it. Uh I think he'll continue to shine when the pads come off. >> How have you seen Hunter pick up from where he left off last year? >> A little bit different. Uh you know, he he uh uh Justin's injury um they were very similar timeline timeline-wise. Uh I think Hunter has it was just a little slower for his development in the spring uh just in terms of healing. But uh you know, he's a smart guy again. He's he's doing a good job right now and he's going to take you know, hopefully take advantage of his opportunity. >> What about what about you guys talking about the guy that has been >> Who's that? >> Colby Wooden. >> Yeah. >> So, transformational throughout his career at Auburn. He does the twirling and stuff. Green Bay, he was nose tackle. Where are you guys in just getting him to where you want to be at Green Bay? >> I'm super happy with Colby. He's uh as you mentioned, he's a multiple position guy. Which you know how this league is, the more you can do the more valuable you are. Uh and he brings a great attitude every day. Uh tough, strong, athletic. Uh that was a great move by Chris and and uh you know, we uh we lost a great player, but I think we got a great player, too. >> Latu told us a couple of days ago that the biggest thing he's working on in year three is that first just right off the line initially play starts. What What comes with that and what have you seen in his in his development? >> Well, again, another guy that's, you know, been here most of the all back in the spring and through through the summer and, you know, every great pass rusher has great get-off, generally speaking. So, he's that's something he's working on and he'll just add that to his toolbox. >> When you talk When you talk about your corners yesterday, you had two plays and two two plays and three plays where one corner makes play and the other makes a play. Do you Are you Do you just say, "Yeah, that's that's what they're here for and to expect that?" >> Yeah, I mean, it We should Those guys, I know they expect to make plays out there when the ball's in the air. And so, we do as well as a group and and we'll feed off of that, but they're two very confident players. Ed Oliver and Air is a third. You know, and then we got the great competition behind those guys, but to answer your question, yes, we do. >> If you can play If you can play man-to-man, does it just kind of open up what you're able to do pressure-wise? >> Uh I mean, I think again, it's a little bit game plan driven, you know. What we You want to be on body in this league. You want to be These quarterbacks are too good to give a lot of open windows. So, you want to be as close to people as you can. So, you know, based on game plan stuff, but what we will definitely move around and change it up. >> You know what Mooney's been through obviously, but and that was He had a lot on his mind coming out of last season. He seems He told us that he's kind of found that love for the game again. Have Have you seen that be evident just in your dealings with him? >> I can't speak for him on that. I know that he's always had a good level-headed Every time I've had a conversation with him, he's been great. I could see a renewed bounce in his step a little bit. But, man, he's, you know, can't walk in his shoes on what he's been through. So, but I'm just happy that he is at where he's at where he's at now. He's in a great place and let's keep moving forward. >> What What does it mean to you to see him happy? >> Oh, it's great. He's a great >> He's happy and he wasn't this time of year but this time last year he was not happy. >> Yeah. Again, I can't speak to where he was at but I know that he's a great human being and I'm I'm I'm a big Mooney fan and root for him. >> I know one of his last one here guys. >> Was there stuff you didn't get to in year two or year one that now systematized you feel like you can get to? I get personnel changed in the second and third level. Yeah. Was there stuff you didn't get to last year? >> Um, I think you know, there's there's always some tweaks that you can go as the years pile on. Um, in matter of fact we did something today that we wouldn't have done on day two in camp. So, to your point, yes, there is. >> I know you said last one but you started it. >> Mooney, I know one of his concussions did not come in the field of play last year but when he's had a season of three concussions, does he um, need to play any different or is there a way to balance staying healthy while also bringing what he brings to the table? >> Yeah, I think it's tough as a football player, you know, to worry about that, you know? Um, I think he's always going to be conscious of it. We're We never teach anything tackling-wise that involves the head. Uh, but sometimes stuff happens, Uh, he's aware of it. He'll play smart, I know that. Um, but uh, you know, it's it's still football at the end of the day. >> All right, thanks. >> Thanks, guys. Thank you.

title: Colts need wide receiver help: Indianapolis Colts camp day 2 recap
text: Day two of training camp is in the books here for the Colts at Grand Park in Westfield. I'm Nathan Brown, your Colts insider with the Indianapolis Star here with Joel Ale Ericson. Uh the one big thing I feel like that stood out for us today at day two of training camp is um the Colts sorely needing uh a little bit more help at wide receiver. Alec Pierce of course is on the physically unable to perform list. He started camp there. He's still working his way back after his ankle surgery about 4 months ago with a 4 to 6 month timetable. Um Josh DS takes um a little bit larger role there. Uh returning the the team is missing Michael Pitman at the moment. But beyond DS and Tyler Warren at tight end, um a couple players jockeying for that third wide receiver role, assuming that Alec gets back healthy. Um but we've seen maybe a little bit less than perfect action from some of those guys. would have stood out to you the most in the couple days looking at that position? >> Yeah, today is kind of a weird day um because Laquan Treadwell did make a couple plays today, but somebody pointed this out to me. Trevarious Ward has caught more passes in the NFL in an NFL game in the last three years than Laquan Treadwell has just by making interceptions. Like this is this is a guy who hasn't really played. Nick Westbrook Aeen, Indiana guy. He's he he was a big play guy for the Titans, but he didn't really do anything with with Miami last year. Deion Burks had a drop today that turned into a pick uh as a rookie. He's a seventh rounder. You can't expect stuff from from that. And then Ashton Doulan has always been a special teamer and that limits what he can do. Like it just feels like when you watch the biggest thing I think from the first two days less than the way they're playing is just when they line up at the start of it without Alec Pierce and you're looking at the numbers out there and you're going, if I'm a defensive coordinator, I'm not scared. And we've seen Eli Pinkle um work into some of those reps even with the first team as well over these first couple days. We've I think only really seen one true deep ball um thrown by Daniel Jones today. That was two Josh Downs um maybe a hair underthrown and that gets broken up. Um so yeah, I I know Daniel Jones is obviously working his way back from his Achilles. We're not going to see everything in the first couple days, but um that position has left some to be desired. Chris Ballard told us on Tuesday that um the team isn't necessarily immediately looking to add from the free agent market to that spot, but there is a chance that they might consider that. Um not necessarily with any consideration related to Alec Pierce, but just um from the notion that they could potentially use some help there. Keenan Allen is the name that always pops up. Um the former veteran Charger who is not on a roster at the moment. We'll see if anything comes of that. He also, I think, gets exposed a little bit because Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward are on the field. They're these guys these are guys who have not really produced to the NFL going against corners who have really produced in the NFL and have all pros to their name. It just it's something that sticks out and I think maybe as we get into camp as Allen maybe wants to skip the first couple days of camp or other veterans like that. I I just feel like there's got to be a move made there at some point. Uh my one play from today Austin AK picking off Daniel Jones. I thought I think Jones so far his only two real misses have been when he's moving and trying to improvise a little bit. That's something to kind of monitor as Kant goes along, but GK makes a nice pick in the middle. He's playing in the middle today because Aake Davis Gaither was not available. And then uh he also made a couple other nice plays in pass. I think we forget about him in the linebacker and he's not going to play I don't think middle or weak, but he played a lot of Sam last year and I think that's a guy who has a role on this defense that we just don't talk about very much. And we saw a good amount of first team reps with um with Austin today. Hakee Davis Gaither was also not out on the field. He's one of those presumed starting linebackers along with CJ Allen who starting camp on the pup list. Colts don't expect him to be out long, but when you're missing um two guys who could very well be your starting linebackers there. giving opportunities to uh guys like rookie Bryce Bcher, Austin, um Wes Weekes, um who we've seen some from over the um first couple days here, Jay Jaylen Carl. Um interested to see how those guys work around while those two are out. We don't know exactly what Davis Gaither is dealing with. Uh but we'll have to to see how that works out. Hey, I I think the the other play that really stood out to me, uh, another interception thrown, um, that that tip pass that you mentioned from Dion Burks over on the the right sideline, Cameron Mitchell, uh, makes a great play with that ball up in the air, snags it out of the air and takes off down the, uh, down the sideline for what very well could have been a touchdown if we were really playing, uh, game action. Um, two interceptions. All all around, I feel like fairly solid quarterback action today. But those two plays really stood out um among the uh the team reps that we saw. >> Right. That that that interception was a Burks interception more than a Richardson interception. >> Yes. Agreed. Agreed. Uh well well that'll do it for us from Colts camp day two at Graham Park. We have two more days straight on Friday and Saturday. Friday morning. Um Saturday mid to late afternoon. We'll have all of your coverage on indiestar.com, our Indie Star YouTube channel. We just taped a podcast last night, the Colts Cover Two podcast. You can check that out on all of your podcast platforms along with YouTube. We'll have several stories posting throughout [snorts] the rest of today and have more coverage for you over the next couple days. I'm Nathan Brown. He's Jo Ericson. Thanks for uh watching us on Anar. >> Yeah, I had to bring my boy. He was hot out there in the sun. Get a little shade. So, you told us about how you you were working through a lot of things last year. This time, >> you seem like you're in a good frame of mind. How's it feel just being here and just being you? >> Uh, it feel good. Feel like I belong out here. Um, I was probably like 85% sure I was going to tie. But, uh, you know, I found a different, different purpose. You know, uh, just doing it for Junior. Um, doing it for Ammani, my daughter. Um, they bring me joy. They put smiles on my face. So, it put me in like a better emotional and mental state to come out here and play and have the energy to come out here and run around these young guys cuz if I'm depressed, it's not like I'm I don't want to go out here and chase around these young guys. So, uh uh I feel good. I got a lot of energy. Uh smiling again. So, uh I think I feel like I belong still belong out here. >> 85% 85% serious. >> Yeah, I'm dead serious. Like you talking to my girl uh talking to my mom, you talking to my age. Like I I'm I was uh pretty sure I was done. Like when I got that second concussion last year against the um before the Corners game, like I wanted to hang it up then, but that was just saying, "Man, just finish." Like that was already been a motto from one of my high school coaches that gave me some advice, just finish. So I went out there, tried to finish the season, but I came back and got another concussion. So I was like, "Damn, just got bad luck." Um but yeah, man, I was pretty sure I was done. But um this offseason, like I said, I just got into a better mood. My spirit was lifted and boosted again. So um I got I got some stuff to give. You got you're here for a reason. You're top corner. Those two plays yesterday with you and and sauce almost back to back. Is that you say >> get used to it because that's going to happen. >> Yeah. Uh that shows you the potential that we got. Uh me and him both all pro corners, great corners. Um but last year we both were hurt so we wasn't on the field so we could show everybody what we could do. But I feel like if we healthy we definitely going to be like a crazy crazy tan. So I just say man praying we stay healthy and just stay tuned and be ready for Sundays. I know you mentioned going through a lot last year on and off the field >> and you're motivated by junior and your family and things like that, but how do you also play free and just do that from >> uh I feel like it's no pressure on me anymore. Um like I made all the money I wanted to make. Um I won a Super Bowl. I went all out pro. I basically did everything I wanted to do in the NFL. So now everything now it's kind of like icing on top for me personally. Um no pressure. I'm not worried. I'm not stressed about anything. I'm not worried about giving up a touchdown cuz I went through the worst stuff imaginable that anybody can go through like losing a child. So that that was bad. Giving up a touchdown or giving up a catch. That's not bad to me anymore, you know? So I feel like I have nothing to lose anymore. Just go out and have fun and ball out. >> Now, I guess along the lines, how motivated are you though to still show? They mention Yeah, I'm super motivated, man. Uh I don't want to come out here and be average knowing that I have been at the top of the top. I don't want to like come out here and feel like I lost a step or I'm slow. I'm not moving as well I used to. Uh I still feel like I can move just like I did when I was 25, 26, 27, still feel like I got speed. Like I said, long as I'm happy, I'm smiling, um in a great mood, um I'm going to bring great energy and I'm going to go out there and ball out. I'm just try to do everything right. Practice walkthroughs and in meetings and um good things going to come to me. >> Going from 80% sure you were going to retire um to be here and rejuvenate. At what point in the offseason did that flip switch for you and and what brought that about? I think it was like when I started back training. Um like I said, I still feel like I can play. Like I go out there and work out and I was moving good. Um some of my training like damn that looked really good. You like the old Mooney, young Mooney, you know. So um once I was getting those words and just talking to my agent, you know, my fiance um just a lot of my family that was telling me, man, like just go out there, you know, try to finish if you can. So um that's what I'm going to go out there and do. It still be days where I wake up. It's not like I'm in a great mood every day. Like I wake up and be sad some days and be like, damn. Like do I really want to go out here and practice? like I already got everything I want but like no like I think about my why you know go out there and ball for junior go out there and ball for money and intrinsically within myself. Um like I feel like my purpose is to bring joy, bring happiness and love the people around me. So I feel like just being out here creating making plays it create great memories. It give you a great feeling. So that's the thing that I like to go out there and do. It's not about like catching an interception but it's about making my coaches happy, making my teammates happy. We all celebrating creating great memories and great experiences. So, um, that's part of the reason why I came back. Like, that's part of the love and the joy that I want to bring. >> When you and >> Last question, Stephen. >> When you and SA on top of your game, what does, what does that do to the other the quarterback? >> Uh, honestly, man, we two of the We are the best in the world. I don't really want to make no crazy predictions, but I feel like we can be the deepest and the best secondary in the league. Long as everybody stay healthy, we come out here and make our plays. We got like, it's not just about me and sauce. Like, Wall-E, that boy can ball. He hasn't played like an NFL game yet. Officially, he played preseason, but Wally can play. Mai, like you saw last year, he was a starter. Jaylen Jones, J got a whole lot better. So, I feel like our whole secondary like we got some ballers back there. We just got to stay healthy and go out there and do it. You know, the co had bad luck at corner like it'd be like four or five corners get hurt every training camp. So, long as we stay healthy and go out there and do our thing, it'll look good. It'll look good for the blue and white. >> Were you aware? anything different um on the field knowing what you went through and last year? >> I'm thinking about a guardian cap. I may worry, but I got the new um new and improved helmet. I got a new helmet that I changed this year. Uh it's it's for concussions. So, um hopefully we don't get another concussion. I'm not really worried about that. My I'll be reading books. I'll be in my hyperag so they keep my mind sharp. So, uh I think I'll be good as far as concussions. >> I know you don't want to play different like you don't want to play less aggressive. How do you balance still trying to play like the moving that you've been throughout your career and you know what happens? >> You know, injuries is going to happen by chance. Like you can go out there and do everything right and it still be a non-cont injury with guys like tear something. So um you can't really go out there on the NFL football field and think about getting hurt like it's going to happen regardless whether you trying to get hurt or trying not to get hurt. So I'm just worried about going out there and making plays like I said and creating good memories and balling out and getting wins for the um the coach coach organization. >> How we doing out there? So you got your you got your quarterback back. Were you surprised that Daniel was back? Everyone talks about, >> you know, his work ethic, no one's really surprised by that, but for you, someone who works so closely with him, like how big is it for you? >> Um, I think it's really awesome to have him back and I think, you know, everybody in the offense would say the same. You know, obviously that's our leader out there. that's the guy we all want to be uh behind and um obviously like you said his work ethic and coming back from an injury like that this fast isn't you know I would say very common um but just watching the way he's worked this entire off season um and just kind of the trajectory he's been on I don't think any of us are surprised he's back you know it's just the amount of work he's put in the amount of time he's been uh in the training room doing everything and or anything and everything to to get back for us um it really just speaks to who he is as a person and as a teammate with an injury like that, with him coming back like that, does that change the offensive line's approach when it comes to the protection schemes or the blocking schemes to make sure that that doesn't happen again or you're not a risk of another injury like that? >> I mean, to an extent, I think, you know, it'll probably reflect in some of the play calls, but I think for the most part, he's pretty comfortable doing everything we asked him to do, and he's pretty comfortable moving out of the pocket, getting on the run. Um, which is again, you know, coming off that injury, it's something as an offense that we really love to see. >> Before you guys put on and obviously all spring there's no pads and so far you haven't. What is the emphasis for you guys? It's not as much on the physicality of the game. I guess what what are you trying to get accomplished when the pads are not on? >> I think it just honing in on your technique and using your hands, you know, especially, you know, no pads, you don't want to throw your shoulder in there quite as much. Really emphasizing, you know, using your hands, hand placement. Um, and then just the fundamentals of blocking, you know. text: Y'all like the new setup? >> I try my best. I I try my best to fight for you guys. I try my best. >> Yeah, I'm ready. >> Hey, Deica, when you have a >> Oh, he got it. >> I got I got two youngers out here. You know, basically, they're both young, strong legs. And what is going to be the evaluation process? That's part of the encourage all this special team that's going to wind up being your starting point. What's all going to go in the imagination when you finally get down? >> Our punting competition is hot and heavy right now. Both Kai and Stonehouse, they both had really good springs coming out. You know, seeing both guys today, they're picking up right where they left off. So, it's going to be a really tight competition. What you look for at that spot, you're looking for consistency, right? And that's what both guys are working towards is getting the consistency on ball placement, right? Especially when we're at plus 50, like how are you executing those plus 50 punts? We know those are huge for us when we can get backed up opportunities. So seeing how both guys compete out here in practice and also we have the evaluation of the preseason games. So we'll go through that and see which way we'll go, which guy win. But both guys have done an outstanding job so far. >> Unfortunate to see Jake go down like that. everybody gathered around to express their concern. Uh just obviously you'll hear from as they evaluate, but just anything you could tell us about Jake. >> Jake went down today. Jake Hansen went down. Uh seems to be a foot injury. We don't know the extent of it. Just happened right now. So we'll evaluate him and see see how it how he knows towards getting back healthy. >> What do you like best about David McGomery? David McGomery. >> And what I like best about David, I love his approach, right? You talk about a true professional. He shows up every day prepared, ready to go, very attentive in meetings. Just seeing his demeanor on the field. It's business-like approach. And that's from my first call. I remember calling him when we first signed him. That's that was the same call that I had. It was the same guy. He hasn't changed from day one. as a business-like approach. He was that way when I seen him play in different different places in Chicago, also in Detroit. Very productive player. He touches the football, he's going to gain yards, right? Very productive, very selfless player. He shared the backfield in multiple spots and you know, he's not not accustomed to that, but when he touches it, he's gonna bring some power. He's gonna bring some juice to our offense as every run he gets. you see the force at which he runs with and just a really great person to have on our team. >> What you got Woody got thrown into things pretty quickly last year with the injury. Joe, what have you seen from him and his growth from last year this year at this point just learning from? >> Yeah, Woody is that year two player where I see the jump happening and I see it I saw it in the spring and I see it now at training camp. Talk about a guy in Woody who's put the work in. You see he's just more confident. feels like he's more relaxed being that second year and he's confident in what he's doing. I see a guy playing faster, making great decisions, and I see a guy who's really going to thrive and make some big plays for us. >> You've seen from Jaden Higgins from spring till now and what do you hope he can be for you all this year? >> Yeah, Jaden, I put him in the same category of Woody. Uh he's taken that year two jump. Uh you're seeing a guy who were able to move around the formation a little bit more, get him inside the formation. He's making some plays um just everywhere we put him. Like first play of practice today around us is a great route. CJ gives him a great ball has just shows his growth, shows a guy you can rely on, guy you can count on, you know, in those crunch situations and we're going to need him. We need a guy to step up opposite Nico and be a threat. And Jaden can be that guy for us. >> That final period, you guys had a few good moments on both sides of the ball. What stood out to you today practice? The one thing that stood out to me is, you know, we got a we had some poor pre- snap penalties. Uh we kind of went backwards offensively. So, those are some things that stood out where we can clean those things up. Uh defensively, we got to finish on the football better. Uh had a couple opportunities to take the football away and we did it. So, both sides right there got things we can clean up on coming back tomorrow. >> Seems like precision is a theme this training camp. You and Nick have mentioned it. The scoreboard's got it. How did you guys identify that as the the big key? >> Yeah, the precision is always key for me. And precision starts with football IQ, right? Knowing what to do, knowing how to do it, but it's also knowing how to adjust. Every time you line up, it's never going to be exactly how you draw it up on in your playbook on. So, can players handle motions? Can they adjust and adapt? And can they be precise with exactly what they're supposed to do when it comes to communicating? Are you so confident to where when you line up, it doesn't matter what the offense does, what a defense does. I'm preparing for that adjustment. I'm precise in how I approach the game, right? And that's been a key for me. When I look back on last year, I look back at our first three games, right? We lose our first three games not on play style, not on effort, not on physicality. We lose those games on precision, right? not being exactly where we're supposed to be, not putting the football away in a precise manner in the fourth quarter. Like those are the little things that cost you games that a lot of pe like a lot of times they go unnoticed, but they show up in the biggest moments. And so we're attacking that right now in training camp. Precision, precision, precision. Are you on the details? >> We ask you a lot about offensive line personnel, but how much does that start with Papa? How much trust you have in the game? develop those players, not just the rookie players, the secondary players, but some of those veterans who have been in the league for a while. >> Cole Cole Papovich has done a really good job when it comes to teaching. I think he's has a unique style of teaching and getting it across to his guys and you see their drill work. It's the consistency at which he operates. It's the same message over and over again. It's the little precise detail on foot placement like how's your angle? Where's your backside hand? All of those little fine details that most of us have no idea about when we talk about O line play. We just see a guy get beat and we want to criticize him. But it's those little fine details that allow you to be a a really great offensive lineman. It's it can get boring. It can get monotonous, but as soon as you're not on those small details that Coach Cole is teaching, that's when you give up a big play. And so, uh, our the veteran guys who come in, they have to do a really great job of kind of unlearning a lot of things because, you know, you've been in other systems, they teach it one way, you come here, we teach it another way. So, how quickly can you unlearn what you've been doing, which is extremely hard, extremely hard when you've, you know, when you've done something for so long, you know, it's hard to unlearn it. But our guys are, they're working at it. Cole is doing a great job of, you know, taking time with those guys. Understand it's going to take a little time for those guys to get caught up to how we do things, but they're they're moving in the right direction. Improving daily. That's all we ask. >> That speaks to that precision part that you just spoke about. >> No doubt. It's it's every position, no matter what position you play, it'll always come down to how precise are you on the details. watching Kayen McDonald a little bit, the low charge from him and the some of the drills on that side of the field. What has Kaden showed you so far as a young defensive tackle? >> And Kaden is really show how strong he is. He's probably one of the stronger guys that we have. You see him doing drills. He's knocking the coaches back a lot. Coaches are trying to hold bags and be tough guys, but Kaden is doing a great job of of showing the strength that he has now. Can he pull it all in? And can you consistently play with the proper hand placement, the proper footwork every single row? >> We talked about goal style and the way he gets his message across. There's a lot of hard coaching during this time of the season. What allows coaches to be able to deliver that point and for players. >> To be a a hard coach and to be on guys, it's really behind the scenes. You really have to show guys that you care about them, right? Nobody's going to listen to you if you come out, you're barking at guys, you're giving forceful commands and you don't have a true relationship with that person and what you're saying just doesn't fall on the ear the right way. And so when you build the right relationship with guys, you can coach them hard and they'll go that extra mile for you. So the relationship building piece will never change in coaching. and Cole. All of our coaches are doing a really great job of connecting and that's what camp is about as well. In training camp, you spend a lot more time with your guys and where you can truly build those connections to where you can coach them. Know that man, I know my coach has my best interest in heart. He wants to see me succeed. He wants to see me be successful. So, I'm going to listen to everything that he tells me. >> Talk about the position flexibility at tight end. Uh, one guy you brought in was Foster Monroe. What what did you like about his state when he was in New Orleans and what do you think he does to add to that tight end year? >> Foster has done a great job in his career playing on the line of scrimmage when it comes to blocking. He's a tough player. Saw that in his tape in New Orleans also back when he played with the Raiders. So, he brings that and Foster brings, you know, something you just can't coat. He has a a very fun personality. Really enjoy being around them. I talk about bringing joy every day. enjoying the day no matter the circumstance. Foster brings that type of joy, right? He's always has a smile on his face, always working hard like but knows how to keep it light as well and uh that's that's needed when you go through a grueling camp as we go through. We need that joy from Foster and he brings it every day. >> Um details you got here. You think that I guess the whole staff understands what you mean by like how you explained about precision and all that. That's been the message you pass. >> Yeah. The the detailed message, the precision message, the staff gets it and I'm I'm really hard on the staff and ask them challenging questions when it comes to what they're teaching the guys, right? And it's about not be not about what our coaches know, but about, you know, what do the players know? what did they hear when you taught them that particular technique? Did they hear it exactly how you wanted it taught? So, there's details in coaching. There is also some humility that comes with coaching because you got to reach, call it 10 different guys in a room. You got to be able to reach all those guys and everybody receives the message in a different way. So, you have to be very detailed and thoughtful as you coach. on the side of the ball you have um your your standard I mean sorry foundation when it comes to your starters. How do you evaluate the depth from you know back to evaluate the depth in camp is easy because we get a ton of reps. All these guys get a lot of reps. Uh in camp all the guys are put in a lot of different positions. So the guys who thrive you see the depth shows up really in training camp when they get a opportunity to play a lot in the preseason games. a guy maybe here on the practice field, he may just looking just average, okay, but then you put him in a game, put him in live action, you know, he's shows up and makes those plays. So, a lot of our depth will be, you know, decided when it comes to those preseason games, which we're all excited to see. >> Obviously, you tal a little bit yesterday regarding the techno. Today we're able to see him doing a little bit more work, especially out on the field, being able to be very emphatic to to join the team, you know, just watching practice just for overall. That's just to see him out there today. >> The daily Tank Dale question, he it's uh Tank is out here. He's working again. He's Man, he's very eager. I would say he's eager to get back out there. So, it's not from Tank. It's me. I'm holding holding Tank back a little bit to make sure when he's ready to go, he's able to stay out there. >> Last one. When you guys uh evaluate CJ in practice, how much the quarterbacks actually general, how much do you guys factor in time to grow when they're, you know, going for the read or whatnot? How much you guys factor that in the sense plays? >> I think I heard it. So when you when you guys are kind of watching over quarterbacks, how much do you factor in time to throw? Like how long to hold the ball is that? >> Yeah. Factoring in in time to throw with the quarterback. It's it's really based on what's the play concept that we have called right there. As we obviously know, there's quick game concepts. There's, you know, seven sevenstep concept. So depending on the concept, it depends on the defense. You know, how quickly does the ball need to be delivered? It depends on what the quarterback is seeing. And one thing I've been harping on with our quarterbacks is just let's be elite decision makers, right? You touch the football every single snap. So, as the quarterback, you have to make great decisions with the football. And sometimes a great decision, it it may not be throwing the football. It may be tucking it. It may be running it. It may be throwing the ball in the dirt. But just make great decisions and know we always have that next play mentality. >> All right. Thank you guys.

title: David Montgomery: “We’re on the Right Track” | Full Q&A
text: This the first time I've been up here. All right. Uh, I think, you know, just I I played for a little bit. I think I'd say that the thing I bring most is experience. You know, I've I've been around some I've been in some special groups and, you know, I've been in some some opportunities and some places where it was really good and other places where it wasn't the best either. And you know, you kind of take things as as things go, but you know, I think I'd just say bringing experience and you know, bringing who I am to to a team that's already special. >> Coach said he really appreciate really appreciates your business-like approach to the game. How much do you think like having that mindset and taking care of everything off the field and getting ready for the game helps you on the field? >> Oh, I think it's it gives you a you know, an an extra edge when you're facing opponents, you know. Uh, the game is fun and it's supposed to be, but it's very intentional always. And um, I try to be proactive with everything that I do. So, when I when I get to game days, I I I feel free. I can play free and I can play the way I I I play when I was a kid, so uh, I think that comes with preparation. Um, you know, making sure you're taking care of your business on and off the field, but like doing stuff when you're not in the building also, so I think just trying to find extra, you know, nicks and things that can help you improve off the field is is beneficial also. >> Demeco's played a lot about pre-snap and the fact that you got to get the wide receivers more involved. What have you seen from the pre-snap and where maybe lacked or needs to improve or how it's gotten better? >> Yeah, um it's definitely improved. It's not where we want it to be yet cuz I, you know, we got I I have high expectations cuz I know you know, what this offense is they're of doing, so um we we've definitely took some steps, but we still got a ways to go and we'll improve. >> How does that improve? What needs to improve when you say it's not where we want it to be? Like what's the missing ingredient? >> I wouldn't say missing. I think just more of just being more accountable, you know, and and and be also you know, us pushing each other more and having high expectations and knowing that it's a right way to do it and and we're there. We just we got to sharpen it up in a few places. It's early on in camp and everybody's still trying to learn chemistry and figure each other out, but we're on the right track. >> Hey, could you talk about the fact that you came out of a situation where you shared a backfield with another outstanding running back and now you're coming to a situation now you're sort of having to be a bell cow label that's hung on you now and you're sort of the running back who you feel that impetus that you need to push it all to the next level. How you adjusting to that and you know, the gap from your own perspective? >> Uh yeah, just being available. Um you know, I don't like to put titles on stuff, you know, like bell cow, split. That stuff don't really matter cuz whoever's out there is going to be out there, you know. I'mma be out there, Woodrow's going to be out there, you know, Jay War's going to be out there. Everybody's going to be out there, so um again, just holding everybody else to the same expectations and knowing that we all going to have to to be out there and whenever I'm out there, me ensuring that I'm holding the standard and and whoever next and they carry the same thing and they and they raise it, so um again, just being prepared for every moment. Making sure like I'm doing things prehab wise and you know, I'm out here conditioning more as much as I can just so I can be ready. >> What's the relationship like within the running back room? >> Oh yeah, everybody rock with everybody, you know. The the position of a running back is is already tough enough and like we we really don't get a lot of acknowledgement for the amount of stuff that we do. But like everyone in the room who plays kind of like understands how important it is for us to have appreciation for that position. And you know, everybody in the room is so different. But they we all bring different things to the table that we all can benefit from. So, I think putting different guys who are who adamant and willing to learn and you know, no one takes anything personal from the top to the bottom like me being able to learn from Noah or Josh, you know, or Ed like me being selfless enough to say, "Okay, like you didn't like that I didn't think I could do that. Okay, where can I improve?" You know, me playing 8 years. And I think it just takes a level of selflessness um to where you can kind of be that way. And and if I can be that way, I know those guys can kind of return the things. So, it's been fun. It's been a very fun room and I think we're going to do some special things. >> You come from a team where you practice against a very good defensive man that you practiced against down here on the against Will Anderson and and Danielle Hunter as well. But you know, going up against Will Anderson, like what is that like when you're on the opposite side of going against him? >> I'm just happy that I'm on the same team as him now, quite frankly. And I'm on the same team as Danielle. Cuz they're both freaks, you know, and I think the first time I came out here and we was in OTAs and we was doing like some team stuff. And I'm watching like the snap and I'm like, "He jumping offsides. He jumping offsides." Whole time he not. He just off the ball like super fast. So, it's like seeing somebody come in, he about his business, you know, him being like a little bit younger and him carrying himself in a way to where he makes me want to get better. So, I love seeing Will go. I love seeing Danielle go. I love seeing that whole defense go cuz it's going to force us on the other side of ball to be better. >> Hey, you mentioned the red zone. It's been something that improved in the red zone. What about your game makes it possible to reach the goal in the offensive game this season. >> Um just being available. Uh just ensuring that I'm I'm accountable in in in my team and my coaches can count on me in in every situation when we down there. And that's not just the red zone, that's just anywhere on the field. So, um I think just me being ready and uh available for for whatever opportunity presents itself. >> Hey, can you talk about um >> Go ahead. >> Thank you. Can you talk about um the expectations of this of the role that you're in? Cuz the people are talking about how the run game has to get better. Does that create pressure? How do you guys respond to that? How do you feel about how the team's going to do this >> Um I've never really been one to like focus too much on pressures, you know. Um at the end of the day it's a it's a game. It's fun. It's supposed to be fun. I've done everything in in preparation up to this point to put me in a position to where I can play at a high level and be really good. And um as long as I'm being attentive and and being very intentional with my work, everything will fall in line. And everybody else in that room will kind of carry the same thing, too. So, um yeah, pressure is whatever you make it. You know what I'm saying? You got to look at the challenge and and take it head on. >> I I know this is the second time you've changed teams, but is there challenges to being on a new team and getting acclimated when you when you move? >> Uh the first time it was. This time not really much, you know. It's not something I want to get used to at all. Um but yeah, you know, it comes with its you know, the things that are they're kind of different. Having to move, you know, put my son in a different school. Um but you know, you got to be adaptive and just be ready for whatever comes when it does come and I'm happy to be here and you know, I don't really want to go nowhere else. So, I'm good here. >> But um what have been your thoughts on Jaylen Hurts? He's been a guy who got last year I said he's taking a step, but this your first time seeing him this year. What have been your thoughts on him? >> You talking about J. Higgs? >> Yeah. >> So, he went to Iowa State. >> Okay, so you knew him. >> Yeah, so I didn't play with him, but I've seen him play. So, I'm not surprised at all. Um you know, I I carry a little bit of extra like umph when it comes to the State guys cuz you know, to that team that TOE that team out east the the black and gold or black and yellow whatever you want to call it. They already look at us like the little brothers anyway, so they already know what expectation we bring. We come from a lineage of a Matt Campbell and you know, there's no surprise surprise in him carrying himself the way he does and being a professional and him taking a leap in a step, so yeah, I'm not surprised at all. >> What are some of your initial thoughts on coach Ryan? What have you seen in him? >> Oh yeah, coach Ryan? He real deal. He for real. And if he don't bring it, he going to let you know. And you know, we ain't got the pass on yet, so but just being able to to to be behind a guy who who believes in his players. He was a player an elite player. Uh he carries himself and he's a he's a God-fearing man. You know, that's who you want to lead the charge, you know? And you get a group of guys who buy in. The defense we got the best defense in the league. You know what I'm saying? And we trying to form our offense and to where we can be the one of the best if not the best in the league also, so you know, him having the expectations and him carrying himself the way he does and him not missing a beat like it forces you to be better, so you want that in a leader and you know, he's I wouldn't ask anybody else. >> Elijah had a little bit of a moment last year. Went over 100 in the game. What's always been so interesting >> AZ cuz Arizona? >> Yeah, what do you see in him? What have you seen in him? Anything that that sticks out? >> Yeah, he a dog, you know? to see you know, DB like have expectations for it not to be a fall off at all going from player to player no matter who's starting who's not and kind of like see it in fruition and it kind of happened like it's good for for jaws cuz he need that and he needed that and you can see his confidence here on the field like he's a smooth runner he's confident and he got a a smile that will light up the room so you see a guy like that putting in the work being committed again being selfless enough to be here and take coaching from everybody and you know it makes sense and you understand why he has the success that he has on whenever he gets his opportunity to just never be a you know a beat of a eye thinking that he can't handle it cuz he's done it before you know and he'll he'll continue to do it and he'll hold himself to a expectation that we all have to follow also. >> Can you talk about your early thoughts on CJ and his leadership how he's been with you all >> Yeah CJ's poised I don't see him like really trip out too much over you know like plays like he'll correct it we'll talk about it and then we'll move on like and that's what you like to see in a quarterback somebody who's leading the offense and the one who's the general on that side of the ball you know you got expectations for any any situation he's got to be the calmest and he's got to be the one to rally the guys and we can have a conversation you know he has to know what kind of energy he needs to breathe depending on what situation it is so you know CJ's done just that and you can tell he's getting more comfortable you know he's starting to trust the guys more it's early on in camp but like I wanted to go throw with him this off season you know in LA and to kind of see how he was and how calm he was and how poised he was like that's what you want that's what you need and I've been around some great quarterbacks you know I was around JG Andy Dalton you know all of these guys like that can sling it and had experience I'm seeing like some of the same characteristics in in CJ. >> Thank you appreciate it thank

title: Jalen Pitre on Reed Blankenship and the Texans Defense | Full Q&A
text: So, how y'all doing? Very eager. Um I think you know, we obviously had a had a good year. Um but there's definitely things that we can build on, things that we can correct, and things that um can help us going forward. So, we're all having an optimistic um look going forward and just looking to improve on what's next. >> Sam, a big change in the secondary was Reed Blankenship's addition. What's it been like working with Reed so far? Getting to know him and kind of football player he is. >> Yeah, great dude, great football player. Obviously, he's playing he's going into year five um and been doing it at a high level since he's been in the league. So, we're happy to happy to add him and um he's going to do nothing but elevate the room. You know, he's obviously won a Super Bowl, so he knows what it takes to get there. And I think that that's really going to help us because obviously, we're all trying to get there as well. So, um real happy that um Reed is in our room and um just looking forward to the production that he's going to have this season. >> You mentioned his production and what he brings to the room. He can elevate y'all. What does he do? What is his game that makes y'all better than you didn't have before? >> Yeah, versatile safety that can play in the back or up in in the line of scrimmage. Going to make TFLs. Um a hard hitter. He can really do it all. Whatever the coaches ask of him. Uh obviously, you know, our coaches are going to give him a set thing that he's going to do and he's going to own it like a pro like he has in these last four years. Like I said, winning a Super Bowl and being a key contributor for that defense. >> And you guys have played him two years ago when he was in Detroit and now he's your running back here. What does a guy like David Montgomery bring to the offense, but just being around him, what has he brought to the locker room for you guys? >> Yeah, David he's different. He's different. Like I remember we're going to go way back. We you talking about when we played the Lions, but we're going to go way back to when I was a freshman in college and we was playing Iowa State. Was the first time I ever seen somebody just get completely ran over as a true freshman and I'm like I don't I'm like is this for me? Like you know what I'm saying? All the question marks popped up but um he's had a great career up to this point. I know he's going to elevate the offense and do a great job for the team this year. >> Have you talked to him about that memory? >> Yeah, I talked to him about that when I seen him in in Detroit after the game. I was like I've been watching you for a long time like from afar. So when I knew I had a little hit on him and I'm like I can't slow down when I got to go hit him like I got to bring it. And we've all seen the highlights that he's had. Um great back that can do everything. Um catch it, run it, spin it, truck it, juke it, like whatever you want. He he's one of them. >> The The Bengals had a scrap game one on third down. You all haven't had anything like that amongst yourselves at least in the week in between here. I guess you two. >> Mhm. >> Is that intentional? Is that a Why is that? >> I don't know. Maybe it's just not hot enough right now. When it gets hotter uh you will probably start to see start happening but I guess it's just not hot enough right now. >> Can you already feel some of the advantages of seeing in Aaron in that you brought so many defensive players back again this year? >> 100%. Um continuity is huge in our room. Um we know what it takes. We know what it looks like um from our DC. Um and everybody's very open to learning. So I think that that does nothing but continue to help us to evolve and continue to grow into what we want to be this year. >> Looking at that last year having 12 wins and the ordering defense so many pieces returning, how many players have gotten deals in the last couple of weeks? Do you feel like there's a little bit more uh pressure for you guys to set the tone early on in the season for what the expectation is going into the regular year? >> From the first play we step out there in the preseason game, it's about pure execution and and energy. Like are we swarming or not? It's it's really black and white with us, black and white with coach DeMeco. And um yeah, it's one standard. So if if if if we not living up to it, it is going to be known and we got to get it fixed. >> What's something you worked on with your skill set this off season? >> Um that's a good question, you know, I tried to take a step away. I love the game of football, so I'm always very like in my iPad, all that stuff, like I'm always just watching some old clips, always got NFL Network on, but I tried to take a step away and when I did like it just turned me up even more. Like when I got back into it, I was ready to go. So, just that hunger for the game um and wanting to be back into it has definitely I've definitely felt it, you know, in these last couple weeks that I've been back and really enjoying um the game of football because obviously I do love it. >> You guys always talk about iron sharpening iron. So, being on the defensive side of the field, what are you seeing from the offense that I know every time you guys go out there, you guys want to win those battles, but then also when you go out there and play, this is your offense on your side. So, what are you seeing from them that that maybe you like to say, "Okay, they can cause problems for other defenses." >> Yeah, I think um like you said uh iron sharpening iron. Every day out here in training camp is a game day, so we showing up and we trying to like impose our will on them and they trying to impose our will on on us. So, um with that being said, the receivers have done a great job getting off the ball and run plays, pass plays, making everything look very um congruent and the same. Like they done a great job at that. Running backs are running hard, good routes out the backfield. CJ is doing a good job dominating um out of the huddle, making sure that everything is looking smooth um in the motions. Like everything is looking crisp. So, I'm excited about what they're going to bring this year and uh yeah, it's been good. Obviously, you're going to have mistakes, defense going to have mistakes, offense going to have mistakes, but it's about you know, come going from one day to the next day. So, obviously, we had some mistakes yesterday, the offense had some mistakes yesterday. It's like I already see them growing on stuff already. title: Confident Texans football team hits camp running, practice updates, Jake Hansen injured foot
text: [music] Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. His teammates took a knee. They gathered around him. They wished him well, and he was carted off the field. So, we don't have a definitive update just yet. I'm sure they will x-ray it, MRI it, and all that stuff. So, a setback for Hansen. And then, as always in football, it's just the cruel reality. someone else will step up. So Hansen who was in the mix for the third linebacker spot. Now you've got Marte Mapu, you have Wade Wood, maybe Jake Hme will be heard from of course Jamal Hill. So there were no shortage of candidates and it's not someone that plays as much as a Niz Alshshire or Henry Toto, but it's still nonetheless, you know, you look at look back at EJ Speed and his production last season, they play significant snaps. And what if you know one of the starting linebackers Aziz or Henry was to go down. You're one play away. So it's an unfortunate situation. He's very good on special teams. A valuable guy. Someone that's really good in the locker room. Really well respected by his teammates. Made this team as an undrafted free agent. Recently talked with him before camp about his opportunity and he's very excited. So tough to see the first injury of training camp. title: C Aaron Brewer meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: First off, I don't think we've seen you since the extension, so congratulations. >> Thank you. >> One of the things I noticed is that you brought along some of the young guys with you. Why did you do that and why was that important to >> Uh because in my position, I can't do nothing alone. You know what I'm saying? It was a collective effort and then also, they're young right now and they're so to like just have them there to see the whole process and just keep them by my side. Like they're they're my brothers right now. And so, we're right now and forever on. So, I just feel it was special to have them there with me. >> As a guy who came through as an undrafted player, what does it mean to you to to get a contract like this? >> Uh it's a blessing, man. You know what I'm saying? Like just coming from where I came from. Always in my my head personally, like probably not in the outside world, but I knew this is where I was going to end up. This was always part of the plan. So, I'm just thankful. I thank God that I made it here and I just stayed the course, stuck to the plan. >> We talked to Hack this morning about just the tone of practice, the difference in practice, but just watching you guys out there, a lot of high intensity reps, it looks like. Not chipping necessarily, but just a lot of intensity. Is that an accurate way to describe practice and what do you think about it in >> Uh 1,000%. You know, practice like you want to make practice as hard as it can be. And that and that's our goal like going to practice this whole year. You know, you want to be aggressive, you want to be intense. Like you want to be uncomparable to the game. You want the game to be easy. And so, when we're out there, I want to we want to compete. We want to push each other, push it all the way to the edge, to get close to the fighting as we can. And yeah, that's the energy this year. >> After you said that start to start to evaluate the first couple days of training camp how do you self-evaluate where you are? >> Uh so, yesterday was our first day and that that's the floor. And so, anything beneath that is we're going backwards. So, every day we need grow, we need to get better and and we're able to see from day before from today, are we improving or we working backwards? >> You feel like each year demands something different for the team leaders. Just what do you believe how do you believe your leadership will evolve this week? >> Um just trying to get everyone on the same page, like the same mentality I have. Like just that same like aggressiveness. Like just doing everything intentional, taking every play one play at a time. We're not worried about the game. You can only control one play. You can only be where your feet at. And so trying to maximize each rep individually in itself, not worrying about the next play, not worrying about the last play. Like making the best of each play while we out there. >> What do you think of the idea of you being one of these pillars that John Eric Sullivan wanted to extend and wanted to keep around as as one of those leaders? >> Uh you know, I'm thankful, man. It's a blessing and I'm just grateful that he believed in me on that level, you know what I'm saying? Like that that's the role I wanted to be in. That's the role I own. And so for him to believe me into being that same role, like it's an honor. >> Bro, how do you see your role in trying to help Kayden Proctor come along and what do you see from him so no, KP he he already like he got a lot of good qualities already. You know, he big, he fast, and he aggressive. As a offensive lineman, that's what you want out of him. And so with him, I'm just trying to keep pushing him and just allowing him to know like it's more. And just have him like not competing with what he see every day out here. Like it's more to the league. There's 32 teams and it's plenty great defensive linemen out there. So I want him to be prepared for when he going against the bottom of the bottom and the best of the best. I want him to be the best player he can be. I want him to be the number one guard in the league. And so that's my goal. That's my attitude with him every day. >> And on the other side, what do you think he could do to help John Allen to be where he's more comfortable on the right side? >> Um same thing. I mean, I said in the spring like him on the right side, he looked way more comfortable. And I've been with him all last season. We've been up here working out together. So I've been seeing like how he may come to work, his intentionality towards everything he doing. And so I feel like it's the same thing with him. Anybody playing on the line with me, anybody on this team, anybody on offense with me, I want them to be the best in the league. And so that's what we trying to push. We trying we preach I'm preaching that every day to them and trying to push each other every day to do that. >> Brooke, can you feel like a cultural difference between this team compared to when you got here a few years ago? >> Uh, yeah, you know, it's two different uh coaching styles. And so, it's definitely a different culture. And, you know, we just leaning to what we bring it to the building. Like, they they coming in as more aggression. And so, we leaning into his identity and what he want this team to be. >> How similar do you see the offense under Mike Sullivan as opposed to only Mike Munchak >> Um, I say it's pretty similar. You know, him and Mike was working like hand-in-hand close together last year. And so, they kind of got that same philosophy a little bit, but they all got their own little thing they different in. And so, it's very similar. >> How do you uh How do you work How do you know when you stay I'm talking about how you guys all kind of stay down here and do your grind out here all all season. >> Mhm. >> Is that spoken? Is that unspoken amongst you guys? And then, what's the value of like all of that extra time that you guys are are working out together? >> Um I think it was like it was kind of unspoken but spoken at the same time. Like, we understand like Pat going to year three, Juwan going to year two, AJ he year seven with me, you know, so we just really we trying to merge together. Like, we want to be better. We want more. And so, just sticking around just growing that bond with each other. We working out everyday together. Pushing each other just continuing to grow that connection with each other. So, I I definitely believe it was definitely intentional. >> You mentioned more a few times in this talk. What's more for you personally and for this offense in life? >> Um, to be better than I was last year. You know what I'm saying? It's it's always want to grow. I wasn't perfect. Ain't no such thing as perfect. But, I'm chasing perfection. And so, that's that's all I got to do. I got to I try to be number one center in the league. We got to try to be number one rushing offense in the league. Number one passing offense. Just number one offense as a whole. I'm trying to go first team all pro. I want everybody else to go first team all pro. You know what I'm saying? Pro Bowl. Protector of the year. Like, those are the top of the top. And so, that's what we striving for. >> Hey Brooke, uh looking at you guys out there doing 11-on-11s and no 7-on-7s. Happily was saying today he doesn't like 7-on-7s. It doesn't include the linemen. He likes real football. Tell me about the mentality that 11-on-11 sets instead of 7-on-7. >> Uh that is real life football. We're not out here playing flag football. Like when you go to game day it's 11-on-11, not 7-on-7. So I feel like it is it's it's more work, you know what I'm saying? It translate from practice to the game and that's what we're trying to do. >> As I say when I watch it seem like more simple pressure is more bringing the blitz and just kind of giving you guys a lot to process up front. When you're tired and it's hot out there, how much value does that mental strain add for an offensive lineman you go through that? >> Um it's the same thing like when you working out. Like when you working out you building your muscles. And so when you get a bunch of different looks, bunch of different bunch of different blitzes like it build your your your mental muscle. Like you able to see different things and you able to like even when you tired process things faster and more clearly. >> You you've been with Austin Jackson for the last two years. What have you seen him go through just trying to stay healthy and and trying to shed that injury prone label? >> Um just staying on top of it. Just bunch of PT work. Take care of the body. Trying different things to just stay healthy, you know what I'm saying? Like it's so much different recovery things you can do out here. And so I see him just really pouring into himself, pouring into his body and trying to be the best version of him. >> How important is he to this line's success? >> He's very important. He's our starting right tackle and everyone know like when he out there like he he's an elite he can be an elite player. He's a great run blocker and a good pass blocker. And so like that is just it's great building blocks to grow off of.
