title: Ben Solak on Vikings Quarterback Reps, Kevin O'Connell's Offense & Run Game | 2026 Training Camp
text: Continuing our Vikings training camp tour, I am now joined by ESPN's Ben Solak. And Ben, you are here. You've been on SportsCenter a couple of times already making your way through different training camps. Now, the last time we talked to you was at the combine. And you said something to me that kind of struck me. I was like, I got to ask this again. >> Okay. >> You usually come out with a top coaching staffs in the NFL. Last year it was the Vikings. How are they doing this year in your in your uh >> Yeah. >> calibrations? >> I continue to rank the Vikings coaching staff extremely high. There there is no better coordinator in the league right now not head coach coordinator than Brian Flores. So, this unit is unbelievable. And then Kevin O'Connell is a guy who obviously coming into last year we're saying, all right, like he's going to build it around JJ. And that plane didn't land. Now JJ has a second opportunity and Kyler's in the building. If you trust Kevin to do anything, it's to get a high floor of play out of a rotating quarterback room, an imperfect quarterback room. And so, while last year was not what you maybe hoped from an offensive perspective, there's still very few offensive coaches I would trust more to make, you know, the best out of what you've got in a quarterback room than Kevin O'Connell. >> What were your impressions when you spoke to Kevin O'Connell about how this is all going to play off in the off and in the training camp season? >> Yeah, I mean a competition is a competition. You want to give the guys equal reps. You want to give them reps with the first team. You want to give them an opportunity to show what they can do. I think, you know, even independent of the week one starter, I think, you know, the Minnesota Vikings have experienced midstream quarterback changes here more than the average team should, right? I think that Kevin wants to make sure that both of the quarterbacks have first team reps because there's a chance at any time that somebody goes down in the NFL. And so, they're going to split time. I think that the better, you know, they'll feel comfortable giving the better quarterback the job and then it that's what it is for 2026 and we'll see what it is for 2027. Obviously, Kyler's not signed and JJ's still on the rookie deal. And so, they're just going to take it a practice at a time, a game at a time, a year at a time. >> I found your article on um a quarterback player relationship to be interesting. You did choose one of the quarterbacks in the competition, Kyler Murray, and how he would work alongside Kevin O'Connell. What intrigued you about that? >> The quarterback run ability. We just we the the most mobile quarterback we've seen play in a Sean McVay system either in the Rams or trickle down anywhere else is Malik Willis with Matt LaFleur and the Green Bay Packers. And those have been like three spot starts that were like three of the coolest, most explosive games ever. And then Malik Willis paid, right? I mean like we do not see a lot of quarterback mobility in this system. So when you start to introduce more shotgun alignments, more 11 on 11, more zone read, more misdirection in the backfield because the quarterback can keep it, you really add a wrinkle to this offense that is a little bit unprecedented. It's a little bit not what we've seen before. And so in the event that we see Kyler for an extended period of time this season, you're going to see an iteration of Kevin O'Connell's offense that has yet been explored and accordingly defenses are going to be living it live as well. And that's an opportunity for some, you know, really explosive games. >> Explosive games obviously on the run for a quarterback like Kyler Murray, but also the run game is hoping to take a step in this season with the addition of assistant head coach Frank Smith to the coaching staff that obviously we know you like. Um he's from Miami. He's known for the different schemes that he can run and and cook up. How do you think that can play into the Vikings run advantage this year? >> So you have in Frank Smith a guy who goes under Mike McDaniel who is a running game coordinator for Kyle Shanahan. And then in Kevin Carter, the offensive line coach who was promoted this past year, you have a guy who who was also coached under Kyle previously and has experience as an offensive line coach, running game coordinator in that system. They are going to commit harder this year than they have in the past under Kevin O'Connell to being a team that can run the football in a variety of ways, but really can major in a wide zone system, can spend a lot of misdirection in the backfield, motions in the backfield. And that that's going to be very good for Jordan Mason. They had a quietly very good rushing season last season. It was their best year under Kevin O'Connell in terms of yards before [snorts] contact per carry, in terms of explosives. They got fewer TFLs and stuffs than they had in years past. Like it Mason, Donovan Jackson, the Will Fry signing, the the the investment in the running game started last year. You started to see some of the fruits of that labor. Obviously the the passing game struggles doesn't let the running game blossom the way you'd like it to. That's going to finish this year with the addition of Frank Smith. It's going to be uh the best running game we've seen under Kevin O'Connell is going to be this season. >> Okay, I love your attitude. For when when you when you all look at the NFL as a whole, why is the importance of that phase of the game kind of felt like a little resurgence? Why is it so important to have that going? >> I mean because defensive coaches are better than ever before at taking away the first thing you want to do in the passing game, right? We have a much deeper menu of coverages on the defensive side of the ball. We have a much better answer to pre-snap motions. We know how to confuse quarterbacks a lot better. We know how to limit coaches like Kevin O'Connell who want to be doing a lot of the, you know, quarterbacking from the sidelines, kind of helping you ID. We know how to disguise stuff a lot better. So, we've gotten really really really really really good at making life hard on the quarterbacks in the first 2 seconds of the passing snap. And so, the answer to that is, all right, cool. What if we just kicked you in the teeth for four quarters, right? Like what if we were able to just dominate you physically in the running game? And now you have to start taking all those resources, those blitzes and those rotations, and instead of pouring them into the passing game, you have to spend some of those resources in the running game. And now all of a sudden life gets a lot easier for Justin Jefferson because of instead of 45,000 different coverages he's going to see and presses and alignments and changes, that menu shrinks. And now you can get back to what you want to do in the passing game. The the league operates on a pendulum. We we swing one direction and then we swing the other direction. Right now for offenses, we're swinging back to running the football. >> Okay, but we haven't talked about Jauan Jennings yet, and that's someone that can also be another option down the field for the quarterback as well as a a weapon in the run game as far >> What were they eyeing when they were like, this is the guy we want for our, you know, wide receiver number three? >> And if you're going to have a dynamic and diverse running game in the modern NFL, you need a receiver who can block, who can line up as a power slot, guy who's tied to the formation, and can go run routes and catch the football, but can be a meaningful blocker at the second level. The like paradigmatic player for that is Jauan Jennings. Jauan is going to allow the Vikings to spend time in 11 personnel, which is where Kevin O'Connell wants to be, but have a far more legitimate run blocking threat at receiver. It's going to allow you to fold in those run plays, then you get into the play-action pass. >> Before you go, you wrote an article recently about a breakout player from every team. >> Yep. Someone that I don't have think has got enough credit or love for being here in Minnesota is James Pierre, a cornerback. There's so much talk about so many other positions. Why was Why was he someone you think is going to jump off the page this year for the Vikings? >> you have a you had really really good stats on a very small sample size last year with the Steelers. He obviously spent time with Flores when he was in Pittsburgh. He spent time with Gerald Alexander, the new defensive backs coach, when he was there in Pittsburgh. The fact that they go and they choose to bring that guy out there having seen him have kind of a little bit of a breakout season with the Steelers in limited action indicates that right they think with his length, with his press ability, and then his eyes and zone coverage, they know exactly what they can do with him. And they don't have to spend a ton of money at the cornerback position in order to get it done. And so whenever you see I think a coaching staff go pull a guy that they saw previously and put him into a starting role, it's because they know something you don't. And so it's nice to bet on that player and then look smart afterwards. >> All right, final question, I promise. I just like to pick your brain. The interior defensive line was really bolstered in the in the draft. You have Caleb Banks, Dominic Rogers, two guys that they're very high on. Now, why do you think they were guys that this Vikings defensive staff wanted to target? >> Because the I think Flo knows that the way that his defense loses with all of its cleverness, with all of its rotation, with all of its blitzes, is if they just get run on up the middle, right? It's just same thing I talked about earlier with Kevin O'Connell on the other side of the ball, right? And so defensive tackle has been a spot where they tried to go the veteran route with Dalvin Hargrave and Jonathan Allen. And I don't think the skill sets were a great fit for the ask in terms of what they wanted those players to do. With Banks and Dalvin Tomlinson, you have a ton of size. You have the ability to really come up the interior. So you can play with light boxes now. You can protect yourself from losing to those teams that are really good downhill running teams. Force more of those third and longs, which typically those blitz downs, those pass rush downs. Flores obviously blitz on any down under the sun, but typically those are the ones that you're trying to get to as the defensive coordinator. >> Well, Ben, thank you so much. We appreciate you stopping by on your training camp tour. Safe travels. And if you want to catch his work, you can check out ESPN and espn.com.

title: Jamal Adams on Joining the Vikings, Brian Flores' Scheme & Learning the Playbook
text: Joining us now here at Vikings training camp is Jamal Adams, one of our newest Vikings. Well, you are a veteran in the locker room right now. What is it like to hear that you're going into your 10th season? >> Honestly, it's it's it's surreal. You know what I mean? Obviously, just hearing different guys calling me OG and Unc. >> [laughter] >> It's honestly, you know, I've kind of got used to it. And you know, obviously, when I was young, you know, I I was doing the same thing. I was calling older guys, you know, Unc and OG and whatnot. So, just for it to come full circle is definitely a blessing. >> How do you hope your veteran presence lifts up the defensive side of this team? >> Well, you know, I just anything they need. You know, I'm out here to, you know, help. You know, that's what I'm about. Even, you know, the young guys that are coming in playing safety, linebacker, whatever the case may be, you know, just just being a vet. You know, coming out here, helping the young guys, you know, recover, whether that's learning football or learning life, anything, you know, I can give them from my game and my knowledge, anything I can help them with, that's what I'm about. >> a big speech guy? You're more of one-on-one? Like, how does that go for you normally? >> Honestly, it can it can go either way. You know what I mean? But, you know, I'd rather speak to you one-on-one to to really, you know, let [clears throat] you know how I feel or, you know, we can really get, you know, deep as far as, you know, life talks and and and things in that nature. But, for the most part, I'm open. >> You mentioned in your press conference that you fit Brian Flores' scheme and he fits what you like to do. What's an example of something specifically that you are most excited to start doing within the Vikings defense? >> Well, really just being unique in different ways. Just using me in different positions to, you know, use my talents and and whatnot. So, for me, that's what I'm really just focused on. I'm just focused on, you know, learning the playbook, continuing to learn my teammates, and be a great teammate as well. >> When it comes to that terminology that you're trying to to learn at this point, what are some of the tricks you use to help help you unlearn and relearn, right? >> Yeah, it's kind of some things that I do at home by myself as far as just, you know, a whiteboard and going over different things, different plays, you know, calling it out like I'm a quarterback almost and giving the play call. So, just going over my plays day in day out and obviously coming out here repping it. I'm going to make mistakes right now. I expect that, but for the most part just picking it up and learning from the guys you know before me. >> So, don't stay next to you in the hotel room during training camp cuz you're going to be yelling and keeping us up all night. [laughter] >> I won't be too loud. I won't be too loud, but I'm definitely going to be in there, you know, you'll you'll hear me a little bit. >> What went into the original decision to be more of that or I guess not even be more, play more into your versatility that X-factor after you made that switch to linebacker last season? >> Well, you know, obviously it was just finding the right group that really just trusted in me, you know, just having that belief that I can, you know, play different positions out here and you know, help the team in any shape or form. You know, it's really just opportunity, you know what I'm saying? For me, for these guys to believe in me, I think it's you know, it means a lot to me, you know, just to come out here and let me be, you know, unique, let me be special out here to to be interchangeable and and run different schemes and do different things. So, I'm excited. >> Have you noticed that in your first couple of days at camp because I know obviously that attracted you here? >> Right, right. Yeah, I mean they're letting me know, you know, it's it's it's definitely going to be some fun things we're going to do, you know, but you know, for me it's just keeping my head down working, learning the playbook and you know, making the making the roster. >> You mentioned your history with Blake Cashman. Obviously you're now teamed up together, but is there someone else on the defense that you've you've watched previously that you're just really excited to team up with? >> So many guys, man, but obviously you got to go with J Jets, you know, obviously you know, from afar I played with his brother, you know, back Ricky Jefferson I played with his brother. So, we were back there at the safety tandem my last year, you know, with LSU and obviously just seeing him come in and you know, come to the camp and he's doing one-on-ones and Ricky's like, man, y'all got to watch my brother. My brother's next up and I was like, who's J Jets? Like, Who's Jets?" And man, you know, obviously we see what's going on. He's a superstar. So, you know, excited to team up with him, but he's excited to team up with the rest of the guys. There's so much There's so much talent on this team. Uh but not only that, they're they're great guys. >> You mentioned in your press conference, and I kind of got the sense that you feel better than you have in quite some time. It's been a long road to recovery. What has really helped you build that confidence back up? >> Yeah. I think it's just It's really just been time for me. You know, uh I really went through, you know, a hard time, you know, that a lot of people don't really know about, you know, behind closed doors and, you know, just mentally just trying to get through, you know, what I was going through. And, you know, when you've been playing football for so long um at a high level, [snorts] making Pro Bowls and All-Pros, and then, you know, you unfortunately get hurt, you got to kind of start all over. So, I call myself I call my like journey the rebuild, you know, so uh just just rebuilding from ground up, mentally and physically. And obviously it took some time. It took about 3 years, should you say? And um I'm just excited to where I am now. >> How has it made you a better player from the guy that walked into training camp as a rookie? >> Oh, man. Uh honestly, just the transition from, you know, going through adversity, you know, fighting through that, um and finding out who you are as a person, you know? When your back is against the wall, you really find out who you are. And uh for me, you know, just I wanted to fight back and and prove to myself that I can get back out there and be who I am and I've always been. And uh you know, I'm fortunate enough God blessed me to get another opportunity. The Vikings gave me another opportunity. So, I'm just very uh you know, I'm thankful. I'm really thankful. >> I can see why your guy, Nolan Teasley, wanted to add you to [laughter] this group. And obviously he's he's a little new to our fans. They don't know him super well. We've We've heard a couple of press conferences. What can you tell us something about Nolan and your time with him that you think Vikings fans should be excited about? >> Yeah, I mean, I think that he you know, he's he's behind the scenes. He's real quiet at at times, and he'll walk around and, you know, keep his head down. But, you know, if you talk to him one-on-one, he he really does care about his players. He cares about winning. He cares about his organization and he's going to do the best thing for the for the organization at all times. So, when you got a guy like that that not only cares about the organization but cares about the players, cares about how they feel and you know, is a family guy, meets your family, like you know, vice versa. You know, you can't you can't ask for a better GM, you know? So, he's going to be he's going to be a great guy for this organization for sure. >> Great. All right. Well, I wanted to to remind you that you still are the record holder for most sacks in a season by a DB. 9 and 1/2 set in 2020. I hear Brian Flores likes to blitz sometimes. [laughter] What do you think it's going to be like to be out there and he just lets you loose on that first play back in purple and gold in front of that crowd? >> to be exciting, you know? I'm excited to get out there and and compete with these guys. I'm excited to get out there and just fly around. There's nothing like this game of football, you know? It's a beautiful game. You go through ups and downs and you know, I think that, you know, it teaches you life, you know? So, just to get out there and have an opportunity, I can't wait. I'm definitely grateful for it. >> You've been in US Bank Stadium before? >> I have. I played there. I played there one time. It's definitely loud. >> Okay. Well, now you're going to be on the other side of it. So, that'll be exciting. Thank you so much, Small. Have a great camp. >> you. Thank you.

title: Minnesota Vikings Team Press Conferences | Training Camp, July 30
text: Uh, basically just the all around game, you know, just understanding the defense, you know, what we emphasize in OTAs, just carrying that into the camp. >> How excited are you for this bigger opportunity? >> Uh, definitely excited, you know, uh, more importantly have to be prepared for it though, but you know, definitely having a lot of positive thoughts for it. >> How would you describe kind of this this front of the defensive front that you guys have? A little bit of new guys, but a lot of the guys coming back. >> I feel like already, you know, we real close with each other, you know, there's a lot of camaraderie, a lot of competition, friendly competition and stuff like that. You know, we laugh, joke, but we also know how to get serious and get to work. So, you know, I feel like every single day the energy is to get better than we were yesterday, you know, knowing that we young, trusting in the coaches and stuff like that, and everything that they tell us what to implement on the field and stuff like that. So, you know, we just going out here and going hard. >> You've had a couple training camps now. Does this just feel like back to normal, or is it still new in a way? >> I would say, you know, every training camp is going to feel somewhat new, but you know, coming into year three, I kind of, you know, get a little feel for it, know what to expect a little bit, but you know, definitely excited, you know, to get rolling with some of the younger guys in the room, so. >> Day one was in the books, starting day two, and just a privilege to be out here back on the grass. All the guys are excited. You can tell even in walk-throughs the pace is a little bit faster cuz we're just excited to be able to go faster, you know, during OTAs it's a little they have to keep your route down, so everybody's engines are firing. >> How do you feel? How was your off-season? >> I feel great. Off-season was amazing. Got got to put in a lot of good work. Had some had my young backs with me. So, it made it that much easier to continue to train, you know, when you have some guys doing it with you. You're looking up to them, they're looking up to you, and you know, you can't you can't fail each other. So, it was a lot of fun, and then just getting to know each other even more on a deeper level. >> How excited are you for fans to be out here finally on Saturday? >> Oh, I'm super excited. The fans give us that that added energy, that push throughout camp, you know, when days get hard or monotonous, we come out here and we see them and we feel their energy, and they lift us up. So, we're excited to see you guys. See you guys Saturday. >> I know it's early, but how's the running backs room you to you? >> Uh, they're looking really good. You know, we got we got guys who can do it all. They can catch out of the backfield, can run, can block. So, I feel like when you got guys who can do it all, it makes it that much easier. And now it's just coming together. How we How do we come together and how do we uh put it together on on Sundays or when we step on the onto the field. >> The whole gang, yeah. >> Yeah, give me two. Come on. Come on. Jerry, give me this. Give me this. >> I'm his like assistant, but you >> Translator? >> All right, there you go. >> Uh, how would you >> Please go right there. >> How would you describe first day first couple days of camp? >> It's been fun. Um, I've been enjoying it. Everything's been going fast, but you know, just taking one day at a time and and just getting ready to ramp it up and get ready to go for the season. >> How fast has it been going? It's a lot of information. >> I don't know, very fast. Very fast. But, I mean ain't ain't nothing to a giant a menace like me, so yeah. >> A menace like you, I like it. What's How are you feeling as far as health-wise? How's your body feel? >> I feel great. >> 100%? >> [laughter] >> Yes, 100%. >> kind of what you want to work on as far as just learning everything in these these first couple weeks? >> Um, really just getting back in my groove of playing football. It's been a minute since I actually like been on the field and really like, you know being myself, being Caleb Banks, playing football, honestly. Um, so really just getting back in the motion, honestly. >> Is this like the longest that you've kind of been away from football? >> Absolutely. >> Like in your life? >> Yeah. And I think it's been about like what, 6 months to a year, you know? So, yeah. >> How weird is that? >> It's very strange, but I mean like I said ain't nothing I can't conquer. Can Can handle it. Can get it done. Just got to go out there and get reps. The more reps you get, the better you get at it, so it's going to come back. >> I'm just coming out here being and you know, obviously out here learning the learning the playbook and learning my teammates and you know, hopefully make the team. >> And hopefully make the team. I think you have a good shot. Is there one prevalent reason why you chose here? >> Um, you know, obviously it's an opportunity of a lifetime, you know? When I got the call from Nolan to you know, come out here and try out, Um it was a no-brainer for me, you know, uh just to come, you know, be a part of this this phenomenal organization. Um they have great people here. Uh obviously the the building is the best in the world. I mean, I've been around, you know what I mean? And this is this is top notch. Uh but, you know, obviously, you know, Bevell. You know, Bevell is one of those guys that I've had a far respect for uh for a long, long time. And you know, there's always that DC that you always want to play for. And uh you know, he's going to use me in unique ways, going to use everybody in unique ways. And just excited to be here. >> Yeah, I was going to ask you about it. He prides himself in finding the versatile guys, the athletes that can play the football players, right? Is that how you see yourself? And what do you think it's going to look like? >> Yeah, absolutely, man. Um I know yesterday I kind of said a lot of different positions and walking the dog and whatnot. But at the end of the day, I'm really just a football player, you know? So, uh you can line me up anywhere. Um you can teach me anything to where I I can I can help guys on the field or whatever the case may be. But for me, it's just being versatile. You know, uh just use me in different ways to to make plays. >> Get to the quarterback, too. >> That's it. That's it. Get that ball. >> We're trying to get to know Nolan Tice. Yeah, yeah, yeah. You know him better than us. What can you tell us about him? >> Man, he's quiet. Man, I just got to ask that. You know, he's quiet. He's he's real, you know, observant and and and he's going to watch people. But man, you get a one-on-one conversation with him, he's a great guy. Um he's a family guy. You know, he cares for his players, you know? And uh for him to, you know, get this GM job, it was well deserved. Um he he's definitely worked his self for a long, long time. I've seen it. Uh he's put the time in under a great, you know, GM in Seattle, John Schneider. And he's learned from the best. So, um there's no better man for the job. I really believe that. >> It's been great so far. Um you know, new spot, uh new people. Um everything's been great. Team's been great. Coaches have been great. Um so so far, first couple of days, um happy about it. >> I guess going off minicamp and and into here, do you feel like you've accomplished a lot in that time? >> Yeah. Yeah. Um you know, when I first got here minicamp, um I was new. Whole new system, whole new scheme. So, um I I the summer to kind of get down. Really take a deep dive into the schematics and what we're doing. So with that little bit of time I was able to really get it down and out here I can play a little bit faster now. >> You've been around for a while but do you still feel like like you have something to prove? New team, new chapter. >> Yeah, I mean this is my first new team. So this is a new experience for me but it's good being around this new group of guys. They're fiery, they're fun. So so being around these new people feel like I want to go out there and you know, kind of prove how I can play, who I am.

title: Minnesota Vikings Training Camp Day 1 Recap!
text: Vikings training camp is officially underway. Let's overanalyze, baby. Woo! You are Locked On Vikings, your daily Minnesota Vikings podcast, part of the Locked On Network, your team every day. >> What's going on everybody? Welcome to the Locked On Vikings podcast, where we're always trying to learn something new. Yesterday was the first day of training camp, baby. We're here. We made it. They're playing football again. We have things to overanalyze. We got quarterback stats. I'm not even going to share them with you. It doesn't matter. Uh we got differing accounts on the actual dropback counts. Some people charted it, different reporters charted it differently. We are in it immediately, baby. So, here's what we're going to do today. I promise the mailbag that you guys ask questions for will be answered eventually, but I feel like a bunch of those questions are irrelevant now. Anyways, uh we'll get to it. I promise this this will dry up. Maybe it'll just be next Tuesday, but uh we'll go over stuff with the QB battle. There's injury news, absences, uh there was an injury at camp, maybe not that big of a deal. We'll go over that as well. Standouts and anything else you might be asking about based on camp notebooks. I haven't been able to get out there uh for a little while, but a lot of reporters are. They all have big writeups. And so what we can do is read through all of them and whatever the common threads are, uh, we can kind of take that and and get a decent amount of information. So, thank you to all the reporters that did this. I got Vikings.com, I got Bring Me the News, I got ESPN, I got Star Tribune, uh, we got all that, right? Yahoo, everybody who was there. So, of course, we will be starting with the quarterback battle. Uh the reps were relatively even. It seems like uh Kyler Murray and started out with the ones and then the second half of practice J.J. McCarthy was with the ones. So there's your even split. Uh Kevin Oonnell said it wouldn't necessarily be 50/50. It sounds like the JJ McCarthy part was like a few snaps shorter. It was at the end of practice, might have just got cut off, but it was by like four snaps. Like who cares? Uh so that was relatively even. And then in terms of the performances of those guys, here's what I'll say. I probably go to if you're going to go to camp, you make your own judgment on it because the the beat reporter type judgments are not like without my own two eyes. I'm I'm only going to trust that. Not to throw any shade at those guys.
