Why? Why'd you do this? You should do that. And like he's he's got a he's got a well-rounded mind, I I think. And it's perfect for being a head coach in the NFL because it's not just about the X's and O's. Yeah, it's about when the buses are coming, when should the plane leave, what hotels we're staying at. Not saying he makes all those decisions, but he's got a hand in it and he's got an opinion on it. >> Yeah, I think that that's one thing, Fred, that >> surprises people that are on the outside looking in about NFL head coaching is how much nonOT there really is that goes into that job. even press conferences and dealing with the media, you know, but all the logistical things that you talked about, like there's so much of that that like sometimes the football is the easy part. Like once they actually get to go, you know, talk and get back into football, but I think what surprised me the most about him is I thought I knew he would be able to like be a rahrh guy and I I knew he would be able to rally the troops and give great speeches and, you know, lead the room and conduct the room. Uh, but his football chops and his football acumen is, you know, I think it's better than a guy like like Dan Campbell. Like I think Dan Campbell is what I'm describing and I think that they have such a perfect setup with him and Josh McDaniels that McDaniels >> probably isn't going anywhere anytime soon and so they don't have to worry about the play caller and the OC and that sort of thing. Uh, so you can hire a coach that has that CEO ability and not worry about the offense. It's kind of it's kind of fun too in the press conferences he doesn't give you much but he gives you a little more than you got from Bill or you know or Gerro Mayo even um you know those kind of things it shows especially you know Taylor questions or those kind of things where you know he gives you enough to know that he knows a little bit about everything >> and and and whether or not it's true at least he he tries to show that he respects the people's jobs that are asking the questions right >> you know and like whether or not he likes them or not that's not the qu that's not what I'm talking about. I think he understands their job and he respects that and he may not always like what they're asking or whatever, but >> that comes through that he he respects the people on the other side. Well, so you knew players of course, you know, respect Bill Bichc's football knowledge, but you know, it's one thing to have the football knowledge, but when you stand up there, and I know Varel probably does this and say, you know, I played in the Super Bowls, I had touchdown catches, I had s, you know, he has been there and done everything there is to do, you know, in the NFL on an NFL football field. And, you know, to capture the players, you know, respect, it just seems like such a a natural progression for him. Um, it's it's it's been really good. I'm excited to see what year two of this program looks like because you hear a lot of the same points. You know, he's kind of hitting on the same points and that to me, you know, establishes he knows exactly what he wants the message to be, you know, in training camp. Earn a role, build a team. Um, you know, all those boxes that they're trying to check and it's it's it's coming together well. The proof was in the pudding last year. >> There's the running back tandem for the New England Patriots, Stevenson and Henderson. >> They're they're just there was a list yesterday. Ted Win pulled a bunch of defensive coaches, defensive coordinators, head coaches on the best offensive architects, play callers in the league and Josh McDaniels was eighth, but he was the top OC, not head coach play caller. So my guy Kyle Shanahan, Shawn McVey, Matt Laflur, guys like that. Ben Johnson, Josh was was eighth. And I just think the tandem together of him and Rael is just it's one of the best coaching like batteries that you could have in the NFL cuz you you have an OC that is really the head coach of the offense and you have some stability there year to year that he's going to keep coming back and then you let Rabel kind of do Rabel things. You know, I would I wanted Ben Johnson a little bit because I wanted a guy to be with Drake May for the next 10 years as his OC and his play caller, but they kind of got there in a roundabout way and now it really makes a lot of sense. So, you know, I thought it was telling that that Josh McDaniels was the top OC on that list, you know. >> All right. Well, we're coming to the end of the show. Um we're coming to the end of where we can film practice. So, I want to thank everyone for watching today, hanging with us. Um just some ad administrative stuff. Uh the next time we are talking to you will be Tuesday uh 1:00 uh on a regular well training camp regularly scheduled uh Patriots unfiltered and then on Thursday we'll be live again, right? Was that the joint practice when >> No, no, that's not until next Tuesday. So yeah, we'll be a week from Tuesday will be the joint practice against the Colts. >> A week from this t next Tuesday. Okay. >> Yeah, we're still a little ways. All right. >> Still a little ways away. >> Both shows uh both shows next week are 1 to three. >> Okay. next week 1 to three. >> Yeah. And and we'll have the campcast after each one of these. So, be sure uh you know, the good stuff's just about to get started. So, we're sorry to leave you now, but we'll be right back, you know, shortly after practice with a full recap of all the good stuff we're about to see. >> All right. So, for everyone on the c on the crew and behind the scenes, thank you for watching. We'll talk to you on Tuesday. >> Hey, this is Deuce. Thanks for tuning in to the show. If you really want to help us, make sure you like us wherever you get your podcasts like Apple Podcast or Spotify. Also, make sure you [music] follow us on the New England Patriots YouTube channel to see this show and everything else that we do here at The Patriots. Thanks a lot. [music]

title: Kayshon Boutte, Caleb Lomu, Eli Raridon & More Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: It's your first day. On the pads. What was it like for you guys? Red zone work and everything >> It wasn't bad. Focusing on the run game a little bit, but um give us receivers opportunity to go crack blocks. So, we will in the block. Um the line, the running back block while we doing pass plays, too. So, it's always good to help those guys out. >> Made some nice catches early on in the game. What's your attitude coming into this game? >> Um I think my attitude, you know, we all hear a lot of the stuff that's going on. I think my main focus was just I'm here to ain't. So, me, I'm here today. My my feet here today. If I'm somewhere else next week, the week after, I mean that's kind of that's kind of what it is, you know? It's part of the business, but I mean taking every day day by day and not thinking about what's next. >> Do you think you're on the trade block? >> I don't know. It might be a fair question or anybody question. >> Have you had conversations with Mike? >> Uh I mean no. We talk football, you know? Um it's not really that's not really his his type of thing, you know? Um we talk every day football, whether it's meetings outside of meetings, uh things we could correct from practice, things we need to work on. It's always improvement. >> Is it difficult to keep that kind of stuff out of your mind when when you're on the field like >> No, I've been playing football since I was seven. I mean it's the same I've been doing. So, yeah. >> Do you want to be here this year? >> Yeah. >> This year? >> KeShawn, a lot of guys might have a different attitude towards this, you know, the number of opportunities that you may or may not get with the lineup of receivers like this, but you are keeping that sort of open-mindedness to it. Is it just treating this like a competition? >> Uh I think think uh me and Kyle was talking yesterday and I was just like don't worry about what the next guy doing, you know? Everybody going to make plays, but don't let that affect your opportunities. Like at the end of the day you're going to get your opportunities. Uh one practice it might be one catch, next practice it might be four. It vary, you know? You never know where the ball going to go. But like I told him, make the most of your opportunities. Y'all seen today he caught two two touchdowns, so. >> Has um have they spent more time trying to get you going or or at least give you intimate knowledge of different spots, X, Y, Z? Because it seems like your skill set can can fit in a lot of different spots. >> I did I did it last year. I'm doing it this year, too. Um, this practice played all three positions uh since I've been back. So, I mean, uh Josh talked in the meeting, too. The more positions you can play, the better off you'll be. So, it's only going to help you. >> Is there one that you prefer? >> No, I mean, I could I could do it all. Yeah. >> So, we've seen you take your game to the next level ever since last year version of the deep threat. Is there a specific part of your game this year that you're really trying to hone in on and take that step up? >> Uh I would say not not specifically. Uh you can always improve in any aspect of your game, but like you said, uh the goal is to get better every year. I think the worst place you want to be the same position as last year, you know? You kind of want to show that you've been working this past off-season, you know? Like Kyle said, pick up where you left off. >> What does that affect your confidence that you have a rapport with Frank? >> Um I'd say it don't affect no confidence. You know, confidence come from making plays. You know, you make plays, you're just going to keep on making them. >> But, it seems like he relies on you. >> Uh We're relying on each other at the end of the day, you know? Um it's not just me. It's other guys out there, too. But, like I said, uh we help him get going, and he help us get going, so. >> that this is a contract year for you, does that provide any extra motivation? >> Yeah. Uh I mean, truth be told, you know, I think if you was in a contract year or your reporting job, you know, you you kind of want that to be your best year. So, um whatever that look like for me, we'll look at all the options and see see what the best position is. >> Your teammates have called you unbelievable in the film room. How do you block out the chatter with it being a contract year? >> Uh it's a lot it's a lot of chatter, um whether it's online, in person, but think when we step in the building, try not to let those distractions uh or let the noise distract you. I come on the field, I don't think about it. Whole time I'm at work, I don't think about it. Like I said, I'm just where my feet at, so. >> Does it feel like there's more competition inside the wide receiver room compared to last year? >> Oh, it's competition every year, you know? Um we got two great guys that came in this off season. Uh we had some guys here already, but uh like I said, it's competition every year. So, just try not to get lost in the sauce of who all around and make the most of your opportunities. >> those additions and considering those additions that happened this off season, how do you focus on keeping your game consistent here? >> I'll just keep doing the same stuff I've been doing. Like I said, I think the word for me this off season, uh now that we're back this training camp is opportunity. Uh make the most of your opportunities, so. >> You asked like David Allen just to compare your role or anything like that? >> No, I mean um I mean it's not my job to tell y'all my role. We'll kind of see it as it play out, so. >> Hey Shawn, do you feel like this is a prove it year for you and are you okay staying here and you know, doing what you do? >> Yeah, um regardless of where I'm at, I still got to prove it, you know? You hear the talk online, everything like that. Every year I've been proving it, so. Man, I feel like everybody say a lot of stuff and then it backfire in the end, so it's kind of the story of my life, so. Yeah. >> Appreciate it. >> When the pads what was it like for you? >> No, it was amazing. Uh a little bit intimidating coming coming out here at first, but uh being able to play with all these guys, all these professionals, it's you know, an amazing opportunity. Uh but again, when the pads just come on, you get that first hit, it's football all all over again from when I was, you know, eight eight-year-old playing uh little league football. It just turns into football, you know, the game that I love, so it's awesome to be back out here. >> What gets you through the intimidation part of the beginning? Is it just hitting somebody? >> Just hitting someone, you know? That's That's all you can do really, knowing uh what to do then just going out there and being physical while doing it. So, just going out there um putting the pads on someone and then just playing football. >> How much more confident are you feeling now, you know, as opposed to, you know, this past spring? >> Yeah, very confident, you know, that's what you got to have coming out here. Everyone out here is a professional. You can't come in here with any hesitation or or doubt in yourself. Got to have that confidence that, you know, you belong on this field. So, that's That's what I think. I know I belong on this field, so I come out here with that confidence and just, you know, play the game. >> Have you had many conversations with Will as someone who was a rookie last year kind of in the similar position just in terms of his draft position as >> Yeah, 100% I talked to Will every single day, you know, about football and then just life in general, you know, the process that he went through last year as well. Uh he's been a huge help to me and that's been super comforting to have, you know, coming in here. Same with everyone on the offensive line, you know, been super welcoming to me, especially Will um and Morgan as soon as I came in, you know, two of the tackles coming in helping me with anything that I need, you know, any questions that I have and then just out here on the field, you know, technique and everything. So, Will's been such a huge um help for me coming in here. >> Gabe, when you're at right tackle, what's your technique and footwork? Do you still feel a little awkward when you're doing things kind of the >> Yeah, so in college I played left and then, you know, coming up here I've been switching around a lot of positions, but, you know, it's just the same thing. You just got to flip the hands and the feet and then that's that's really it. Um I feel super comfortable at right right now. Just I know I got to get down the footwork and the the hand techniques, but then it's just football at the end of the day. >> I guess building off of building off of that, does it take anything different to be a jumbo tight end than the sixth offensive lineman or is it sort of just the same position? >> It's really the same thing. You're just called a, you know, jumbo tight end, but you're still an offensive lineman going out there to block, um pass protect, do whatever. So, you're going out there have the same job as anyone. Got to protect the ball carrier and so you go out there be a physical player, just protect. >> How are your hands How are your hands in route running? >> Uh they're they're ready for whenever uh that's later down the road, but they're they're always ready. >> First thing >> Go ahead. >> I'll take you back to the one of your reps in the one-on-one pass block drills. What's your mentality on finishing and >> that first rep and sort of how you did that. >> For sure, you know, finishing is the biggest key as an offensive lineman. You got to be able to know it to do and then do it with the violent demeanor and be able to finish finish longer than the guy with the ball um is what we say. So, as an an lineman you're going to have those plays where quarterback starts to scramble or the running back switches ways and goes all the way along the field. So, you got to be able to strain as long as you can, strain longer than the guy you're going against, and then being able to finish. You know, that's the biggest thing being an offensive lineman, you know, finishing the guy in the dirt, um being able to just finish longer than he's going to play. That's the biggest thing making sure your guy doesn't get to the ball carrier. And so, that's my mentality going into every single rep, every every play that we have is just to finish longer than the guy. >> Did you notice a difference first day in pads in the NFL compared to hitting guys in college? >> Yeah, everything things just a, you know, a lot faster. Uh the guys here are a lot faster, bigger, and stronger, but still football at the end of the day, you know, you got your assignment to do. You got to be able to come out here on the field and execute that assignment. People just here are at a whole 'nother level skill-wise, and so it's a little bit more difficult, but still football. >> How did you feel you did? >> I feel pretty good. You know, there's I'm never going to have a perfect practice or game, uh perfect anything. You know, football I'm coming out here to the get to close as I can to perfect, but I never will be perfect, and so, you know, going back and watching the film to see what I did wrong, see what I can improve on, and then coming out, you know, tomorrow and fixing that. >> If there was a piece of advice that stood out to you the most heading into your first day of pads here in the NFL, what would that be? >> Just being a violent player. An offensive lineman, you know, pads, no pads, offensive, defensive line, you have the same job. You're going against another guy every single play. You're hitting someone every single play. Now, with the pads, you can just be a little bit more violent, and so, you know, that's the mentality going into it. That's what you got to have in your mind every single play. You know, I can't take any play plays off. No rep is a a coffee break, and so, just going out there every single every rep, every practice, and being violent, being a physical player. >> What's it like to soak up the knowledge and wisdom and everything that comes with Morgan Moses? >> Yeah, he's been a huge help to me. I mean, I'm sure you guys see it every single day, every rep that I have, every, you know, period that we do, I'm going to him right after. He's helping me through it. Uh he's a vet in this in this league. He's been with many teams and has so much experience, and so, being able to gain that experience that he has and then learn from him, you know, that's been the biggest help and I know this is going to only help me grow even more. And so, having him is a major help. >> Let's take two more. Caleb, how's How's training camp going? Do you have a roommate and you guys doing rookie skits? Like how was How was it like in >> It's been fun, you know, it's it's long days uh getting in that playbook, physical practice, and meetings. But, you know, it's fun, you know, we're here we're here all day. I don't have a roommate. Um just in the in a hotel by myself, but not there for too long anyways. I'm here most of the day. But, it's been fun, you know, learning the learning the playbook, being with the guys all day, coming out and and competing. It's It's long days, but it's, you know, what we signed up for. >> What's it like for you switching around in a bunch of spots? And do you feel like that's eventually going to make you a better tackle? >> Yeah, 100%. The, you know, biggest thing is coming out on the field, being able to know more than one position is a huge thing. If you want a role in the team, you know, learning more positions is the biggest key to that. And so, when I came out here switching around positions, was more than happy to do it, play any position. Just love playing football. And so, wherever I can be to be on the field is where I want to be. >> Awesome. >> Not yet. Thank you guys. Appreciate it. >> How are you guys doing? >> Good. How are you? >> Good. >> How's your How's your How's your first NFL training camp going? >> It's going well. Um you know, I've got a lot of great people in the tight end room to learn from. Um got a lot of good uh like Hunter Henry, he's been great to me. Um just learning every day, trying to apply it on the field, and um just playing as hard as I can. So. >> It seems like the last two days you've popped a little bit with with some catches. Just are are things starting to click for you or slow down? >> Yeah, for sure. Yeah, I think being here in the spring and uh learning uh the offense then really has helped me um kind of apply it on the field and start playing faster. So. >> What Coach Vrabel was saying that he wants you guys to play fast and not worry that much about mistakes at this point. How helpful is that? >> It's really helpful. I think it's a great mentality to have. And uh to win in this league you're going to have to play uh you're going to have to play fast. And, you know, as a young player it's hard to um you know, not be thinking about a lot of stuff out there. And um I think it's great. I think we can uh play fast. You know, obviously play smart but not worry too much about making a mistake and as the offense starts to come together, it's going to get easier. So What's up? Nothing nothing's really surprised me. I kind of came in here expecting it to be really really hard and you know, obviously training camp is meant to be difficult and make you uncomfortable and it's been that so far. So Yeah, I think as a tight end room we all need to step up. Um we all need to um you know, play it play our hardest and fill in that role that's that's missing and you know, I'm praying for Julian and hoping he has a fast recovery. Yeah, I think you know, things are starting to slow down for me. Obviously, you know, I'm not 100% acclimated with the offense but compared to the spring it's a night and day difference. So it's going well. Yeah, I know we we were all signals in in college so that's been an adjustment and a lot of different terminology. So it was a lot to learn initially and there's still a lot more to learn but it's starting to slow down. So Yeah, he's he's showed me some old clips of some routes we ran and may not necessarily be a tight end sometimes it's you know, receiver like Julian Edelman or sometimes we you know, Gronk's up there too but it's Uh, really cool to see those guys under the same offensive system and um it's it's been helpful to watch film from um back when when they were playing, so. >> Do you see a lot of opportunity to play right away considering, you know, it's Hunter and a lot of unproven behind him? >> Yeah, I'm kind of just taking it one day at a time and um I'm just going to put my head down, be the best player I can be, play my hardest, and you know, if that gets me to play, then great. And if not, then um then it's yeah. >> Saw you on the one-on-one. Did you feel like you got two feet down in the end zone there? >> I don't know. It's It's close call. I was I was uh excited to go back and watch that, but um it was close. >> You know, like the other day I saw you run over to the crowd with Tanner and hype them up. Yeah. How did that come to be? >> Yeah, um kind of, you know, what you got to do as a rookie and sometimes those bets tell you something you got to do it and it's kind of one of those things, so. >> You comfortable in that role? >> You know, I just kind of embrace it. You know, it's not really that's not really who I am, but uh in this process, that's what I'm going to do, so. >> How's Hunter helping you out? >> Yeah, he's uh he's been great great to me and um such a good guy to have in the room. I'm I'm very lucky to have a vet like him who is so uh smart and knowledgeable with this offense and um also just his character, he um you know, he's he's very welcoming and um you know, he's he's willing to teach me, which, you know, not a lot of you know, teams have, so it's been great. >> What position are you studying? >> Oh, um you know, right now I'm just kind of focusing on offense. Um you know, just learning the system and watching um old players play and watching Hunter play, so it's all I focus on. >> What's it been like working with Drake behind the scenes? >> Yeah, it's been awesome. Um Drake's been super nice to me and um you know, we've been working on some things after practice and in the route game and um you know, he's been great as well. Great guy. >> All right, thanks. >> How are you guys? >> Uh how much do you enjoy getting out here with pads for the first time? >> Uh man, it feels great. Uh Off-season was good, but it definitely feels back to be at it, working back at it, and getting back to the main goal. >> What was the job for the offensive line for you guys [clears throat] as the line today to get the work in? >> Um the first was really just let the pads do the talking. Um it's been a while. Obviously, there's been a lot of pass rushes and pass reps these last couple of days in OTAs, so definitely just getting back to real football, putting the pads on, and running the ball. >> Mike, there's been a lot of talk about tempo >> Uh-huh. >> trying to go faster >> faster >> on offense. Have you noticed that, and how can that help you guys offensively? >> Yeah, I definitely I definitely thinks it helps us keeps us on the ball, keeps us on pace, keeps the defense on the field, and yeah, we've been doing more and more of that. I mean, ever since last year as well, but it's important to work it out, so when we get in those situations, we already accustomed to it. >> Mike, >> You said about ABT? >> ABT's been good. You know, definitely a great athlete. I'm happy that we got him. Um I know this line is going to be way better with him or, you know, obviously with a better player. But, um Jerry back to his natural position. Will back at left. Uh Mo still at right as well, so you know, everyone just getting back out here, getting comfortable. >> Mike, you're not only a veteran of this team, but a veteran of the league. How have you used your experience to help kind of the young guys like Lumo Lomo like develop? >> Yeah. I mean, Will has already had had that mindset on him. Um Obviously, Mo and all the tackles I've kept kept on him since Caleb has been here. You know, Caleb has been good. He's been like a sponge. I mean, taking it up whatever position he's playing, whether it's getting reps at guard or getting reps at either tackle. Um I think he's done a good job of that. I think just as the days go on and as the practices and as these, you know, camp days and we get into joint practices, you know, we'll see that real football and the real competition and the day-to-day work where it's, you know, go to practice one day, and then you're going against the same guy the next day, and you know, it's kind of like a game where as you're game prepping, you're seeing and guys, you know, you kind of know what they're going to do. They know They know what you're going to do and just preparing for that. >> Mike, you reworked your contract >> after these conversations. Like, did they come and approach you? Did you approach them? What >> Yeah, I mean, they approached me. It was just kind of like business. I mean, obviously the contract is the contract, but, you know, I just excited to get back to ball and get back with my boys that we just went to the Super Bowl. Get back there. >> How special was last year considering you've been here for some some rough years? When you look back at >> Just how special was >> Yeah, last year was special. I mean, you know, every day felt surreal. I was more so just happy for the guys around me. Obviously, it's a lot of younger guys and you know, handful of guys who've been around for more than a couple of years, but, you know, I really was happy for my teammates and everybody getting uh to be in that moment and go through >> Last season with this year, what do you think the line should do? I think with each year or even with with each game, you know, every rep, you know, the line improves. The more we play together. Jared is back to his natural position at center, so I'm excited to see him work out there. ABT at left. I'm excited about that. You know, I just think the more reps we get, the more physical days we get, you know, it'll just improve and help us get ready for the season. >> Mike, what's spoke to us about working out in the off season? >> Mhm. >> What kind of improvements have you seen in his game? Does it seem like that he was around those guys and there's a difference in his >> Yeah, I mean, I'm not really watching him directly, but, you know, he's seeming more stronger in his in his base and his set. Hands are much stronger. He's going at guys, you know, not really setting back and waiting for guys to come to him. He's taking a fight to them, so I think that's something important, you know, seeing as rookies and you know, going through it next year, knowing the pace of the game and playing through the games and kind of knowing how people are going to rush you and people are going to run and attack you. >> Mike, you've been in this offense Yeah, it's been fun, definitely. Being in one position, for sure. Really just playing next to the guys that I'm playing with, you know, Jared. I'll say I'm missing my guy Garrett, but you know, Jared is back in there. And Mo's me and Mo's back on the same side, so run game we going crazy, pass game we working on that and getting to it. >> Like you've been in this offense as long as anyone. Uh-huh. Yeah, I mean he's a great player. AJ has, you know, definitely a superstar. So I mean like anytime the ball is going to him, you know, it's a it's a big play target or it's a big play. It can be a big play. But you know, just with the run plays, with the pass plays, whether it's receivers blocking, you know, seeing him buy into that, seeing him communicate with Drake, whether it's on motions, shifts, or alerts, or you know, giving him a different signal call, seeing the defense, seeing if the safety's rotating and you know, he got a slant or something like that. You know, seeing that working, just seeing that relationship blossom is great to see. >> Let's take two more. >> What does it say to you when you see a guy like Taylor [clears throat] go to see some better tackles in the off season and try to learn and and get better at his craft? >> Yeah, I think it's great, you know. I'll say as an athlete, you know, you want to get better, you want to be like the guys that, you know, you want to imitate. So definitely picking those guys' brain and even working with them in the off season or throughout the season, talk to them, seeing how how they see different looks, see see different defenses or, you know, whether you go against the same guys, same teams and stuff like that. Just getting that uh workshop or just getting an assessment on the player and seeing what type of player they are as the defense, I'm saying. >> What's what's Morgan's value, I guess, as a veteran? Morgan's value is very immense, you know, he's definitely a great player, great leader. Um you know, he's always been vocal, good with the younger guys, but also with the older guys. You know, it's only a handful of us, but you know, we just got to work every day. You know, we really not taking nothing for granted. Obviously he's older than me, but you know, I see him and I see his work ethic. You know, it makes me want to go harder, makes me want to do more and just really just be the best I can be. So, I mean, that that all trickles down throughout the whole room and everyone sees it. You know, he's a great example for us and uh we follow his lead. Yep. Yes, sir. >> First day First day pads out there, how do you think you guys fared? >> I thought we did pretty good. Obviously, the offense made some plays, but you know, we did good as a defense. Just got to keep getting better. >> How's it feel to get out there and get a hit? And then hit somebody, get hit after >> It feels good. You know, OTAs is a a pass-heavy camp, so you know, being able to put the pads on and it really feeling like football season feels good. >> How do you feel like the off season's going with you? You're receiving more >> Um it's going great. You know, I feel like I've taken advantage of every opportunity I've gotten. You know, I'm blessed to be in this position. And you know, just help the team win as much as I can. So. >> Christian had a couple of really nice things to say about you. >> What's it like getting more reps with that group of guys? I know you came on towards the end of the year last year, but getting in the camp with these guys, getting regular rotation, getting in with the regulars, you know, what's it been like with them? >> It feels good. You know, earning the confidence of my teammates, I feel like I've earned the confidence of everybody in the building. So, you know, that's a big thing is just being able to earn the confidence of the guys playing around you, knowing that, you know, I'll do my job and make the play when it comes my way. So. >> Why you wearing that number? >> Um just I'm a ball player. You know, I've always been a ball player. I just It's all about timing timing and place in the NFL with guys that have had like careers like me. So, you know, I feel like this is just the right time and right place. So, the confidence is always there. It's just the opportunity. >> Has there been anything that you've had to adjust in your game in practice so far playing more in the slot? >> No. Um I'm a very physical player. I think people seen that last year. You know, I love putting my hands on people, you know, knocking people back. So, no. Just being able to, you know, take more of a workload this year. That's really the thing I've been focusing on the most. >> What's it like playing on defense with Calais Campbell? >> Um it's dope, you know. Obviously, having the best corner in the game behind you, uh it's a lot of confidence. You know, we kind of it goes hand in hand, you know, we work with them. So, just trying to create opportunities for him, get to the quarterback, you know, make the quarterback make a mistake so he can make a play. It's big time. >> You were able to get up field a lot last year from the Do you think you'll still be able to do that playing more than ever? >> Yeah, for sure. That's how That's what our defense is. I'm the point of the defense, you know, they want me to play in the back field every play, so you know, it's that's that's my job. >> Are there I guess like 20 adjustments you know playing right up the middle? >> No. you know, obviously it's it's a lot faster pace the game cuz the center's so close, but no. I mean, I get a lot of one-on-ones. I feel like I'm, you know, a lot better than a lot of centers in the league. I'm a lot bigger, so you know, I'm excited to be in that position. >> Have you played the 3-4 before? >> Yes. Um I played it in college uh for a year or two, so. >> Carl, what did you guys do well against the run today? It seems like, you know, there wasn't that too much momentum for the run. >> Yeah, um you know, just that's our mentality. Our mentality is to stop the run, you know, we we want to stop the run and then earn the right to rush the passer, so that's why it's kind of a law for our defense. You stop the run and then you earn the right to rush on third, so I feel like we did what we do. Um I feel like we are the best D-tackles trio in the league. I feel like, you know, we're going to have one of the better D-tackle rooms. Obviously, those are two big-time players and I'm just trying to, you know, show them guys that I can keep up the slack, hold hold up my end, so I feel like we complement each other really well. Thank you guys. >> First day in pads? >> Yes. >> What are you What's the What's the feeling? What's What's your overall take? >> it's full bag day. >> [laughter] >> Uh yeah, it was a little wet out there today, so it was kind of hard to find the footing and you know, obviously not hitting for a year or so, it's it's a little difficult to find that fit, but it's coming along. >> How was the acclimation process for you when it comes to joining a new franchise? >> Uh this is my first time doing it, so uh it's going well. Uh just trying to adjust and you know, learn the new system and figure out how, you know, the Patriot way and how we do things here versus where I was last. >> Anything surprise >> Um no, at the end of day football is football. So, I mean, they call it all these different words and whatever thing else, but you know, the verbage is different. That's all. But, it's all football at the end of day. Same concept, same schemes. >> What are your initial takeaways, thoughts on the offense? >> Uh I love the offense. Uh McDaniels is a lot of a lot of fun to play for. And um he uses a fullback. Yes. >> Did he give you a message to you maybe to play fullback in this system? >> Yeah. Yeah, so he's he's showed me a lot of film and, you know, with um uh Devlin, James Devlin in here, he said, you know, watch a lot of him. What we do with him is is what we're trying to do with you. So, I'm looking forward to that. >> What's one of the biggest thing you've learned off of that James Devlin film? >> That you could be anywhere. You know, you could be in the backfield, you could be at tight end, you could be split out, you could be anywhere in this offense. >> How do you feel like you guys did creating space in the running game today? >> Uh I think there's definitely more work to do, but uh I like where we're we're headed. >> I know Devlin was famous here for his neck roll. And I'm always curious about fullbacks and the neck roll. Why do you not go with >> Uh I tried I tried the Q-collar for a couple games and it works, but it's kind of uncomfortable. I don't like something squeezing my neck. And the neck roll I I not for me. >> But, we saw Tanner Arceneaux sliding in the hole today in this practice. What did you see from him so far in this system? >> Tanner's a dog. I love the way he plays ball. He he gets his pads on people. He gets his hands on people and it's hard to let go. I don't know if you saw it out there today, but he put a few a few people down. >> As your first day of pads, obviously you guys are a really good defense. What stands out to you just the first time lining up against those >> The front seven. They play downhill, they play fast, and they they are in their gap. They're very well coached and disciplined. So, you didn't see a whole lot of creases today because the guys are where they're supposed to be. >> I know you played a lot of special team snaps over the last years, especially last year. What sort of idea do you have in terms of what special teams here and how much you think you'll be able to play with coach Ross? >> I mean, that's what got me into the league. When on my first year in 2020, I was a special teamer all the way through in college. I was a special teamer. So, it's always been a big part of my game. So, from the day that I signed here doing the press conference up there in the whatever room that was, me and coach Springer sat down and talked schemes and how I did things in Buffalo and how he's going to use me in these different ways. So, special teams will always be a big part of my game. >> Is there like, I guess a fullback fraternity in the NFL? Like other guys who >> Yeah, yeah. I've I've talked about this before, but there is a fullbacks for life group chat and it's got all the current fullbacks and some of the the legendary guys in there, too. So, yeah, there is a little bit of a fraternity. >> Who's the leader? >> Yes, he is. >> Well, who's who's the guy in that group that maybe if there's a hierarchy that everyone >> I know Lorenzo Neal is kind of like the coordinator of it. He had like a charity golf event in there. He got a bunch of the fullbacks out there. I wasn't able to make it, but I think Lorenzo Neal and uh Mike Alstott are kind of like the the founding fathers in there. >> Anything else? Good? >> All right, thank you.

title: Mike Vrabel: "This is a Great Opportunity For Us." | Patriots Press Conference
text: Christian Gonzalez looked uh um so far and do you anticipate him being a full participant today? >> I don't think uh his participation is going to change. I I've heard anything or you know, I mean, I thought he's come out and looked uh looked good, looked exactly how we would expect him to look and uh came in ready to go. Um you know, executing the multiple coverages and when he's in match, he's been close to his guys, been um you know, I think the one thing we've tried to challenge him on is some of the other opportunities where he can go and you know, use his athleticism, use his speed, use his length and his instincts to to go make plays. There's going to be times where he's going to be you know, matched up and there's going to be times where he's going to have other opportunities and uh some of that has shown up early on in camp and and hopefully that continues. >> Mike, you said last year that this is the day that you maybe your most exciting day when they first get out there in pads and usually there's one or two guys that look different. Do you remember who that was last year? Maybe who stood out and and how much do you like this day of of the year? >> Well, I mean, I just think it's the next step for us. It's uh it's another opportunity to come out there and really start to to come together and see what uh see how the fundamentals and all the technique worked that the guys have tried to put in through the off season and through the early part of camp. Um you know, I don't want to single anybody out, you know, I don't really recall. I I actually thought about it for for a quick second and then I said I'm going to need to focus on what today is and and this year, but uh you know, whether that's young players or you know, tight ends or the opportunity to to run and and you know, this is good work for us to be able to work in the weather, work in elements, stay up, work our footing uh to be able to play and operate and take care of the football, you know, from a quarterback center exchange to the way that we catch it. Uh there's going to be times where we're going to have to play in the elements and you know, this is uh this is a great opportunity for us. >> Mike, DeAndre Hopkins [clears throat] stood out to the team and what was it like having him around? >> Well, it was a great experience, you know, Hop's uh you know, not here. Um but it was a great experience for I think all of us and I think that's what we try to do when you know, you have some of these, you know, unique situations where, you know, a player or you know, former player or whatever it may be wants to come in and help and learn and they love football and so I think it was good for everybody. >> Mike, give me an update on Marquise Brown. >> Uh he won't be out there today. I wouldn't expect seeing him today or or or obviously any of the PUP guys. Gabe continues to progress well. Uh I would say that he's uh closer to the return to play uh element and that we we talk about a lot. Transitioning to uh to Frank and his crew, um getting closer. So, excited about that. >> [clears throat] >> Mike, Charles Woods also left. Did you check him? >> Yeah, I don't think that was anything major. >> Thank you. Um how how is it going with Drake and and A.J. Brown? I know when we spoke to A.J. earlier, um he was talking about, you know, getting to know Drake, getting to know the offense. And does their growing connection get easier because Drake's command of the offense is growing, too? >> No, I mean, you just have to go out and execute and then you know, I think it's you know, I know everybody tracks the numbers and everything else. I I'm confident that uh you know, they'll continue to progress and you know, again, it's it's good work. It's it's good competitive work out there and you know, guys are in tight coverage or challenging and whatever that may be and you know, Drake's had a lot of passes to a lot of different guys and I I the one thing that we continue to try impress upon everybody is that whether it's Hunter or the guys at the receivers or there's opportunities for for Ramondre in the passing game or you know, match-ups that we've had and I'm really confident that that's going to that relationship will continue to grow and AJ will have plenty opportunities to to help us. >> Like what's been your impression of Kayshon Boutte so far this camp both on the field and just however he's been comporting himself uh you know, off the field? >> It was exactly the same as it was last year. I would say very professional. He's he's ready to go. He knows what to do. Take it takes advantage of his opportunities. Uh it's been great to see him show up and and be very productive early on in camp and that was no different than than last year. So, I've got a lot of respect for him. I I tell him that and uh you know, excited that he's gotten off to a good start. >> How would you describe what you've seen from the rookie class? >> [snorts] >> Um you know, I think that it's a it's a learning curve for these guys. I think that the spring is one thing and then getting training camp is something completely different. Um I think they try to improve. They try to learn. Uh you know, Caleb playing O-line in this league and and doing those things is is a new experience. There's new techniques. It's uh you know, much different line of scrimmage I would say than than college football. So, um you know, he rarely makes the same mistake twice. He practices hard. He tries to learn. He tries to fix mistakes. You know, Eli's learning and figuring this game out and I think he can find a way to to help us and you know, on and on and on I go down the line and like I said, I mentioned Gabe earlier. You know, he's he he wants to be out there as soon as he possibly can. And I and I told everybody this and I told Gabe this that there would be a you know, return to play when he got back and um you know, so he's he's attentive in meetings and he's watching practice and, you know, he came in on his off day and then met with Smitty and, you know, did all those things that he needed to do. >> I know you did practice yesterday. He made an appearance just obviously not participating though. Is that something that you encouraged given that he wasn't here for some of the spring >> Well, he wanted to be out there. Some guys that I'd say that closer they get to coming back, I'm probably more likely to have them come out to practice, you know, if they're not very close to to coming back, then maybe they won't be out there, but, uh, I'd say that's probably just a case-by-case basis and, you know, he he wanted to be out there and he wanted to watch and and learn and see what was going on with the with the drills and everything else. So, um, that's what we did. >> Is that Harold out there, too? Is Is that sig- significant that maybe he's getting closer to returning as well? >> Uh, I probably would say Gabe's closer to coming back than Harold is. So, >> Mike, Mike, we have heard from both Winston and Ponder mention that they changed their diet, changed their eating habit this off season. Is that something that the young players, uh, come to realize as they mature where how much it comes from your supporting nutrition staff, uh, contribute here? >> Well, I think it's at the, you know, some of these players are at an age where, you know, they're just now getting into where they could be physically at their best from from a strength and conditioning and and and speed factor in some players that happens a little earlier than than other players, but, uh, I think that, you know, those guys were, you know, looking at what they needed to do to improve or what they could do to improve from year one to year two. And, uh, you know, Ted and his staff, Ted and Sam do a fantastic job with with, you know, each player's dietary needs and what some players need less and more. Um, you know, coaches could probably use a little less, uh, calories than than some of the players, but um those those guys have worked hard, and um excited to see where they continue to grow. >> Mike Mike you can't What do you make of the offense's operation from the play call coming into the snap? >> Oh, I think it's good. Yeah, I mean, I think it's good. I think it's you know, I mean, you want to compare last year, it's probably better. I don't know. We talk about um our overall tempo at practice. I think that the tempo and the speed and the urgency I think is good. I think the the execution, what I told the team and told the offense, I think the execution, uh, has to be better. I think it will be better, but overall, we're moving with a pace that I think you know, can can help us. And you know, we try to work with a play clock, and we try to, you know, get to the line of scrimmage, and whether we huddle or whether we don't huddle, and allow Drake to to get us in a in a good call, and you know, I think all those things are are good, and we'll continue to build and and work with that, and it could always be better, but, uh you know, being able to to play with a tempo, whether we huddle or not, is something that's critical. >> It seems to you though when we've seen him, I mean, on a couple of occasions over the course of the the summer, work is that kind of that jumbo tight end, that extra tackle out there, kind of the role that they are had last year. What goes into the decision to say he might be a good fit here as opposed to someone else? >> Well, I think it's you know, what what their skill type may be, whether, you know, the further way you get from the ball, and being able to to work in space, or some of those blocks out on the edge, um and how that translates. It's usually, you know, a tackle. You know, if you look at the open side of the play, whatever they may do, just kind of pretend that they're the tight end, and see how that translates. So, we'll work some other guys through, and and continue to to look at that, but, you know, wanted to try to give him a role early on or give an opportunity to to have a role early on and you know, we'll see where that, you know, develops. He'll be in there, you know, sometimes when when warm Morgan's not out there, and then some other guys will. >> Seems like you guys have been leaning into some more three safety looks than maybe you did last season. What do you look for in a safety playing that nickel spot, and what have you thought of the competition there so far? >> Yeah, the three the three safeties is just a body to, you know what I mean? It's a guy, and so you know, really, you know, Marcus isn't the the biggest guy, and you know how much we love Marcus. It's just you know, gives you an opportunity to probably play against, you know, teams that are, you know, going to run the football out of 11 personnel or play against 12 personnel. Um and much like the conversation we just had with Caleb is just trying to find guys to have roles and you know, who can play where. Pretty confident that that Marcus knows, you know, that stuff and knows how to to play in there, uh and then given, you know, some of the safeties an opportunity to to have another role as well. >> I think you guys are pretty deep at wide receiver. Is that a position you might be willing to move a player, or do you like having that depth? >> Well, I mean, I love having depth, but I I would say that, you know, we're always going to try to look to, you know, im- improve, whether that's by adding, you know, draft capital or obtaining a player or you know, keeping the guys we have. We we want to try to provide competition throughout the roster at each position. I think that's something that's critical. I think that's what good teams do every year is year in and year out that they're they're making the roster as competitive as possible. And so that those position battles and, you know, who's the sixth lineman, who's the fifth, sixth receiver, who's the fourth tight all these things are you want to be as competitive as possible. Uh And something that I've always, you know, I was a part of as a player and I think that's important to do uh here in training camp. some quarterbacks and coaches around the league, including Josh Allen, have talked a little bit about reading defenses last season and how it's getting harder to use safeties as keys. Um is that something that you guys think about when you're teaching your quarterbacks? Do you have to teach them differently? Is that even a thing that you're really thinking about that that trend of this concept too? >> Well, I mean I think we're always, you know, I mean offensively I think we're always trying to figure out what's going on and what they're trying to do and how we can set the defense and make it look like we're going to snap the ball or to Andrew's point, our tempo and our operation. I mean if you just stand out there and the the quarterback's just standing straight up and down, you're not going to give them any reason to to get into position or to show maybe what they're doing. Um I would say that there's some pre-snap and then the post-snap reads that go involved in whether the coverage opens up or you know, it stays pretty tight to the to the line of scrimmage and there is some sort of match or you know, the non-traditional Tampa looks that that people are running and everything else. So, I would say that you know, we only have one team to game plan against right now and that's the other side of the ball for the Patriots and you know, Drake will have to study the our guys and what, you know, Craig's doing, what Kevin's doing. Um linebacker location, all these different things that that go into it. Um guys staring, you know, in at the ball, maybe somebody pressed when they're not normally pressed and I would say we try to give them a few things, but not too many things that that that you can't go out there and and play fast. >> When it comes to handling protections, were there any ways that you wanted to see Trey continue to improve this season after he kind of went into handling it last year and how have you seen him grow there? >> Yeah, that's always, you know, that's more about the disguise and how would I like to see him handle it? I would like to see him make sure that the slides go into where they're pressuring from. I would like to try to get as many guys to where they're pressuring from as possible. They don't tell us they don't show us the card before the play. So, um what's always important is that we listen to the quarterback and that we you know, that if he's hot, he's got to know that he's hot and he's got to have an answer, right? I don't think protections ever going to be 100%. Um what's important is that you have you know, way to you know, save the day and know where your hot throw is or know where your issues are. So, I would say that that's something that we're always trying to improve on. You'll see these guys working during special teams. You'll see them working blitz pick up. Um too weak, too strong, you know, corner pressure. Oh, you know what I mean? It's It's just I think a constant um thing and again, I love the way that uh Rhamondre protects and you know, Traveon is continuing to work on that. If you have backs that can pick up pressure, it's one thing to be able to get over there and know where the pressure is coming from. It's also another to to you know, you got to go block them. And uh you know, defensively, we talk about if we get on a running back, we we have to win. We have to disrupt be disruptive when we're we're blitzing on a back. And so, um I think the first part is getting the quarterback to to get us in the right protection. And then you know, you got to go over there and block them. And then if we don't get in the right protection, the quarterback has to know uh what the answer is and and where he's got to get rid of football. Thanks, guys. Enjoy the day. >> Enjoy the rain.

title: 2 minutes at Patriots Training Camp: A.J. Brown, Kyle Williams bounce back on Day 5

title: Top Takeaways from Day 5 of Patriots Training Camp
channel_name: Greg Bedard Patriots Podcast with Nick Cattles
text: This is the Greg Bedard Patriots podcast with Nick Cattles. >> Everybody, welcome to the Greg Bedard Patriots podcast here at Gillette Stadium after the Patriots wrapped up their first padded practice of training camp. The weather mostly held off. It rained a little bit during practice. Uh the stands were about half full considering the conditions, but still really good day of work uh for the Patriots. Uh couple news items at the top. Uh Carlton Davis, who went out of the last practice uh with a hamstring injury, was not on the field today. We'll have to see how long that'll keep him out. Uh if you remember Christian Gonzalez had a hamstring injury last year, and he missed the first three games of the season. I It didn't look that serious with Carlton Davis, but you never know with those things. Uh Mike Vrabel said before practice that Gabe Ikard is getting closer to getting on uh the field for the Patriots. The The same cannot be said of Harold Landry. Uh Vrabel just said that Ikard is a lot closer than uh Landry at getting on the field. Of course, without Landry and Ikard, that leaves um the edge group, which was probably thin coming into camp, including those two guys, even thinner when we're talking about one-on-one pass rush drills, uh which we did get um today. Uh as far as that goes, offensive line decidedly beat the defensive line in the first bout of one-on-ones, 14 wins, three losses, six defeat on the on the uh defensive side. Uh it was uh excuse me one second. I I think it was Oh, uh Eric Gregory, the defensive tackle who had a really nice day, had some impactful uh p- uh reps in team as well. He was a perfect 2 and 0. Both were against Ben Brown. He had a decisive win against Ben Brown where he pretty much dusted him. Ben Brown barely got a hand on him. But pretty much everybody did well on the offensive line. I would say the only guy who didn't do well was Ben Brown. Will Campbell among the starters Will Campbell, Jared Wilson and Michael Wenue were all 2 and 0. Morgan Moses again did not take part in one-on-ones. Caleb Lomu took his reps. He was 1 0 and 1. Marcus Bryant and Caden Wallace were also 2 and 0 for the offensive lines. Um Let's see what else on that. Leonard Taylor was 0 and 2. Corey Durden was 0 and 2. Milton Williams was 0 and 2. Sort of seems like the defensive line sort of gets rounded in the form. Christian Gonzalez was on the field today, participated fully, did a really nice job in one-on-ones. He was good in team. Again, there's a lot being made of this about Christian Gonzalez being on the field. Some of it is kind of annoying me. There's a lot of people who are saying like why is he even on the field? title: Aaron Glenn Training Camp Press Conference (7/30) | New York Jets
text: Good morning. Uh two injuries that we had today, G. Scott, uh calf injury. Uh I can't really say exactly the severity of that when I get in there. Um and then Waldhall, uh he had a hamstring, so those are two guys, the receiver Waldhall, uh and I'll see how those injuries are um once I get back inside. Uh today nothing changed, you know, we're just building off what we did yesterday, so um again, I I I like where we're at. I want to love where we're at. It's just the second day. Um but I like the way the guys are working. So, any questions? >> It [clears throat] looked like David Bailey had a pretty active practice today. Can you just give us some thoughts on how he's done? >> Yeah. Yeah. Um he's everything that we expect him to be. And it'll be really exciting once we put the pads on. And I think we all understand through these acclimation days, uh we're still in shorts, but to just be able to see the um the energy and the speed and the quickness off the edge and the ability to hold a strong edge, um and the way that he wants to play the run game, um it's everything that I imagined from that player. Uh and it was actually just more than him. I mean, you saw J.J. Encoe Ebari, right? You saw him, he was pretty active today, uh playing on the edge, so um I'm happy with all those guys. Will did some good things also today, you know, so when it just comes to that edge group, I I those guys did a pretty good job today. >> I'm curious, just your perspective as a rookie defensive lineman, just what are their like what do you think their biggest is far as like coming into the league, what do they need to work on specifically? >> That's funny you asked that because um just from just from my years of of of coaching, uh the one thing that's that's an adjustment for those guys is really listen to the linebackers when there is movement that that happens. So, for example, if the tight end goes across and we want to jump the front, you know, sometimes it takes a while for those guys to get that, you know, cuz they're usually just get off the ball and going, you know, but everybody has to be in sync. So, that's the one thing that most of those guys have to work on. Um and then just the technique that they're learning, you know, so um but listen, Dabo does a really good job with that. Uh he holds those guys accountable. I think our linebackers do a really good job of communicating and making sure cuz if they don't, they'll go up there and tap them on the butt to make sure they do move. So, um but we we're all in sync when it comes to that, but that's really the development that they have to have. >> Coach, how big a part AJ, how big a part of this team are these rookies been this year? You got obviously the three first-rounders, Pons in the second round. >> Yeah. >> And then, you know, Jackson's out there today. How big a role do they have on this team today? >> Well, the expectations is for all those guys to have a role, but they have to decide that themselves. And uh you guys have heard me say this before. I mean, we're we're out there trying to compete, and no one's given anything. So, they determine that role. Um and I'm always be honest with those guys in that aspect of listen, here's what we need you to do, here's how you can do it, and here's how you got to compete to beat this guy out because that guy's not going to let you just have it. So, and I want to create that type of environment here, you know, so the expectations, yes, they have a big role, but they have to decide that themselves. >> What do you say about how Klubnik has progressed? >> Man, he made some throws today, didn't he? Um listen, we we knew exactly what we were getting. >> [clears throat] >> Um we understand his trajectory when he got to Clemson, how when he came to Clemson as the I think he was the number one recruit when it comes to a quarterback. Um and then he had some issues, you know, but then he picked himself up. So, we know that the heels that he's had in his college career. And that's the thing that we're intrigued by him because he was able to bounce back and continue to go. And to me, that shows leadership, too. When things went down, man, he continued to go. So, um I thought he made some really good throws today. Um he's still improving in what we're asking him to do. And again, we look forward to see how he progress during camp. >> Until 10 minutes, the guy has been moving around a lot on the offensive line. Kind of what you see from him just during your time here? >> Yeah. And when you say moved around, I think it's only been from center to guard. So, I don't want to say it's a lot of moving. Um but I will say this. Uh and it's no different from what I said last year. I mean, he was a guy that coach, whatever you needed me to do need me to do, I'll do it. Um and I think he's really embraced playing the guard position now. Um listen, obviously we signed him because we know what type of player he is. We know what type of leader he is and type of man he is. And that's one of the reasons why he's here. And we want to continue to build this team with men like that. So, um very unselfish, uh communicates very well, uh does a good job of getting along with his teammates, um and does a really good job in the locker room. So, I'm happy. I'm happy to have uh him where exactly where he's at. >> Whether it's uh Cooper or Mitchell or some other guys out there making pretty good catches, it seems like maybe you have more compliments to Garrett at the receiver position than he than he's had in his career other than the year he played with Davante Adams. What can that do for the offense as a whole and for Garrett? >> Well, it really opens us up to um anytime you want to try to double Garrett, I mean, we have other, you know, I would say high-level players that can go out there and make plays. And you just named two of them that I think it's going to do a good job for us this year. But not just that, I mean, our tight end room, which I talked about last time I was up here that those guys are still improving. Then you have the running backs, you know, those guys with themselves can make some plays, too. So, I'm happy exactly where we at on the talent level when it comes to the offense. Um I know Garrett is because that's going to open him up just like you just said. So, uh but we just got to continue to improve every day. That once you get that 101, you have to win it. And our guys know that and I expect them to do that. >> Coach, it's kind of a logistical question, but I'm curious if you could share your thought process on like a no practice tomorrow, no practice Sunday. I'm wondering how the cadence how you guys >> Yeah, yeah. Um, here's and I I I'll give you a a small bit of of what um, I talked to the players about. What my job is as a coach is I understand the acclimation from the NFL as far as man, you go from the off season then now you in no pads trying to get in the pads and I truly understand that. But my job is to acclimate our players to get ready for the regular season. So, what we try to do is and I and I show them a graph to where the first week man, the highest amount of reps we get is 24 reps. And then man, we're going to recover and I'm going to bring it down. So, we have two practices on and then we bring it down for recovery. And then it jumps back up. So, the next week the highest amount of reps we'll have is 32. All right? And then man, we'll recover again. Then the next week the highest amount of reps will be 40. So, what I'm trying to do is get our guys to be ready to play 65 to 75 plays a game. And that's my job as a coach to be able to do that. So, each week you'll start to see those reps go up. You'll you'll start to see that yardage that they have to have and that's the analyst part of it. Yardage go up also. So, um, and that's what I try to create. You know, so when you say the day off and the days on, you'll see it go like this here. And that's the reason why man, I'm trying to get max reps then I'm trying to recover. Max reps then recover. Hopefully that makes sense. >> Are you guys going to go to pads on like Monday or >> We're going to pads on Monday? >> Absolutely. The league allows to do it. Absolutely. You don't have to check that. >> [laughter] >> I know you you knew Frank and you played with him and everything like that, but what was the conversation like cuz he was out of the league for a couple years for you to bring him back to you. >> Um the conversation just just throughout just checking on me. And from his words of man, listen, I know exactly who you are as a person, as a man, I know as a football coach. Man, you just keep your process and keep going straight ahead and don't let anything on the outside just deter you from what you trying to do. And that's encouraging. Um especially coming from him. And I don't know how much you guys know him, but he's a man of faith. Um been married for a number of years, have a beautiful family. And man, it is um it is a luxury to have men like that in your life cuz we all need men that we can lean lean on. So, um from a former teammate to somebody I've competed against um to now being, you know, on this staff, uh those conversations were nothing but positive, you know, and we've always just talked football. And just hearing what his um his philosophy is, I would always think, man, I I feel the same way. And man, how can I do this as as his job as a head coach, how can I navigate myself this way? And he would always give me his opinions on that. Um and it's been good. It's been good, man, and I'm glad he's here. Glad he's here. >> Coach, we're talking about before training camp, there was a report that the Jets had inquired about Kerry and Arnold. I'm wondering what is the current level of interest in him? >> Yeah. Well, nothing has changed when it comes to how me and Mooj operate that man, we're always going to look to add guys that that we feel like they can help us. And when I say add, well, I mean, look at guys. Let me let me take that back. We're always looking at guys that we feel like we can help them. We do our due diligence. And listen, that doesn't mean that we're going to bring everybody in. The thing is, man, we're just going to turn over every stone to make sure that man, is this a guy that can help us man with everything that's going on, which we don't know. And I let those guys figure that out. Um will be a good fit. And we're going to do this no matter what. No different than Russell Wilson, no different than anybody else that we look at. >> You and DeMario You and DeMario >> Last one. >> You and DeMario have had a relationship for a long time. >> Now he's a defensive signal caller though. How advantageous is that going to be for you to have him relaying your calls out there and then and [snorts] then seeing things progress pre-snap? >> That's that's huge. Um it also goes into what I'll talk about Duca, a guy that knows me, like I know how how I think. Um the gold the guy that knows exactly how I sort my play calls to make sure that I put us in the best position. And DeMario knows exactly how I call a game. And listen, I know we've been away from each other for a while, but he still understands that foundation that I've always talked about when it comes to playing defense. So, um he can be able to relate that to the players, relate it to the players. And again, I'm glad I have him. And he's he's a guy that and this has happened yesterday in the meetings that it doesn't matter who you are the best player on the team, but the highest paid player on the team or any practice squad guy. Listen, if if I see an issue, I'mma call it out in team meetings or I'mma call it in a defensive meeting. And he's a guy that doesn't blink, you know, cuz he's a guy that I will say something to also in front of everybody else. And I think that's how a coach should operate. And it like he doesn't take that as, man I'm I'm the top guy, you shouldn't say anything. No, he just listen, coach me just like I'm a rookie. And I feel like that with everybody. I'll go and ask your question. I know you've been waiting to ask questions. So, who was it over here? >> I appreciate that. >> Go ahead, ask him. >> I was going to ask about Dane Belton cuz he's a guy who had a lot of ball production across town, but didn't get the opportunity that it looks like you're going to give him. >> Well, uh that's the reason he's here. He's had a lot of ball production. He's a damn good player. He's a damn good special teamer. So, um again, anytime we can find guys that can help us improve, we're going to bring them to the on this team. All good? All right, fellas. >> Mhm.
