title: Devaughn Vele on excitement for season, Tyler Shough | Saints Training Camp 2026
text: What what excites you about having a full year now to play in this system and all the other wide receiver pieces in this room for you guys? >> Uh it's it's exciting for me. Um understanding the playbook a lot better and not having to worry too much about the X's and O's, but actually being able to go out there and uh you know, play the game that I how I play. Um Showcasing what I can do and I'm excited for our room as well. We got a lot of talent in the wide receiver room. Uh the rookies hold us to a high standard as well. They're always asking great questions. Uh eager to learn and so it's all pushing us as vets. Um you know, have that spark as well and you know, surprise a lot of people this year. >> How much enthusiasm do you have coming into this season, especially after the way you had a stretch last year and then it ends prematurely? >> Oh no, I'm excited. Uh obviously I want to stay healthy as much as I can. So that's that's my number one goal this season, but you know, I want to contribute as much as I can to the team, whatever they need me to do in uh blocking, pass catching, or even supporting the guys from the sideline, whatever they need me to do. At the end of the day we want to win games and you know, make the playoffs and so that's that's our goal and that's what we're we're aiming for. >> And does it excite you when Kellen says, you know, "Hey, we need to find ways to get him the ball more?" >> Yeah, I mean obviously any receiver you can ask and they would want the ball 100 times out of 100, but um like I said, I'm one of those guys that even if I don't get the ball a lot, uh as long as I'm contributing and helping the team win, that's all I care about at the end of the day. >> Last season you did really start to get the ball a lot. What do you think changed? >> I think it's just opportunities. Uh I don't think it's anything too crazy to where like, "Hey, we came into this game plan. We're going to throw Valdes-Scantling the ball." I think it was more so, you know, I got in the right spots at the right time. Shurmur trusted me, gave me opportunities to make plays and I made them. >> So I I mean as soon as it's an obvious answer, is it frustrating when when it finally starts to click to to have it like end like that? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean it was it was definitely hard mentally. Um you know, especially building that chemistry with him, but um at the end of the day it gave other guys opportunities to make plays um and you know, kind of catapulted us into this season understanding, "Okay, what kind of guys do we have in the room? What can we do with that?" And obviously make a push for the playoffs this year. >> And I mean you guys added so much in the skill position whether it's a tight ends, running backs, receivers. Um is there kind of a sense of like a like a lot of mouths to feed and like how do you kind of navigate that, balance that, and all >> I mean like I said, at the end of the day we care about winning games. Um I I think individual stats is what's going to hinder a team if you're only chasing those things. At the end of the day we want to make the playoffs, obviously win a Super Bowl. And so we're going to make sure we give the guys that give us our best opportunity to do that. And if that means somebody's got to touch the ball more, then that's that's what we're going to do. >> And then Justin Reed was talking yesterday about just the way Tyler throws the ball. He's kind of describing it as like it's got zip and it's catchable, you know? Like how would you describe that and just like as a as a receiver like is it receiver friendly the way he throws the ball? >> I think it it for sure is. I think the other thing I like about the way Shuck plays is he gives guys opportunities. Um I know there's some guys uh who if they see their guy covered they're not going to give it a shot unless he's wide open, but Shuck is one of those guys that he'll put the ball somewhere where he believes that his guy's going to make the play outside of the defender. And so um you know, as receivers we appreciate that a lot because that means he has a lot of trust in us. And we just got to make sure we reciprocate that back to him by making those plays. >> Would the Miami touchdown be an example of that last year? >> Yes. That's the perfect example, yeah. >> Do you see more of those opportunities in a training camp setting where you know, the risk is different but you can take a little bit more kind of risk in these situations? >> Yeah, and I feel like it's also one of those things it helps him understand uh which guys he can trust. But on top of that, it helps him um you know, find that that good balance of when it's a little too risky and when he can push it a little bit. Uh kind of letting his own character show is the way he plays. And so uh it helps us as receivers understand like even if we're running a route that we're not expecting the ball, we should be expecting it because Shuck's going to be the one to throw it. So uh I think training camp is a perfect opportunity to do something like that. >> With how limited last year was, when you you talked yesterday about the trip to San Diego, how beneficial was that for you and for Shuck to build that chemistry with Tyler and to get your rhythm going? >> Yeah, it's good. I mean you get outside of football. Uh getting in a setting where you guys are training together, but you also spend some time outside of that. Understanding there's more things to football um outside of it. And so, um you know, building that camaraderie and that brotherhood, I think it helps a lot, especially when, you know, we get into those uh points in the season where things may start getting tough. Um it helps us understand that we we got brothers we can depend on, we can turn to, and uh help keep pushing us to be great. >> You talked about the versatility of this offense, but what does it do for a player as far as making things things a little easy for you, getting better looks, >> Could you repeat that again? >> Does the versatility of the weapons around you, does that open up the game a little bit more for you individually or whoever it may be getting >> Oh, yeah, absolutely. I I think it's one of those things is uh when you have depth, it helps it a lot where um say you you get tired, you're gassed, and you need to take a play or two off, you can trust the guy that behind you that he's going to bring the same energy, same level of play, maybe in a different play style that even when you're out, you guys are still not missing the stride and able to make plays and keep driving the ball down the field. And so, I feel like we have that as an offensive unit. Um obviously, we're going to keep continuing to build and fix the little things. That's That's the point of what training camp is for. And so, uh we're finding those guys with that versatility and those guys that we can trust. >> Now, Jaylen Booth was here last year, but now that you're finally getting to see him do stuff that he's, you know, what what have you made of him and just, you know, after knowing him and seeing him go out there >> He's a very professional player. Uh I I respect his game a lot. Um he's very smooth with the way he runs his routes. Um and he's a very smart player as well, understands the plays, understands coverages. And so, um I'm excited for him. I know uh there's been things about him, but I don't I I think he's one of those players that's going to shock a lot of people, and I'm excited for him this year. >> When you were out in San Diego for the week, talk to Drew Brees. >> I So, I actually wasn't able to make it out there. I had a family emergency that occurred. So, I unfortunately wasn't able to make it. But from what I heard, I heard it was it was a lot of fun, a lot of guys kind of were fan girling seeing Drew Brees and all that stuff. So, it was pretty cool.

Um but for him he's always had it and the thing is I think um you know Kellen is nourishing that like he's kind of nurturing that by having him to you know break it down and stuff like that. I think that's good not for just him but I think for everybody to get accustomed to his voice and being that presence and I think that's really good and the testament to Kellen just be like yeah this is who we're going to hear this is our guy this is our leader this is our quarterback and you know and I think Tyler's kind of ran with it. He's been good and especially in the off season you know taking us as guys on trips getting together you know kind of having some camaraderie I think that's been the biggest thing for us. >> Could you describe your connection with him on the field? It seems like you two guys are on the same page >> Yeah. Yeah. Uh I just know where he wants me and I think that's the biggest thing. Um you know when you you spend a lot of time together and like you you watch film together and you know you kind of see where he his eyes are at you know he sees where my eyes are at and honestly I just try to be savvy and I think he's you know he kind of reads where I'm supposed to be. I think it's the biggest thing. Having a lot of reps with a quarterback I think is the biggest thing. And um you know it's it's kind of tough when you're on the sideline trying to figure out like you know but if you're watching film and you know you're having actual reps with him I think that's the biggest thing. That's been good for us. >> Is savvy is that like is that a word that you would say that like that's your biggest like strength that's your superpower is like knowing where the holes are and knowing where to find spots? >> I I would say I mean I'm some people say like I'm fast quick but I'm not the fastest guy. I mean I'm a big guy. Um I mean there's some attributes about me that are different from other tight ends but I feel like the biggest thing that kind of had me to stick is just, you know, being smart about coverages and being smart about where, you know, guys are at and treating leverages and trying to trick the defender and things like that. That's kind of like been my thing just to have like a little edge cuz I mean, you think about the NFL, everybody's the same speed, everybody's same height, all that. But, if you could have like a quick edge, that's kind of been like, you know, my MO. >> Is it different this year to last? Do you feel more comfortable? >> Uh in terms of what? >> Your knowledge? >> Your rapport? Are there things that go into Yeah. Uh I would say a lot of it is yeah, just, you know, being immersed in the offense, you know, just knowing that you don't have to learn a different offense probably the the best thing for me. But, um you know, just going in and knowing that, you know, you have your your number one QB, you know, you got your running backs, your tight ends, you know, your receivers cuz sometimes last year it was just like, man, are we going to be a a one tight end, you know, set team or we're going to be two or three, you know, you just you just never really knew, but I think since we have, you know, like kind of the offense under our belt, we kind of know where we're going into. You kind of know where you're going to be, you know, if they say 11, 12, 13 personnel, I know 13 personnel, I'm probably going to be outside. So, just knowing like where you're going to be in certain situations has been really good for me. >> A different system and offense in the running game for sure. In terms of just like >> Well, I just like I mean, you guys brought in A.J. Green, you brought in David Edwards. >> You have the possibility to run it in different ways with different tight ends. Well, I hope I run the ball. That'd be nice. Shoot, [laughter] that'd be good, too. Shoot. No, I mean, it's it's it's I I think it's actually been good. We have a lot of um diversity. I remember I was talking to one of the tight ends yesterday looking at film. I was like, man, we got some nice running backs. Let alone just like our addition, like we got nice running backs in the backfield that we could do a lot with. I mean, sometimes people just forget about Kendra. Like Kendra is explosive, dude. And so, just knowing that, you know, you know, despite, you know, what he's been through, um he's still an explosive and exciting player. so you know, just knowing things like that, you know, it's been good and knowing that you have, you know, Trave in the backfield, AK in the backfield, it's just like you have so much versatility you can have, and so we haven't even like scratched the surface of what we can do from a run game standpoint. We honestly have been keeping it, you know, pretty vanilla so far, but um, I mean, I guess we'll see in a couple weeks how it'll like pan out, but I think, you know, in terms of just adding David, David's been really good for us, you know, and that add knowing David is just like that. The guy on the left side is kind of like moving the whole line of scrimmage has been really good for you know, our guys in the backfield. >> How was the >> guy Being an undrafted guy making your way in the league, making a name for yourself, I mean, did Taysom's journey at all kind of inspire you like while you were doing that cuz he was a guy that was here that Yeah. >> similar path as well. Like was that inspiring at all for you during that process? Uh, his journey for sure. Um, I would I would say um, Taysom's journey and a lot of guys just just has been through the Saints, you know, organization. I feel like they have a great reputation of just hiring hiring um, getting um, undrafted guys. And so knowing that those guys that come through the Saints organization have stuck and have been around, um, just kept their head down and just kind of pushed through has been honestly has been one of the things that um, I really been like admiring. Like especially guys like Taysom, guys like Adam Thielen, you know, guys who've done a a great deal and have almost made like Pro Bowls and things like that. Um, it's been really good for me to to see that cuz it's possible. You know, sometimes when when people get undrafted they think it's not possible to make an impact or, you know, not possible to make a team, but you know, if you keep your head down, you know, you stay healthy, um, and honestly you're just not not making trouble. I feel like that's the biggest thing of just staying here. Like it's not the most athletic guys are making the teams. It's just like the guys who stick who are smart, who are savvy, that's just, you know, who are able to just stick it out. >> How was the um, Trautman but how the trip to California? I think Tyler said your family stayed in the same house. It was a full house. Three kids. You know, two dogs. Oh man, it was It was a lot, but it was extremely fun. I think you know, like like I was telling someone before, you know, when you when you have like camaraderie and you're able to be around people, even staying in the same house. I feel like you learn a lot about people and I feel like, you know, and that translates on the field, believe it or not. >> Uh-huh. >> And people think it's not, but it does. It just it does something to you, like you just know where to be at the right time because you guys got up at the same time and ate breakfast together. Right. I I don't know, but God just be doing stuff just like, all right, you guys supposed to be on the same accord on this route right here. And it just works. But I think the biggest thing is like I know that I'm going to fight for him and I'm going to you know, do whatever I can to make plays because, you know, we took that trip to San Diego or we started throwing routes in February or we went and did, you know, did some things together, went on a ride together. It's just like the things that you spend time together, you you you find ways to dig a little deeper because you know that person on a more intimate and deeper level. >> Did you learn something about him that you that you didn't know? >> All right, y'all y'all y'all We're talking at the same time now. >> Now are there some things you learned about him that you didn't know that that are shareable? >> Uh >> [sighs] >> let's see. Um Yeah, so we're about to go on this ride and um you know, this ride says 6'5". 6'5" and below. So it's a height maximum. So I never knew that before at SeaWorld. And so um you know, we're going and the guy says, "Yeah, can we uh get your height?" And he just walks right by. So he already knew that he was probably going to be in some trouble. So I was like, "All right, well, I just can't ignore him." So I sit there, you know, I get my height checked. He said I'm good. I just got my hair cut, so I was like, "All right, I'm all right." So we're walking up and then we get to the ride and the guy's like, he pulls us out of the ride and he's like, "Hey man, you guys get checked." I said, "We just got checked downstairs." Knowing that Tyler didn't. So, you know, we get our we get our head checked and we barely like get that we we grazing the line. So, I was like, "Man, just keep our feet up when we going through this ride." But, it was it was amazing. But, um one of those things is just you know, when you determine to do something cuz that was the only ride we went on. When you determine to do something, you just do it. And so, uh I just thought it was funny that he just walked right by the dude. >> [laughter] >> I don't know if he heard him or not, but I was like, "Dude, I know you heard him cuz I just heard him." And we were right next to each other. But, uh I don't know who we rode with. I can't remember. But, it was like only two two like high-rise in SeaWorld. Not many of them. But, uh we went on and it was it was fun. It was a good time. But, I was scared cuz I don't think he was going to be able to ride it. I never heard of height maximum like ride maximum. It's crazy. >> If we ever see Tyler listed at 6'6", we know he's wearing cleats in there. >> Yeah, no doubt. No doubt. That's the cleats. He's definitely not 6'6". He's like 6'6". Well, apparently 6'4" according to SeaWorld. >> Yeah, so. Yeah. Yeah. It's fair. Fair. No no doubt. No doubt. >> No doubt. All right. Uh they weren't my dogs cuz my dogs not coming on that trip. Me and I had two girls I had the two girls and they had a great time with his dog, uh Murphy. And um you know, that my girls just love dogs. But, I think the biggest thing is just getting the family together. You know, you have family together and knowing that you're about to do something special. Uh I think that's kind of the biggest thing is just and just friendship. Like, I don't think everything had to be transactional to translate to football. But, it was just you know, good to have the families together. >> You said y'all played board games. So, this is your chance to air it out if he cheats at board games or >> No, I ain't play board games. I No, I ain't play board games at all. I know they was cheating cuz they was saying some stuff that I ain't I ain't know. So, I was like I think they was trying to play Clue. And they were like, "Oh, let's play Clue." I was like, "No, y'all been playing for a couple hours. So, I'm good." They start cheating and making up rules on me. I don't like that. >> I got a quick uh health science question about the >> Health science? >> Yeah, I'm just curious. >> Shoot. >> We're working on a story. It's 25th anniversary of Corey Stringer. >> Okay. >> Um so, being in a hot weather team, are there are there things about the way the practice is um planned out that you can tell that heat exposure is a real consideration on how they're you know, the time of day they're putting you out there how long they're putting you out there and how they're monitoring you? >> Yeah. Um I think there's a benefit truly to us being out there um in the heat. I think it's an advantage for us to you know, kind of go out and get it a little bit cuz I say when you know, the Jaguars are a team, you know, they have preseason but say a team like LA, they come out here, it's going to be a totally different experience. And I think it's one of those things where we have an advantage. They kind of go into the year knowing that we've been in the heat. We're accustomed to it. We've been grinding away. And then we get into a cool area, you know, um I mean, we can really go and get it and and get after some teams. But, I think the biggest thing is you know, us going out there at 9:00, it's a little different than going out there at 12:00 cuz we probably wouldn't be out there as long. But, um I think there's a benefit to what Kellen and you know, Ted Rath and those other guys are doing in keeping us safe and things like that. But, um yeah, I think you know, getting some heat exposure, I think that's kind of been a good thing that kind of gets us into the year and gets us acclimated for you know, the season what the season might present. >> How do they emphasize recovering from the heat exposure? >> Well, we have 3 hours right now. Um we have 3 hours to kind of get our bodies back, um cool down before we you know, get into meetings and stuff. I think it's been a big thing, yeah. And so, I mean, obviously we got IVs and we got all that but I mean, the biggest thing is it's really on you. Like, they can't they can't baby us and everything. Like, we're we we get paid a lot of money to to take care of our bodies and work out and do those other things. So, you know, we get done practice, you know, they give us 3 hours to recover, get your bodies back, hydrate, eat, um yeah, I I I've never been in a place where, you know, you get that much time off to get your body back so we could go into meetings and stuff like that cuz usually it's like right after. Or we get an hour and a half and so they are being cognizant of what, you know, we have with our time, but I think us as adults, us as professional athletes, we know what to do to to take care of our bodies. >> All right. >> Thank you.

title: Charlie Smyth on kicker competition, special teams room | Saints Training Camp 2026
text: Yeah. Yeah. All righty. >> Hey, congratulations Ross, by the way. >> Thank you, man. I appreciate it. >> That was awesome to see you in the homeland. So, yeah. Yeah. >> [laughter] >> There you go. >> It was great to be out there. I'm going back. >> Good time? >> Yeah, yeah. >> Weather was good as well. >> Yeah, oh yeah. >> Everything was good. >> Yeah. >> How was your off-season? >> Oh, yeah, it was brilliant. Um, after mini-camp I went back home for 3 weeks and um, just reset. Just spent time with friends and family and then uh, yeah, it was it was good. It was good. It was the weather as I said, the weather was great. It was terrible weather golfing and um, did a bit of kicking but I think the biggest thing for me was just really not overthinking things when I get home and uh, probably was doing a little bit of that in OTAs but um, but I think that's the time of year too, you know, just um, just go over things and try and come up with a finished product for training camp on onwards then and um, but yeah, now I feel like we're we're in a good spot. So, yeah. >> How do you How do you feel you you've been put in positions of a lot of competition since you've been here from the tryout with the two free agents last year to Cade this year and now you're back at it again this off-season. What what about kind of the competitive environment? The how do you feel you operate in those situations? >> Yeah, as you said Ross, I've had a lot of experience in that now um, and I've kind of figured out what works best for me is just really focusing on myself and not getting too much um, involved with like an outcome based approach of like is it going to be me or him and thinking too far ahead. Really just trying to delve into um, just my process and whenever I go out there and I'm just thinking of my process and what I'm doing to help me make kicks like uh, and then I also like how was I feeling whenever I had the game on the top last year? How was I feeling when I had the Miami um, the first time against Miami? And delving into that emotional state. I feel like in practice sometimes I've gotten myself a little too like jazzed up for it and I'm trying to smash everything whereas trying to come with a little more control and just process based and just putting the ball through the uprights instead of, you know, maybe trying to show out off my leg, which maybe I've got caught up with in the past, but at the end of the day it's three points three points, so that's really where my mind's at now, and I think I've matured a lot and especially this this year and having the experience of playing in the games last year, taking the learnings of those into this off-season and then yeah, just trying to go out and have a good camp now and just see where it takes us, you know. >> Kind of kind of related to that, I mean, like how how important is that live game experience, you know, versus like your first two years when it was just it was just training camp and Yeah, preseason games. >> Yeah, exactly. And then just to like in the season then just like one thing for me I was figuring out last year was sideline management during games. So obviously having experienced that before, so just know how it works for me, maybe what doesn't, taking the learnings from that and then taking it into the season and uh yeah, that's that was those games were so valuable from the start and I think for everybody honestly, like we really saw the growth of our team in the last nine weeks or nine or 10 weeks of the season and you know, we were starting to figure out like what was working for us, what was not, creating an identity and yeah, I suppose in this off-season as well, just becoming a lot closer as a team. It was great the way we had those little SWAT teams, which I think you all were aware of um and just going out to dinners and just getting to know more about our teammates and maybe helping out the rookies and you know, like how does a undrafted rookie make a roster and that's for me in terms of like being involved with special teams, telling them how much you need to be dialed into that and it's not all about offense and defense and just like trying to add in any sort of tips where I can, I suppose, and but yeah, look, I'm still figuring out my own things as well, so just it's good we're we're in a good place, you know, where we are. >> What happened to your thumb and is that an injury you can kick through? >> Yeah, I mean, it's funny actually cuz I was saying to everybody anybody asking is like, you know how it is like it's just people see it and it's everybody asking me. I don't even thought I don't eat my hands. The only player in the team who doesn't eat my hands. So, I was actually in the cabin in Gatlinburg again this year couple of weeks ago and slept on it and I landed and um, but I'm good. I mean, I don't eat my hands so >> Yeah, I'm just glad it wasn't anything else now. It was probably the best injury I could ask for. >> But yeah, it's a little inconvenient but it's it's all good. I mean >> also right-handed? >> Right-handed, yeah. So, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, so So, the turf was turf was a little hard and then I I went to plant and then I braced behind me and then I looked at my thumb and I was like, okay, there's something going on here but I'm still able to kick that thing and kick pretty well so Uh, if any of you I don't know if any of you have seen me throw a football before but it's not pretty so >> You know, I suppose it's it's like the boys give me a we have a a hoop in the team meeting room and the boys give me a hard time about my jump shot. So, but yeah, still a work in progress but >> you know, still make more buckets than some of them anyways. >> What what's the special teams room like? A little bit different this year? >> Sorry, you say that again? Yes. Yeah, obviously Ryan's come in and he's got a wealth of experience from Minnesota and Ryan's obviously worked with the all-pro kicker last year in in Record and just for me it's great to be picking his brains cuz he's been so experienced. He's had four years already in the league. Had a really really good year last year and deserved what he got when he when he came here. And it's great for me to just be able to pick in somebody's brains who's been doing it for a long time and obviously I've got Zach who's been here the whole time and it's been great and Zach's amazing and so really the the the chemistry hasn't really changed too much because it's it kind of starts with the snapper and then the holder adjusts to what I want and you know, so it's been good that that way and yeah, it was great. We were around at Ryan's house all the coaches there specialists and we had a dinner last week and it was great just you know girlfriends and wives all met up and it was it was a good time. Yeah, so it's yeah, we're we're still building that relationship. We're still getting to know each other and it's it's been awesome so far and hopefully that continues that way. >> Do you have any thoughts on the World Cup? >> Yeah, so it was funny actually. I was just hoping anybody but England would win. >> So cuz as in Ireland we obviously Gaelic football is our main sport and we don't make the World Cup very often but if we don't make it then it's like okay just anybody but England so I thought Spain would win and and they did so yeah, it was good but again I was at home for the three weeks and then the games were on a bit later so I wasn't really too focused with you know being on the sofa. I was more out and about with my friends and family and enjoying the late evenings and having a good time at home. >> So was it your hometown Gaelic football club that >> So that's funny actually. So I'm from Mayo Bridge but that's County Down. But Mayo the county they're out in in the west and there's actually a funny story with that so they haven't won an All-Ireland championship in 75 years and there was a curse put on them and since 1989 they've lost 11 All-Ireland finals. And the curse was when they last won in a priest came out and they they were kind of like partying and celebrating through a funeral and in Ireland you're supposed to turn the the car off the engine off and be respectful but the priest because they were kind of disrespectful to the funeral the priest says as long as every member on this team is alive you'll never win another All-Ireland and the last member of the team died in 2023 and the last 11 All-Ireland finals since and they won it there on Sunday morning and it was absolute scenes back home so >> I would I would encourage everybody to listen to the Midwest radio commentary of that it's absolutely brilliant. >> I actually I knew that story but I I thought it was your hometown so I >> Yeah, yeah, yeah. No, no, not quite my hometown. I But But yeah, I know. So, It was good story, yeah. Yeah, it was it was a good feel good story for everybody at home. So, uh >> All right, story time over. >> Yeah. Yeah. All right, yeah. Sorry, I keep keep me off the hook. Yeah. >> I was watching you throw the ball. It's funny seeing the the Irish guy and the Australian guys try to throw a football and be like, "Oh, you've been playing for Yeah, yeah, yeah. It's It's not pretty, but maybe we can talk around that. Yeah. Yeah. All right, thanks everybody. >> See you back. >> All right, hey fellas.

title: Chase Young on edge rusher group, Kaden Elliss | Saints Training Camp 2026
text: Chase how do you feel about the edge group this year getting after it today? >> Yeah man, we're getting after it. Uh comfortable going into year two um in this in this scheme. Um so everybody uh we we clicking from day one. >> What is it about this scheme that just led to your breakout year last year as far as you know career accolades and sacks? >> Yeah man, shoot. Not playing a full eye, not playing six eye, playing on the edge. Um just being able to fly. >> How nice is it, you know, to see how you had 10 sacks in 12 games? >> Like this this scheme is great for me. Like I imagine, you know, what I'll do before season. I mean, how much does that give you even more confidence and and how nice is that? >> It's it's nice man. Just taking it one day at a time man. Uh day to day we in camp. We we trying to get through camp right now. Um and uh I know if we just taking it one day at a time and, you know, stay locked in and uh you know, the sky's the limit for our defense. >> Chase, I may be reading too much into still pictures, but uh they sent out the pictures and the videos of you guys even when the workout program started in March and April and OTAs and all that. After you said at the end of last season you finally feel like you found a home. I mean, did that carry over through the off season and and energize you through that whole process? >> Yeah, I feel like uh for sure. Um think I I I'm out I I I worked the whole off season you know, since we I think I took like four days. Um but I just know uh I just know what I can do. and it'd be a shame if I don't show it. >> Chase, uh last year like Cam and some other of your teammates were kind of vocal about like we need a lot from Chase Young. What did that do for you kind of in the moment during the on the motivation and >> Yeah, I mean uh motivation for sure, but um you know, my teammates I know they got faith in me. Um just how I got faith in them. Um and it's just one of those things like even this year we need some guys to step up. Right? Bresee just went down. We're going to need, you know, uh Vernon to step up. We're going to need J.R. to step up. We're going to need Shed We're going to need all the whole interior D-line to step up. Um and you know, and I have faith that they will. >> Can you talk about that room a little bit? What do you like about them? What do you see from them? A little bit of mixed everything. >> I mean now, we you know, down the from top to bottom, we got horses. We got big boys. They they they can run. Um they're physical. Um they're everything that you want from a real, you know, that old school interior nasty D-line. Um you know, from Divine Guerschon to JR to Vernon to to Shep, you know, them boys ain't nothing to play with. Um and I you know, that's one thing I I I I feel like us as a defense never worried about was our interior D-line cuz we know them boys is nasty and they're just ready to play. >> Chase, I think Brandon said you you can be a dominant defender in this league. Do you feel like you're just kind of scratching the surface? So, how how much more do you feel like you have? I guess we're going to see. I'm going to take it I'm going to take it one day at a time and and just stay locked in. We're going to see what happens. >> Chase, in addition to opportunity, is there anything you think you're doing better than you ever have before in the last year or so? >> Uh I think this year I'm just trying to, you know, I want to be in the the best shape I can, you know, never have to come off the field. >> How would you describe your day-to-day time and playing? I mean, is that Is that what's kind of helps allow you to >> Say it one more time. >> you keep mentioning like one day at a time, taking like that, not thinking like too much big picture. Is that kind of allowed you to have success like having that mentality? And how important is that mentality for your day-to-day? >> Yeah, man, you know, that's uh I feel like you get anxiety when you think about the future and you think about the past. You know, I just feel like if you just live today through the present, you know, you don't got to really worry about tomorrow cuz I'm taking care right now. So, um you know, like Coach Daily, you know, he say just take care right now. Um you know, I'm about to go do some uh I'm about to go lift and that's where I'm about to be at, you know. I'll worry about tomorrow tomorrow. >> Could you talk about your relationship with Coach Daily? It seems like he did a lot of things right to free you up, right? >> Yeah, man, I think it's just his defense. His defense is built around his edge uh edge rushers. Um you know, his defense needs good edge rushers and he needs us to to be great. Um you know, to make our defense thrive. So, um you know, it's uh it's something when your coach has faith in you and you don't want to let him down. Right? Um so, I feel like me and Coach Staley uh we have a great relationship and uh you know, you know, if if if if I'm be one of his horses and I'm I'm I'm a hustle. >> He was just talking about you from day one. Like you felt that from the minute he walked in the building. >> Yeah, for sure. For sure. I mean, uh you know, we we have our we have our talks. Um and um you know, I just know if I I stick to it then um you know, we're going to make some shake. >> So, what have you seen early on when it comes to adding Kayden Ellis to the interior as an interior pass rusher in the run game as well? >> Yeah, man. I'm excited cuz uh Kayden, he's going to help us as a D-line um out. Um he's a known rusher. Uh when when Kayden comes to the line of scrimmage, they have to account for him. Period. Um so, you know, what that does is it takes the chippers off us. You know, might make a team go 5-0 um and we get our one-on-ones. >> Saw a couple sequences where Kayden was lined up right next to you when y'all about to rush the passer. What are you thinking when you know y'all are both going to go off that same edge? >> You know, we we know that we can uh play off each other. Um you know, just with our defense, you know, with the certain calls we got where he is lined up with me, even when he's lined up on other side of the line uh with Grandon, um it's all built in together. So, um we we we're definitely all excited. >> Chase, that approach you were talking about not getting too high, too low. Is that something you uh have always had and it's helped you deal with the ups and downs of your career or you developed that after some of the >> Well, I mean, l- life is ups and downs. You got your ups and downs, right? >> Yeah. >> Okay. So, it's it's not about football. It's about life. Um you know, in in life life ain't easy. I just play football. You know, so you you you can't you can't be too high, you can't be too low. You just got to ride that wave through and through. >> I know you mentioned Ryan earlier. I mean, you've been through this fortune like that in your career, I mean >> Right. >> What do your thoughts go when you see a a brother and a teammate go down? >> Um It's it's it's saddening cuz I know what what year he wanted to have this year. you know, I was I was I was excited for him about this year. I would say the bright side is you know, ACLs now we know you can get back. Right? So, that's the bright side and I say just, you know, just attack it. Um we know that you're going to heal. We know you're going to get better. And um you know, you know what you got to do when you get back. That's you know, that's name of the game. >> Coaches have kind of mentioned, you know, your path or your model as an example for Tyree Wilson. How can you kind of help with his development and what do you just say to him? >> Yeah. Yeah, man, it's uh you know, Tyree great player, tall with 40-in arms, arms longer than mine. Like he, you know, if he extends his arms, you can't touch him. Like um and that's a definitely a big thing that we've been telling him like use your length. Um but I think he's going to be a real great addition for us, a real big monster coming off the edge who's athletic, who's able to bend. Um I'm excited for him especially um in in this defense um where it's you know, where edge rushers can you know, where edge rushers can fly. >> When you mentioned earlier that you know, your teammates have faith in you and they have faith in you like that and then you go out and produce the way that they have confidence in you. What does that do for you as well? >> Uh it just sets a standard. Um I think what I did last year, it just set a standard for me for this year, right? Everything I I see all y'all now what I did last year. Now y'all got expectations, which I don't really look at, but you know, um you know, I'm just that's why I just take it day-to-day. My teammates can have expectations for me. My coach can have expectations for me and and that's what we talk about and that's why we take it day-to-day and and don't worry about the future. We worry about this lift. A great one, man. Juwan, man, one of the best tight ends in the league, especially in terms of catching the ball and getting open. I think he proved it last year. I think he was top eight in yards this year. Top four. Excuse me. My bad, Juwan. All [laughter] right, top eight. You know, I mean, he he's going to do it again this year. I have no doubt about it. Excited for him. You know, he's getting just like me, year two on the same scheme. You know, everybody's comfortable. He's comfortable. It's no thinking. He can just run out on the field and play fast. That's that's my brother, man. We stick close and I'm just excited for him, man. >> We talked a lot last year about it, but what does a second year in the system really unlock you as a player? >> Just being comfortable, man. Just from day one, like yesterday, it was literally no thinking, right? Cuz you know, the first time you get into a scheme and you know, you just got to make sure, especially the first time, where either I'm dropping or he's dropping. It's like you got to get that down, but now it's just like we already know. You know, we season. You know, we just comfortable when we step on the grass. >> Do you actually have me bumping into Chuck out there? >> Yeah, man. You know, sometimes you just you just full head of steam. It's a I don't want to stop too fast. >> [laughter] >> You talked a lot last year about what DeMario Davis meant to you. Do you feel like you're you're one of the people that can help fill the void there? >> For sure. said >> he brings it in all areas. >> Sure, man. I'm ready, man. I'm I'm ready. Um I'm ready, man. I've I've been working. Uh you know, I've been playing football my whole life for for these types of moments, so um I'm not the person to shy away from leadership or um anything like that. I'm I'm definitely noted I'm capable of filling the void. Um and I believe I will. >> You spoke about the athletic players that have to pick the chapter. What are your early impressions of the rookie Christian Barmore? >> Man, big. He big, man. He big, athletic, and he nasty, man. He might talk a little something to you. You know, I I we like that. You know, we like you know, we like to you know, be yourself, right? Be confident on the field. If you if you like to talk trash, do it. I know I do, so you know, we we love that. That just fuels that gives us energy. Um gives everybody else energy and uh just keeps the the practice exciting. >> Do you have a specific kind of trash talk you lean into? >> Yeah, I can't say it up here, man. >> Um you you said last year uh I think Mike just talked about it mentioned it to you about feeling like you found a home here in New Orleans. This off season, you see guys like Cam Jordan and Alvin Kamara extend their options to be able to finish off as a lifer here. What does that mean for you as a player, too? >> Uh it means a lot, man. I'm just excited to get AK back. Um I still say he one of the best when he get the ball in his hands. Uh very the most durable player. dynamic when he gets it, hard to bring down. Um you know, not a lot of running backs you can say that's just flat out better than AK. I don't care, you know, how old he is or regardless, he's one of the best. Um Cam Jordan, um you know, I'm definitely excited to get him back. Uh just one of those um guys that uh I I like I said, I get nuggets from every day just about learning how to be a pro. Uh you know, give me tips on talking to y'all. Um you know, just all around the all around the board. >> And just for your your kind of like future prospects with the team to see, you know, what kind of commitment both ways like that. >> For sure. For sure. I mean, that that that's a testament to Mickey, Kai, um the front office. Um you know, I mean, if they weren't doing the right thing, who knows what Cam and AK would have done, right? Um you can just I mean, just being here their whole career, um you know that it's uh it's just a it's a family environment here. And you know, that's what you just know about New Orleans Saints since since I was a kid, um just a great place to be, great front office, and place that wins. >> Chase, have you seen much difference in Kellen Moore from year one you mentioned to this year? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah, I mean I mean, I think he was comfortable when he got here. I mean, you know, where he came from, what he did, um you know, even go look at his college stats. I mean, he always been a dog. So, I mean, it's he never shied um from anything. Um and uh you know, he he he's on what he has to do as a coach, and we see that, and that's why we trust him as our leader. >> Chase, how do you How would you describe your relationship with >> Ooh. Loud, talkative, Energizer Bunny. you know, man, just uh you know, we going we going to lead together, right? Even if I don't have the energy that day, I know Granderson going to have it for me. If he don't have it, I know Cam going to have it. It's like we all hold each other to um just a high standard. Uh you know, um all together. So, um yeah, man, we uh we we we going to be ready to rock week one. >> What would it mean to you to have a captain's badge this year? >> Uh it it it it it'll mean everything, man. Um to be recognized by um your teammates um as a guy who's leading, it'll be great thing. >> Thanks, Chase. Chase. Chase.

text: [music] Guys, I'll just open it up. Ready to go. >> What happened on the play? The interception from Tyler that uh Quincy Riley got was that a mismutation? >> Yeah, Quincy made a good play. Yeah, we'll we'll use training camp and preseason games and all these opportunities to kind of evaluate that and we'll we'll have a good opportunity there. We got some talented guys in that room. Obviously not playing much last year, but how has he grown just over the last year from from that injury and all that? >> Yeah, I thought he put together a plan that was good from uh the circumstance that he was dealt. he was limited for his movement through most of the season as he was recovering, but you know, he was in here as much as he can with recovery with the weight room, uh, still being around the team and kind of seeing the football aspect of it. And so, um, obviously, you know, we drafted him for a reason. We felt really good about him coming in. I felt like he had a great fall camp last year and, uh, now it's time to get take advantage of this one. >> What's that about having Chase? Yeah, Chase Chase is playing really good football and uh you know, he's going to continue to get better and u you know, we feel really good about where he's going. >> How valuable is the veteran experience of a guy like Nathan Shepard who's played a similar role to what Brazy's done? >> Yeah, Shep's played a lot of football. Um you know, obviously he's getting acclimated as he's kind of gone through. He wasn't around a ton during the spring, but he'll get acclimated just like all these other guys and uh it'll be a great opportunity. >> Ken, can you talk about your kickers competition? What do you like about them? >> Yeah. Yeah, I think yeah, we got two talented guys. Uh they both uh are ready to go and have earn earned the right to compete for this thing and so this will be an everyday process. Uh you know, we'll alternate them every day uh leading up to those preseason games and uh this will be a great opportunity for both of them. >> Kell, have you I'm assuming you saw Taesm's message, the the farewell message he sent to News. What did that happen [clears throat] for one season? What did it mean to for his message and the city and the fans for him to send that out after this long time here? >> Yeah, Ta's the best. He's uh one of the best people you ever meet uh in this world. Uh he's a phenomenal person, player, competitor. Uh for him to come back from that injury. Uh the previous season was incredible and uh you know, he he's had so much success in this uh community. Um playing for the Saints and the impact he's had on this community has been awesome. And uh you know, he's a guy that a lot of our guys can look to as an example of, you know, growing in the NFL and finding roles and finding opportunities. And um you know, everyone's for the last few years been chasing let's find the next TAM and there's really just one TAM. Have you had conversations with him either right before then or right after like in the last week let's say? Have you guys talked and and how did that I don't know decision you know come about? >> I have I have not talked to him very recently. Uh I saw him once at during the summer and uh you know Mickey's talked to him a few times through the spring and I've met I've talked to him but uh you know that it's kind of those personal matters and uh but he's been great through this whole thing. >> Would you say it was mutual between the two of you? The fact that he's not here. I >> I think he's at that stage of his career where he's just kind of navigating uh you know a lot of variables but uh you know I can't say enough good things about Tason the person and what he did for our team last year. I mean to to hang with uh when you're a veteran like that and to hang with a situation where we're you know in some challenging situations. Uh he was one of the big time leaders that helped us get through all that. >> Did you ever have to sign off on 100 records wearing seven? [laughter] >> I don't get a whole lot involved with numbers to be honest. So uh I saw seven. >> We're going to talk to Jon here in a second. What do you like about your tight end? How much more can you utilize that? >> Yeah, depth, versatility. It's important that these guys um you know at the end day they got to be able blocking the run game in some capacity and we got to find that which works and so uh Jan's done a great job every year of just growing into that tight end role being somewhat new to it a few years ago and so um yeah he's going to be a leader of our team >> back to the young obviously he had 10 last year bring back saw a play where both rushing off the same [clears throat] pass rush Yeah, rushing the passer. I mean, there's a lot of that goes into it. And I think the amount of pieces that you have that can rush in various ways is obviously going to be a huge asset. And so when you have uh guys that can rush off the edge, rush uh interior, and then, you know, from a second level linebacker position, that just adds things at the end day. Um it's a math problem. You're trying to isolate people and create opportunities oneonone. >> How did Chris Rump's um going to off linebacker kind of pull it out? >> Just an offseason discussion of trying to find value. uh as much as we can for him in various roles like a lot of these guys are always trying to find different opportunities. He's played really good on the edge in the NFL for a long time. He's obviously a big-time special teams player. Um he's always played that and so now it's hey we feel good about our edges but also how can we add some components that maybe put him off the ball so far? >> Great. Great. He kind of started it right at the end of OTAAS the last few days and then u he's got a lot of exposure early on in camp so far and I thought it's been really good. Obviously seem to have a little bit different kind of connection with Tyler. They they seem to they seem to see each other a lot. >> Yeah. Yeah. I think that's a fair assessment. They uh they have some history together previously and so u I think they work really hard together during the offseason. So all those guys when you invest a lot of time in into this thing together and the amount of throws that you make together um inevitably you know you're going to have a higher level of comfort. >> Did uh anything happen with that looked like Ike was out there at the end? Yeah, I think he just kind of rolled rolled his ankle a little bit. So, uh, just precautionary. Nothing big. >> Uh, you weren't here obviously for Kaden Ellis's first, >> you know, time with the team. What did you hear about him from the front office guys who wanted to bring him back and then what have you kind of learned about him since he's been here? >> Yeah, I knew the football player. Uh, the person was raved about as soon as it came up as a possibility and so this this building has a lot of uh appreciation, respect for him. Uh obviously the football player I've seen him you know particularly in Atlanta the last few years. Uh we played him each each year and so uh saw the impact he has on the field. >> And I mean from your own experience you were you know undrafted free agent built a career in the NFL for a guy to be a seventh round pick to kind of ascend to where he's at right now you know third contract all that sort of like how rare is that I guess as a >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, and I I think it's credit to him of his development in the NFL. Uh even when he maybe didn't play as much early uh because there was so much depth at linebacker here. He's a guy who came in, he played everything at Idaho. I remember him, you know, just because I, you know, connections back there and it's like he played every position, you know, he was just kind of there do it all. He'd play offense, he played defense, and so uh it was just a matter of time defining what his role is. And so, uh he's a versatile player. He's he's really talented. >> How do you think you guys will be able to generate the same type of interior push? Is that that that's still goals don't change. Uh goals don't change. We still got, you know, plenty of guys in there that uh we'll we'll be able to take advantage of an opportunity. >> What have you seen so far from Kristen Miller as just as a part of that as early? >> Yeah. Yeah. Limited exposure, I think, for all these defensive linemen. Once we get to pads, it gets a little bit more uh accurate evaluation. And so, you know, it's just a matter of time to see these guys going. But Christian's done an awesome job. He's he's been phenomenal all offseason. uh coming, you know, through a rehab process early and then uh working his way to where he's at right now. >> Kind of the emphasis on the run today, kind of an anticipation of pads. >> Yeah. Yeah. Um yeah, every day we're going, you know, again, training camp is your number one opportunity for the run game on both sides of the football. So, as much exposure as we can get, that's critical. >> It's not hold out, but they're moving to hold. I guess you have two high profile players that are doing it the right way. What does that mean to an organization and for you to be able to have them here? Work through there off the field issues but be on the field. >> Yeah, I think the biggest thing is there's business side and there's the football side obviously and we know sometimes those two overlap. Uh it's inevitable and I think communication is the key as long as we all communicate. We're all on the same page. Um the thing we always have to remind ourselves everyone's everyone has the same goal. Uh everyone's shooting for the same things. Uh it's just, you know, sometimes the business side takes a little bit of a a lead on this for for a matter of time and we'll just work through that. >> Thanks, Helen. >> Okay. Thanks, guys. >> Thanks. >> What excites you about having a full year now to play in this system, all the other wide receiver pieces in this room for you guys? >> Uh it's it's exciting for me. Um understanding the playbook a lot better, not having to worry too much about the X's and O's, but actually being able to go out there and uh you know, play the game that I how I play. um showcasing what I can do and I'm excited for our room as well. We got a lot of talent in a wide receiver room. Uh the rookies hold us to a high standard as well. They're always asking great questions. Uh eager to learn and so it's help pushing us as vets um you know have that spark as well and you know surprised a lot of people this year. >> How much enthusiasm do you have coming into this season especially after the way you hit a stretch last year and then it ends prematurely? >> No, I'm excited. Uh obviously I want to stay healthy as much as I can. So, that's that's my number one goal this season. But, you know, I want to contribute as much as I can to the team, whatever they need me to do in uh blocking, pass catching, or even supporting the guys from the sideline, whatever they need me to do. At the end of the day, we want to win games and, you know, make the playoffs. And so, that's that's our goal and that's what we're we're aiming for. >> Now, does it excite you when Kell says, you know, hey, we need to find ways to get him the ball more. >> Yeah, I mean, obviously any receiver you can ask them, they would want the ball 100 times out of 100. Um, like I said, I'm one of those guys that even if I don't get the ball a lot, uh, as long as I'm contributing and helping the team win, that's all I care about at the end of the day. >> Last season, you did really start to hit the ball a lot more. What do you think changed? >> I think it's just opportunities. Uh, I don't think it's anything too crazy to where like, hey, we came into this game plan, we're going to throw Bailey the ball. I think it was more so, you know, I got in the right spots at the right time. Chuck trusted me, gave me opportunities to make plays, and I made them. >> So, I I mean, assume this is an obvious answer. Is it frustrating when when it finally starts to click to to have it like end like that? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, it it was definitely hard mentally um you know, especially building that chemistry with him, but um at the end of the day, gave other guys opportunities to make plays um and you know, kind of catapulted us into this season, understanding, okay, what kind of guys do we have in the room? What can we do with that? And obviously make a push for the playoffs this year. >> And I I mean, you guys added so much of the skill position, whether it's the tight ends, running backs, receivers. Um, is there kind of a sense of like like a lot of miles to feed and like how do you kind of navigate that, balance that and all that? >> I mean, like I said, at the end of the day, we care about winning games. Um, I I think individual stats is what's going to hinder a team if you're only chasing those things. At the end of the day, we want to make the playoffs. Obviously, win a Super Bowl. And so, we're going to make sure we give the guys that give us the best opportunity to do that. And if that means somebody's got to touch the ball more, then that's that's what we're going to do. >> And then Justin Reed was talking yesterday about just the way Tyler throws the ball. just kind of describing it as like it's got zip and it's catchable, you know? >> How would you describe that? And just like as a as a receiver, is it receiver friendly the way he throws the ball? I >> I think it it for sure is. I think the other thing I like about the way Chuck plays is uh he gives guys opportunities. Um I know there's some guys uh who if they see their guy covered, they're not going to give it a shot unless he's wide open. But Chuck is one of those guys that he'll put the ball somewhere where he believes that his guys going to make the play outside of the defender. And so, um, you know, as receivers, we appreciate that a lot because that means he has a lot of trust in us and we just got to make sure we reciprocate that back to him by making those plays. >> The Miami touchdown being an example of that last year. >> Yes, that's a perfect example. Yeah. >> Do you see more of those opportunities in a training camp setting where, you know, the risk is different, but you can take a little bit more kind of risk in these situations? >> Yeah. And I I feel like it's also one of those things it it helps him understand uh which guys he can trust, but on top of that, it helps him um you know, find that that good balance of when it's a little too risky and when he can push it a little bit. Uh kind of letting his own character shows the way he plays. And so uh it helps us as receivers understand like even if we're running a route that we're not expecting the ball, we should be expecting it because Chuck's going to be the one to throw it. So uh I think training camp is a perfect opportunity to do something like that. with how limited last year was when you we talked yesterday about the trip to San Diego. How beneficial was that for you and push to build that chemistry with Tyler to get you quick? >> Yeah, it's good. I mean, you get outside of football uh get in a setting where you guys are training together, but you also spend some time outside of that understanding there's more things to football um outside of it. And so, um you know, building that camaraderie and that brotherhood, I think it helps a lot, especially when you know, we get into those uh points in the season where things may start getting tough. Um, it helps us understand that we we got brothers we could depend on, we can turn to, and uh, help keep pushing us to be great. >> We've talked about the versatility of this offense, but what does it do for a player as far as making things a little easier for you, getting better, those kind of things? >> Could you repeat that again? >> Just the versatility of the weapons around you. Does that open up the game a little bit more for you individually or whoever it might be? >> Oh, yeah. Absolutely. I I think it's one of those things uh when you have depth, it helps it a lot where um say you you get tired, you're gassed and you need to take a play or two off, you you can trust the guy that behind you that he's going to bring the same energy, same level of play, maybe in a different play style that even when you're out, you guys are still not missing the stride and able to make plays and keep driving the ball down the field. And so I feel like we have that as an offensive unit. Um obviously we're going to keep continuing to build and fix the little things. That's that's the point of what training camp is for. And so, uh, we're finding those guys with that versatility and those guys that we can trust. You >> know, Jaylen Bul was here last year, but now that you're finally getting to see him do stuff, but he's, you know, what what have you made of him and just, you know, after knowing him and seeing him go out there, >> he's a very professional player. Uh, I I respect his game a lot. Um, he's very smooth with the way he runs his routes. Um, and he's a very smart player as well. Understands the plays, understands coverages, and so, um, I'm excited for him. I know uh there's been things about him, but I I I think he's one of those players that's gonna shock a lot of people and I'm excited for him this year. >> When you were out in San Diego, you get to meet and talk to Drew Brees. >> I So I actually wasn't able to make it out there. I had a family emergency that occurred. So I unfortunately wasn't able to make it, but from what I heard, I heard it was it was a lot of fun. A lot of the guys kind of were fangirling, seeing Drew Brees and all that stuff. So it was pretty cool. >> Thank you. Thank you so much. everything up. >> Chase, how how you feel about the uh edge group this year? Getting after it today. >> Yeah, man. Getting after it. Uh comfortable going in year two um in this in this scheme. Um, so everybody, uh, we we clicking from day one. >> What is it about this team that just led to your breakout year last year as far as, you know, career accolation sacks? >> Yeah, man. Yeah, I feel like uh for sure. Um I think I I mean I worked the whole off season, you know, since we I think I took like four days. Um but I just know uh I just know what I can do. Um and it'd be a shame if I don't show it. >> Hey Chase, uh last year like Cam and some other few of your teammates were kind of vocal about like we need a lot from Chase Young. What did that do for you kind of in the moment in terms of kind of motivation or anything? >> Yeah, I mean I uh motivation for sure, but um you know my teammates I know they got faith in me um just how I got faith in them. Um and it's just one of those things like even this year we need some guys to step up right just went down. We going to need you know uh Vernon to step up. We going to need JR to step up. We going to need Shep. We going to need all the whole interiority line to step up. Um and you know and I have faith that they will. >> Tell me about that room a little bit. What do you like about them? you see comes in a little commit to everything. >> I mean, no, we, you know, down to from top to bottom, we got horses. We got big boys. They they they can run. Um, they physical. Um, they're everything that you want from a real, you know, that old school interior nasty D line. Um, you know, from Devon Gotcha to JR to Vernon to to Shep, you know, them boys ain't nothing to play with. Um, and you know, that's one thing I I I I feel like us as a defense never worried about was our interior D line because we know them boys was nasty and they just ready to play. >> Chase, I think Brandon said you you can be a dominant defender in this league. Do you feel like you just kind of scratching the surface or how how much more do you feel like you have? >> I guess we going to see. I'm going take it take it one day at a time and and just stay locked in. We're going to see what happens. In in addition to opportunity, is there anything you think you're doing better than you ever have before in the last year or so? >> Uh, I think this year I'm just trying to, you know, >> I want to be in the best shape I can, you know, never had to come off the field. >> How would you describe one day at a time? I mean, is that is that what's kind of helped allow you to >> say it more time? >> Uh, you keep mentioning like one day at a time taking like that, not thinking too much big picture. So, um you know, like coach Staley, you know, he say just take care right now. Um you know, I'm about to go do some uh I'm about to go lift and that's where I'm about to be at. you know, I'll worry about tomorrow. >> Could you talk about your relationship with coach Staley? Seems like he did a lot of things right to free you up, right? >> Yeah, man. I think it's just his defense. His defense is built around his edge uh edge rushers. Um you know, his defense needs good edge rushers and he needs us to to be great. Um you know, to make our defense thrive. So, um you know, it's uh it's something when your coach has faith in you and you don't want to let him down, right? Um, so I feel like me and Coach Staley, uh, we have a great relationship and, uh, you know, you know, if if I'm be one of his horses and I'm I'm I'm a hustle. >> And he was talking about you from day one, like you felt that from the minute he walked in the building. >> Yeah, for sure. For sure. I mean, uh, you know, we have our we have our talks. Um, and um, you know, I just know if I I stick to it, then um, you know, we going to make something shake. What have you seen early on when it comes to adding Kaden Ellison as an interior pass? >> Yeah, man. I'm excited because uh Kaden, he's going to help us as a Dline um out. Um he's a known rusher. Uh when Kaden comes to the line of scrimmage, they have to account for him, period. Um so, you know, what that does is it takes the chippers off of us. You know, might make it 10 go 5. Um and we get our one-on- ones. >> Saw a couple sequences where Kaden was lined up and you're right next to you when you're about to rush the pass you. What are you thinking? You know, y'all are both going off that same match. >> You know, we we know that we can uh play off each other. Um you know, just with our defense, you know, with the certain calls we got where he is lined up with even when he's lined up on the other side of the line, uh with Grando, um it's all built in together. So, u we we're definitely all excited. >> Chase, that approach you were talking about not getting too high, too low. Is that something you uh have always had and it's helped you deal with the ups and downs of your career or you developed that after some of the >> Well, I mean, life is up and downs. You got your ups and downs, right? >> Yeah. >> Okay. So, it's it's not about football. It's about life. Um, you know, and life life ain't easy. I just play football, you know.
