I mean in terms of you leading your family, you you know you're leading you know your job or whatever just leading yourself. Somebody has some sort of accountability and leadership. Um but for him he's always had it. And the thing is I think um you know Kell is nourishing that like he's kind of nurturing that by having him to you know break it down and stuff like that. I think that's good not for just him but I think for everybody to get accustomed to his voice and him being that presence and I think that's really good and the testament to Kell just be like this is who we're going to hear. This is our guy. This is our leaders our quarterback and um you know and uh I think Tyler's kind of ran with it. He's been good especially in the offseason you know taking us his guys on trips getting together you know kind of having some camaraderie. I think that's been the biggest thing for us. >> Could you describe your connection with him on the field? It seems like you two guys are on the same page a lot, right? >> Yeah. Uh I just know where he wants me and I think that's the biggest thing. Um you know, when you you spend a lot of time together and like you you watch film together and you know, you kind of see where he his eyes are at. You know, he sees where my eyes are at. And honestly, I just try to be savvy and I think he's you know, he kind of reads where I'm supposed to be. I think it's the biggest thing. Having a lot of reps with a quarterback, I think, is the biggest thing. And um you know it's kind of tough when you're on the sideline trying to figure out like you know but if you're watching film and you know you're having actual reps with him. I think that's the biggest thing >> that's been good for us. >> Savvy is that like is that a word that you would say that like that's your biggest like strength. That's your superpower is like knowing where the holes are and knowing where to find spots. >> Yeah, I would say I mean I'm some people say like I'm fast quick but I'm not the fastest guy. I mean I'm a big guy. Um, I mean there's some attributes about me that are different from other tight ends, but I feel like the biggest thing that kind of had me to stick is just, you know, being smart about coverages and being smart about where, you know, guys are at and treating leverages and trying to trick the defender and things like that. That's kind of like been my thing, just to have like a little edge cuz I mean, think about NFL, everybody's the same speed, everybody's same height, all that. But if you could have like a quick edge, that's kind of been like, you know, my MO. >> Is it different this year to last? Do you feel more comfortable? Uh in terms of what? >> Just your knowledge before those things that go into making. >> Yeah. Uh I would say a lot of it is yeah just you know being immersed in the offense you know just knowing that you don't have to learn a different offense probably the best thing for me. But um you know just going in and knowing that you know you have your your number one QB you know you got your running backs your tight ends you know your receivers. Cuz sometimes last year was just like man are we going to be a a one tight end you know set team or we going to be two or three you know you just you just never really knew. But I think since we have, you know, like kind of the offense under our belt, we kind of know what we're going into. You kind of know where you're going to be. You know, if they say 11, 12, 13 personnel, I know 13 personnel, I'm probably going to be outside. So, just knowing like where you're going to be in certain situations, it's been really good for me. >> What differences do you notice in the run game? >> Sure. >> Yeah. in terms just like >> just like I mean you guys brought in a Chan, you brought in David Edward and >> you have the possibility to run it in different ways with the different tight ends just >> like >> Well, I hope I run the ball. That'd be nice. Shoot, [laughter] that'd be good, too. Shoot. No, I mean it's it's it's I I think it's actually been good. We have a lot of um diversity. I remember I was talking to one of the tight ends yesterday looking at film. I was like, man, we got some nice running backs, let alone just like our addition. like we got nice running backs in the back field that we could do a lot with. I mean sometimes people just forget about Kendra. Like Kendra is explosive, dude. And so just knowing that, you know, you know, despite, you know, what he's been through, um he's still an explosive and exciting player. So, you know, just knowing things like that, you know, it's been good. And knowing that you have, you know, Trav in the back field, AK in the back field, it's just like you you have so much versatility that you can have. And so, we haven't even like scratched the surface of what we can do from a run game standpoint. we honestly have been keeping it, you know, pretty vanilla so far. But, um, I mean, I guess we we'll see in a couple weeks how it like pan out. But, I think, you know, in terms of just adding David, David has been really good for us. You know, that add knowing David is just like that guy on the left side, it's kind of like moving the whole line of scrimmage has been really good for, you know, our guys in the back field. >> Um, being an undrafted guy, making your way in the league, making a name for yourself. I mean, >> did Tason's journey at all kind of inspire you like while you were doing that because he was the guy that was here that >> had a similar path as well? Like was that inspiring at all for you during that process? >> Yeah. Uh his journey for sure. Um I I would say um Taesm's journey and a lot of guys just just been through the Saints, you know, organization. I feel like they have a great reputation of just hiring hiring um getting um undrafted guys. And so knowing that those guys that have come through the Saints organization have stuck and have been around um just kept their head down and just kind of pushed through has been honestly it's been one of the things that um I've really been like admiring like especially guys like Taesm, guys like Adam Thielen, you know, guys who've done a a great deal and have almost made like Pro Bowls and things like that. Um it's been really good for me to to see that cuz it's possible. You know, sometimes when people get undrafted, they think it's not possible to make an impact or, you know, not possible to make a team, but you know, if you keep your head down, you stay healthy. Um, and honestly, you're just not not making trouble. I think that's the biggest thing and just staying here. Like, it's not the most athletic guys who are making the teams. It's just like the guys who stick, who are smart, who are savvy, that's just, you know, who are able to just stick it out. >> How was the um touch on, but how was the trip to California? I think Tyler said your family stayed in the same house. >> Yeah. It was a full house. Um, three kids, you know, two dogs. Oh, man. It was it was a lot, but it was extremely fun. I think, you know, like like I was telling someone before, you know, when you when you have like camaraderie and you're able to be around people, even stay in the same house, I feel like you learn a lot about people. And I feel like, you know, and that translates on the field, believe it or not. Like, and people think it's not, but it does. It just it does something to you. like you just know where to be at the right time because you guys got up at the same time and ate breakfast together. Like I I don't know, but God just be doing stuff just like all right, you guys supposed to be on the same accord on this route right here and it just works. But I think the biggest thing is like I I know that I'm going to fight for him and I'm going to, you know, do whatever I can to make plays because, you know, we took that trip to San Diego or we started throwing routes in February or we went and did, you know, did some things together or went on a ride together. It's just like the things that you spend time together, you you you find ways to dig a little deeper because you know that person on a more intimate and deeper level. >> Did you learn something about him that you didn't know? >> All right. Y'all talking at the same time now. >> Well, there's some things you learned about him that you didn't know that that are sharable. >> Uh [sighs] let's see. Um yeah, so we're about to go on this ride and um you know this ride says 65 65 and below. So, there's a height maximum. So, I never knew that before at SeaWorld. And so, um, you know, we're going and the guy says, "Yeah, can we, uh, get your height?" And he just walks right by. So, he already knew that. He was probably going to be in some trouble. So, I was like, "All right. Well, I just can't ignore him." So, I sit there, you know, I get my height check. He said, "I'm good." He just got my haircut. So, I was like, "All right, I'm all right." So, we walking up and then we get to the ride and guy's like, he pulls us out of the ride like, "Hey, man. You guys got to get checked." I said, "We just got checked downstairs." Knowing that Tyler didn't. So, you know, we get our we get our head checked and we barely like we we grazing the line. So, I was like, man, just keep our feet up when we going through this ride, but it was it was amazing. But, um, one of those things is just, you know, when you determine to do something, cuz that was the only ride we went on. When you determine to do something, you just do it. And so, uh, I just thought it was funny that he just walked right by the dude. [laughter] And I don't know if you heard him or not, but I was like, dude, I know you heard him cuz I just heard him and we was right next to each other. But, uh, I What ride was it? I can't remember. But it was like only two two like high rides in SeaWorld. Not many of them. But uh we went on it and it was it was fun. It was a good time. But I was scared cuz I don't think we was going to be able to ride it. I never heard of height maximum. Like ride maximum. It's crazy. >> If we ever see Tyler listed as 66, we know he's wearing cleats in there. >> Yeah. No doubt. No doubt. That's a cle. He's definitely not 66. He's like six. Well, apparently 6'4 according to SeaWorld. >> 64. >> Yeah. [laughter] Yeah. Just like to see all doubt. That makes it [laughter] >> the dogs go along. >> Uh it wasn't my dogs cuz my dogs are not coming on that trip. I had two girls. I had the two girls and they had a great time with his dog Murphy and um you know my girls just love dogs. But I think the biggest thing is just getting a family together. you know, you had family together and knowing that y'all about to do something special. I think that's kind of the biggest thing and just and just friendship. Like I don't think it had to be transactional to translate the football, but it was just, you know, good to have the families together. >> You said y'all played board games, so this is your chance to air it out if he cheats at board games or >> No, I didn't play board games. I No, I ain't play board games with them. I know they was cheating cuz they was saying some stuff that I ain't I ain't know. So, I was like I think they was trying to play Clue and they like, "Oh, let's play Clue." I was like, "No, y'all been playing for a couple hours, so I'm good." Y'all start cheating, making up rules on me. I don't like that. >> I got a quick health science question. >> Health science? >> Yeah, maybe. We're working on a story. It's 25th anniversary of um Cory Stringer. >> Okay. >> Um so, being a hot weather team, are there things about the way the practice is um planned out that you can tell that heat exposure is a real consideration on how you know, the time of day they're putting you out there, how long they're putting you out there, and how they're monitoring you. >> Yeah. Um I think there's a benefit truly to us being out there um in the heat, I think it's an advantage for us to, you know, kind of go out and get it a little bit cuz let's say when you know the Jaguars are a team, you know, they have preseason, but say a team like LA, they come out here, it's going to be a totally different experience. And I think it's one of those things where we have an advantage. They kind of go into the year knowing that we've been in the heat, been accustomed to it, we've been grinding away, then we get into a cool area, you know, dome. I mean, we can really go and get it and get after some teams. But I think the biggest thing is, you know, us going out there at 9:00 a little different than going out there at 12 because we probably wouldn't be out there as long. But, um, I think there's a benefit to what Kellen and, you know, Ted Raph and those other guys are doing and keeping us safe and things like that. But um yeah, I think you know getting some heat exposure I think that's kind of been a good thing that kind of gets us into the year and gets us acclimated for you know the season what the season is about to present. >> How do they emphasize recovering from heat exposure? >> Well, we have three hours right now. Um we have three hours to kind of get our bodies back um cool down before we you know get into meetings and stuff. >> I think it's been a big thing. Yeah. And so I mean obviously we got IVs and we got all that but I mean the biggest thing is it's really on you like they can't they can't baby us and everything like we're we get paid a lot of money to to take care of our bodies and work out and do those other things. So you know we get done practice you know they give us three hours to recover, get your bodies back, hydrate, eat. Um, yeah. I I I've never been in a place where, you know, you get that much time off to get your body back. So, we could go into meetings and stuff like that because usually it's like right after or we get an hour and a half. And so, they are being cognizant of what, you know, we have with our time. But, I think us as adults, us as professional athletes, we know what to do to take care of our bodies. Thanks, John. Thanks, John. Absolutely. >> What does uh what does SeaWorld have you officially?

title: Saints lock in Olave: Is the offense fully-built and ready to compete for multiple seasons?
text: It took a little bit of time to get this one done, but the Saints and Chris Olave have finally agreed to a 4-year extension that is worth $33 million per year with $90 million guaranteed. Chris Olave and the Saints are locked in together through the 2030 season. Presumably, at least on paper, always always got to be a little bit aware how these things are going to play out down the line, but if Chris Paul's out and he keeps doing what he's doing, he's going to be here through 2030. And I think that's a great thing for this team. I think it's a great thing for Chris. I think it's a great example to set for the other players that if you put the team first and you work and you go to the off-season program and you're you're a leader of the team and you're embracing the younger players that they are going to take care of you. I think that's a great way to reset and have the culture built going forward. Now, a little bit of posturing, a little bit of loggerheads here at the end to get it over the finish line, but it got over the finish line 2 days in the camp. Really no harm done. Pads aren't even out yet. And now Chris is going to be able to get back on the field and get the work. And look, it was killing him not to practice. Um >> [laughter] >> I I think one of the reasons this got done even faster is because was because he was putting pressure on the situation to get it done. And it gets done and it gets done at a fair level. Drew Rosenhaus was here earlier this week before camp started. He was back out there again today. He went in there, he negotiated after practice today, and they got it done at $33 million per year. And I think that's a really good deal. I think it's a really good deal. And if you're looking for really good deals, you can also find them at Matt Bowers Auto Group. Any one of his locations will take care of you and get you into the car of your dreams. So, as we look at this, the guys ahead of him on the average annual value list, JSN, Ja'Marr Chase, Drake London, Justin Jefferson, CeeDee Lamb. And then it's Chris Olave at $33 million. Then after him, DK Metcalf, Garrett Wilson 32.5. That was the big comp for me. Shares the same agent, from the same school, basically the same draft pick, numbers are basically the same, basically the same number of games missed. Now, Garrett missed some games this season. I I think when you set them down on paper, they're basically the same exact player. Difference is Garrett got signed a year ago. So, you're coming a year later, you have to get above that number. And And they did. I always thought 32.5 was the number that they were going to have to try to overcome. I I just didn't see a reality where it was getting done for for less than that. And then obviously A.J. Brown's on there at 32. That's an older deal. Amon-Ra, I'll get back over it at some point. Aiyuk, Nico Collins at 30. McLaurin at 29. Tee Higgins at 28.7. And you keep going down the list until you get to like Alec Pierce and and some of those other guys. But, this is a deal now that that I think slots in exactly where it was supposed to slot in. A Drake London got signed earlier this offseason. Zay Flowers will probably get signed here in the coming days or weeks. And And he might top this deal. But, for now, Chris is the sixth highest-paid player in the league. He was on the a second-team All-Pro, which meant he was named one of the six best wide receivers in the NFL. Logically, it just kind of all comes together and settles in in a place that that makes a lot of sense. And you know, the details are going to be a big thing that matters here. We're going to see how it all looks and and what all the contingencies are and everything. From what I've been able to gather is that the the the 90 million guaranteed is a real number. So, that's a good thing for him. And um you know, I think the number overall is extremely healthy and respectful. And I think it's reflective of what he is to this team and and where it's going. And it's core piece. It's a core piece of the team. It's a guy that that deserved to be rewarded. He had earned it. And like I said, I think it's a good thing for this team for that to be the example to be set. Now, I know the big thing here getting on the field. Camp's underway, 2 days in, nothing's really missed yet, but there's a lot of momentum going forward for this offense and I think the sky's the limit for this team and that's why you do this deal. You You got Jordan Tyson on a rookie deal, you got your quarterback on a rookie deal, both your tackles are on rookie deals, now your wide receiver's paid. You got a lot of room and there's still like if you want to do invest even more in this offense, you could, but you got one big investment there, the rest of your team's basically free, ATN cost a little bit of money, um you know, Edwards cost a little bit of money, but in those big positions that cost big money right now, you're in a spot where you don't got to pay. There is a very wide open window here right now for this team and I think if you run your team in a structure to where you're paying one receiver and you're drafting and you're building and you're going like that, I I think your window here is open for quite a while. Next year is going to be all about defense, but this is the last piece to get set on that side of the ball and I think you have invested everything on that side. I think it is completely built now and I don't think there are big question marks on where you're going on offense. You've got your receivers, you've got your tight ends. Juwan just got paid, you just signed Fant, you just dropped drafted Doubs. Your offensive line, God willing, is set to where it should be and now you move forward like that and there aren't really big contracts to give out after this. You got Chase Young, that's the guy that's going to need a huge deal and after that, you're kind of set for a while. Like you're waiting for somebody else to step up and earn that money. So, they're in a very good place, they're in a very healthy place. Uh big deal done here, this is clear skies now. Cam Jordan's done, clear skies there. Alvin's done, clear skies there. Like they've settled all these waters, everything's in place. Now it's time to get rolling and get ready for football and I don't think there's anyone more excited about this, not the money, about playing football than Chris Olave, man. This guy just for years has been ready to win and this team is now in a position where it could theoretically win some games and if they do, he's going to be a big reason for it. Check his set, money set, offense is set. It's time for them to get rolling on that side of the ball.

title: Saints WR Devaughn Vele on offensive depth, building chemistry with Tyler Shough, Year 2 with Saints
text: What would excite you about having a full year now to play in the system like all the other boxes even pieces in this room and guys? >> Uh it's it's exciting for me. Um understanding the playbook a lot better and not having to worry too much about the X's and O's, but actually being able to go out there and uh you know, play the game that I how I play. Um showcasing what I can do and I'm excited for our room as well. We got a lot of talent in the wide receiver room. Uh the rookies hold us to a high standard as well. They're always asking great questions. Uh you get to learn and so it's all pushing us as vets um you know, have that spark as well and you know, surprise a lot of people this year. >> How much enthusiasm do you have coming into this season especially after the way you had a stretch last year and then it ends prematurely? >> Oh no, I'm excited. Uh obviously I want to stay healthy as much as I can. So that's that's my number one goal this season, but you know, I want to contribute as much as I can to the team whatever they need me to do and uh blocking, pass catching or even supporting the guys from the sideline, whatever they need me to do. At the end of the day we want to win games and you know, make the playoffs and so that's that's our goal and that's what we're we're aiming for. >> Does it excite you when Kellen says, you know, hey, we need to find ways to get him the ball more? >> Yeah, I mean obviously any receiver you can ask him they would want the ball 100 times out of 100, but um like I said, I'm one of those guys that even if I don't get the ball a lot, as long as I'm contributing and helping the team win, that's all I care about at the end of the day. >> Last season you did really start to get the ball a lot more. What do you think changed? >> I think it's just opportunities. Uh I don't think it's anything too crazy to where like, hey, we came into this game plan, we're going to throw Vay the ball. I think it was more so, you know, I got in the right spots at the right time. Chuck trusted me, gave me opportunities to make plays and I made them. >> So I I mean I assume this is an obvious answer. Is it frustrating when when it finally starts to click to to have it like end like that? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean it it was it was definitely hard mentally. Um you know, especially building that chemistry with him, but um at the end of the day it gave other guys opportunities to make plays um and you know, kind of catapulted us into this season understanding, okay, what kind of guys do we have in the room? What can we do with that? And obviously make a push for the playoffs this year. >> And I mean you guys added so much at the skill position where there's a tight end, running backs, receivers. Um So there's a kind of a sense of like like a lot of mouths to feed and like how do you kind of navigate that, balance that, and all >> I mean like I said, at the end of the day we care about winning games. Um I I think individual stats is what's going to hinder a team if you're only chasing those things. At the end of the day we want to make the playoffs, obviously win a Super Bowl. And so we're going to make sure we give the guys that give us the best opportunity to do that. And if that means somebody's got to touch the ball more, then that's that's what we're going to do. >> And then Justin Reed was talking yesterday about like just the way Tyler throws the ball. He's kind of describing it as like it's got zip and it's catchable, you know? Like like how would you describe that and just like as a as a receiver like is a receiver-friendly way to throw the >> Uh I think it it for sure is. I think the other thing I like about the way Shuck plays is he gives guys opportunities. Um I know there's some guys uh who if they see their guy covered, they're not going to give it a shot unless he's wide open. But Shuck is one of those guys that he'll put the ball somewhere where he believes that his guy is going to make the play outside of the defender. And so um you know, as receivers we appreciate that a lot because that means he has a lot of trust in us. And we just got to make sure we reciprocate that back to him by making those plays. >> The Miami touchdown being an example of that last year? >> Yes. That was a perfect example, yeah. >> Do you see more of those opportunities in a training camp setting where, you know, the risk is different but you can take a little bit more kind of risk in these situations? >> Yeah, and I feel like it's also one of those things it helps him understand uh which guys he can trust. But on top of that, it helps him um you know, find that that good balance of when it's a little too risky and when he can push it a little bit. Uh kind of letting his own character show is the way he plays. And so uh it helps us as receivers understand like even if we're running a route that we're not expecting the ball, we should be expecting it because Shuck's going to be the one to throw it. So uh I think training camp is a perfect opportunity to do something like that. >> With how limited last year was with football, we talked yesterday about the trip to San Diego how beneficial it was that you went through and to build that chemistry with Tyler to get your rhythm back. >> Yeah, it's good. I mean you get outside of football, uh get in a setting where you guys are training together, but you also spent some time outside of that, understanding there's more things to football um outside of it. And so, um you know, building that camaraderie and that brotherhood, I think it helps a lot, especially when, you know, we get into those uh points in the season where things might start getting tough. Um it helps us understand that we we got brothers we can depend on, we can turn to, and uh help keep pushing us to be great. >> We talked about the versatility of this offense, but what does it do for a player as far as the being a little easier for you, getting a better look at the >> Could you repeat that again? >> of the weapons around you, does that open up the game a little >> Oh, yeah, absolutely. I I I think it's one of those things is uh when you have depth, it helps it a lot where um say you you get tired, you're gassed, and you need to take a play or two off, you you can trust the guy that's behind you that he's going to bring the same energy, same level of play, maybe in a different play style that even when you're out, you guys are still not missing the stride and able to make plays and keep driving the ball down the field. And so, I feel like we have that as an offensive unit. Um obviously, we're going to keep continuing to build and fix the little things. That's That's the point of what training camp is for. And so, uh we're finding those guys with that versatility and those guys that we can trust. >> Now, Jalen Book was here last year, but now that you're finally getting to see him do stuff that he's he'll What do What have you made of him and just, you know, after knowing him and seeing him go out there and >> He's a very professional player. Uh I I respect his game a lot. Um he's very smooth with the way he runs his routes. Um and he's a very smart player as well, understands the plays, understands coverages. And so, um I'm excited for him. I know uh there's been things about him, but I I I think he's one of those players that's going to shock a lot of people, and I'm excited for him this year. >> When you were up in San Diego, were you able to meet talk to Drew Brees? >> Uh so, I actually wasn't able to make it out there. I had a family emergency that occurred. So, I I unfortunately wasn't able to make it, but from what I heard, I heard it was it was a lot of fun. A lot of the guys kind of were fan girling seeing Drew Brees and all this stuff. So, it was pretty cool.

title: Saints EDGE Chase Young talks building on success, depth behind Bryan Bresee, offseason mentality
text: Hey Chase, how do you feel about the edge group this year getting after it today? >> Yeah, man. We're getting after it. Comfortable going into year two in this in this game. After you said at the end of last season you finally feel like you found a home. I mean now we you know, down the and talked about it. We got horses. We got big boys. They they they can run. They physical. They everything that you want from a real, you know, that old school interior nasty D line. You know, from Javon Godchaux to JR to Vernon to to Shep. You know, them boys ain't nothing to play with. And I you know, that's one thing I I I feel like us as a defense never worried about like interior D line. We know them boys is nasty. They just ready to play. I guess we going to see. We're going to take it We're going to take it one day at a time and and just stay locked in. We're going to see what happen. >> In in addition to opportunity, is there anything you think you're doing better than you ever have before in the last year or so? >> I think this year I'm just trying to, you know, I want to be in the the best shape I can, you know, never have to come off the field. >> You keep mentioning the way you talk about the one day at a time thing. I mean, is that is that what's kind of helped allow you to >> Say it one time. >> You keep mentioning like one day at a time taking like that not taking like too much big picture. Is that kind of allowed you to have success like having that mentality and how important is that mentality for your day-to-day? >> I mean, you know, that's I feel like you get anxiety when you think about the future and you think about the past. You know, I just feel like if you just live today through the present, you know, you don't got to really worry about tomorrow cuz I'm taking care right now. So, you know, like coach Staley, you know, he say just take care right now. You know, I'm about to go do some I'm about to go lift. That's where I'm about to be at. You know, I'll worry about tomorrow tomorrow. >> Could you talk about your relationship with coach Staley? Seems like he did a lot of things right to free you up, right? >> Yeah, man, I think it's just his defense. His defense is built around his edge edge rushers. You know, his defense needs good edge rushers and he needs us to to be great. You know, to make our defense thrive. So, um you know, it's it's something when your coach has faith in you and you don't want to let him down. Right. So, I feel like me and coach Staley we have a great relationship and you know if I'm be one of his horses and I'm a hustler. >> He's talking about you from day one. Like you felt that from the minute he walked in the building. >> Yeah, for sure. For sure. I mean, uh you know, we have our we have our talks. Um and you know I just know if I stick to it then you know we're going to make some shake. >> What have you seen early on when it comes to adding Kenneth Murray to this defense? >> Yeah, man. I'm excited cuz Kenneth he's going to help us as a D-line out. He's a known rusher. When Kenneth comes into the line of scrimmage, they have to account for him. Period. So, you know, what that does is it takes the chippers off us. You know, it might make a team go 5-0 and we get our one-on-ones. >> So, a couple of sequences where Kenneth was lined up right next to you when you're about to rush the passer. What are you thinking when you know y'all are both going off that same edge? >> You know, we know that we can play off each other. Um you know just with our defense, you know, with the certain calls we got where he is lined up with. Even when he's lined up on the other side of the line with Grandall, um it's all built in together. So, we're we're we're definitely all excited. >> Chase, that approach you were talking about not getting too high, too low. Is that something you have always had and it's helped you deal with the ups and downs of your career or you developed that after some of the >> Well, I mean, life is up and down. You got your ups and downs, right? >> Yeah. >> Okay. So, it's it's not about football. It's about life. You know, in life life ain't easy. I just play football. You know, so you you can't you can't be too high, you can't be too low. You just got to ride that wave through and through. >> After you mentioned Brian earlier, I mean, you've been through this fortune like that in your career. >> Right. >> What do your thoughts go when you see a a brother and a teammate >> Um It's it's it's saddening cuz I know uh what what year he wanted to have this year. You know, I was I was uh I was excited for him about this year. Um I would say the bright side is you know, ACLs now we know you can get back. Right? So, that's the bright side and I say just, you know, just attack it. Um we know that you're going to heal. We know you're going to get better. And um you know, you know what you got to do when you get back. That's you know, that's the name of the game. >> You just kind of mentioned you know, your path or your model as an example for Tyree Wilson. How can you kind of help with his development and what do you just made of it? >> Yeah. Yeah, man. It's uh you know, Tyree a great player, tall, 40-in arms, arms longer than mine. Like he, you know, if he extends his arms, you can't touch him. Like um And that's a definitely a big thing that we've been telling him. Like use your length. Um but I think he's going to be a real great addition um for us, a real big monster coming off the edge who's athletic, who's able to bend. Um I'm excited for him, especially um in in this defense uh where you know, where edge rushers can, you know, where edge rushers can fly. >> When uh you mentioned earlier that uh you know, your teammates have faith in you and they have faith in you like that and then you go out and produce the way that they have confidence in you. What does that do for you as well? >> I just set the standard. Um I think what I did last year, it just set a standard for me for this year, right? Everything I I see all y'all now what I did last year, now y'all got expectations, which I don't really look at. But, you know, um you know, I'm just I that's why to just take it day to day. My teammates can have expectations for me. My coach can have expectations for me and and that's what we talk about and that's why we take it day to day and and don't worry about the future. We worry about this lift. >> Chase, you talked about what you want out of the practice with the relationship you have and how much growth have you seen in him? >> A great one, man. Juwan, man, one of the best tight ends in the league, especially in terms of catching the ball and getting open. I think he proved it last year. I think he was top eight in yards or something. Top four. Excuse me. My bad, Juwan. >> I was going to say top eight though. I mean, that is >> All right, top eight. >> [laughter] >> You know, I mean, he he's going to do it again this year. I have no doubt about it. Excited for him. You know, he's getting Just like me, year two on the same scheme. You know, everybody's comfortable, he's comfortable. It's no thinking, he can just run out on the field and play real fast. That's that's my brother, man. We we stick close and I'm just excited for him, man. >> Chase, you talked a lot last year about it, but what does a second year in the system really allow you as a player? >> Just being comfortable, man. Just from day one, like yesterday, it was literally no thinking, right? Cuz, you know, the first time you get into a scheme and you know, you just got to make sure, especially the first time, where either I'm dropping or he's dropping. It's like you got to get that down, but now it's just like we already know. You know, we seasoned. You know, we just comfortable when we step on the grass. >> You accidentally bumped into Sack out there? >> Yeah, man. You know, sometimes you just you just full head of steam. It's a I don't want to stop too fast. >> You talked a lot last year about what Demario Davis meant to you. Do you feel like you're one of the people that can help fill the void >> For sure. >> that he brings in all that areas? >> For man, I'm ready, man. I'm I'm ready. I'm ready, man. I've been working. Uh you know, I've been playing football my whole life for these types of moments. So, um I'm not the person to shy away from leadership or um anything like that. I'm I'm definitely know that I'm capable of filling the void. Um and I believe I >> You spoke about a plethora of talent at defensive tackle. What are your early impressions of the rookie Christian Ringo? >> Man, big. He big, man. He He big, athletic. And he nasty, man. He might talk a little something to you. You know, I I We like that. You know, we like You know, we like to, you know, be yourself, right? Be confident on the field. If you If you like to talk trash, do it. I know I do. So, you know, we we love that. That just fuels. That gives us energy. Um gives everybody else energy and uh just keeps the the practice exciting. >> Do you have a specific kind of trash talk you like? >> Yeah, I can't say it up here, man. >> Um You You said last year, uh I think Mike was talking about mentioned it too about feeling like you found a home here in New Orleans. This off season, you see guys like Cam Jordan and Alvin Kamara extend their options to be able to finish off his life here. What does that mean for you as a player? >> Uh it means a lot, man. I'm just excited to get AK back. Um I still say he one of the best. When he get the ball in his hands, uh very the most durable player. Um you know, dynamic when he gets hit, hard to bring down. Uh you know, it's not a lot of running backs you can say that's just flat out better than AK. I don't care, you know, how old he is or regardless, he he's one of the best. Um Cam Jordan, um you know, he definitely excited to get him back. Uh just one of those um guys that uh I I like I say, I get nuggets from every day just about learning how to be a pro. Uh you know, give me tips on talking to y'all. Um you know, just all around the whole all around the board. >> As far as your your kind of like future prospects with the team, to see, you know, a kind of commitment both ways like that. >> For sure. I mean that that that's a testament to Mickey Loomis, um the front office, you know. I mean, if they weren't doing the right thing, who knows what Cam and AK would have done, right? You could just I mean just being here their whole career, you know that it's it's just a it's a family environment here. And you know, that's what you just know about New Orleans Saints since since I was a kid. Just a great place to be, great front office, and place that wins. >> Chase, have you seen much difference in Cam Jordan? Year one year two, being comfortable >> Oh yeah. Yeah, I mean I mean I think he was comfortable when he got here. I mean where he came from, what he did, you know. Even go look at his college stats. I mean, he always been a dog. So I mean it's he never shied from anything. And you know, he he he's on what he has to do as a coach. We see that, and that's why we trust him as our leader. >> Chase, how do you describe your relationship with Cam? >> Ooh, loud, talkative, energizer bunny. you know man, just uh you know, we going we going to lead together, right? Even if I don't have the energy that day, I know Granderson going to have it for me. If he don't have it, I know Cam going to have it. It's like we all hold each other to just a high standard. Uh all together. So I'm yeah man, we we going to be ready to rock week one. >> What would it mean to you to have a captain >> badge this year? >> Uh it would mean everything, man. To be recognized by your teammates as a guy who's leading. It would be great thing.

What did that I mean you only had him one season. What did it mean for his message in the city and the fans for him to send that out after his long time here? >> Yeah, Taysom's the best. He's one of the best people you ever meet in this world. He's a phenomenal person, player, competitor. For him to come back from that injury the previous season was incredible and you know, he's had so much success in this community playing for the Saints and the impact he's had on this community has been awesome and uh you know, he's a guy that a lot of our guys can look to as an example of you know, growing in the NFL and finding roles and finding opportunities and you know, everyone's for the last few years been chasing let's find the next Taysom and there's really just one Taysom. >> Did you talk to him before he left? >> Did you talk to him either right before then or right after? Like in the last week let's say. Have you guys talked and and and how did that I don't know decision you know, come about? >> I've I've not talked to him very recently. What do you think that would do for the pass rush overall? >> Yeah. Rushing the passer, I mean there's a lot of that goes into it and I think the amount of pieces that you have that can rush in various ways is obviously going to be a huge asset and so when you have guys that can rush off the edge, rush interior and then you know, from a second level linebacker position that just adds things. At the end of the day it's a math problem. You're trying to isolate people and create opportunities one-on-one. >> How did Chris Rumph's going to off-ball linebacker come about? >> Just an off-season discussion of trying to find value as much as we can for him in various roles. Like a lot of these guys you're always trying to find different opportunities. He's played really good on the edge in the NFL for a long time. He's obviously a big time special teams player. He's always played that and so now it's like hey, we still get about our edges but also how can we add some components that may put him off the ball? >> How do you like him in the sun so far? >> Great. Great. He kind of started it right at the end of OTAs the last few days and then he's got a lot of exposure early on in camp so far and has been really good. >> Obviously Kendall, you seem to have a little bit of a different kind of connection with Tyler. They they seem to they seem to see each other a lot. >> Yeah. Yeah, I think that's a fair assessment. They they have some history together previously and so I I they work really hard together during the off-season and so all those guys when you invest a lot of time in into this thing together and the amount of throws that you make together, inevitably, you know, you're you're going to have a higher level of comfort. >> Did anything happen with Folau at the end like Ike was out there at the end? >> Yeah, I think he just kind of rolled his rolled his ankle a little bit, so just precautionary, nothing big. >> Uh you weren't here obviously for Kaden Ellis's first >> Mhm. >> you know, time with the team. What did you hear about him from the front office guys who wanted to bring him back and then what have you kind of learned about him since he's been here? I knew the football player. Obviously the football player, I've seen him, you know, particularly in Atlanta the last few years. We played him each each year and so saw the impact he has on the field. >> And I mean from your own experience you were, you know, undrafted free agent. What's career in the NFL for a guy that be a a seventh round pick to kind of ascend to where he's at right now, you know, third contract, all that sort of thing. Like how rare is that I guess is a a >> Yeah. Yeah, and I think it's credit to him of his development in the NFL even when he maybe didn't play as much early because there was so much depth at linebacker here. He's a guy who came in, he played everything at Idaho. I remember him, you know, just cuz I have, you know, connections back there and it's like he played every position, you know, he was just kind of their do-it-all. He played offense, he played defense and so it's just a matter of time defining what his role is and so he's a versatile player. He's really talented. >> For Z, how do you think you guys will be able to generate that same type of interior push cuz that like an area that >> That's still Goals don't change. Goals don't change. Yeah, limited exposure I think for all these defense linemen. Once we get to pads it gets a little bit more accurate evaluation and so, you know, it's just a matter of time to see these guys going, but Christian's done an awesome job. He's He's been phenomenal all off season uh coming, you know, through a rehab process early and then uh working his way to where he's at right now. >> Is kind of the emphasis on the run today kind of in anticipation of pads today? >> Yeah. Yeah. Um Yeah, every day we're going, you know, again, training camp is your number one opportunity for the run game on both sides of football. So, as much exposure as we can get, that's critical. >> So, they're going to pull out some league rules and they're going to be holding them back. I guess you have two high-profile players on the team and a lot of weight on them. Uh it's inevitable and I think communication's the key. As long as we all communicate, we're all on the same page. Um The thing we always have to remind ourselves, everyone's in everyone has the same goal. Uh everyone's shooting for the same things. Uh it's just, you know, sometimes the business side takes a little bit of a a lead on this for for a matter of time and we'll just work through it.

title: Saints TE Juwan Johnson on relationship with Tyler Shough, learning from Taysom Hill, Saints offense
text: Payton, just like that message he sent out on the Payton show. >> I I I had no idea what happened. Yeah, so I just found out. Um you understand, you know, the feel of where the quarterback wants you. And I feel like that's been the biggest thing cuz that's actually taught me a lot of um where I was supposed to be. Taysom taught me a lot. And so, uh some things some verbage is QB's I'm like, "Bro, I don't know what that means." Since you've known him and and and you've you know, you guys are close, is this something like like he's always been this and now he this is his opportunity to kind of like now I can show this and and and distribute it or is it something he's just kind of grown in to the you know like recently? >> Yeah, he's always had it in him. I feel like everybody has like some sort of leadership capability. I mean in terms of you leading your family, you you know you're leading [snorts] your you know your job or whatever just leading yourself. You somebody has some sort of accountability leadership. But for him he's always had it and the thing is I think you know Kellen is nurturing that like he's kind of nurturing that by having him to you know break it down and stuff like that. I think that's good not for just him but I think for everybody to get accustomed to his voice and being that presence and I think that's really good and the testament to Kellen to just be like yeah this is who we're going to hear this is our guy this is our leader this is our quarterback and you know and I think Tyler's kind of ran with it. He's been good and especially in the off season you know taking us these guys on trips getting together you know kind of having some camaraderie. I think that's been the biggest thing for us. >> Could you describe your connection with him on the field? It seems like you two guys are on the same page a lot. >> I just know where he wants me and I think that's the the biggest thing. You know when you you spend a lot of time together and like you you watch film together and you know you kind of see where he his eyes are at you know he sees where my eyes are at and honestly I just try to be savvy and I think he's you know he kind of reads where I'm supposed to be. I think it's the biggest thing. Having a lot of reps with a quarterback I think is the biggest thing and you know it's it's kind of tough when you're on the sideline trying to figure out like you know but if you're watching film and you know you you're having actual reps with him I think that's the biggest thing. That's what it's been good for us. >> Is savvy is that like is that a word that you would say that like that's your biggest like strength that's your superpower is like knowing where the holes are and knowing where to find spots? >> Yeah, I would say I mean I'm some people say like I'm fast quick but I'm not the fastest guy. I mean I'm a big guy. I mean there's some attributes about me that are different from other tight ends but I feel like the biggest thing that kind of helped me to stick is just you know [snorts] being smart about coverages and being smart about where, you know, guys are at and treating leverages and trying to trick the defender and things like that. That's kind of like been my thing just to have like a little edge cuz I mean, you think about it, in the NFL everybody's the same speed, everybody's the same height, all that. But if you can have like a quick edge, that's kind of been like, you know, my MO. >> Is he different this year than last? Do you feel more >> Uh in terms of what? >> Your knowledge. >> Before. >> Things that go into making Yeah. Uh I would say a lot of it is, yeah, just, you know, being immersed in the offense, you know, just knowing that you don't have to learn a different offense probably the the best thing for me. But, um you know, just going in and knowing that, you know, you have your your number one QB, you know, you got your running backs, your tight ends, you know, your receivers. Cuz sometimes last year it was just like, man, are we going to be a a a one tight end, you know, set team or we're going to be two or three, you know, you just you just never really knew. But I think since we have, you know, like kind of the offense under our belt, we kind of know what we're going into. You kind of know where you're going to be, you know, if they say 11, 12, 13 personnel, I know 13 personnel, I'm probably going to be outside. So just knowing like where you're going to be in certain situations that's been really good for me. >> What differences do you notice in the run game this year? In terms of just like >> Uh just like I mean, you guys brought in H Chan, you brought in David Edwards, and you have the possibility to run it in different ways with different tight ends. Just I just >> Well, hopefully I run the ball, that'd be nice. >> Yeah, too. [laughter] >> Yeah, too. Shoot. No, I mean, it's it's it's I I think it's actually been good. We have a lot of um diversity. I remember I was talking to one of the tight ends yesterday looking at film. I was like, man, we got some nice running backs. Let alone just like our addition, like we got nice running backs in the backfield that we could do a lot with. I mean, sometimes people just forget about Kendra. Like Kendra's explosive, dude. And so just knowing that, you know, you know, despite, you know, what he's been through, um he's still an explosive and exciting player. So, you know, just knowing things like that, you know, it's been good and knowing that you have, you know, Trave in the backfield, AK in the backfield. It's just like you you have so much versatility you can have, and so we haven't even like scratched the surface of what we can do from a run game standpoint. We honestly have been keeping it, you know, pretty vanilla so far, but um I mean, I guess we will see in a couple weeks how it will like pan out, but I think you know, in terms of just adding David, David's been really good for us, you know, that add knowing David's just like that. Going on the left side is kind of like moving the whole line of scrimmage has been really good for, you know, our guys in the backfield. >> How was the Being an undrafted guy and making your way in the league, making a name for yourself, I mean did Taysom's journey at all kind of inspire you like while you were doing that? Was he a guy that was here that Yeah. >> had a similar path as well? Like was that inspiring at all for you during that process? Uh his journey for sure. Um I would say um Taysom's journey and a lot of guys just just has been through the Saints, you know, organization. I feel like they have a great reputation of just hiring, well, hiring, um getting um undrafted guys, and so knowing that those guys that have come through the Saints organization have stuck and have been around, um just kept their head down, and just kind of pushed through has been honestly has been one of the things that um I really been like admiring. Like especially guys like Taysom, guys like Adam Thielen, you know, guys who's done a a great deal and have almost made like Pro Bowls and things like that. Um it's been really good for me to to see that cuz it's possible. You know, sometimes in when people get undrafted, they think it's not possible to make an impact or, you know, not possible to make a team, but you know, if you keep your head down, you know, you stay healthy, um and honestly, you're just not not making trouble. I feel like that's the biggest thing in just staying here. Like it's not the most athletic guys who are making the teams. Like, I don't think it had to be transactional to translate to football, but it was just you know, good to have the families together. >> You said y'all played board games, so this is your chance to air it out if she cheats at board games or >> No, I ain't play board games. I ain't I ain't play board games at all. I knew that it was cheating cuz they was saying some stuff that I ain't I ain't know. So, I was like, I think they was trying to play Clue. And they were like, oh, let's play Clue. I was like, no, y'all been playing for a couple hours, so I'm good. Y'all start cheating making up rules on me. I don't like that. >> I got a quick uh health science question, probably. >> Health science? >> Sweet. >> We've been working on story, it's 25th anniversary of, um, Corey Stringer. >> Okay. >> Um, so, being in a hot weather team, are there are there things about the way the practice is, um, planned out that you can tell that heat exposure is a real consideration in how they're, you know, the time of day they're putting you out there, how long they're putting you out there, and how they're monitoring you? >> Yeah. Um, I think there's a benefit, truly, to us being out there, um, in the heat. And I think it's one of those things where we have an advantage to kind of go into the year knowing that we've been in the heat, we're accustomed to it, we've been grinding away, and then we get into a cool area, you know, dome. I mean, we can really go and get it and and get after some teams. But, um, I think there's a benefit to what Kellen and, you know, Ted Rath and those other guys are doing in keeping us safe and things like that. Um, we have 3 hours to kind of get our bodies back, um, cool down before we, you know, get into meetings and stuff. I think it's been a big thing, yeah. And so, I mean, obviously we got IVs and we got all that, but I mean, the the biggest thing is it's really on you. Like, they can't they can't baby us in everything. Like, we're we we get paid a lot of money to to take care of our bodies and work out and do those other things. Um, yeah, I I I never been in a place where, you know, you get that much time off to get your body back so we could go into the meetings and stuff like that cuz usually it's like right after or we get an hour and a half and so they're all being cognizant of what, you know, we have with our time, but I think us as adults, us as professional athletes, we know what to do to to take care of our bodies.

title: Giants Training Camp Preview | New York Giants
text: [music] Welcome to Giants Training Camp preview presented by Citizens Bank, the official bank of the New York Giants. I'm Bob Papa. Training Camp 2026 in full swing. We got a big show lined up for you from Isaiah likely. Some sound and bites from day one of training camp. plus a look at the coordinators. But to get things started, Sean O'Hara had a chance to sit down with the head coach of the New York Giants, John Harbaugh. Honored to be joined by the head coach of the New York Football Giants, Coach John Harbaugh. Coach, great to see you. There's been so much energy and excitement around the building uh since you came aboard and obviously now with training camp on the horizon here. Um what what what kind of excitement does that bring to you as a coach as you head into training camp? >> Oh, absolutely. That's kind of what it's all about. You point toward training camp, you you build your team in training camp and the guys have been great. The building's been great. There's so much activity going on. You walk back in here and all the preparations for Greenbryer and all the preparations even for the build for the new facility. I mean, there's a lot of changes. A lot's going on just structurally in the place. But then we get focused on, you know, the changes with the football team, the things that are really going to impact our guys on the field. That's that's what we got to focus on, you know, and our guys are doing a great job. I've seen the guys come in. We've had 15 20 guys even every single day in the building before we even leave. Uh the players are excited, coaches are excited, we're ready to go. >> Obviously, a ton of work has gone into this offseason. What What did you like about the team and what you guys did there? And how do you carry that progress into training camp? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, it's just it's a it's a day-to-day kind of a thing. It's just it's hard to assess, you know, how far you've come, where you're at. You never know where you're going. You just can't you just can't know. All you can do is do your best every single day. And I feel like what I feel best about is the fact that everybody's done that. Everybody's [snorts] been all in every day uh all the time to do their best to do everything they can as well as they can. And if you do that, you you know, you at least give yourself a chance. You know, you earn the right to have a chance to compete and that's what our guys are doing. >> Coach, you mentioned the Greenbar Resort in West Virginia. For the first time ever, the New York Giants are going to West Virginia. Uh what does it do for a team to actually go away for training camp? Well, you know, you've done it and you know what it's like to have training camp away. Uh there's benefits to both. There's a lot of ways to do it. We've seen it done every kind of way it can be done. But I'm excited about this trip with this team at this time. I think our chance to get away to bond a little bit uh 247, you know, be about our football team and each other. That's going to be really valuable for us. Our guys like each other anyway. They seem like they like being around one another. And I'm just excited about the chance to be, you know, all football all the time for that period of time. There's some new faces defensively. Um, obviously through free agency, Tummaine Evans comes aboard and Arll through the draft. What did you see from Tummaine Evans during the offseason on the field in the OTAAS? What does he bring to this defense? >> Well, Tmaine, he's he's a he's a real natural leader. You know, he's 28 years old, but he's been playing for nine years. It it's incredible how much experience he has under his belt, how much he's seen, and yet he carries this he's really got a a humble heart toward learning and toward getting better and being a part of the team. I think he wants to understand every part of the defense in a way that he can kind of, you know, play it the right way, but also impact the other guys around him. You know, he's a middle linebacker. He understands the responsibility that goes with that. So, yeah, it's just great to have a veteran leader in that spot. And what about Arll? You got a chance to see him on the field and kind of in p not in pads, but in helmets and jerseys, running around in person. What What has impressed you? >> Well, the talent level jumps out at you. You know, you saw that too, Sean. Oh, yeah. It's it's pretty impressive. and both those guys, but but also the fact that here's a guy that really is uh dedicated toward everything his coach tells him, everything coach Bush tells him to do. He tries to do it exactly like that. He wants to be perfect in in how the defense has played exactly right. He's he's a stickler for details. It's going to carry him a long way. >> Yeah, I know the coaches love that. The coaches love like a sponge soaking it up. How about offensively? Uh, a lot of new weapons. Uh, obviously Isaiah Likely and Pat Ricard. Ricard's more of a blunt weapon, if you will, but two guys you know really well. And then a slew of receivers. You've got all kinds of of fresh faces in the receiving core. Uh, what is that competition going to look like in training camp? >> Well, what what you're saying I think is exactly right. I mean, I I we're in the process of kind of figuring that out. Like what are we going to look like? We have a lot of really talented parts pieces, a lot of motivated guys, a lot of competition like you said. So, let's get at it, you know? Let's get into training camp and see what it looks like because we've got to figure out kind of who we are. We we understand the principles. We understand what what's required, the type of team that we want to be, but how's it exactly going to look in terms of the schemes, who's doing what, how, when. Those things we have to put together. >> So, Jackson Dart obviously is going to have to, you know, get some rhythm with them and get some chemistry. Uh year two for him, a new offense though. They got to make sure the motion goes to the right spot, the ball snapped at the right time, that the communication in the huddle is exactly right, that everybody's got their eyes, you know, on on the quarterback. But how that exactly takes shape that you know the identity the personality uh the purpose all those kind of things are are unique to every team. text: Is there a difference with with fans here? Energy wise? >> I'd say so. Yeah, I'd say so.
