Uh ones against ones a lot of times, and and he looked good. He's not the only guy, but he had a heck of a practice. >> How much can it help a guy like Adbul, who's still a young player, to go up against a guy like Andrew Thomas and you know, it's hard technically every day? >> Help him a ton. You're right. And plus they talk, you know, it's not just going against each other, but that's where it starts. And then they talk about the plays afterwards on tape. They might talk a little bit at each other during practice, but afterwards they're talking about the play itself and sharing ideas. And then and a guy like AT, you know, he'll give him a lot of pointers. >> When you you watch Adbul on tape, you obviously can see the talent, but what does he have to do, when you look at it in your opinion, to take his game to the next level? >> I think he would tell you a just a consistency level down after down after down. All downs, all situations, you know, being a complete a complete player on the edge. And we'll move him around, too. And that means that includes even dropping him in the coverage sometimes, you know, I mean, all those things. Play the run, rush the passer, all the movements, stunts, things like that. Cover for guys on on movements. All those things that he's really he's determined to do. I've heard him say it many times to be a complete player. >> What have you seen from his approach just behind the scenes? >> I've seen that. You know, I've seen I've seen an amazing work ethic and a uh a really a really deep determination to do every little thing right. Very serious minded guy. You know, he smiled a couple times today. That was the first time I see him smile since camp started, so it was good to see. >> Where was Art Green? >> Art had a little little tightness, little muscle tightness, so he was out of practice. >> And like serious? >> I don't believe so. I mean he's getting some tests. I don't think so, but we haven't heard yet. >> You mentioned that Abdul and you know AT go at each other sometimes and talk. That's not Andrew's way though. >> Well, no. I'd say probably you're right. Probably Abdul's talking more and Andrew's just kind of looking at him. >> Is that Is that Is that what you like from a left tackle? Just You know you know what I'm saying? >> Just go you know what have you seen from him? >> Well, Andrew he he's special. I mean he's he's one of a kind. You know, elite elite football player, elite left tackle in every way. He's in he's in phenomenal shape. He's moving great. He's worked super super hard. He's healthy. He's ready to roll and he looks really good. >> John, what do you think of the jawing back and forth? Is that just a natural part of things getting more physical? >> I think it's just the guys are having fun and competing and getting after it and it was good. It was all good-natured and and it was a it was a high highly intense practice, you know. It was fun to be a part of. It was fun to be in the middle of it. That's why I said we come off the practice field, you know, you we just had football practice, you know, in the NFL in a beautiful setting. It was it was awesome. >> What was the story with the patches on some guys' jerseys? >> The The patches are something we've been doing since '08. They are like kind of an I guess an honoring the the military award medal type things. So, we start those. There's two patches right now that for for the guys so far it's the off season program. They made a certain amount of the off season program. And then there's guys who who had the the the the the sword is a playoff appearance for the Giants at some point in time. Well, then there's other things you'll see as we go once we get the games going. Yeah, Pro Bowls will be in there. They Maybe maybe we don't have the Pro Bowl patches yet. I don't know, but Pro Bowls will be part of it. Game game awards the different kind of game awards that we have us throughout the year. >> John, John, I know we we talked about Jackson yesterday. Probably could talk to you about him every day. We talked about how perfect he wanted to be every play in the spring. Is this kind of the proving ground? I know you said you're chasing execution, but this is kind of where you want to see him take some chances. Let's see what, you know, what you can make out of some of these calls and don't be afraid to make a mistake or make an interception or something like that. >> No, yeah, I I do think there's truth to that. You know, you you push the envelope a little bit in practice and see where you can fit throws in and things like that. I would hope they, you know, they would do that and I think that's definitely his his mindset. >> He's been under center on these first two days. Didn't do a lot last year. Why is that important and what are the challenges for a quarterback to be under center? >> Well, I mean, you know, he I don't know how much he's done it, but he looks good doing it. You know, it hasn't been an issue at all. Uh it does, I would say, under center in the passing game, it does really discipline your footwork cuz the drops are so important under center and I think it enhances and maybe he would tell you it makes even it helps even in the in the in the gun, pistol, or whatever, but um it's just another element. It's part of our offense, what our offense is going to be. We're going to be in various elements and and that's one of them. >> You know, we saw a few guys have a penalty, one off the field. Is that kind of a discipline, uh not discipline, but more just kind of like emphasizing how important it is to be disciplined and not get penalties? >> Absolutely. I'm going to try to be penalty-free in practice if we can be. Uh you know, something we'll we'll look at them all. We'll we'll we'll evaluate them tonight as a staff. Uh we'll we'll show them to the guys tomorrow. Uh there'll be a lot of arguing in the in the team meeting about whether it was We had one yesterday, was it a push-off? If you remember the one, I think Jaylen had it on uh Tay, right? You know, was it a push-off? Is it not a push-off? Didn't get called. Uh so, we don't have NFL officials right here, so we don't have that luxury of them making those calls, but um these guys are doing a great job, so that's really important. >> John, yesterday came out, got in the backfield, tipped a pass from James today. The pick six, what have you made of his burst and his hands that he's been showing? >> I'd like to see a lot of that, you know. That's what you want to see. I mean, he's he's a pretty athletic guy. He's aware. He does have good hands. The ability to rush the passer and also the awareness to bat balls down is massive. I mean, batted balls is a big stat in defensive football in terms of getting off the field. So, that's something we work on. We do not coach our guys against batting balls down in any drill we do. We want to practice it. >> Coach, I know you talked about your projections of West Virginia playing WVU when you were a college athlete at Miami of Ohio. That was the start of the Don Nehlen era, which was a very prosperous era for WVU football. How much do you recall from that time playing the Mountaineers if anything at all from Coach Nehlen? >> I remember Coach Nehlen beat us really bad when I was coaching at Cincinnati. He beat us really, really bad. But, but I was a special teams coach and our punter, he had like the best day in the history of football. He averaged like 50 yards a punt and he had about 15 punts. So, it was quite a day. You can go back and check it out. I'm going to say 1989. It was a bad day for the Bearcats. But, Coach Nehlen played with my dad at Bowling Green. My dad coached for Coach Nehlen in 1967, '68, '69 at Bowling Green State University. And and Coach Nehlen came back and coached with my dad and under Bo Schembechler Michigan in the '70s. Danny Nehlen was long time equipment guy there and I we were buddies. We played played basketball just about every day when we were when we were growing up and they were coaching there. So, a lot of great ties to the Nehlen family. Coach Nehlen, Mary Ann, they just had the most awesome Vicky, her daughter Danny. Just love that family so much and uh yeah, treasure those days. >> Good job. >> Two more. >> Back to Kevon really quickly. Do you like how he's handling playing largely with the second string defense so far? He's mainly been a starter in the league for the most part or alternating. Do you think he's bringing a good attitude to that? >> Absolutely. I don't think he's worried about it. He knows he's going to play a bunch. We I I And these guys know we we have three starting We have three starters at outside linebacker. It's just those are Those are all starting football players. So, you know, slice it how you want, do a depth chart any way you want, those guys are all going to play a ton of football. Same thing for inside backer. I put Mike in the same category. We We've got three starting inside linebackers. That's a really good situation. We treat them appropriately, all those guys, and you know, it's they're going to play a lot of ball. >> John, something that I asked you yesterday, I know you joked that, you know, Cam like you wish you would have stuck the landing on it, but we didn't ask you about the Scat with with the flipping. How much do you feel the need to talk to him about stuff like that or just being careful or, you know, of the surroundings and him, you know, taking care of himself outside the building and or or not? >> No, it's a To me, it's a very good question. And the And it is something that we talk about everything all the time. So, those things, you know, that other things have come up every day with Scat or anybody else. You know, there's a lot of guys that talk to every day and we're having interactions with every everybody on the team. But so Scat and I have had, you know, I don't know, five, six really good conversations since he got back. And And you know, that might have been talked about in there with some other stuff. >> Might have been? >> It might have been. It might have been. It's a There's There might be a good chance. Um so I But I think, you know, it's it's just part of the ongoing process, just communication, being on the same page. Uh trying to be the best we can be in everything we do, you know, and he's great, you know, he wants to be great. He listens and talks and gives, you know, tells you what he thinks and it's it's all good. >> What's your message for something like >> The message is that we stay we The The big picture message is you want You want to take care of yourself. You want to take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good, you know? What does that mean? You know, the next It's not going to be the same situation the next time for anybody. You know, it's going to be different. So, it's really the principle that you talked about. >> Okay. >> [music]

title: Jevón Holland: ‘We’ve got a close locker room' | New York Giants
text: Did you guys have a good day today? >> Yeah, it was fun. Yeah, good day. Good day. >> Pretty active trash talking. >> Yeah. That's a day-to-day thing. Uh we got a close locker room, so a lot of guys like to, you know, trash talk and makes the day fun. Yeah. >> there's you know, there's only been 2 days here. And so the first day it looked like the offense played well and did some of the things they wanted and it looked like the defense today prevented a lot of that. Is that the the natural ebb and flow that you see in a training camp where you get effort one day, then maybe they get you the next day and then you feel bad and you go back You know what I'm saying? It's kind of like, you know, one day one day. I mean, you want to be great every day, but it doesn't always happen. >> Yeah, I mean, you know, it's it's uh the coaches do a great job of bringing in individuals that are pretty pretty equal both sides. Obviously, you want, you know, offense and defense to, you know, have similar firepower on both sides, so of course it's going to go back and forth, you know. Um Every day changes cuz, you know, you install new plays and whatnot. Offenses has an emphasis and they're trying to, you know, A lot of the time each side is trying to put themselves in a difficult situation so that when we do get on the field, it's a lot easier, you know, those stress those stressful situations we're comfortable in, so uh it will change day day by day. >> When you see what a tool is capable of obviously you saw it last year, but just today when you see what he's doing out there, just how much does that excite you as a as a DB watching him up front just making his hell basically? >> Yeah, it excites me a lot. >> How so? Like what what goes through your mind watching him just be get that be that disruptive force? >> Uh I mean, I'm just, you know, usually when he's getting to the quarterback fast, the ball comes out fast, which or like disrupts the quarterback, so um gives us an opportunity to make a play, you know, kind of ruins the offense's timing, which is always great. That's kind of what I'm thinking aside from my job. Uh but yeah, no, just I'm excited for him. He's going into year two. you know, he had a good last year and I know he's going to just excel this year, so >> What was it like seeing the fans for the first time this season? >> It was great. Yeah, everybody was cool. Just signed some some jerseys or whatnot, you know, kissed some babies. It was cool. It was a good time. It was good It was a good time. >> You and you and Reuben have been together it's like, you know, and now you're the old couple on the back end, but the communication-wise comparatively from last year to where you are now, I know it's a new system. How would you describe the way you guys are now able to work together on the field, you know, going back to >> Yeah, uh really just like a kind of a feel thing, you know, this is my first time in my career I'm going into a second year with the same playing mate next to me. So, just us building rapport over the off season, you know, um being close friends, you know, communication, kind of understanding how he plays, how I play, how he thinks, how I think, so uh we're starting to like I mean we were last year, but obviously it's a new defense, so within the defense starting to just, you know, kind of pick up on our nuances and what and whatnot. And uh yeah, it feels good. >> Have there been plays over Have there been plays already where it's kind of been unspoken that after the play is over you kind of look over and you're like >> Yeah, just like kind of, you know, seeing him moving, his body language, communication-wise. Um you know, it's happened a few times and we've been on the same page on all of those, so uh I think, you know, just through communication kind of telling him what I'm thinking, him telling me what I'm what he's thinking, uh we kind of gain, you know, more knowledge about how to play specially uh with each other. >> Is there growth in his game that you can see? >> Yeah, absolutely. >> In what way? >> Uh I would say just overall, you know, as a as a player in the league you want to advance every year, um you know, in every aspect. Communication, uh you know, disposition on the field, uh you know, body awareness, um kind of seeing the play before it happens, pre-snap, things like that. So, I think in every aspect Lou has, you know, taken another step, just like he took a step last year from camp to the season to the late in the season, you know, he's continually taking those steps. Uh it's a new staff, new defense, but, you know, he's taking it within stride, so I think he's doing a great job. >> What's up Darious at the secondary? >> AD's great, bro. He's uh he's just like a real cool, like low-key, just like knows what to do, knows his game, plays fast, covers ground. yeah, he's fun to play with. He's fun to play with. Me, him, and Nube out there all together, it's fun to play with. Jay Penn, too. You know, all the all the safeties, everybody has their own like personality with their strengths and weaknesses are. And I think the coaches do a great job of pairing us together to complement each other's style no matter who's on the on the field. So, yeah, it's fun playing with all of them. >> What's your sense of training camp in the Allegheny Mountains and in in this setting and things like that? >> Uh it's fun. You know, I like I like being, you know, near trees and whatnot. I'm from the Northwest, so, you know, I was from Canada, went to Oregon. Trees are are my friend. I love it. So, you know, I'm I'm enjoying the atmosphere. >> You imagine there's enough of them here for you? >> Yeah, yeah, yeah, there's plenty, plenty. I'm just not out at night, you know, I heard about the Appalachian Mountains and whatnot. You know, all the skinwalkers. I'm a bit of a conspiracy theorist, but I don't know. I asked the bus driver yesterday, I was like, "You heard about, you know, skinwalkers?" He was like, "I just let it go in one ear, out the other." So, that's all I needed to know, not to go out at night. >> Has anyone mentioned Mothman to you yet? >> even I see you getting into a whole 'nother area. I don't even want to get into that. I don't even want to get into that. >> Do you think that the way that you guys practice, like live periods basically throughout the entire practice, does that set a kind of urgency from Harbaugh on down to the team? Do you think that can prepare a team differently or better for a season compared to other camps you've been in? >> I mean, it really depends on, you know, the formula of the head coach. You know, some teams some coaches may say that doing walkthroughs, making sure that we're going through things in a slow manner, you know, can put you in mentally a clear space when they you know, the bullets are flying, you don't have to think about it, you've already been through the steps. Other coaches say that, you know, you need to do live periods on a consistent manner so that when you are in those situations for the first time and you're in stressed, when you get in in in the game, then it's easier to be, you know, reactive rather than thinking about it and try to make a play, try to force a play. So, it just depends on, you know, what coach you're going with. With Harbaugh, you know, we do a lot of live periods. We also do some walkthroughs and whatnot. You know, you kind of just adapt to the head coach and the team takes the personality of the head coach. >> How do you think the team is receiving his pace of play so far? >> it's great. Yeah. >> Take three more. >> What's been your opinion on the rookies so far, specifically Ar'Darius and Cole? Have those guys shown some big flashes so far? Is there still a learning curve with those guys? What have you seen so far? >> Yeah, absolutely. They've shown a lot of growth. They're picking it up fast and they're making plays. You know, as a rookie for myself, like I tried to just like find my area, you know, find my space and grow in the space, gain the confidence of my teammates and then from there I can take on more of a responsibility. And I think they're doing just that, you know, I think they're doing a great job as being rookies and knowing that they don't know and asking questions when they need to ask questions, but then also realizing having the confidence in themselves that they are here for a reason and they can make plays. So, I think they're doing a great job. >> You mentioned personality of the head coach. What do you think this team's personality is going to be based on John Harbaugh and sort of what do you thought of his his coaching style so far? >> I mean, I think Harbs is a old school head coach, but he's very he's very self-aware and he's he's very clear with the players. I think he he has a defined you know, standard for what we want what he wants and he's explained that to us through OTAs and he's given us examples and you know, I think the team has already kind of like taken that mindset and just like the small things, like if someone you know, we don't want to do something or people are complaining like, you know, you get to or you got to do it cuz you got to do it. That's just what it takes. It takes what it takes. So, yeah, just got to do the work if you want to be good. >> Last one. >> Is there a specific part of your game you're looking to improve the most this year physically, mentally, being a leader? Is there something you're looking at specifically to improve the most on this year? >> All of them. As a leader, you know, physically, mentally, every aspect I'm looking to to grow.

title: Malik Nabers: ‘It felt good to be out there with the guys’ | New York Giants
text: How are you feeling? >> Feel good. Feel good. >> What was it like to get out on the field yesterday? And get back to playing football with your full team? >> It felt good. I mean, I might not show it. I know I I like to be I like to be a person that you never you never know my facial expressions. I'm always just smooth and calm, but it felt good to be out there with the guys, get a couple throws. Um you know, just move around. You know, I never moved around a long time, but running routes felt good out there. >> Do you expect to play week one? >> Um there's no target date. Just stacking days and you know, I'll continue to let everybody know how I feel and when I'm able to you know, get back out there. >> How did you feel? How did you feel after running routes yesterday? I mean, we saw you back out there today doing some more work. >> Yeah. I mean, I feel great. I mean, nobody continues to you know, stack and days and the training staff have a you know, a good plan on what they want me to do. So, you know, I'll continue to you know, keep that keep that in mind and just tell them how I feel and continue to get out there as much as possible. >> What's your optimism level right now? You feel it seems like you feel good about everything. What's the word what's what's your mindset like? >> Uh my mindset is just stacking days. Um trying to get back out there with my teammates. So, if I can just stack keep on stacking days with you know, the training staff and they continue to see improvements on my body, continue to see improvements on you know, my knee and where I'm at, you know, it's it just gives me more confidence to go out there and be able to play. >> I think the last time we talked to you you said you know, you're not going to put a timeline on it. You're going to listen to your body. >> Yeah. >> Do you anticipate being ready for week one? >> Uh like I said, you know, no target dates. Just continuing to listen to the training staff and you know, they continue to ask me questions and you know, when I'm ready, I'm ready. >> When you had to get that second procedure done for the clean up, was that like an an extra mental hurdle for you to get over as far as rehab and processing what that was going to take? >> Um when was that date that I had the second surgery? Yeah, like when I had the second surgery that everybody thought I didn't. So, I don't know where that's coming from, but >> You didn't have Oh, you didn't have a procedure. >> I didn't have it on that date. So, I don't know when that came out, but I never had it on that date. >> it earlier earlier than that? >> I don't know. I just never had it on that date. >> Well, wait. When people talk about having surgeries like you had, guys talk about it all the time. The rehab life is kind of a It can be a lonely life. It can be a dark times and stuff. For you mentally, how hard was it and to When did you feel like you finally got over that hump to feel like, you know what? I can kind of see a light at the end of the tunnel. >> I mean, this is my first time I've battled with mentally like mental, you know, mental battle that I have a mental battle, but um I would say just keeping, you know, friends and family close. Um people that know exactly, you know, how they see you, you know, in the near future or what they see and you know, and how you attack things. Um I think just having positive people around you. Um that helps, you know, in this long-term battle. Um cuz you can get you can definitely get lost in your own mind and just, you know, you never know when you're going to be able to do something. Um and I've I got stuck in that also just dealing with this, you know, rehab. Um and just long-term and just doing a lot of stuff and you're not seeing improvements and you're always staying in the same spot week by week, but you know, just seeing the light at the end of the tunnel, you know, is is that is that everyday process is just thinking that you're going to get better and believing that you're going to get better and just stacking days like I said and just trying to make everyday a positive matter. Like don't go into the day um you know, just not expecting to get something out of it. Um I think I've, you know, attacked this rehab as I'm trying to get better everyday. Um no day is different, you know, and outworking the the day before and just trying to improve on the matter just getting back healthy. >> Well, Vic, do you think you're going to get back to where you are or better? Or do you know you will get back to where you were? >> Um I got extreme confidence in myself. Um and I'm not going to I'm not going to put myself in any any spot that I feel like I'm not going to be better than what I was before. So, I don't see myself being what I was before. What I was before, which y'all saw my rookie year, I felt like that was basic. So, I mean, I got high standards for myself and I know everybody has high standards for me also. But, the standard that I hold myself to is very high and I feel like whatever whatever that standard that I hold myself to, you'll see sooner or later. >> You said your rookie year was basic. >> My rookie year was just basic to me. I I left a lot of stuff on the field and I missed a couple games. So, I'm just excited to, you know, to see what where I will be when I when I know I'm >> What have you seen Jackson grow the most in since year one to year two? >> I've just seen him be like that leader that, you know, we need. You know, game manager. That person in the locker room that gets everybody going. You know, and and picking guys up. You know, he's picked me up through this process also. But, just, you know, he can read people very well. He reads me. He's like, he's always coming up to me. He's like, "What you thinking about?" Cuz I'm I'm always in my head. You know, I'm always thinking about, you know, stuff. And he's always like, "I know you're thinking." And you know, I have great talks with him and he's always, you know, pushing me to be better. Pushing me to just continue to stack days. Pushing me, you know, and just, you know, getting back to what I once was. So, you know, we could, you know, play together and be great together. >> As a running back As a running back, did you see for you guys building chemistry from having a lack of from last year? you know, we had to talk about that and, you know, I'm basically I'm a ba- I'm basically a friendly quarterback. I'm I'm basically a receiver's I'm a I'm a receiver's friend as quarterback. Like, I'm able to be at any spot you need me to be. Like, I talked to Jackson all the time and he's like, "You know, you're always exactly where I need you to be." Even in walk-throughs, I'm always there. I'm always seeing what he sees. So, I'm a friendly person with the quarterback. Like, I'm I'm I I feels what he feels and I know what feels, so you know, just having those talks with him also outside you know, of football even when we sitting on side each other just talking through plays and I'm able to see what he sees before he sees it and that's always makes everything better, too. >> How big is that to not start this training camp on PUP just to be able to keep kind of building that connection with him and get the work in since you're able to do more? >> Uh I don't know what PUP is, so I'm I'm It was new to me. I don't know, yeah. I I got to do more research on that. So, it's a I don't know is that I was just happy to be out there and let them let those guys see, you know, what improvements I made. I kind of let I kind of let everybody talk on the internet about it and then just just stayed in the dark and just did my own thing. >> But has there has there been a moment, you know, I know you're limited in what you're doing, but you are pushing yourself and has there been one moment on the field where you've done a cut or a little spin or a little push off the knee or something and you thought to yourself, "Yep, I'm good, you know, that I'm I'm I'm I can see this." You know what I mean? Just one physical thing that Um >> I'm do after these two days? >> Um no, I feel like, you know, the training staff did a very good job on getting me ready before I was even even I stepped foot out there. Um those cuts I've been doing with the training staff, those routes I've been doing with the training staff, so I wasn't it wasn't anything normal to me that I was able to go out there and do it full speed. >> We know your history with Odell and running routes. >> Three more three more. >> Hm? >> We know your history with Odell and then you had something you wanted to be teammates with him. What has the last month and a half been like to have him around and to be able to bounce stuff off of him? >> Uh just a just a a great a great role model, a great leader that, you know, we put in the room. Um you know, you know, he's had a few injuries in the past. He had the same injury as me. Um so, just talking through with him on just how he handled that um and what he what was his rehab process and what things that he did to help himself come back. Um and you know, just keeping him, you know, in the back corner and just, you know, always he's always feeding me good energy. So, it's good having him around. Um he's always still lifting me up. Always continue to call me, ask me how I feel, sending me um text messages on just motivation. So, just having him around has been great, for sure. >> Is it surreal? Is it surreal for you? >> Yeah, it's surreal, I mean. >> We know the story going back. >> Yeah, yeah. It is surreal, you know, I got family members and, you know, friends that, you know, it's it's it's so crazy that, you know, they see me playing with him or see me on the side of him. But, um you know, I'm just taking every moment in. >> When did you start running When did you start running routes? And when did that When did you Did you reach that progression? How important, if at all, is getting in a preseason game to test yourself? I don't really know the exact day on when I started running routes, but >> Like weeks ago? Just now? This week? >> Uh yeah, it >> Months ago? >> Weeks ago, for sure. Weeks ago, for sure. >> And preseason, is that important to you? Like, is that a goal for you at all? Is it to be able to test it, or you just >> We'll see what, you know, we'll see what Coach Harbaugh wants for me. Uh we'll see what his plan is. We'll see what the training staff game is, and we'll I'll take it from there. >> Who do you reach out to? Who's been maybe the best resource for you on the team? You talked You talked about Odell kind of what he's been through with his injury. Is anybody on the team that's a good resource to talk to just to kind of like keep your spirits up, keep your mental going through all this? >> I just feel like, you know, overall it's never It's not basically one person. I always seen videos of him as a kid and to be here and able to meet a legend like him is amazing, you know. One of my coaches in college actually played for the Eagles back in the day. And he played with him. His name is Nick Graham. He was a cornerback as well. So, he played with him and Lito Sheppard back in the day. >> Interesting. What's the biggest challenge of coming to a new city, new team, new scheme, all that stuff? >> Uh just being myself. I feel like I'm like the new guy in class. I feel like a rookie again, you know. New playbook, new team, new fans, new city. But at the end of the day, I still got to be myself. I still got to come here and work hard. I was here doing OTAs and you know, that that's one stepping stone uh in the in the right direction just because I got to learn the plays and the scheme and some of my teammates. But now that we really get into the season and it's a training camp where it's a lot of hard work going on. I just want to continue to grow and you know, continue to be a great teammate and to to continue to gel with my teammates as well. >> You mentioned feeling like a rookie again. What's it like stepping into a secondary that's played so much football together and has kind of already built up so much continuity? >> Um honestly, it's pretty cool because now it's just learning how to fit in with these guys, you know. I I know my personality. I get along well with everybody. I like to crack jokes with everybody on the team. They laugh and stuff. So, uh just being able to become close with these guys, you know, that's all I really care about because, you know, I got to be the best version of myself. And for me to do that, I got to be comfortable with them. And for me to be comfortable with them, they got to be comfortable with me and they got to get to know me and I I to get to So, throughout this whole process that's going to happen and I'm excited. >> Sorry if you've already been asked this, but what what are your kind of impressions of Quinyon? Like what and how good can he be this year? >> Oh no, you good. Shoot, honestly, my impressions since OTA to now is amazing, man. I watched film even before I got here, so I knew what type of players I was going to be playing with and to be able to join this team and join them is going to be a lot of fun and as we go through training camp you will see what we all working on. >> How have you been adapting to Philly itself? >> What happened? >> Oh yeah, I'm in pretty chill. I like the weather. Shoot, I like the food here, so I feel like I'll like it. >> From your time so far just learning the system and learning from Dick and the coaches, is there anything in particular about the system that you feel will be a key improvement so far in your game? >> Shoot, just the different ways we play certain things, you know, I feel like here I'm playing a little bit more off and in my game I would like that just because I'm known for a press corner, but it'd be nice not to press every play too, right? You know, so just to give a receiver a different look is pretty awesome and to be able to, you know, learn under Vic is amazing. >> What's that adjustment look like, you know, playing more off? What's the challenge in kind of doing that more? >> No, just trusting my speed, trusting the tempo, just trusting the space around me and trusting where my help is at, but that goes along with learning Vic's playbook, but it's not too far off from what I played in Seattle or what I learned in Seattle, so to be able to be a coached by Vic is going to be pretty awesome. >> What impresses you and I'm talking about you and Avonte Maddox today? >> That's that's the third one. Do I got to answer that one though? Do I got to answer that though? That's the third one. >> He's one of our guys, that's all. >> You have a different answer at least. Honestly, shoot, they cool as hell and you know, they easy to talk to. Whenever I first got here, you know, they they shot me a text, you know, we talked it up on Instagram and they embraced me as a brother, so to be able to be here with them now is amazing and I keep learning every day from both of those guys, and they they work very hard. And for me to be alongside with them, I'm excited. >> What do you think about your two tackles? >> Last one here. >> All right. I think we're done, right? >> Oh, that was a That was a good one, though.

And then all of a sudden, like at IOB, you know, you know, Jiad can't play and now Bond's got to work with Troder. Well, we don't want the first time that happens to be in a game. They they need to work with each other in practice some. Same thing with state. Those are the two main positions.
