title: Football at Four: Fangio Speaks at Eagles Camp And Looking at The AFC West
text: And football at four powered by the Inside the Birds podcast. [music] It is brought to you by the Fanatic Sports Book at Ocean Casino Resort in Atlantic City. [music] The Football at Four takes us to Eagles training camp. And camp is open >> [music] >> for business. Yesterday, Howie Roseman and Nick Sirianni did the honors. They took the podium. We just played for you the Vic Fangio press conference from earlier today. We'll get a couple quick Eagles questions for Andrew before we look at the AFC West as our division previews continue here on the Sports Bash Live. The first question I would have for you Andrew would be Jonathan Grahnard will miss a good bit of training camp here. Is this a concern hearing that come from Vic Fangio on his first day that he meets with the media? >> Uh a mild one. It's not something you that you just want to say there's nothing to see here. Jonathan Grahnard had a shoulder injury last season that limited him to 12 games and he hasn't yet participated in team drills and I'm including the spring of course. He is a veteran. He has played a ton of football, but as Vic Fangio outlined today, he's going to have to do some different things that he hasn't had to do in his career. So you would ideally like to get him on the practice field and and work him through some of those things, but it doesn't it's not a it's not a long-term concern as of this time and they're expecting him to to be ready. >> All right. Well, what other quick one? He pleaded the fifth I guess if you will on the safety position. Why does he not want to show his hand at safety yet? >> Uh I think he was I mean kind of joking when he said that, but he he also added that it's a competition. And he's not just going to hand the job over. First of all, Cooper DeJean's going to be the safety when the Eagles are in nickel, but the question become or when the Eagles are in base, excuse me. The question becomes who's the safety when the Eagles are in nickel? Right now, the front-runner is Marcus Epps. I wouldn't rule out Michael Carter the second, but you have to let that play out. He He's not going to tip his hand one way or the other because there's still a lot that has to be determined. >> All right, Andrew. Our division previews we're flying through. We're almost to the NFC. We're the AFC West today, which means we are getting really close to the start of the season. And of course, the Eagles this season in the AFC West, they will not play anybody from the AFC West. So, we will not see an AFC West team on the schedule. But one of the big teams is the Kansas City Chiefs as we know. They did not make the playoffs for the first time, I think since 2014 that the Chiefs have not made the playoffs. But let's get your initial thoughts on what their offense will look like this year with Patrick Mahomes towards ACL is LCL LCL, but it is expected that he will be back. He's got a couple of new toys here. >> Yeah, on paper it should be a fairly dynamic Chiefs offense. You added Kenneth Walker from the Seattle Seahawks. I think he's one of the better running backs in the game in my opinion. And then you of course, you have three speedsters in Tyquan Thornton, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy. The offensive line, Creed Humphrey leads the way there, one of the better centers in the game. Kingsley Suamatai'a is a guard, Josh Simmons. And you have Travis Kelce still. We'll see how much he ultimately has left, but they have certain key pieces from which to build. >> Uh they did lose running back Isaiah Pacheco from violence. They also lost wide receiver Hollywood Brown to Philadelphia. Uh you take a look at that offense with Patrick Mahomes and Kelce, adding Kenneth Walker. Sounds like you like what they've done offensively, but what about on the defensive side of the ball? They'll all trust McDuffie. Uh when you look at their defense, uh is this a championship-level defense? >> Well, like Chris Jones up front, George Karlaftis. They added Armon Mason Thomas in the draft, who's a player that I really liked. I spoke to him at the podium at the NFL Scouting Combine. Uh Peter Woods in the first round. Um so like they have pieces there. And I mean you look at the second level, Drue Tranquill's a underrated player, I think. He's been around. Nick Bolton's someone who Eagles fans are probably well accustomed uh you know, well acquainted with with his play in the Super Bowl 57. And then you have uh a secondary that I'm not overly enthused with. Anytime you lose a Trent McDuffie, you're you're not a better team. A Jaylen Watson, you're not a better team. And you know, you're talking about Alohi Gilman comes over from the Ravens. Uh uh Keanu Neal from the Dolphins. I mean they did draft uh Mansour Delane, the kid from LSU, and I like him. But it takes time for players to be able to step in there and help you. And I don't know if they have a ton there on the back end that you could really hang your hat on year one uh you know, kind of ready to go. Uh L'Jarius Sneed is a player who's bounced around while he's with the Tennessee Titans. He's a little bit older now. Well, you know, they have they have some pieces, but I don't know if if they have enough. >> Well, they had a problem last year in one score games. They were one and nine in one score games last season. And in the division where they have dominated, they went one and five in the division. They were 20 and four in their previous four seasons. Their big addition though was Kenneth Walker, who obviously was a huge factor for the Seahawks last year. How much better do you think or different will you do you think Walker will be over what they've had in the past at the running back position? >> Uh I like Isiah Pacheco. I think he's a nice story as a seventh-round pick, local guy out of Rutgers. And they they They they upgraded pretty significantly in my estimation with Kenneth Walker. That's that's something that they could really lean into the ground game and they have DiMarco Amari DiMarco who they I believe he was with the Cardinals if I'm remembering that correctly. They drafted Emmet Johnson in the fifth round as well. So I think they're going to they're going to lean into the running game because for as talented as they are at receiver I mean I I Tyquan Thornton is sort of an unproven entity. He's speedster but there's still questions there and then you have Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. So yeah, I like Kenneth Walker. >> All right. The Chiefs did not make the playoffs. We'll see if Andrew thinks they will be back there. Let's go to the Chargers. 11 wins under Harball and he has done that each of his first two seasons but they have not won a playoff game here. And when you take a look at the ad and subtractions here, not a big name that jumps off the roster. They got rid of Greg Roman. They're going to have a new offensive coordinator there. But this is Justin Herbert now in season number seven. Can he finally get this Chargers team deeper into the playoffs? >> Yeah, I mean Justin Herbert is a a very talented quarterback. I feel like that needs to be reiterated because I know he he takes some you know, he takes some shots not necessarily nationally but locally because of the list that come out and who he's compared to but yeah, I mean he needs to be able to deliver in the post season plain and simple but there's a lot of layers as to why the Chargers haven't reached expectations. He hasn't played well in the post season but he's also a big reason why they are a they're viable. So yeah, I mean I think he's I mean I feel like I say this every year but I feel like he's ready to to take a step forward and and lead this team to to another another uh you know, post season run. >> Yeah, 54 sacks last year. Their offensive line was a mess but you know, Andrew when their offensive line was healthy, you could make a strong argument that they possibly could have been a Super Bowl contending team. >> Yeah, they just didn't have the offensive line and I think it you know, if if if those out there haven't watched Chargers football, think back to the Eagles-Chargers game when the offensive line was just really leaky and I mean Justin Herbert was playing banged up in that game and he took a lot of hits. They they've added different pieces like Jake Slaughter out of Florida. He's going to play guard for them, I believe. They took him in the second round. They have Biadasz at center. Cole Strange comes over. Joe Walt is there at tackle. Rashawn Slater. So, if they're healthy, and that's a big if, they they should have enough pieces up front to support what they have in the skill position with Quinton Johnston and Ladd McConkey, who I like quite a bit as a route runner. He's really good working the intermediate levels of the field. Amari Hampton at running back. So, yeah, I mean, I do like their their complement of skill players. >> All right, defense. They By the way, they changed coordinators on offense and on defense. Their defense was really good last year. Jesse Minter. He's now the head coach in Baltimore. When you take a look at the defense, they drafted Messidor from Miami in the first round there. What do you When you look at that defense, this is a pretty darn good defense if that offense can be more consistent. >> Yeah, I mean, the defense isn't too bad. A player who I really like, who's not quite a household name, but he should be is Daiyan Henley, their their linebacker. He's a sort of an undersized outside linebacker, but he's extremely fast, covers a lot of ground. Tuli Tuipulotu is is an edge rusher that they have. I like him and Tarheeb Still, one of their corners out of Maryland, is someone that I was at his pro day and I thought pretty highly of him. He was drafted in the fifth round in 2024. He's slated to start for them. They also have Cam Hart out of Notre Dame. I interviewed him before the draft in 2024. Another really interesting player there and yeah, I mean their back end, you know, apart from Derwin James maybe has some questions cuz they're they're not exactly household names, but I think that there's a lot of really interesting pieces for for them to really work with. >> All right, there's the Chargers. This is a really interesting division. I think you can really make an argument for any of these three. We'll see who Andrew likes at the end of our AFC West preview. We go to Denver was neck and neck last year. They lost Bo Nix in the playoff game last year and that really changed the whole dynamic for them. They did add Jaylen Waddle. You could possibly say that is that the difference-making move for the Denver Broncos. >> Yeah, I mean I like this offensive bunch. You're talking about Bo Nix and I'm expecting him to take a leap forward next season. Having that postseason experience. He's coming off the injury, of course, so we'll have to wait and see, but the the running back situation. They they have JK Dobbins, RJ Harvey at UCF who was teammates with Eagles cornerback Mac McWilliams. Courtland Sutton is primarily he's an underrated player. He's sort of a big body possession guy, but someone who knows how to use his frame to his advantage and he's a quarterback friendly option. Jaylen Waddle comes over. Troy Franklin from Oregon is there. He was a fourth round pick in 24. Yeah, I mean I think that this is a unit that that you look at it and there's a a lot of continuity there and with Bo Nix I think of being such a young quarterback, I think that'll be especially paramount. >> They traded their first round pick away to get Jaylen Waddle. 14 wins for the Broncos last season, but they got 68 sacks, 11 more than any other team. When you think about the Broncos, their 14 wins weren't because of this high-flying high-powered offense. This might be the best defense in football, Andrew. >> Yeah, Mike, it's really interesting. They they have a lot of pieces and every time I I've talked to a young pass rusher at the podium at the combine, a lot of those players were comparing their skill sets to Nick Benito. And that's seems to be someone who is widely recognized as and rightfully so as one of the premier pass rushers. He has a lot of intriguing tools. He leads the way there. They have Jonathan Cooper, another pass rusher, Zach Allen on their defensive line, D.J. Jones, Alex Singleton, former Eagles linebacker is there. Their secondary, they have Riley Moss. Ja'Quan McMillian's been a really good story as an undrafted free agent. He was a really When I looked at Christian Parker, that was really his first developmental project there and he's really established himself as one of the better nickel backs in the NFLs and Patrick Surtain's, you know, every he needs no introduction. >> Andrew, obviously, you take a look at that team, the Denver Broncos, that's going to be Nix. Where where are you on Bo Nix? They need healthy Nix, but I don't even know what a healthy Nix are are they good enough? >> I have my doubts, especially you have a quarterback that I'm not quite sure that he has, you know, the I don't know that they have the infrastructure in place to be a pass-happy offense. And I think with a young quarterback like that, you need a running game, a strong running game to be able to support that. I don't know that they have that. J.K. Dobbins has been awfully banged up of late. R.J. Harvey's a really good complimentary piece, more of a pass-catching back, has good quicks. But I I mean, I don't I don't know that they have enough there offensively to really make a dent. They're going to have to be a defensive-heavy team. They're going to probably win a lot of their games based off of their their defensive prowess, I would imagine. >> All right, let's finish up with the team that had the number one overall pick and that was for Fernando Mendoza. Right now he is listed as the backup. They went out and made a ton of moves. Tyler Lindenbaum, they got a new coordinator, they got a new head coach, they got Nakobe Dean on defense. You got Kirk Cousins who currently is the starter. When you look at this Raiders team, have they made significant steps? Let's start on the offensive side of the ball. >> Man, I don't think so. I look at Tyler Lindenbaum who I like. He's their center. They have Jackson Powers-Johnson out of Oregon. He's their guard. So interior from an interior perspective, I like it. But in terms of just their overall group of skill players, aside from Brock Bowers and I mean you're looking at you're talking about Trey Tucker, you're talking about Ashton Jeanty where I don't know if they have enough from an offensive line standpoint to really for him to really be able to make a difference. Nor do I believe that they'll be in a position where they can lean into the running game. I think they'll be throwing a lot and I don't know that they're that they have a lot of options Jack Backs is another interesting player. They signed Jaylen Nailor who I think is a really good number three option. He was with the Vikings if you remember. So yeah, I mean we'll have to see how things shake. But right now I think that that's going to be a really really lackluster offense. >> Nakobe Dean is there. Quay Walker is there. They got Maxx Crosby back. Quitty Pay they signed. Have they done enough on defense to make them interesting? >> They also have again the Thomas Booker who former Eagles defensive tackle. He's he's a starter for them. And he was acquired in that trade that Tyquon Bennett got to Philadelphia. The Quitty Pay, Quay Walker, Nakobe Dean. I like that group right there. That adds some structure, some stability to that group. You talk about Maxx Crosby, Jeremy Chinn. I liked him quite a bit coming out of Southern Illinois. He hasn't really been able to stick. Eric Stokes with the Green Bay Packers. I was a little higher on him coming out of the draft out of Georgia, I believe, and he really hasn't been much more than a number two, a capable number two corner. So, yeah, I mean, that you could you can see some of you could see the progress. I still don't know that they're ready to contend for anything in the from a divisional perspective this year. They still feel like they're a couple years off, especially by that point Mendoza should be up to speed and they should have a little bit more firepower offensively to help them out. >> All right, Andrew, let's see who wins the AFC West. What is your predictions for this season? >> I'm going to say the Chargers, Mike. I'm going to go with the Chargers to win this division, followed by the Kansas City Chiefs, the Denver Broncos, and the Raiders. >> Wow. All right, so Denver 14 wins in third. >> Yeah, Denver was a tough one for me. I just don't know if they have enough offensively there to to be able to to put up enough points. You're you're going to be asking an awful lot of your defense every week based off of how things look on paper. >> All right, we will stay in the West. We'll go to the NFC West next week when we look at our division previews. The Eagles training camp continues. Andrew DiCecco for the Inside the Birds podcast, insidethebirds.com. You're on today's Football 4. All right, man, appreciate it. >> No problem.

title: Football at Four: More on Eagles' Carter Contract and Greenard Situation
text: Now time for football at four. Andrew DiCecco is joining us. Nick Earnshaw alongside PG. Now Andrew, big news coming down yesterday as the Eagles finally agreed to a four-year $152 million deal worth up to a $160 million deal with Jalen Carter. It finally got done Andrew, and how did it get done? >> Hey Nick, what's going on? Yeah, this is something that felt inevitable. Howie Roseman is not in the business of giving away or letting, you know, premier talent walk out the door. So it just felt like something that was going to happen. It just took a little bit of time. Actually, it didn't take all that much time, but the Eagles, you know, struck the deal and it was very timely in doing so because then it pours cold water on any potential you know, thought of a ripple effect of what that could mean in terms of practice participation and things like that, but the Eagles keep a centerpiece in the fold for the foreseeable future. And let's not forget they also locked in Jordan Davis back in March with three-year $78 million extension. They have their interior tandem for the foreseeable future. >> Andrew, now what does this mean going forward for guys like Cooper DeJean, Quinyon Mitchell? I know Howie Roseman spoke earlier today along with Nick Sirianni. What does it mean for those guys and their potential contracts long-term? >> Yeah, it's a great question and this is something that the Eagles have already envisioned. They they knew that these contracts are going to be coming down the pike and it's something that they've they've taken into account. And so in doing so, you have to alter the way you configure your roster, right? So they've been very offensive heavy. There's been a lot of money that's in been invested on that side of the ball and they've drafted on the defensive side. Now you almost have to do the opposite and you have to pay your young talent on the defensive side and start drafting and getting younger on the offensive side to to be able to afford these players, but make no mistake about it, guys. The Eagles know what they're up against. They know that Kyron Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, those are elite talent and much like Jalen Carter, there's zero chance that they're going to let those guys get away. So, it is it's not something that they that that was just sort of sprung on them. It's it's it's always been in, you know, at the at the front of their minds. They're not just looking at the roster as it stands now. They're looking at that what it's going to be, you know, you know, two years down the road, two, three years down the road. >> Does that mean Andrew maybe sacrificing a guy like Nolan Smith or Moro Ojomo coming up though? I mean, obviously Cooper DeJean and and Kyron are the two main guys, but sacrificing maybe a Nolan Smith or a Moro Ojomo coming up here? >> Yeah, they're they're going to have to. There's going to be some talent that unfortunately they're not going to be able to keep in the building. And I look at Moro Ojomo and that's a great example because that's someone who had a career high in sacks last year. He had six sacks. And I think that the arrow is very much trending up on him. He's a very good interior pass rusher. He has good quickness. If he's able to replicate that, then you're going to see Sorry about that background noise, but um you're going to see a team being willing to to pony up that kind of money much like they did for Milton Williams and it's going to price himself out of the Eagles budget more likely. Nolan Smith is interesting because he has that first round tag and he's a younger player, but he hasn't quite been able to put together a complete season. Injuries have sort of derailed his progress at times. He's an exceptional run defender at 245 lb. I would argue that pound for pound, guys, he's one of the more physical edge defenders in the game in terms of just setting the edge, but the sack numbers aren't there. And you may have to you're going to have to make a decision whether it's Jaylon Smith or Nolan Smith and I think Jaylon Smith has shown to be the player with more upside in terms of pass rush. And yeah, I mean you're just not able to keep everybody. They're going to have to make some difficult decisions. So, I I agree with you there. >> Andrew, today Roseman said his his famous mantra draft, develop, and resign. When it comes to roster building in the NFL, how important is that to have that philosophy that Roseman has had for years in that draft, develop, and resign? >> Yeah, it's incredibly important. You look at the evolution of Howie Roseman as a general manager. Earlier in his tenure, if you remember, it the rosters were largely predicated on on those free agent signings, right? Or or or striking on a trade instead of you know, drafting and developing. And I think right now what you've seen is sort of a shift in philosophy, but also Howie Roseman and his draft team deserves a lot of credit for the evaluation and being able to to really get these picks right. And then there's it's a multi-layered conversation because what they've done, and I like to really shed light on this, is the Eagles have assembled a a very strong group of assistant coaches that pride themselves on player development. And that also is something that that starts at the top. Nick Sirianni prioritizes player development, and that trickles down to his coaches, and the teaching element I don't I don't think can be overstated because that's something that a lot of these coaches, when we're talking to them in the spring, they say, you know, we look at ourselves as teachers first, then as a coach. And you look across the board, whether it's Clint Hurtt, whether it's linebackers coach Bobby King, Christian Parker, who's the defensive coordinator on the offensive side, you know, Jeff Stoutland for all these years, that doesn't happen by mistake. And so, the whole drafting and developing, it takes so many different people to make it work, but the Eagles have found a successful formula to draft some of these young players and then put them in position where all of a sudden they are the nucleus of your team, and you're setting yourselves up for sustained success. >> We're talking with Andrew DiCicco, Football at Four, Nick Earnshaw, PT, filling in for Mike Gill today, powered by the Inside the Birds podcast. Andrew, you were down at the first day of training camp today. Uh any takeaways you noticed from the first day of camp? >> Yeah, so all all the all eyes are on the offense, right? That's been the predominant storyline going into the summer. And what I can tell you, and it's only one day of practice, so you never want to get too carried away one way or the other, but what we have to go off of is one day, and I thought Jalen Hurts looked pretty sharp in terms of just ball placement, delivery. There was a lot of the middle middle of the field throws today, which is a hallmark of this offense. And there was a throw in particular, I think it was a dig route to DeVonta, where Quez Watkins had pretty tight coverage, but the throw was better. Jalen gets that one in. There was another one where Darius Slay makes a nice catch, where Jalen Hurts sort of drops it in the bucket there. Darius dives just a little bit to come up with it. But by and large, I thought that he looked sort of comfortable in there, didn't see the happy feet, and he was throwing with good anticipation. Again, it's just one practice, but it's certainly encouraging moving forward. And Josh Sweat, guys, on the defensive side was a one-man wrecking crew. There's no pads on. This is still part of the acclimation period, but what you're seeing from Josh Sweat is really a continuation of what I saw last summer and what you all saw during the season and what I saw in the spring. And that is a player who is now putting everything together. Now, the the understanding and the grasp of this defense has has caught up to his athleticism. He used to be able to kind of turn it loose and play freely. He has a more refined approach as a pass rusher. There's more moves. He is able to have more of an attention to detail and know how to read offensive tackles. And there was plays where he's storming into the backfield, where he's giving Jordan Mailata, uh uh, you know, some trouble because he's very quick off the snap and things like that. So, I thought J looks hot early in practice, especially, was someone who caught my eye. >> Yesterday, the news was Jalen Carter. Today was a little bit of injury news, uh, with Jonathan Gnarl. He goes on the pup list to start camp with a pectoral strain. Any updates you can provide the audience, Andrew, uh, with Gnarl's injury? >> Yeah, well, he he suffered the the pec strain lifting before training camp, and it's not expected to be a long-term concern. Now, there is certain layers to this conversation, right? Because Jonathan Gnarl is 29 years old. He had a shoulder injury last year that limited him to 12 games, and he hasn't yet participated in team drills with the Eagles. In the spring, he was a non-participant during team drills, but that was all part of the plan. That was, you know, Gnarl's camp and the Eagles, they they came to that agreement. But, it's I don't know that it's something that you can just say nothing to see here, and and there's no concern. I mean, anytime you have a a top-tier pass-rusher that's dealing with something like this, and and pec strains can be tricky, uh, especially when you're talking about that position, where you have to be able to extend and and shed blocks and things like that. So, I don't know that you want to rush somebody like that back, and they're starting him on the PUP list. And while that's not good, we have to still let it play out and see how it goes, and it's going to give more opportunities to Jobe Sant and Nolan Smith and and some of those guys to just get reps and continue to to hone their craft. >> Andrew, this might be a question for a couple weeks down the line, but I'm going to ask it to you. Um, should we anticipate that the Eagles kind of go away from their philosophy of not playing their guys in the preseason game with the new offensive coordinator and the brand new offense that this off that uh these players are going to have to um go through here. Should we anticipate a change of philosophy here from these Eagles? >> I I don't know that you will. Uh and the only reason why I say that is it just seems like there it's hard to argue with results. And I understand that there's just the newness of the offense and it would lead one to believe, well, you got to get reps in a game before you get into the regular season. But that's where the value of joint practices come in where it's largely the first team and a little second team that that gets most of the work. Um that the Eagles have two practices slated with the New England Patriots. That's going to be something that I think they're going to look at it as being hugely invaluable to laying the foundation and really fine-tuning some of the details of this offense. I don't know that you want to put any of those players at risk. I mean, you're seeing some of these injuries already across the league. The Eagles have seemingly uh a really good grasp on how much work they need or or certain certain levels of of of of work that they need to get their starters through throughout the summer that they deem to be acceptable. And if they if they uh or come to the conclusion that the offense isn't quite where they want it to be, well, then maybe that becomes part of the conversation. But I don't see Nick Sirianni deviating from an approach that has been so successful over the, you know, the past few years uh at the for the sake of the offense being new. I I I believe it there's going to they'll find other ways to ensure that they get that work in. >> Andrew Di Cecco, Inside the Birds. One more before you go. The LeBron James conversation made its way through camp. I was seeing all that going through. Uh what were some of the the interesting answers that you saw from some of the players? Saquon, I know was asked about it. Jalen, DeVonta Smith. I mean, that that buzz is continuing through training camp, am I right? >> Yeah, man. How about Jordan Davis sits down? The first thing he says is, "What do you guys think of the LeBron trade?" Like >> [laughter] >> that that that conversation, Nick, and and you know this, it it it just it is it's not going to let up. It's It has the city buzzing right now. Players who have grown up watching him play are are thrilled that they get to play in the same They're playing in the same city. He's playing across, you know, right there. Um it The excitement's palpable and it extends beyond uh you know the you know, fans. You're seeing players like that that are that are kind of uh almost almost like a kid on Christmas morning knowing that a player who they've watched and you know, all these years is now playing here in Philadelphia. So, it's just a really good time time here in Philadelphia. And yeah, if you needed any other further indication of that, just look at what Look at the players' reactions. >> Yeah, it it was stunning. A lot of the players were talking about it through camp today. First day of training camp for the Philadelphia Eagles. Andrew DiCecco, Inside the Birds. Thank you so much for joining us at Football 4, man. >> You got it, guys. Have a great day.

title: Zyon McCollum & Ben Bredeson on Being Back on the Field | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Hey everybody, how we doing? >> So is it pretty good to start off camp with an interception on day one for you? >> Absolutely, it's always good to touch the ball, but you know this business you're judged by the present moment, so it's about what I do moving forward. >> message to you guys at the start of training camp in terms of setting the tone for the 2020 season. >> Yeah, he was really just not expecting everybody to put everything together on day one. He just has been preaching getting better from day to day, focusing on, like I said, the present moment, focusing on the now, and just doing finding one thing every day to get better at. By the end of the training camp we'll be where we have to be at. We're not starting over though, you know, OTAs was a big moment for us to continue to come together as a team, build our camaraderie, and we have to take that momentum so that by the time we're going into the preseason we're starting on all cylinders. >> There's so many new faces on defense this year. You could have as many as five new starters on defense. That's about half the unit. Are you surprised how quickly it those pieces have fit in and come together? Is that like a a testament to the off season work you guys did cuz the first two days you guys have held your own in training camp. >> Yeah, Bowls has put a lot in and you know, he's demanding a lot from a lot of these new guys, but the way that they came in during the off season, during the OTAs, it doesn't surprise me because you could tell right off that these guys are professionals. You know, the free agents that we got and and some of the new faces, you could tell right off their demeanor that they take things professionally, they take things seriously, and you know, they don't put too much on their shoulders either. You know, they're here to have fun and smile, but when it's time to get in between those lines, it's all about football. >> What has it been like with these new vets that have come into this defense? Tom Coughlin yesterday was talking about like their eagerness to compete and and to win here. So what has it been like with their addition? >> Yeah, it's been fun, you know, seeing new faces, getting new energy. It's always fun because they have so much to offer as well, you know, they've been in other systems, they've played a lot of football, so they have experience. So, being able to soak in some of that experience, being able to learn the way that they see things, too, kind of gives us new perspectives that we can kind of fit into our defense here and kind of put everything together. >> Zion, Thomas talked about Keontay Scott and how impressive he's been. He used the word phenomenal the way he's processed his defense. From your perspective, how impressive has it been considering he didn't get much in the spring and is able to come out playing different positions out there on defense and the way he is playing now? >> Yeah, exactly. They probably thrown the most at him and I understand it. I mean, he's been playing safety, nickel, and corner, so he knows the entire defense and he didn't take a rep but like not even a rep in our OTAs. He come out here and he's already played all three spots, so he's real cerebral, he's real smart, he understands the game, but he also has his hat on fire all the time. He brings the energy, so you could tell he's going to be a fun player to play with as he continues to grow. >> Zion, through two camp practices, what what are your thoughts about the give and take between the offense and the defense? It looked pretty even early on and then kind of the offense took over late. >> Yeah, if you start chirping at Baker, then it just turns him on, you know what I mean? So, it's fun to play with Baker because, you know, he's going to give you your best his best every single day and he's going to get his guys going and then he's going to let us know about it and so it's we'll be eager to continue that battle tomorrow. I'd say we're probably like even right now, so defense has got to come on top tomorrow. >> You mentioned Keontay Scott. Also wanted to get your thoughts on Jacob Harris because he's handling more outside corner duties. Just how has that transition been from your perspective? >> Seamless. Jacob's a dog, you know, and he's real smart, too. He's He's more quiet, but, you know, he's like a silent assassin. Like he's going to come from behind and he might be small, but he plays big. >> So, you saw today Johnson score three touchdowns today. What's it been like going against him in his second season? Where have you seen him grow a little bit then maybe try to go against him now and allow all those touchdowns from? >> No, I think what I've seen the most from him is his patience. You know, early on he you know, he's a guy he's come from Oregon with Bucky and he he saw Bucky make all these big plays and you know, he wanted to kind of step into that. But, he's matured a lot and he's grown in his patience. You could tell that him and Baker's relationship has grown and I think he knows who he is as a player now and I think Zach has done an amazing job fitting him into the offense. >> What are your initial impressions of Ted Hurst who's one of the bigger receivers here on this roster now? >> He's smart, too. I mean, he's really really quick. A lot faster than you would expect and quicker than you would expect for a tall receiver. You know, he's still learning like all the young guys, but he's going to be a fun addition to the offense. I can tell, you know, him and Baker's connection is already starting to grow. You know, Baker's trying to get him going and and get him to make that jump coming from a smaller school, but it doesn't affect him out here. You know, he's a fun guy in the locker room and then when he shows up to work, you know, he's all business. >> Jake Browning had a day today in terms of, you know, the end of practice throwing those touchdowns. What What have you seen from the new backup quarterback? >> Yeah, I think like they just want to compete and the way that we play, you know, you could get the starter. He could be going against the starters on defense. You know, everybody's rotating in at all time and I've seen a real cerebral take from the offense coming in with a new offensive coordinator. You know, everybody has to be really locked in and detailed and you kind of learn a new system, but these backup quarterbacks, you know, they're trying to prove themselves just as much and that's what this camp is about, competition. >> What difference have you noticed in the coaching in the quarterback room now that Rashad Johnson's kind of taken over? >> It's been It's been more detailed. You know, we go out and we find one thing to work on to get better at each and every day and he tells us what he expects from us, you know. Today we're working on this, this, and that, and I need to see it translate. And so in indie drills, you know, that's all we're working. We're working these specific drills, and then it translates over, and then we continue to work on other things moving forward, and by the end of camp, you have a full body of armor. >> What is your initial about giving away any state secrets about this this offense this offense this project? What is the overarching thing that that you have noticed, or what's the big takeaway? >> I think it's real situational. You know, they have real good situational awareness, and getting everybody on the same page. They're communicating well. It's a lot of movement, a lot of moving parts, and the personnel groupings have been, you know, confusing from a defensive standpoint. So being able to lock in and kind of understand, you know, that they're going to give us every look, every personnel grouping. You don't know what's coming, and, you know, it's fun to go against now, cuz it's really preparing the defense for the future and for the season. And then I'll be excited to see our offense go against other defenses. >> Zion, do you like You'll have the pads on in a few days. Is your game better with pads? Are you like playing more physical? Cuz right now guys are kind of just slinging by in their pajamas right now, but do you like when the pads come on? >> Pads have to come on. That's that's what we play for. That's the reason we play football is to hit and to be gladiators out there, and, you know, slow down some of these quicker offensive guys a little bit with a little bit more weight. But as a defensive guy, I like putting the pads on. You pray for things like that. You know, it's finally get some physical contact in and play the game the way it's meant to be played. >> Thank you guys. >> Thank you, Zion. >> Thanks. >> Hello, everybody. >> Hello. >> Good morning, Ben. >> Good morning. >> So The he came up here and he mentioned that fully healthy this offensive line, he sees it as a top three unit. How good does it feel to be back out here and kind of have the group at full strength? >> Obviously, uh you know, we love playing with each other. We This is going on year three now of uh having that group. Um unfortunately, last year, as we all know, like with some poorly timed injuries and injuries all together, we weren't able to get that unit out there. Um but being able to come out here and kind of see see it all coming back together, it gets us all excited. Uh obviously, we had good success in '24 with uh um when everyone was healthy, and hopefully we can keep everybody on the field this year. >> And what are your impressions of Zach Robinson's offense and just kind of the the tendencies and situational football that you guys have been playing so far? >> Yeah, I'm very very impressed with it. Um you know, a little bit more of a you know, some wide zone stuff going in, and it's um you know, it's something that I I feel can work, and it's obviously worked with um you know, Atlanta in his previous stops before that. So, uh I'm excited for it. >> used the phrase "It's all about ball." >> about our time. You just talk about just what I mean with with what's going on off the field with him and others. Just what in the locker room how >> is it reassuring to have that mentality to have? >> Yeah, I mean Baker hasn't missed a beat or changed one bit through anything that's going on. You know, he's still our quarterback. He's still the same leader, friend, guy that we all love. And you know, when he says it's all about ball, he means it. Um you know, he's probably one of the most consistent and locked-in individuals I've ever had the chance to play with. And uh you know, it's an honor going to work with him every day, and no matter what's happening outside of the building, uh he has not changed one bit and is ready to go at all times. >> What was it like for you to be able to watch Baker go through what he went through um as not just a teammate, but a friend >> Yeah, it was uh you know I it's tough anytime anybody gets hurt. And uh you know, Cody's was obviously an interesting one because he finished the game in Houston. So, nobody really had much information at the time and then to get the news that he was out for the season was um you know, a little it was shocking at the time. And uh for someone like Cody who really never missed a snap his entire life, I believe, not just his professional career, but his entire football career. Um that was a huge blow for for him. And uh but he took it as as well and professional as you could. He went in there and did his rehab. Um kept his head up, helped us as well as he could. Um and then, you know, we had some good discussions about it, especially at the end of the season when we were both in the training room nursing some some knees. Uh you know, we talked about it and he was in a good head space at that point, but uh you know, Cody's a tough guy. He's one of the toughest toughest guys I've ever played with, for sure. I mean, he's a farm farm boy from North Dakota, so fits fits pretty well. And uh you know, he handled it as well as anybody could. Uh how he's playing, sorry? Yeah, I mean, he's going to fit in just fine in the room. I'm not concerned about um personality-wise fitting in. You know, he's a great kid, works hard, um good sense of humor, so he'll be fine there. Uh playing-wise, I mean, he's he's got good hands and he's a he's a good athlete. Um you know, he's young guy and out there busting his ass every single day, working hard. And uh we saw improvements from when he first came in here right after the draft to uh the end of OTAs, and I think he's getting better over the summer break. So, um you know, he's on the right track and I'm excited to see where he goes. >> You had to play center last year. Just curious to get your thoughts on Graham Barton and kind of his development. A big year for him. >> Yeah. >> Just being the center of communication. >> I think he's gotten a lot more confident and uh I think he's done a a great job leading the unit in terms of making the calls. Um he's got a he's got a good grasp of how the offensive line should be run. I think he does a very very good job of making sure that everybody's on the same page. Um from a physical standpoint, Graham's always been pretty a freak athlete for an offensive lineman. Um you know, he's extremely fast, strong, bends really well. And I think a big improvement from this last year to the point we're in right now, his technique in pass protection's gotten a lot better. He's really working on uh you know, bringing his feet and his hands together and using them all at one piece to keep guys off of him. Um he's doing he's doing them very well. He's making improvements every every every week through OTAs and again, like much like Billy, um I thought he made a good jump from so far. I mean, we're 2 days in from OTAs to now. So, um no, it's same answer with Billy. I mean, Graham's off to great start for his year three. Can't believe Graham's already in year three. We still always made fun of him for being a rookie. So, um he's doing really really well. Brought him. >> Anything else? >> We spoke about Cody and talked about his journey last season, but can you just speak to what it's like having him back out there, you guys all being back together and why he's so important >> Yeah, I think I hit on it before. I mean, Cody's Cody brings a toughness to the O-line. Um you know, you see it in his ability to finish plays and finish blocks. And uh you know, he's a a physical guy. and put him next to Luke and Graham and you know, he does great things in the run game. He's extremely strong in the pass game. Um and to be completely honest, his personality helps us a lot. Cody is a funny guy, keeps everything loose and light. So, you know, it's a good offset out there and uh I'm just really excited to have him back. Good? Thanks, guys.

title: Todd Bowles on Rueben Bain Jr.’s Intelligence | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Morning. >> I thought Jake Browning had a pretty good end to practice. What have you seen from your new backup quarterback so far? >> Like I said, he's experienced. He's very good knowing where to go with the football and learn a new scheme. He understands it quicker than the other two guys right now. So, very happy with what I'm seeing right now. >> Tez made a lot of plays, especially in the end zone. He got in the end zone a lot last year. Just what is his development a slight guy who seems to have a knack of getting in? >> Well, mentally he's been outstanding. He he he's playing fast because he knows the system or he's getting it down a lot quicker and he's become a very good pro and a studious person right there. So, that allows him to play even faster than he's already played. So, and he can get down the field and make plays and he made them. >> He had some drops yesterday and he comes back and has a big day today. What does that say about his growth not just physically but mentally? >> I mean, it's day two. You're going to work on the things you got a worse at yesterday. So, he got better today and he worked on that and he concentrated a little more and just just got to be a steady progression for everybody. >> Scott's been getting some reps at outside corner, which you said he was going to. How's he looked so far? What's that process been like for him? He's he played so much inside in the slot. >> Well, for him it's it's been great because he he went yesterday for the first day after missing the whole spring. He played corner, he played nickel and he played safety. So, to process that kind of information and to come out on your first day and then come out today and do what he's been doing has been phenomenal to see. It really helps him learn the defense moving around playing different spots. So, his mind is outstanding. So, we just look for him to keep getting better. >> Does it help you with the play caller because with him and Jacob Harris and you know, Tykee and Winfield and Zion, you've got a lot of guys that you can kind of rotate in the slot if you want to? >> It helps in case of injury and things come up. You know, you can juggle guys around that's done some things. You don't really have to panic. >> Reuben seemed to be in the middle of a lot of things. What did Reuben think today? >> He is a very smart player, you know, his intelligence really shows when you see him. It It probably more than the toughness and the the sack ability and that's saying a lot because he's he's outstanding at that, but to picking up the system and just understanding things that a lot of rookies don't understand coming in. He's been great at that. >> How much of that intelligence is like instinct versus like preparation and and and going home and and doing the homework? >> I think it's both. It's all that plus the coaches he had formerly, you know, you send a lot of credit to them too, the guys at Miami and the guys at his high school because he came in here like that. We can't take credit for that. It's been only two days of practice in training camp, but he prepares, he understands, he asks questions and he's very bright. >> Coach, we saw Chris Godwin in the steam today. Is that more of a maintenance day for Chris Godwin or was it a thumb? >> Yeah, no, it was a maintenance day. We have Chris on the schedule and we know how when we're going to practice him and when we're going to take him off. >> We didn't see you today on the field. I know you tweaked back during um the conditioning test and I I didn't see Tristan out here either. Were they just inside getting treatment? >> They're inside. >> Can you give a better sense with Tristan and how long you might want to hold him out, when he might be back to practice? >> Don't know. A hamstring's a tricky thing. I'm waiting to hear from the trainers and get a better idea on that. But right now, I'm really not sure. >> Talk about the first open practice for the general public. Talk about the atmosphere and you guys putting on a a good show, a couple nice catches from Mike Evans. How was it here for the for the fans to watch every time? >> I mean, it's great on a Thursday coming out and a lot of people are at work, but these guys come out all the time and support us and they've been outstanding over the years and they've been outstanding today, you know, and Te'o has had a heck of a day, so everybody got to see that, so that was fun. >> Yeah, a lot of kids wearing the Baker jerseys. Kids yelling, "Baker's the goat." Talk about Baker continuing to be, you know, a face for this franchise. Obviously, the contract situation is what it is, but these fans are really behind him. >> I mean, they they love him. I mean, next to Brown going to Philly, I mean, Baker probably second most popular guy out here right now, but, you know, he does a lot for the kids, especially right in the community, and they really love when he does comes out here, and they they support him a lot. >> Our Shaq freaking blocked it last year. Is he starting to show some some receiving skills out here, too, as well? >> Uh the thing he is showing is his athleticism. That's what we're most excited about right now. I want to see him in pads, so I want to see what the blocking and everything else looks like, but the athleticism out of pads have been great to see for him, so I'm really excited to see him when he gets some pads. >> Aside from a competition standpoint, what have you seen from the inside linebacker position? It looked like John Bostic had a good day out there. >> They're all They're all smart, you know. They're all smart. Other than Trotter, you know, Bostic's been here last year, and Nick Jackson's been here for a year. Other than the two free agent rookies, those guys are pretty much veterans, so it's going to be a lot of competition. They're all savvy in their own right. They understand how to make plays. They understand to put themselves in position, even though they're all different athletically, and it's going to be a good battle, so Bostic had a great day today. He had a great read. He had an interception right there. He's a very heady player. He has a lot of recall from last year, so he's just got to keep getting better. >> And what have you seen from Zion McCollum? He had an interception yesterday. Just him in coverage, making improvements heading into this year. >> Yeah, with day two, just working on little things for Zion as far as reading the hip, moving his feet, in press coverage, understanding when he can get picked and when he can't get picked. It's more of the the tiny mental things that he's been working on day by day, and not really trying to do the bigger things. He understands the picture, but he's expanding his game to see where all his help is around him, so he knows exactly what he's doing. >> Alex Anzalone called timeout late in practice there. Is that something that's pretty unique, or is that something he did on his own? >> No, we talked about it. Uh it's game plan situation. When you're down to the last play, and the offense comes out, and you have a chance to see what the formation is and we have one timeout left. He's heady enough to make a timeout call so we can assess the situation and come back with a call that we think that they're going to that's going to defend what they're running. Alex is a hell of a man coverage guy and Bucky's a heck of a receiver so, you know, he doesn't panic out there like most guys do uh being at the backer spot. He kind of covers like a safety so he has very good awareness and headiness about that and you're looking at two good athletes play. Alex just won that one. No, it doesn't force him on the field earlier but Jaymac and Mecca can do that as well so we're not we don't have a problem there. We just started him out there. He's the tallest and when you get a rookie like that in here you usually try to concentrate on one position right there so that's kind of where we have him at. Thanks.

title: Baker Mayfield: ‘I’m All Ball’ | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How you doing? Great. Not a whole lot have been going on, guys. What are you doing? >> You guys you set the deadline and you're done talking, apparently. Just how disappointed are you you couldn't bring that to fruition based on what you've done the last 3 years and what are your feelings about it? >> Yeah, I mean, obviously I've I've told you guys I've been pretty upfront and honest about my feelings about Tampa, um it being home for now our our family, raising kids here. We love it here. Um I wanted the deal done and set the deadline and told them it was going to be all ball after that and I I did mean that. And I don't know if they thought I was just going to take some of the offers that they gave, but um I'm at the point of my career and understanding what I've brought to this franchise, one I'm I'm very, very thankful for the chance they gave me. Do not get me wrong on that. But I also know I I really know what I've brought to this franchise leadership-wise, um and even play-wise. It's been some of the best years of of my career and I think it's only going to trend upwards. Just being comfortable and feeling that. So, um disappointing in that regard to to not have you know, to feel disrespected a little bit. And um that's really the disappointing part to to feel undervalued after you know, thinking you've earned it. Um this is not a poor me thing. It's there's a lot other people that have it way worse off, but I can sit here and and look at other quarterbacks and peers and um evaluate myself based on that and and put myself in certain categories that uh I deserve to be compensated for that. And I think I'm a franchise quarterback. I've been told I'm a franchise quarterback. Uh it's been said publicly from ownership down here. And so, to not have a deal done is very disappointing, but I said the deadline was the deadline and um I addressed the team to let them know I I meant that. It's it's all ball. I'm with these guys. I think all the guys that have been here know exactly who I am. Uh the guys that are new here, I wanted to address that cuz they might have had a a a notion prior to coming here about who I am as a person, but it's it's all team. It's all about winning here now and uh what we're going to do and you know, hopefully Vita gets his back fixed and and gets his his deal done. I mean, he's the second longest-tenured Buck behind CG and Vita deserves that. He's the anchor of our defense and so I hope they take care of him. Um it's disappointing to say the least, but it's all ball here and I know I'm going to have a good year. I know this team this the things that we went through last year uh put us in a good spot for this year depth-wise. A lot of guys have been thrown in the fire uh to be able to grow and learn uh fast and it it didn't go the way we wanted, but it's a new season and it's it's going to help us in the long run this year. Added some new pieces and so I'm excited about it. It's all ball from here. Um you know, after today like I'll answer a few more questions about the contract, but after today I'm not I'm not answering anymore cuz I'm not negotiating anymore. >> You've never heard of shoulder chips, but in some way they can make those always bet on himself. >> Yeah. >> They'll do it again. You get to the end of the year, you have a great year without a effect. They can always franchise tag you. There's other options that they have. What would you do for your relationship? Do you want >> Uh it's disappointing. It's you know, I'm not I'm not the first one to go through it like this. This is kind of historically how they've done negotiations, which is disappointing when you think you're a cornerstone of the franchise um to be treated like that, but disappointing. I know I know I'm no dummy. I know I know the contract and salary cap what's going on. Franchise tag isn't exactly in play for them. It'd be a lot of dead money. Um so it's it is what it is and like I said, unfortunate, but I'm excited. I'm in the best shape I've ever been in in a really good place uh and I'm feeling really confident with the staff that that Todd's put together um that we're going to have a really really good team. >> You you've talked about the fact that you've seen how the team operates. You've seen Antoine Winfield Jr. go out and ball out with one of the high-speed defensive backs in the league. You've seen Mike Evans have to go through a contract twice. You've seen Chris have to do it and receive very fair fair market values. Do you have some hope or maybe faith that after this season, that their number will go up and that you'll you'll be a Buccaneer? >> I I mean, obviously, yes. Um but I've been on the other side of the nasty business that it is the NFL. And so, uh yeah, I have hope, but expecting and and and hoping is is two different things. And so, um yeah, I hope so, but all I can control is how I play this year and how the team does this year. And for me, that's wins. Good things happen when the team wins, and uh the rest will take care of itself. But yeah, I've sat here and and watched these guys go through it. Uh even Tristan. And so, um talk about the best best tackle in the league. Only person in NFL history that's been an All-Pro at right and left. Had to had to have a hold in in training camp to get it done. So, um disappointing. You hope they take care of their guys. And uh but like I said, it's going to be a good year. >> Do you think the departmental what? Is that your deadline? Is that your deadline because you think it would be a distraction to engage in something >> Yeah, I mean, it's Like I told you guys, it's all ball. And it's I don't want to talk about it. And if you've waited this long to take care of your franchise quarterback, that's too bad, cuz it's only going to get worse from here. Yeah, I'm going to have a really good year. >> How do you compartmentalize things for yourself when you have to come out here and focus strictly on football? >> That's the business side of it. Uh um it's it's two separate things. You know, it it's We all come out here and we're playing the game of football for a job. And so, we we do have to take back uh take a step back and realize that. Um but there is a business aspect of it. So, you separate that. When you come out here, like I said, if you win, you play well, good things happen. So, that that's what I'm focused on. So, that's how you compartmentalize it. It's that's in the past now. That's behind me. And right now, all I can do is is focus on this year. >> Thank you. For the last year, you saw Mike walk out the door for less money to go across the nation. You just mentioned Vita's situation, your situation. Are you concerned that the way this organization is handling their franchise players that that's going to reverberate through your locker room? >> Not at all. Um I think that I think that's an easy scapegoat for the outside media to look at, but to be honest with you, inside the locker room all that does is bring us closer together. Um it's the downstairs aspect of our building is really, really special, and our guys know that, and they cherish that. So, uh it's only bringing our guys together. Um you know, that might be a negotiating tactic on their part, but uh this is like I said when I got here in 2023, it's a really close-knit locker room, and that's the leadership that was here prior to me getting here, and just the way they carry each other, uh carry themselves, lead by example, and when it comes to the things like this, it's it's separate from the football thing. It's you take care of each other, you play on the field, good things happen, you take care of each other, and and go from there. >> You seem so at peace about it, Baker. Was Was it difficult to get to that point mentally? How long did it take you to just be so at peace with it? >> Um I think if I hadn't gone through a couple different situations earlier on in my career, I'd probably be in a different headspace. Uh it also helps being a little bit more mature now, uh and having different priorities in life. But, uh yeah, I'm at peace. It's I think what I've done here is my resume, and I think it spoke for itself, and so if that's not recognized, that's okay. I'm just going to go continue to add to it. >> Baker, internally, is this I know you talked about the deadline, but internally, is this something that drove you or maybe you used this as motivation to push you through? >> It No. Money should never [clears throat] be the motivation in football. It's It's how do I help this team win? It's never going to be the motivation for me. Um when it comes to having a chip on your shoulder and all that, it And for me, it just puts me in the mindset of betting on myself, and that's something I'm pretty familiar with, you know? Um and it's it's a good place to be as a as a high competitive guy. Um sometimes you have to put yourself in backed into a corner, and fight your way out, but I have a lot of guys and a lot of staff around me that are with me. And so, I'm not alone in it. Uh we're fighting for the same goal and that's to be playing in February. I mean, they're not They're not talking to me. I know that. If my agent answers it, he's not going to bother me with it unless it's actually recognized for my value. Yeah, and that's And like going back to the first question when I opened up, like Tampa has felt like home from the beginning. The community has embraced Emily and I. It's felt like home and that's that's probably the worst part about it is we do want to spend the rest of my career here, however long God willing that is. Um but it's it's always been home. We'll come back here. I found a great routine, great gym to train. The people that are here um it's it's an awesome community. We love this city. We love giving back to it, helping it become a great place to raise kids and families, uh and just support each other. That's what good communities do and so, uh yeah, when it comes to kiddos, it's the best. >> Speaking of family, you've had a chance to watch the Quarterback series now, I'm sure, on Netflix. What were your thoughts? Did it meet your expectations and how you wanted it it to be presented? yeah, I mean, to be honest with you, I didn't watch the full series. Uh they they sent all the clips of us in it just so I could give the final okay. Um Apologies to the families with little kiddos cuz the language on there is actually not very suited for them. Um it's might might be a little angry elf on the field every once in a while. Uh so, that's probably the part that I I do regret a little bit, but that's that's the fire on the field, unfortunately, that that comes out uh on TV. But um yeah, I wanted to portray that I'm all ball. It's You can say what you want in the media. You can say I'm cocky um and whatever, but it it's all ball. I love my teammates, I love this game, and I love playing it. >> Talk about fire, was it you and Seth? >> J.R. Baker from the The Cuts Big Board of Education. >> There's a few things. >> You talked about fire, was that you and Seth that I saw talking back and forth a little bit out there? And you had some battles with with Carr. >> He just needs to figure out that the Miami green on the on the Bucks red is a horrible look. It's July, it's not Christmas time. He needs to figure that out. >> He's trying to clear his royalties, right? You know, maybe show Bain some love at the same time he's trying >> He hadn't been here since Bain and Scott showed up. >> Was Was it difficult or how easy was it just to turn the page and to focus on football like you said? >> Uh on the >> Knowing the deadline had passed. >> Walking back out on the field, >> [snorts] >> was it easy to turn the page and focus solely on training camp and football? >> Uh really easy. Um when you're not presented with an offer appealing whatsoever. yeah, it's easy. It's easy to turn the page, but also it's just that time of the year where you're itching to get back on the field. You're itching to see how this team comes together, how the how the how the offense comes together in a new system with a new coach, and uh it's just the exciting time of year that on paper we got a lot of potential, but it's just potential. And so we know we have to to put that all together. So, yeah, it's easy to to put that in the past when you're coming together with a great group like this. >> Baker, real quick, uh offensive line >> Are you saving one more question for the new voice of the Buccaneers? >> [laughter] >> Thank you, appreciate it. Offensive line's healthy now and everything. What What's it like to be out there with them and and your thoughts on the offensive line? >> Yeah. Um I mean, it's a it's a top-three unit in the league. Unfortunately, last year they didn't play one snap together. Um which stinks Stinks for me, but for us as a as a group, for our young guys, it gave them a lot of experience and depth. Uh they were Like I said, they were thrown into the fire, but when all five of those guys are out there rolling and some of those guys those guys got that experience last year, it's a very freeing feeling to have those guys out there. They're savages up front. They're really good. They have their chemistry is unbelievable. They know what we're trying to get done and when they're on the same page, uh our offense is just clicking. So, it starts with those guys and it goes from there. Yep.
