And uh he's he's probably I mean, everybody's in a competition, right? But he's pretty much pegged to be the Mo linebacker. We have the Mike and the Mo. Uh he's also a guy that you expect to be a leader. I know he's new to the team, but he's put a lot of years in in this league and he's going to wear the green dot. And so, he's going to be calling plays on defense. And uh I just feel like this is a guy that's going to be one of our defensive leaders and a big force for us over the middle of the field. >> And then, of course, Jose Ramirez. We kind of mentioned him a bit, but um what do you feel like the the hopes could be for a guy like that? If it's it's a tough position, especially if you're talking about the green dot with Todd Bowles' defense as a rookie. Is this something that they're sort of hoping he could step into and and be ready for in this rookie year? >> going to wear the green dot, but Tryon um Tryon would be one of the guys battling for the Mike position. Uh it's funny you think back Lavonte David just retired. We just talked about that. He was a second-round pick uh in 2012. And now here we have another second-round pick from the Midwest from a Midwest school. Uh hoping that they will be able to go from day one just like Lavonte David was. And Todd Bowles obviously, we talked about this a little earlier, really likes how um he is like a he calls him a downhill thumper. But a lot of uh scouts and so on in our personnel nail department around the draft time were defending the idea that even though he didn't do a lot of pass coverage at Mizzou, uh he has the skills to do so. And he's confident. He's talked about it as well. So, uh, I I don't think they expect him to be a liability in that regard. And if he's not, then I think he's got the inside track to be the starter there. >> And it's interesting, he's only 21. I think that it's it's incredible how young he is to be coming in. And so, even if there maybe are some areas that he hasn't done a lot of or could use some growth in, he's so young that I think they're like, "Oh, he's going to be able to have time to think about this and and figure this out." >> maturity standpoint, the fact that he's the son of Jeremiah Trotter and his father is probably probably held pretty high in that regard. >> And so, Servasier Dennis, this is the guy who obviously played a lot last year. What are the thoughts on him in the mix >> So, he'll be battling, too. To, you know, he started all of last year next to Lavonte David. You know, again, we talked about how our middle-of-the-field coverage was a liability for us. So, that would be something he would have to display, and early in his career, that was considered a strength for him. So, you can't count him out, but he definitely has competition for that job now. >> And then I know also the other addition to the room was Christian Rozeboom, and we just really needed two long-haired guys to add to our linebacker room. Apparently, that was what they decided we were missing. So, tell us a bit about Christian Rozeboom and and what we know about him. >> yet another guy who'll be competing for that Mike job. And even if he, you know, even if it ends up being Trotter, it's nice to have that depth. I don't think we've had veteran uh, depth, you know, proven experience veteran depth at that position much in recent years. You know, we've been rolling with more more like undrafted rookie guys like Nick Jackson and so on. So, even if he doesn't, and of course he will try and then you don't want to count that out that he, you know, he had 122 tackles for the Panthers last year. Also, a guy that you anticipate being very very much involved on special teams. >> Mhm. And then I know the other guys to kind of round out this room, you mentioned one of them, Nick Jackson and John Bullock. One of my favorite things about preseason is there inevitably ends up being some rookies and especially even kind of some undrafted guys or guys you don't expect who make some big plays, really kind of force the team to consider them for the roster or the practice squad and both of these guys I felt like had that last year. >> Nick Jackson in particular, he really filled up his stat line in the preseason last year and I remember as it was coming down it was clear that there was one spot open and probably Nick Jackson or John Bullock was going to get it and you looked at Nick Jackson with all of the stats and you thought it's probably going to be him and it ended up being John Bullock and that was because they thought he would be more of an asset on special teams and sure enough he did play a ton on special teams. But Nick Jackson was with us too on mostly on the practice squad for most of the year. So both those guys are back. If you keep five of them, you could see it's possible those two are battling for the same job. >> Mhm. All right, we are going to take one more break here and when we come back, we are so excited. We are going to get a chance to introduce you to the new voice of the Buccaneers play-by-play announcer Tony Castricone and so to already introduce you before he slides in here into the studio with us, he caught up with Chris Godwin yesterday after practice so take a look. >> What's up crew? Tony Castricone here with Chris Godwin, the OG in the wide receiver room getting ready to start year 10. I'm new to Tampa. I need all the advice man. Like what's your favorite thing about Tampa outside of football? >> Favorite thing about Tampa outside of football, honestly it it's got to be the people. I it it's such a laid-back community. Like whenever people see you around like they'll they'll say hi. Like they'll come in and they want to take pictures and stuff. But people are so respectful of the players, of like the Bucs organization and they're so welcoming. So it's got to be the the community. >> All right. Well, you're coming off the off season. What was different about this off season for you compared to some of your other off seasons in the past? >> I think this one it was it was nice to get a full off season to train. Like last the last one I was rehabbing an injury so that takes a whole new life of its own and puts a lot of stress on you mentally and physically. So it was nice to get back to being able to train for performance and not just like rehabilitation. >> Was there anything in particular you were really focusing on during the training? >> Um just mostly just getting back to like like being on my P's and Q's like top of route stuff, being really good like at my stances starts. Just like the fundamentals. It's football is a com- can be a complicated game, but it's like if you take it back to the fundamentals the basics and you like really refine those and really like makes it a lot more simple. >> All right, tell me what's the best thing about being a receiver when Baker Mayfield is your quarterback? >> The play is never over. It's like there like there's a a drawn up play and then there's the the play within the play where it's like when he scrambles when the play breaks down you get to find you get to run open space and you know that he's going to he's going to keep fighting till the play is over. >> All right, tell me this wide receiver room looks a little different than the wide receiver rooms in the past. What what defines this room to you after day one of camp? I know there's a long way to go, but but what how would you describe this this group of guys? >> I would say versatility. Uh we got a bunch of guys that can play multi- like all three positions. Um I think Z Rob's going to do a great job of putting guys in position to be successful, but we got guys that can play in the slot that can play outside. We work together really complimentary. Um and a bunch of guys that are like looking to prove themselves, right? Like got a bunch of young guys in the room that want to like prove their their value that want to show what they can what they can do to the world. Um I'm eager to get back to it as well. So it's you know we we got a really fun group lot of personality, but we got a lot of hard workers too. >> You'll be a lot of fun to watch. >> All right, looking forward to getting to know your personality all the rest of your personalities, but thank you for the time Chris. Really appreciate >> Welcome welcome to Tampa. >> All right, we are back here for training camp report presented by Advent Health and truly so excited to welcome in here with us the new voice of the Buccaneers play-by-play announcer Tony Castricone. Tony, thanks for being with us. >> Yeah, thank you for having me Casey. Appreciate it. >> And man welcome. Just I know all the Bucs fans are so excited to get to know you and hear a little bit more about your story. We figured day one we wanted to have you on here start of a new era and so for people who don't know a ton about you yet just tell them a brief history about how you got into this and where some of your stops have been before here. >> Mhm. Well, it it kind of my mom says it started the day I was born. Uh she put me in the nursery in the hospital and all the babies were going wah wah wah and I was going wah. So, >> she said that he's going to do something with that voice someday. And then uh I kind of had to because when I wanted to play football in second grade, I stepped on the scale and I was 7 lb light, not even close. I It's a lot of bull weaties short of uh being able to to make a a second grade football team. So, you know, I I always follow the sport, had a great passion for it, decided that I wanted to try to cover it for a living. I went to Ohio University and majored in broadcast journalism and just could not get enough of being in the student TV and radio station, basically lived there. My grades suffered, but all that stuff went really well and um was lucky enough to to come out and work in my hometown, Columbus, Ohio, for 5 years, then went to Winston-Salem, North Carolina, worked corporately at IMG College, Learfield, which which uh got me in the door with Clemson basketball. That's how I saw Gene Dekerhoff twice a year for for three seasons. That was a lot of fun. Then went to the University of Washington and I spent nine great years doing football and basketball there. And um you know, I just saw guys like Cade Otton and Jalen McMillan, uh they had such a great time going from Seattle to Tampa Bay, I thought I'd join them. >> Yeah, we needed to continue that pipeline going, you know? We didn't We didn't draft a lot more. We were like, we need we need another Husky in this area. And I know that's got to be great for you to already have some familiarity with the guys. And you mentioned you had some familiarity with Gene Dekerhoff and I think you've done a great job of honoring his legacy and and knowing about that as you come in. So, what did you already know about him and love about him before you got this job? >> Yeah, I mean, Gene is one of one. Like, there's no replacing Gene Dekerhoff. Uh he's a Hall of Famer, he's a goat. Whatever superlative you want to put on Gene, he deserves it. Um and I'll tell you like early in your broadcasting career, it's kind of funny thing like I didn't have connections to the broadcasting industry at all. I knew I wanted to do this, but had no real idea how to. And so, I was just kind of scrapping and clawing trying to find ways like you know how do you even do this and so I would scour the internet I think it was like broadcast.com or yahoo.com at the time like 20 years ago and I would just click around listening to whoever I could find and try to sample do I do I like what this guy's doing and what's he saying and I listened to Florida State and I was like that guy's good and so I downloaded his stuff burn it onto a CD drove around and was listening to it in the car trying to get his cadence down and his verbage and how does he describe this part of the field and I mean he was on a short list of people that I would listen to and then so you fast forward and then professionally you meet him and that's kind of surreal you know when I was at Clemson and crossing paths with him and he's just when you listen to Jean you smile I mean he's he's such a great personality wasn't just great at calling a game he's such a great person and personality and so crossing paths with him was really really cool and then the morning that the news came out that that I was making the move here got a phone call from that area code that you know is probably going to be Jean I answered the phone he just goes fire them cannons big fella so it's surreal and he's the best and now I'm just looking forward to to being me and and bringing what I bring to the table for the 2026 season >> and I'm glad you said fire the cannons because you know everyone's wondering if you're going to say it I'm not going to make you answer that here if you want to know you have to listen to the broadcast to find out what this guy's going to be doing but whether it's that or whether it's something else that you decide to do what is that like to to step into a new place and have to decide what your catchphrases are going to be or what those things are that are going to be unique to Tony as the Bucks announcer and how do you formulate that >> I want to be authentic I don't want to like force anything there are parts of the game that you script because you know it's a tight window and you want to get it right like maybe that sentence that you say before the team comes onto the field for the first drive of the season, you want it to like have some impact, but everything else I think will just come naturally. So, I mean, fire the cannons is great because it's literally what's happening in the stadium, right? I mean, it just paints such a perfect picture. But, um you know, watching closely through the binoculars everything that happens, I I think there's just going to be some things that organically take place as I build a rapport with Dave Moore, which is going to be important. And And it's really I mean, it's it's not just about play-by-play. It's about the whole broadcast. And it's the the whole crew. It's about us all experiencing it together. And so, as I get to know the fan base, get to know the players, and get to know these storylines, those phrases will just emerge naturally. >> Awesome. Well, it's been great getting to know you. I know our fans are excited to hear you on Sundays coming up here in September and even the preseason before it. So, uh again, congratulations on the gig, and we're so happy to have you in Tampa. >> Yeah, I'm fired up to be here. Go Bucs. >> it. All right. Well, that's going to do it for us on this first edition of the training camp report presented by AdventHealth. We'll be back out here tomorrow morning, so join us then.

title: Todd Bowles and Baker Mayfield Speak After Training Camp Practice | Press Conference Live Steam
text: Morning. >> What Jake Browning had a pretty good end to practice. What have you seen from your new backup quarterback so far? >> What's up? Like I said, he's experienced. He's very good knowing where to go with the football and learning a new scheme. He understands it quicker than the other two guys right now, so very happy with what I'm seeing right now. >> What's up? Tez makes a lot of plays, especially in the end zone. He got in the end zone a lot last year. Just what is his development been and for a slight guy, he seems to have an knack of getting in there. >> Well, mentally he's been outstanding. He he he's playing fast cuz he knows the system where he's getting it down a lot quicker and he's become a very good pro and a studious person right there, so that allows him to play even faster than he's already played, so and he can get down the field and make plays and he made them. >> He had some drops yesterday and then he comes back and has a big day today. What does that say about his growth and >> I mean, it's day two. You going to work on the things you got a worse at yesterday, so he got better today and he worked on that and he concentrated a little more and six that just got to be a steady progression for everybody. >> Scott's been getting some reps at outside corner, which you said he was going to. How's he looked so far? What's that process been like for him? Cuz he played so much inside in the slot. >> Oh, for him it's it's been great because he he went yesterday for the first day after missing the whole spring. he played corner, he played nickel, and he played safety. So, to process that kind of information and then come out on your first day and then come out today and do what he's been doing has been phenomenal to see. It really helps him learn the defense moving around playing different spots. So, his mind is outstanding. So, we just look for him to keep getting better. >> Does it help you as a play caller because with him and Jacob Harris, and you know, Tykee, and Winfield, and Zion, you've got a lot of guys that you can kind of rotate in the slot if you want to? >> It helps in case of injury and things come up, you know, you can juggle guys around that's done some things and you don't really have to panic. >> Coach, Reuben seemed to be in the middle of a lot of things. What were your thoughts on him today? I know there were no pads, but his reaction to the things he was doing was like picking it up pretty quickly. >> He's a very smart player, you know, his intelligence really shows when you see him. It It probably more than the toughness and the the psych ability, and that's saying a lot because he's he's outstanding at that, but to picking up the system and just understanding things that a lot of rookies don't understand coming in, he's been great at that. >> How much of that intelligence is like instinct versus like preparation and and and going home and and doing the homework? >> I think it's both. It's all that plus the coaches he had formerly, you know, it's a lot of credit to them, too, the guys at Miami and the guys at his high school because he came in here like that. We can't take credit for that after only 2 days of practice in training camp, but he prepares, he understands, he asks questions, and he's very bright. >> Coach, we saw Chris Godwin today. Was that more of a maintenance day than Chris Godwin was a couple of days ago? >> Yeah, no, it was a maintenance day. We have Chris on the schedule and we know how when we're going to practice him and when we're going to take him off. >> We didn't see him today on the field. I know he tweaked his back during um the conditioning test, and I I didn't see Tristan out here, either. Were they just inside getting >> Can you give a better sense of Tristan and how long you might want to hold him out and when he might be back to practice? >> Don't know. It's a hamstring, the tricky thing. I'm waiting to hear from the trainers and get a better idea on that, but right now, I'm really not sure. >> Talk first uh open practice for the general public. Talk about the atmosphere and you guys putting on a a good show, a couple nice catches from Mecca and Tays here for the for the fans to watch every time. >> I mean, it's great on a Thursday coming out and a lot of people are at work, but these guys come out all the time and support us and they've been outstanding over the years and they've been outstanding today, you know, and Tays had a heck of a day, so everybody got to see that, so that was fun. >> And a lot of kids wearing the the Baker jerseys, kids yelling "Baker's to go." Talk about Baker continuing to be, you know, a face for this franchise. Obviously, the contract situation it is what it is, but these fans are really behind him. >> I mean, they they love him. I mean, next to Bron going to Philly, I mean, Baker probably second most popular guy out here right now, but, you know, he does a lot of for the kids, especially right in the community and they really love when he does comes out here and they they support him a lot. >> You know, our Shaq pretty good blocker last year. Is he starting to show some some of the receiving skills out there too, as well? >> Now, the thing he is showing is his athleticism. That's what we're most excited about right now. I want to see him in pads, so I want to see what the blocking and everything else looks like, but the athleticism out of pads have been great to see for him, so I'm really excited to see him when he gets in pads. >> Talk from a competition standpoint, what have you seen from the inside linebacker position? It looks like John Bostic had a good day out there. >> They're all tough They're all smart, you know. They're all smart. Other than Trotter, you know, Bullock's been here last year and Nick Jackson's been here for a year. Other than the two free agents and rookies, those guys are pretty much veterans, so it's going to be a lot of competition. They're all savvy in their own right. They understand how to make plays. They understand to put themselves in position, even though they're all different athletically, and it's going to be a good battle, so uh Bullock had a great day today. He had a great read. He had an interception right there. He's a very heady player. He has a lot of recall from last year, so he's just got to keep getting better. >> And what did you see from Zion McCollum? He had an interception yesterday. Just him in coverage making improvements heading into this year. >> Yeah, with day two, just working on little things for Zion as far as reading the hip, moving his feet, uh in press coverage, understanding when he can get picked and when he can't get picked. It's more of the the tiny mental things that he's been working on day by day and not really trying to do the bigger things. He understands the picture, but he's expanding his game to see where all his help is around him, so he knows exactly what he's doing. >> Coach, Alex Angelo called timeout late in practice there. Is that something that's pretty unique or is that something you did on his own? >> No, we talked about it. Uh it's game plan situation. When you're down to the last play and the offense comes out and you have a chance to see what the formation is and we have one timeout left. He's heady enough to make a timeout call so we can assess the situation and come back with a call that we think that they're going to that's going to defend what they're running. >> Coach, were you impressed by that play Baker went to Bucky Hodges when he was all over him? What are your thoughts on that play? What are your thoughts on that play? What are your thoughts on that play? >> Alex is a hell of a man cover guy and Bucky's a heck of a receiver, so, you know, he doesn't panic out there like most guys do uh being at the back of the spot. He kind of covers like a safety, so he has very good awareness and headiness about that. And you're looking at two good athletes play. Alex just won that one. >> First, is you going to talk about that true freshman receiver first? Uh Mhm. Playing that position with his physique and speed and all that. Who else would go out there if you needed him to? And does that force him on the field a little sooner maybe because he has that skill set? >> No, it doesn't force him on the field earlier, but Jay Mack and Mecca can do that as well. So, we're not we don't have a problem there. We just started him out there. He's the tallest and when you get a rookie like that in here, you usually got to concentrate on one position right there, so that's kind of where we have him at. >> Anything else? Okay, thanks. >> Thanks. >> No, I was going to say thanks for the >> Mhm. >> Just for me, Mike? You're sweetheart. How you doing? Great. Not a whole lot been going on guys. What are doing? >> You guys you set the deadline and you're done talking apparently. Just how disappointed are you you couldn't bring that to fruition based on what you've done the last three years and what are your feelings about it? >> Yeah, I mean obviously I've I've told you guys I've been pretty upfront and honest about my feelings about Tampa and being home for now our our family raising kids here. We love it here. Um I wanted to deal done and set the deadline and told them it was going to be all ball after that and I I did mean that and I don't know if they thought I was just going to take some of the offers that they gave but um I'm at the point of my career and understanding what I've brought to this franchise. One I'm very very thankful for the chance they gave me. Do not get me wrong on that. But I also know I really know what I brought to this franchise leadership wise um and even play wise. It's been some of the best years of of my career and I think it's only going to trend upwards. Just being comfortable and feeling that. So um disappointed in that regard to to not have you know to feel disrespected a little bit and um that's really the disappointing part to to feel undervalued after you know thinking you've earned it. Um this is not a poor me thing. It's there's a lot other people that have it way worse off but I can sit here and and look at other quarterbacks and peers and um evaluate myself based on that and and put myself in certain categories that I deserve to be compensated for that. And I think I'm a franchise quarterback. I've been told I'm a franchise quarterback. Uh it's been said publicly from ownership down here and so to not have a deal done is very disappointing but I said the deadline was a deadline and um I addressed the team to let them know I meant that. It's it's all ball. I'm with these guys. I think all the guys that have been here know exactly who I am. Uh the guys that are new here I wanted to address that cuz they might have had a a notion prior to coming here about who I am as a person but it's it's all team. It's all about winning here now and what we're going to do and you know, hopefully Vita gets his back fixed and gets his deal done. I mean, he's the second longest tenured buck behind CG and Vita deserves that. He's the anchor of our defense and so I hope they take care of him. Um it's disappointing to say the least, but it's all ball here and I know I'm going to have a good year. I know this team is the things that we went through last year uh put us in a good spot for this year depth-wise. A lot of guys being thrown to the fire uh to be able to grow and learn uh fast and it didn't go the way we wanted, but it's a new season and it's it's going to help us in the long run this year. Added some new pieces and so I'm excited about it. It's all ball from here. Um you know, after today like I'll answer a few more questions about the contract, but after today I'm not I'm not answering anymore cuz I'm not negotiating anymore. >> You never out of shoulder chips, but in some way maybe for you it was always better on himself. You'll do it again. You get to the end of the year, you have a great year with that effect. They can always franchise tag. There's other options that they have. >> Uh it's disappointing. It's you know, I'm not I'm not the first one to go through it like this. It's just kind of historically how they've done negotiations, which is disappointing when you think you're a cornerstone of the franchise um to be treated like that, but disappointing. I know I know I'm no dummy. I know I know the contract and salary cap what's going on. Franchise tag isn't exactly in play for them. There'd be a lot of dead money. Um so it's it is what it is and like I said, unfortunate, but I'm excited. I'm in the best shape I've ever been in in a really good place uh and I'm feeling really confident with the staff that that Todd's put together um that we're going to have a really, really good team. >> You you you've talked about the fact that you've seen how the team operates. You've seen Antoine Winfield Jr. go out and ball out, become the high-speed defensive back in the league. You've seen Mike Evans have to go through a contract year twice. You've seen Chris have to do it and receive very fair fair market values. Do you have some hope or maybe faith that after this season that their number will go up? Is it >> Yeah. I mean, obviously, yes. Um but I've been on the other side of the nasty business that it is the NFL. And so, uh yeah, I have hope, but expecting and and and hoping is is two different things. And so, um yeah, I hope so, but all I can control is how I play this year and how the team does this year. And for me, that's wins. Good things happen when the team wins and uh the rest will take care of itself. But yeah, I I've sat here and and watched these guys go through it. Uh even Tristan. And so, um talk about the best best tackle in the league. Only person in NFL history that's been an all-pro at right and left. Had to had to have a hold-in in training camp to get it done. So, um disappointing. You hope they take care of their guys. And uh but like I said, it's going to be a good year. Yeah, I mean, it's Like I told you guys, it's all ball and I don't want to talk about it. And if you've waited this long to take care of your franchise quarterback, that's too bad cuz it's only going to get worse from here. Yeah, I'm going to have a really good year. That's the business side of it. Uh um it's it's two separate things. You know, it it's we all come out here and we're playing the game of football for a job. And so, we do have to take back take a step back and realize that. Um but there is a business aspect of it. So, you separate that when you come out here. Like I said, if you win, you play well, good things happen. So, that's what I'm focused on. So, that's how you compartmentalize it. It's that's in the past now. That's behind me. And right now, all I can do is is focus on this year. Not at all. Um I think that I think that's an easy scapegoat for the outside media to look at, but to be honest with you, inside the locker room all that does is bring us closer together. Um it's the downstairs aspect of our building is really, really special, and our guys know that, and they cherish that. So, uh it's only bringing our guys together. Um you know, that might be a negotiating tactic on their part, but uh this is Like I said when I got here in 2023, it's a really close-knit locker room, and that's the leadership that was here prior to me getting here, and just the way they carry each other, uh carry themselves, lead by example, and when it comes to the things like this, it's it's separate from the football thing. It's you take care of each other, you play on the field, good things happen, you take care of each other, and then go from there. >> You seem so at peace about it, Baker. Was Was it difficult to get to that point mentally? How long did it take you to just be so at peace with >> Um I think if I hadn't gone through a couple different situations earlier on in my career, I'd probably be in a different headspace. Uh it also helps being a little bit more mature now, uh and having different priorities in life. But, uh yeah, I'm at peace. It's I think what I've done here is my resume, and I think it spoke for itself, and so if that's not recognized, that's okay. I'm just going to go continue to add to it. >> Baker, internally is this I know you talked about the deadline, but internally is this something that drove you, maybe you can use this as motivation to push you through? >> Uh no. Money should never [clears throat] be the motivation in football. It's It's how do I help this team win? It's never going to be the motivation for me. Um when it comes to having a chip on your shoulder and all that, it And for me, it just puts me in the mindset of betting on myself, and that's something I'm pretty familiar with, you know. Um and it's it's a good place to be as a as a high competitive guy, um sometimes you have to put yourself in backed into a corner and fight your way out, but I have a lot of guys and a lot of staff around me that are with me. And so, I'm not alone in it. Uh we're fighting for the same goal, and that's to be playing in February. >> Baker, they were saying I mean, they're not They're not talking to me. I know that. If my agent answers it, he's not going to bother me with it unless it's actually recognized for my value. Yeah, and that's And like, going back to the first question when I opened up, like Tampa has felt like home from the beginning. The community has embraced Elyse and I. It's felt like home, and that's that's probably the worst part about it. It is we do want to spend the rest of my career here, however long God willing that is. Um, but it's it's always been home. We'll come back here. I found a great routine, great gym to train. The people that are here, um, it's it's an awesome community. We love this city. Um, it's might might be a little angry elf on the field every once in a while. Uh, so, that's probably the part that I I do regret a little bit, but that's that's the fire on the field, unfortunately, that that comes out, uh, on TV. But, um, yeah, I wanted to portray that I'm all ball. It's You can say what you want in the media. You can say I'm cocky, um, and whatever, but it it's all ball. I love my teammates. He needs to figure that out. >> He's trying to declare his loyalties, right? You know, maybe show Bane some love and at the same time >> He wouldn't He hadn't been here since Bane and Scott showed up. Uh on the Yeah. Uh really easy. Um when you're not presented with an offer appealing whatsoever. yeah, it's easy. It's easy to turn the page, but also it's just that time of the year where you're itching to get back on the field. You're itching to see how this team comes together, how the how the how the offense comes together in a new system with a new coach. And uh it's just the exciting time of year that on paper, we got a lot of potential, but it's just potential. And so we know we have to to put that all together. So, yeah, it's easy to to put that in the past when you're coming together with a great group like this. Are you saving one more question for the new voice of the Buccaneers? >> [laughter] >> Yeah. But when all five of those guys are out there rolling and some of those guys those got that experience last year, um it's a very freeing feeling to have those guys out there. They're savages up front. They're really good. They had their chemistry is unbelievable. They know what we're trying to get done. And when they're on the same page, uh our offense is just clicking. So, it starts with those guys and it goes from >> Thank you. >> Thanks. Thanks. Thanks. >> Good seeing you.

title: Sam Darnold: "The Offensive Line Sets The Tone For Our Offense" | Seattle Seahawks
text: back. I feel like this is the most practices I've gone without talking to the media. So, it has been. I've been itching to talk to you guys. Um No, I think you know, first of all, it's great to be you know, just with the guys on the grass. Uh it's always great. You know, it's it's great to have a couple months off, but but to be back and, you know, in this building, um not only with the coaches and my teammates, but everyone that works in the building, it's it's so great to be back and uh in this beautiful city. So, um we're all enjoying our time here, but we know what's at stake, right? We got a lot to work on. Um some new faces and um obviously new coach in Brian Flores, so we're all just trying to to learn the best we can the playbook and um just continue to learn each other and and build consistency um with each other and grow from there. >> Is this the first time in like 5 years that you've been in a camp with the team you played with the year before? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, for sure. I think um you know, having that stability and understanding kind of what you're coming back to. Also with Flurry, you know, the offense not really changing a ton. There's some tweaks here and there, but it's nice to be back with the same guys. >> Now you've had a little bit more time with coach Flurry. What are some things that stand out as you you know, you've gotten to see how he operates in the training camp setting? >> Yeah, you know, I think with Flurry, um just his mentality, like whether it's a good play or bad play, uh you know, his mentality never really changes out there on the field, which I already kind of knew about being in San Francisco with him, but he was always very even-keeled. But now getting to spend a little bit more time or a lot more time with him as the offensive coordinator, it's really fun to be able to watch him work every single day and just see his mentality out there, you know. Um he wants our offensive line to attack and and take control and um and I think that's a really good mindset for an offensive coordinator to have and he's just going to continue to to be that driving force behind our offense and uh you know, it's going to be fun to figure out what our identity is here in camp and going into the season with him. Yeah, I mean I think with Flurry like you you kind of you think he's very or he is very stoic and he's very even killed but he's got a very dry sense of humor and he he's very you know, funny at times. So we got to continue to get that out of him a little bit but no, he's been he's been great and yeah, Saban Saban's just told us that he's just very consistent and I think you know, the guys the players can really appreciate that when a coach is very consistent and you you know what to expect day in and day out. Yeah, I think his his route running special first and foremost I think you know, his consistency with how he runs the routes but you know, he's never going to tip anything off to the defense. You know, all of his routes look the same but for me as a quarterback I kind of know what to expect in terms of the timing and and that's the other thing too like he can run a route different like he's not going to run one one route the exact same every single time but he knows the timing you know, he knows the timing and the rhythm with our feet is really important and he's always going to come out of his break at the right time. So I think that's something that kind of separates him and then another thing is just his football IQ. You know, just his his awareness of space spatial awareness and understanding defenses and coverages so that you know, if the route allows him to kind of sit in a window he can he can do that and fill the space. Yeah, it's great. It's great to be able to throw with guys, obviously, in the off season. I think more than anything, it's just really fun to be able to talk with them more because, obviously, out here we're in meetings and stuff, we talk all the time, but it's a lot of it's football. So, to be able to spend time with him off the field and kind of chat about what's been going on this off-season and kind of get to know the person a little bit more was awesome. Yeah, I think I think it's just more more time on task, you know? Uh, getting a guy in mid-season, especially a receiver, it can be tough to to build chemistry and build that timing, which, again, I don't think we really struggled with that much, maybe early on the first couple weeks, but again, kind of like Jags, he's a really friendly receiver to throw to. Um, he's really fast, so if, you know, he's got a post or a go ball, I know I got to get the ball up and down. Um, or up in a hurry. But, yeah, he's just again, he's he's very easy guy to throw to, and and we're looking forward. I know he is, but I am as well. I'm looking forward to him continuing to get more reps, um, and kind of build that chemistry so that we can see him uh, you know, just more often, you know, getting catches and, um, doing his thing at at the receiver position. >> Sam, you guys finished 31st last year in targets for running backs in the passing game, but it seems like here early in training camp, that's a more of an emphasis, a lot of opportunities for Kadara and George and the rest of the running backs. How How did you Is that help you as a quarterback when you have more of that threat there? How does it make things difficult on the defense and maybe open up some other things for you when you have that option? >> Yeah, I think, you know, it helps the quarterback a ton because, like you said, it it does present a different problem for the defense. I think sometimes the defense assumes, especially on third down, that the running back's going to stay in and protect, so they can kind of build their pressures off of that. But, you know, when you're getting five guys out on a route and you're you're in scout protection and, you know, sometimes you got to throw hot and, you know, the defense is going to make you hot, but if you get the protections right and you're not hot and the running back's out on a route, sometimes that's a mismatch, you know, with a linebacker, especially with a guy like J.D. George, um, you know, we got a ton of backs in the backfield this year that can make people miss, um, linebackers and safeties miss. So, it's uh it's it's going to be really fun to kind of see what those guys can do coming out of the backfield. Uh, it's been great. We're loving it. Um, you know, it was funny. It was it was a top talking the QB room. It was like, "Who's going to change and who's not when the camera's going on?" You know, in the in the uh you know, just in the locker room. And no one's really changed, which I'm I'm proud of. So, uh you know, it's been fun though. It's I think after the first first three or four days, you kind of forget the cameras are there, which might be a bad thing, but um no, I think, you know, we're all kind of used to it at this point. It was nice to to hear that they record, I think, 300 hours of film every single day and only 1 hour gets used throughout the day. So, um that was very uh that was very nice to know that. >> As the starting quarterback, you're probably going to be a big like focal point of the show. Do you feel like you're more prepared for that now than you would have been maybe a like a few years ago? >> Uh, I mean, yeah, I think however you want to look at it. I think I would have been prepared a few years ago, but I think experience and you know, just being around the locker rooms and being a little bit older, I guess, maybe more mature, uh I think, you know, that can help a little bit with this experience, but it's been great, man. To to be able to have the crew around, the crew's awesome, too. Really good people, so it's been awesome to have them around. >> Is that the last one on Hard Knocks? Who do you feel like whose personality you feel like the world is going to learn about that maybe they didn't know about it. >> [laughter] >> Oh man. >> Really? >> Honestly, I think I think the head coach, the head ball coach, Mike. I think I think he'll shine bright on on Hard Knocks just for people to kind of see his personality and uh his personality come to life. I think is um cuz he's a great guy, obviously. We know him. We know who he is as our head coach and as a person. And I think for the entire world to see that is going to be really cool. >> Saints defense every single day. They were just ranked 10th in the league by Madden. Uh you have any thoughts on >> No. >> So you heard We heard from Jack the other day. You know, for everything he accomplished, he still sees a room to get better and grow. I imagine you're wired similarly. Like you've done a lot these last few years personally, team-wise. What what's next for you? What do you How do you want to evolve? >> Yeah, I think I can always get better. I think I think there are a lot of things like for me especially. I think moving on in my progressions and working from one field to the to the other. I I felt like I was thrown behind some targets especially if I was going left to right. Um there were a couple throws in the Super Bowl that I'd like to have back. Um and then not only during the Super Bowl, but you know, before that as well. Um where I just kind of I missed some guys going through my progressions. So I think just being calm with my feet, making sure my feet don't get super wide and I keep you know, a lot of guys like to keep their base wide. Um but for me like my base has always been wide and sometimes I get too wide. So I think just making sure that I keep keep my base more, you know, hip hip width apart um is going to make me a little bit more accurate. So just working on little things like that and always working on the deep ball every off season as well. >> Is that exciting to you to feel like when you've done a lot and you feel like, "Hey, there's still there's still more out there?" >> There's always I mean, this game is so tough. It's so difficult. Um and there's so much that goes on for us as quarterbacks, um Um, you know, mentally. So I think making sure when we get to the game that like everything physically is just muscle memory and that's why that's why you work so hard in the off season so that you're not thinking about those things when you get out there on on Sunday. >> You obviously know what the narrative was about you last year in the interview. Were you glad those were kind of all gone now and you know it's kind of a different I mean you won a Super Bowl and all that. >> Yeah, I think for me like I've never paid attention to stuff like that. Um, you know, I've been very confident in myself. I've been very confident in my my teammates and the coaches that I have. So, I've Yeah, I don't allow myself to really uh, pay attention to anything like that and if I do catch wind of it, um, you know, I I have my process process on on how to, you know, handle that. But, yeah, I think for me it's just about again, like I just said, it's about handling my process and doing it my way so that, you know, I get out there. It's not about what I've done. It's not about what I'm going to do. It's about what I'm doing right now and I think if I just continue to have that mindset as we go on, uh, you know, we'll be just fine. >> Sam, your whole defensive your whole the offensive line is coming back. What does that do for you as a quarterback? >> Yeah, I love them. You know, the offensive line, they're great guys, characters all around. Um, just a great group, man. It's uh, it's so fun to be able to work with those guys every single day. They really set the tone for our offense, too. Um, I think a lot of people don't realize that or just the offensive line in general in football I don't think gets talked about enough. Um, they're such a vital part to a team's success. Um, cuz even shoot, even you know, our offensive line setting the tone and our defensive line feeling how they're coming off the ball like that sets the tone for the entire team. And I don't think they like I said, I don't really think they get enough credit um, for how they practice and how they play on on game day. So, um, I'm always going to make sure they they get love and and you know, all the things that I feel like they deserve. But, they're an incredible group. A really fun group to be with and I'm glad I I get to be with them every single day. >> Thanks, Sam. >> Appreciate you guys. Sam.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps The First Padded Practice Of Training Camp | Seattle Seahawks
text: I don't know if it gets much better than this. Beautiful weather, training camp, pads on, playing football. We got bald eagles flying. We got the Blue Angels in the sky. It's uh pretty awesome. So, we're very blessed. Awesome day, great practice. Uh guys were after it. You know, 10:00 a.m. practice. Coming off an off day, guys were in it. It was um just a all around really great day. So, really really pleased. >> When you say it's a great practice, I guess what makes it a great practice? >> Well, just like the intent was there. There was physicality, both sides making plays. Um just incremental gains operation-wise. Uh didn't have a lot of guys on the ground, which is great. Um just back and forth. So, just noticed a lot of great things like individually and and uh in each unit. >> When the pads go on, what do you what are you really looking for in training? >> Uh no, it doesn't change I mean the the circumstances change on like, you know, the physicality of the game and you know, you can feel guys a little bit more, which is nice. But, uh we got plenty of ops with our pads here and then um you know, going against the Titans and then playing in some of these preseason games. So, uh this I think is his first of about eight or nine padded practices we have the rest of the rest of the way. >> We got to see Andre Fuller and Michael Davis we get their hands on the football quite a bit today. How have you seen them handle their first training camps? >> Yeah, it was exciting to see, you know, today. You know, when when you do put pads on, it is you know, it's more playing football again, you know. So, to see them make plays playing football is is is great. But, those are it's an indication of the work they put in. They've done a great job up to this point and they're rookies, so they're swimming a little bit um schematically and but um that's as expected and then you just got to kind of work through the fog until start making plays like today, you know, they gain more confidence and so just keep rolling. >> When you see a running play succeed out there, are you thinking that was well blocked or that was poorly defended? >> Uh both. Both. Sometimes it's man, that was a great play. Sometimes it was we screwed up on defense. Sometimes it's a combination of both. There's a a plays today that I think might be just great by our offense, also symptoms of things that we need to address defensively on structurally and how we're playing some things. So, that's good, you know, it's good work. >> What what are your thoughts on playing Marks, his progression so far? >> Yeah, Marks has done a nice job. I'm looking forward to watching today's practice. Probably his best practice so far the last practice, so uh we'll see what we'll see what it looked like today, but uh great spirit, executing well, communicating well. Um he's put a lot of work in, so walk. He's done a great job. >> We got to see the running backs get a lot of opportunities in the passing game. As a defensive play caller, how does how does that potentially strain you when you're facing a team that really utilizes their running backs and adds another thing for you to deal with? >> Well, it's another matchup that you have to consider. so if they're not going to be on the route, then you're not really worried about it, but if they're constantly on the route, then you have to account for that matchup. >> Watching Byron Murphy in those one-on-ones, the combination of speed and power right now, you've been around a while, but is that just still a work in a while you wouldn't consider him physically ready? >> He's uh he's one on I'm again I I didn't watch that drill today. I was I was on uh seven-on-seven, but um really expect Murph to have a spike in productivity rushing the passer. He's earned it. Um but he does it every day, you know, so and it's great work for our offensive line. It's great. He's he's in a great he's in he's in a great spot. >> You have a couple of guys we saw today not practicing, Jake Bobo Julian >> Yeah, nothing long-term, just couple things they're working through. Camp type of stuff, so it's a bummer, but we'll get them back soon. >> Uh Cooper Kupp was asked today if he owned the team, what's the first thing he would do, and he said he'd ask the coach, he'd ask Mike, "What do you need to get an edge?" What would you What would you What would your answer be? >> Um probably keep that between me and our bosses. But uh we got to lot I'll tell you probably the first thing I'd say is we have a lot of things that are really, really great. And, uh some things that I think that we can leverage, but um I mean, how could you be I mean, we were we have we have great ownership and and we're and leadership right now, so um but it's exciting, you know, it's exciting to just have an opportunity to keep pushing is what we've been what we've been trying to do since we got here and now you're working with a different group, but uh but we got a lot of great things here, man. It's mean it's pretty awesome. We're we're in good shape. >> Mike, going back to Byron Murphy, just how have you seen him grow into who he is consistently as a leader and just become a consummate professional? >> On Earth? >> Yeah, primarily. I think he's been very intentional on on his own development and then how he's like invested his time, uh how he's how he's handled his body, where he's trained, who he surrounds himself with. There's just no wasted like there's no wasted time, you know, it's just he's very he's very deliberate on on how he goes about his business and um it's a great example for the guys on how like, you know, nothing's going to change overnight, but having that deliberate process and we talk about stacking wins, moment moment moment by by moment mindset, I mean, those things come to life with Byron. >> Mike, what what have you told your guys about just handling the cameras? >> [laughter] >> Well, I said they're really good at capturing uh and doing what they do. Let's let's make sure we're us. And then and then trust that uh what's displayed is is us, you know, so look, you can't control what they capture, what they, you know, all those things, but you can't control is how we go about our business. I mean, we had an episode the other day that um that I I wasn't we weren't us and I was really the I was the culprit. I was responsible for it and uh when you notice it, you just got to go make it right, you know? But, that that's what we do, you know? We If we mess up, or if we go across the line, or we chase an edge, and we and we miss, we got to you know, be smart enough, and and have the humility to come back come back over to the uh to the other side, and and go move forward. So, you guys have been great. Feel like Feel like we've been us the whole time. Had a great spirit today, so I think uh I don't know if I'll watch it, but I'll be I'll be looking forward to seeing what they come up with. >> That was a moment in practice you're talking about? >> No, no, it was just something how we operate in the building. >> Whether or not you watch it, do you like who on the team, whose personality are you getting most excited >> I don't know. I don't know. It's a good question. There's a lot of guys. You got anybody in mind? Yeah, Brady would be great. I hope they feature Brady. He'd be awesome. He's He's interesting dude. Talented guy, too. I mean, like in in life. >> Like, how much how much >> with football sense do you have the veto power or editing power over what they actually air for the rest of the world to see? >> I mean, they I think we respect the fact that they they have to they have a show to put on, you know? So, you can't can't just watch paint dry for an hour, or however long it goes, you know? So, I hope it's interesting. I hope there's storylines. I hope there's some sort Hopefully, not too much conflict, but, you know, um so, I think with that in mind, but I you know, they they've done a great job of saying that we're you know, we're working together on this thing. Yeah, it's just kind of simple, but >> You said you might watch it, or you don't know if you will. >> I don't know. I don't know. I start making all these things of what I watch and what I don't watch, and all of a sudden, it's something you hold me to, so. >> And and passing since you've made space for Kobe Bryant and other players to find their way around the field even when there are already starters there. >> Yeah, is Tyreek Snyder a guy that might be looking for a chance to get >> Yeah, great point. Um Tyreek's has had a great camp. He's really has. He's done a great job and um there's ways to get him out there, you know, so it's that's a great example of like you don't need to be counting like the people ahead of you and where do I stand and depth chart and all this like just put my best foot forward and all the things and let the let let us figure out how to get you on the field. Um and so he had he had a great workout. Uh this guy we've been tracking for for a while, so we have great we have a great relationship with him over the years, so just made sense to come in and he's really he's done a great job since he's been here, so we're excited about it. >> Have you seen Sam kind of grow from, you know, this time last year he's new, everything's new and now he's had a whole year and he's opening camp kind of hitting the ground running. How much different does it feel? I mean, we're all growing, so it's hard to like it's kind of like you're with them every day, so you know, you don't see your uncle for like a year or two and you're like, "Oh, yeah, you've changed, you know." Like but uh you see Sam every day, so it's kind of like the same guy, but tell you right now he's being really decisive with the ball, he's taking care of the ball, he's making great decisions, he's playing fast. Um he's being aggressive when he needs to be, he's doing a lot of great things. Great great command. Um his process is really cool. Thing I appreciate about Sam's and a lot of court mean, but you can't speak for everybody, but just every rep is a rep. So, if it's like if it's in the quarterback room and they're going over the script like he treats that rep the same as he does here if it's practice online or We're, know, we're in a game. It's just it's all the same. And that's the That's the uh that's like the mental approach that we want to We We want all of our guys to take. >> Anthony >> He's He's He's not in He's in a He's in an adverse situation. And and he's attacking it. And that's all you can ask him to do. He's made a lot of progress, which is exciting. And so uh you know, it's one of these things where you know, you don't want to put a timetable on it cuz you don't want to limit him or you don't want to you know, you don't want to put him back. But just go rip it every day, you know, and we got great people surrounded by him and and uh just go see where we get. But um return so far, he's done a great job and it's not going to be easy, but but he's uh just the man for the job. >> With Withers Witherspoon, it seems like I think you may have mentioned this the other day. It's like the energy and enthusiasm is the same every day. >> What's going on with the contract? What can you say about it? Yeah, that's uh I'm really impressed by it, honestly. It's It's um just one of those things where it's just it's something that you're not used to dealing with as a player, you know? Like, you know, just how much he loves football and how much how he wants to be out here and try to get better. So, um you really respect his approach so far. His practice habits at Georgia have to be I've never heard anything like it. So, to get to this point where I don't think he's had as good a career in the NFL as as many people think. title: Robert Saleh Training Camp Update | Day 2 Press Conference
text: With just a couple injury updates, so JC's coming off pup today. So, you'll see him with a helmet. He won't be fully integrated in the practice, but we'll continue to work him in. Hopefully getting him into practice Saturday, so we'll see how the next couple of days go. You'll see Ridley out there. He's feeling a lot better than Trubisky. We'll see how he feels after the first initial part of individual. >> Just clarifying, you said you're shooting for full practice for JC Saturday? >> Not full, but integration into practice for Saturday. >> [snorts] >> Thank you. You said you said sorry, you said yes to Volson yesterday. >> Yeah, I apologize. It's guys, it's an open competition. So, you might see Volson starting out today. They're all at a bunch of spots. There's going to be it's going to be a revolving door. And and I'm I'm leaving the I'm trusting both coordinators, all position coaches to handle it accordingly. >> What do you like what you're seeing from Jace the since you've been here? >> You know what? JC's worked his tail off, man. Like uh I know he had a little setback at the end of OTAs with the pec. But, he you know, give him credit. He stayed here the entire summer. He's worked relentlessly to get back in to get that thing back to strength the the strength he's needed. He's at a really really good weight to allow him to have foot speed. Like the man doesn't have a weight problem. Like he holds it really well. He's he's got a lot of lean muscle mass. He looks really really good. He just but he understands that he doesn't need to be as big. Bigger you are, the less foot speed. And he's he's attacked the heck out of it. And I'm I'm really excited for for the season that he's going to have. >> That's something he said he kind of struggled with his rookie season, kind of the the weight management for lack of a better term and playing at a weight that's comfortable. Do you guys have a plan for a plan for how to keep him on track throughout the course of the season? >> Yeah, and part of that's maturation, Buck. You know, like he's you know, these kids come in and they're they're learning how to be a professional. They're they're on their own. And um the thing with J- like he's blessed, man. I mean, he looks at a weight and he gains 5 lb of muscle. It's fascinating. The guy is uh he's a an incredibly gifted human. He's just got to be conscientious that, you know, like every extra he doesn't need all that weight. He's already going to at at 340, he's going to push people around. At 350, he's going to push people around. So, he doesn't need the 360s and 370s. You know, he needs to focus more on foot speed and I think he's recognizing that. And um and he's like I said, he's attacked the heck out of it. Really really really excited about where he's at. >> He said after last year, when he had some penalty problems, his big thing for the off season was mental. Jeff talked about working on mental. How do guys work on mental when they're as far away from game day as they can be? >> Yeah, you're you're you're always working. Every day every rep in practice, the the mental part, you know, from uh letting the last play go to to understanding your responsibility within each play to um putting yourself in a position where you can use all of your God-given ability without having to think about what your responsibilities are. So, there's a lot of different ways to approach mental, the mental toughness part of it, the the uh uh creating short-term memory. There's there's all different aspects of it, but uh and and I'll hit it again, you know, a lot of these young men they come in here with expectations. He's a first-round pick. Um and the game is way different than college. And so, there's there's a maturation that takes place, too, and a confidence that he'll continue to gain. And as he grows as an individual and as a player, he'll get better. >> In your opinion, what is Dan Moore's best attribute on that left side? >> Uh he's he's he's security blanket, man. He's a he's a starting NFL's uh tackle. He does a really nice job. He's a great communicator. He's really smart. Uh he's got great size, length. He's strong. And um you know, he's he's he's reliable. >> What did you see from the tape for him last year that maybe he didn't he didn't work on >> It's the same things. I'm going to keep all that stuff. I don't want to reveal what we see and give it to the to the opponent, but uh there's always going to be things that all these guys can work on. Like I we've talked about what their just one things. Um, you know, and again, I'm going to leave that to the individual, but but all these guys are going to be working on things that continue to help them get better and coaches I think Carm did a really nice job identifying one single trait along with a a bunch of things that all these players have to get better at to help them attack that we feel will will see dividends during the season. >> The offensive line has been kind of a nightmare around here for the last 3-4 years and you even took advantage of that when you were coaching the Jets. >> I think there's a fear amongst Titan fans given Jermaine kind of worked Dan yesterday or got the better of Dan yesterday that this line with holes maybe at center or competition at center and right guard is going to be an issue this season. How with limited padded practices and limited preseason reps can you ensure that the offensive line is not going to hold the team back this year? >> Yeah, no, that's a great question, Jay. You're going to you you attack every position in a way to give them all the best chance to get better as with all the limitations that we have, but like I've said, you know, one, the O-line is at the biggest disadvantage when we're in non-padded practices. That's just a given. The the D-line is at a significant advantage all the way throughout the league. But we we're we're putting the screws to our players with regards to all the different inter-squad scrimmages we're having. We're taking advantage of as many padded practices as we can. And we're challenging our guys with the deliberateness at which we attack walk-throughs and all that, but it is limited. You're not wrong in that, but but we're going to push the envelope with as much as we can to to build that to allow them the opportunity to build the confidence that they need to have for us to be successful. >> What do you see in a guy like Crenshaw, Dixon battling for the swing tackle job? What what some of the things he's bringing to the table? Obviously, a pretty big guy. >> Yeah, the the swing tackle, I mean that at the end of the day and I and I hate to say this word, someone's going to get hurt and you know, having the versatility to be able to swing and work on both sides of the ball and uh work both sides of the line of scrimmage, like that's uh those guys are invaluable and um you know, they're they're big discussion pieces in free agency in the draft even and on what the the the the role is for individuals. So, uh we're hoping that he continues to develop and and become a reliable piece. >> When you've got somebody like Famina, where a lot of what you think he can do in this position is hypothetical, he's never had to do it before, how how do you balance the projection you have of what he can be versus what you're actually learning about him? >> Yeah, uh one thing I'll say with Fam is I mean, he looks good coming off the bus, right? I mean, he he looks awesome. Um the other thing I'll tell you is that he will I am not a I am I will put myself on a on a chair and screen that he will play with elite effort and strain. Like that is unquestioned. Uh just being with him through OTAs and uh the first day. You're right, he's he's raw in the sense that he has not had a lot of opportunity to rush the passer and to do the things that we're going to ask, but I've got a lot of confidence in the fact that he's going to at minimum produce enough just based off his effort, his length, his athleticism, his tenacity, his strain and we'll continue to develop the skill set that he needs to be able to win those one-on-ones on a consistent basis. So, he's a young man, he's raw to the position in terms of what we're going to ask him to do, but he's got all the he's got the mindset and the athletic traits that uh we covet to to attack from a developmental standpoint. >> A guy like that that's so athletic and he's he has a good get-off, etc., do you kind of limit what you ask him to do as far as like dropping back in the covers and those type of things and just telling him to go get the quarterback? Do you feel like that will help him get to the surface better? >> We limit everyone's job on defense. Like I said, like our nickel has maybe five techniques that he's got to know and and so like I mean, I think Aaron will blow this building up if I dropped the D-lineman. >> [laughter] >> Even though it's going to happen a couple of times, but that's not what they're meant to do in our system. Our our system is meant for them to go forward to set edges, attack the line of scrimmage, and get to the quarterback. and that's what we're going to ask them to do. >> How do you supervise the offensive coaching staff? Specifically Brian. I mean, he's the offensive play caller and designer, and yet you're the head coach of the team, but you're also coaching the defense. When it comes to reviewing offensive practice tape, when it comes to maybe asserting something that you want to see out of the offense as far as the whole team's concerned, how do you supervise while still allowing Brian to do his job? >> No, for sure. Jared's on fire today, man. Got a couple good questions. Um so, we're when you look at the relationship between offense and defense, we're constantly communicating with what they need from us and what we need from them to to give us both the looks that we need to to have a successful day with regards to development. Um I'll ask questions. I'll give my feedback, but at the end of the day Daboll is an expert on offense with good knowledge of defense, just like I'm an expert on defense with good knowledge of offense. So, we'll have constant dialogue. We'll have thoughts. He'll spit all ideas to me, and I'll go back and forth with him. Uh but at the end of the day, like I you hire these guys because you trust that they're the best in the world at what they're doing. And and Daboll's had a tremendous amount of success in the past, but the dialogue doesn't stop. Questions, the standard at which we're trying to operate, that that doesn't change throughout the building, and those conversations will always be had. But like from from my perspective, like I don't think a player can ever get enough discussion, especially in our team room. You know, the relationship between a receiver and a DB in the game they're playing and just trying to educate our players on what all these different um the the game within a game for their position. So, there's there's a lot of dialogue that's happening as far as being a micromanager, if that's what you're looking for. I don't think micromanaging is the right thing to do. Um we I hired Dave's for a reason. Uh just like I hired my linebackers coach for a reason, my DB coach for a reason. They're the best in the world at what they do and and I'm going to give give them trust, but I am going to ask questions. I'll probably be a thorn in his ass every once in a while. >> Consider Jake Martin unique among the ends and can can you kind of characterize what he brings? >> Unique in which way? >> Maybe rushes differently, maybe >> They they all have They all have um different skill sets. So, like um but I do think he brings a lot of power. So, Jermaine Jermaine is a big powerful man. Um Femi is going to be a big powerful man that's that that plays with a lot of strain early. Uh Jacob has a little bit more wiggle, but he can also bring power, but uh I think the the the variety and the versatility and the differences we're not looking for a cookie-cutter player. Um you want guys who cuz like I said, we're we're bringing these guys in waves, right? And the idea is that they're they're a bunch of change-ups, just like Solomon Thomas in there. I mean, he's a he's a a a three technique that's a lot smaller than the other guys, but he gets into your chest a heck of a lot faster. He's he's faster, he's quicker, he's um he's lower to the ground, he's got more leverage. Like they're just different. So, when we're sending all these guys, having that versatility uh and being a different style uh adds a uniqueness to all of them. >> our wiggliest? >> Uh I don't have that answer right now. Uh like I said, but when pads come on, I'll have a much better feel for for the the cuz a lot of guys are shifting over from from that 3-4 principle. And even Fem Fem you when he gets his pads on, it's just you know, you got these pads on the the the the wiggliness, for lack of a better word, kind of shows differently. >> What were your notes coming out of practice yesterday, and what are you looking for today? >> So, one more time, please. looking for today? Specifically, where are you going to be? What are you looking for? it's just the first day. Like the these first, call it eight to 10 practices, all the way up really to the blue-white game next week, we're constantly installing. And so, really the challenge for the guys is to try to stay ahead mentally, so the the the mental load of all the installation doesn't slow them down athletically, which usually is the case early in the first two weeks of training camp. A lot of guys are thinking a lot, and so it kind of slows them down. Uh so, the challenge really is to just continue to stay ahead of your install, build on what you had today, uh master the install one, figure out install two, get to your point to where you master it, and just keep on moving, and um but but really it's just try to find a way to build on what we did yesterday and get better. >> They will They will uh touched on it in OTAs, and then Cam mentioned it again yesterday, saying that when different quarterbacks are in, even in the same period, they often get a different set of plays or run different things and get different looks. What What can you kind of explain why that is, and what the benefit of it is? >> Uh uh give me that one more time. I'm sorry. >> Cam touched on it yesterday, said that the plays that are called for him in a like in the in the same in a red zone period or a team period might be different than what's called for Mitch or or Will. >> No, for sure. So, you're you're trying to install, and you're trying to get some things on tape. So, uh what we had what we what we will do though is the the plays that Cam doesn't get or the plays that Will or Trubisky don't get, they get them in walk-through. So, at some point during the day they're touching that play, but you know, you're limited to how many plays you can get and you're trying to get things on tape so you can go back in and teach it. Uh so you don't want to repeat, you know, the same four plays for everybody. You're just you're you're limiting the amount of teach tape that you have once you get to the film room. So you're trying to hit everything uh so that way Will can learn off of Cam, Cam can learn off of Will, True can learn off both. Like you're just trying and the same thing for all the positional players. Um there's still a lot of information to be gathered by watching your teammate play football. >> Fireman Ed went on a podcast in New York and he said that you said he's heard that you said to people that you plan to kick the Jets' ass. Did you say that? And if not, what's your response to Fireman Ed? >> I I don't know, man. It uh it was I was just made aware of it like 15 minutes ago. I I must have had over a thousand fan interactions at that event, so uh who knows, but I mean, isn't that the objective anyway though, man? Like I don't think the Jets are coming here week one to sit at the 50-yard line and roast marshmallows and talk about our summers, so we're getting after it, they're getting after it, and um may the best team win. >> Thanks, guys. >> All right, guys, appreciate you, guys.

title: Jermaine Johnson, Dan Moore Jr., Femi Oladejo & Cor'Dale Flott at Titans Camp
text: Coach was saying guys coming into this system, Yeah. a lot of times find themselves kind of falling forward. >> Yeah. >> Have you seen that? Have you talked to guys about that that transition? What's like >> falling forward in terms of >> like at at the snap as they learn to do? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Um 100%. I remember coming in as a rookie into the system and I mean more often than not u college guys are kind of taught to read and stuff like this. This is the complete opposite. Um, so it's definitely a lot to learn. Um, technique and everything like you are running off the ball, sprinting off the ball and um, that's just it's kind of a little bit of a learning hurdle for for some people. I know it was for me, but once you get it um, it's definitely I think I think it's the best front the best style of playing football. >> Sala, talk about having you guys rush in waves, but having versatility. Where do you feel your skill set like what does your skill set bring to the the pass rush rotation? uh a kind of tenacity and effort like play that's uncommon. Um and uh not to mention, you know, the talent and stuff like that. But I'm big on the intangibles. Like I said, NFL, everybody has talent. Everybody is uh physically gifted. Um but what can you do that that that separates you and a lot of times that's the intangibles, the effort, the passion, and the violence. Um can't really teach that. And uh if you have it, you have it. If you don't, you don't. And that's why this style of play, this defense is not for everybody. But I know we got the right guys, not only in the room, but on the team, on the defense, to play this style. >> What makes this defense the style for you? >> I was made for this defense. This defense was made for me. And um I'm just happy to be in it. >> Now that you're two years removed from the injury, you started to feel kind of more like yourself prior to that. >> Oh man, I'm on fire right now. I feel great. Um feel great. Everything's just uh working in my favor right now, and I thank God for that. And uh yeah, I couldn't be more uh well off in in every facet of my life. uh you know just that's the truth. >> What's your mindset for you heading into the year five first year here? >> Um just kind of no hype, just give me my helmet. Like I just want to go play football and I want to be myself and uh be the player I know I am. I don't really care about potential talk anymore. Um I got to go do something this year and uh I believe I'm top five, top 10 in my position in NFL, but that's not the case statistically. Um, and I got to go change that this year. >> How do you feel the off seasonason went for you and where you feel like you are heading into camp? >> I feel great right now. Um, probably another week I'll be ready for the season. Um, I feel ready now, but you know, football moving. The best way to get in shape for football is to play football. So, um, I mean, I feel great right now. I know in another week I'll feel even better. Um, but yeah, I'm just, like I said, I'm on fire right now. I'm ready to go. >> You got and Jonathan in New York and now you've got Jeff and Jonathan here. What what are your impressions of of two days on the practice field and what they do for you? >> Um, they do a lot for me.
