It's just going to be a tandem that's going to be tough me uh for me seeing any team handle. Um, so I'm just excited to play my part, win my one-on- ones, and uh dominate the run game. You guys are so big across the front. Jacob's a little bit less big. What What do you see in him and and what kind of X factor like he did? >> Oh goodness. Uh Jacob don't I mean don't let that size uh fool you or whatever. And I don't even think he's small by any means. Uh he will I've never he'll stuff any tackle, any tight end. He's a very physical person. Pride his game on that. And uh Jacob was my vet when I got drafted to uh to uh the Jets. And um same with John, same with uh a lot of those guys. But they really showed me how to play defensive end in this position um in this defense. So I mean [clears throat] you'll see what Jake does this year. >> Does it make him maybe a little more wiggly kind of >> Oh yes, 100%. Very efficient mover and very great pass rusher in terms of having a plan and then having a plan off that plan and he wastes no time getting to it. >> Right now the numbers don't portray where you think you are in this as as an edge. What what do you think those numbers need to be for you to be the player that you think you are? >> At least 12 10 to 12 sacks and then I I I want to be feared in the run game. I have to be feared in the run game. I want it to be a detriment to the team not having me on the field in terms of how much I I am a asset and a pillar to the team. And if I'm not doing that, I I feel I'm wrong. So, um I know I'm coach Solless guy and everything like that, but I mean I just have a lot to prove not not to anybody else but myself this year. Um, >> a lot of people hear fast and violent and they just think that's hitting you. Salah said yesterday, it's much more than that. It's about how you pract for people how fast and violent permeates everything you guys do in practice. >> Yeah. Um, 100%. So, I mean, just speaking Dline in individual, the first drill we're doing is running as fast as we can off the ball and hitting a bag because that's that's essentially what every play has to look like for us. And the premise of that is um we we make the offense adjust to us um in terms of the D line. They got to figure out a way to block us, not the other way around. And um and there's nothing else I'd rather be in because when you're holding that kind of power, it's it's a lot of fun to play in. Um but then again, like I said, you need the right people uh to be able to play that and I feel know that we do. when you break in a new scheme, it takes time sometimes to jail, but how much given so many guys have been with Salah before, how much can that accelerate the curve that it takes? >> Uh, it definitely helps having guys that, you know, have been with coach Solid before and in the system, but more than anything that this defense starts, this front starts with a mindset and um, like I said, everybody in that room has the same mindset and if you don't, you will stick out very, very, very quickly. Um, and uh, yeah, I just know we're all excited. We're all very excited to uh, get those pads on and really put this uh, this defense on for sure. >> Can you describe that mindset for us? What's the kind of chatter between you and other leadership on the line? >> Honestly, is uh, uh, they they don't know what's coming when we get pads on. Um, but we say that in the best way possible. We're just eager to really play this front the right way and you can only do that with pads on. So, uh, we're just very excited. Have you thought much about Have you thought much about what it's going to feel like for you to go back to the stadium where the injury happened? Whenever that comes, >> that's part of the game, bro. I uh every time I kind of go out to the field, I close the casket in terms of anything can happen. Um so that just happened to happen on that field and that's in the past. So I feel good and anything can happen on this field, practice field, whatever the case may be. I'm not really superstitious like that. I'm a big believer in God and that happened. Went through the trials and tribulations for that and I came back stronger. I feel great. as you're counting on the mic to to communicate things after the headset goes off. I think that's 15 seconds. How much happens in those 15 seconds for you guys? >> Uh Dline is pretty quick, pretty easy for us. We hear the call and we pretty much know everything we got to know. Um so like I said, it's uh this defense is I like to call it simple stupid. Keep it simple, keep it stupid, especially for the front. But then again, you need the right people to be able to play it because if you don't have it, it will look very different. So, uh, we got the right guys to play this, uh, defense, and I can't wait to to put it to the test. >> One last one. You good? >> Thanks so much. >> But a lot of changes around you. >> Yeah. Um, I just feel good energy in the building. Um, you can just feel good vibes as soon as you walk in. Uh, I think they did a good job with coaching changes. Uh, brought good leaders in and you could just feel the flow of things. Um, it feels professional, feels organized. um just feels like winning winning culture. >> Do anything different this offseason and uh what what's your kind of mindset going in? >> Did you do anything different yourself this offseason to get ready for this year and how do you feel going in the year? >> Uh it wasn't so much of doing things different. I think coming off of last season um I was a lot more healthy going into the offseason. Uh I think I was able to get a lot more out of my body and a lot more out of my training that I wanted to. Um, so just just feeling a lot better in terms of this point this year as opposed to last year. >> How different is it? >> Uh, asking you guys >> in terms of different >> in what you do up front in style of >> Yeah. Um, I mean, Karmmes Karmmes is a a great coach. Uh, he's been some he's been places. Um, he's coached some great guys. Um, I'm pretty familiar with him coming out pre-draft. He was in New England. Um, I mean, Karm, he he's going to push us. Um, he's forcing us to do some some some different things. I won't say I won't say force. Um, but he's opening up our our outlook to some different things. Um, and challenging us in different ways. Uh, few different techniques, but more so schematics. Um, I think he's just bringing a different approach. >> Does it fit you better? That's a great question. Um, >> find out, right? >> Uh, yeah, we'll find out pretty soon. I mean, I think guys are responding well to it, to his coaching, uh, and his flow of how he runs the room. Um, that's all I can say that right now, though. >> Another year with you and Peter on that left side. Just how huge is that just for consistency purposes on that side of the line? Yeah, any anytime you have someone next to you consistently um and you get that that gel factor, especially playing offensive line, I mean, that's that's half of the game, honestly. Um being able to read demeanor, uh communication, um just knowing and expecting what a guy needs, what he wants from you. Um, yeah, >> Dan, with the scheme change, uh, you know, Cam's talked about how it's, you know, uh, Dave's wanting to, you know, do things that fit him. When you're on the offensive line, how much does scheme change maybe affect what you guys are being asked to do? Uh, or is it more little tweaks and technique things? >> Um, it it affects it affects a lot actually. Um, where the QB is setting up and his in his drop backs. Um, how he's communicating to us, what he needs from us in terms of communication. Um, but one thing about Daves is he's very offensive line conscious. Um, he knows in his system, um, you know, what what we're susceptible to. Um, and he's definitely not just on us, but also on Cam. Um, we're all taking on. >> Dan, probably the biggest external question about this team is what step Cam takes. How much is it on you guys up front >> to protect him and give him a better chance than last year to expand his game and elevate? >> Absolutely, man. We want to keep that guy upright at all times. Um he's he's fearless, right? He doesn't care about getting hit. He he does not care. But regardless of that, we want to keep him we want to keep him clean. We want to keep him safe and feeling comfortable in the back field. Um, so we've definitely had communication with Cam as far as, you know, pocket presence and um, just what he needs from us in terms of protection. And if anything is below that bar, then he's going to let us know. >> How do you think that your game needs to evolve to not only help with that, but also help with the system that you're now? >> Absolutely. Um, you know, I got to I got to play to the ability that I know I can play to. Um, I won't even I won't even say anything about contracts or what coaches think. I know the standard that I have set for myself is higher than with any other person's standard. Um, so I know that as long as I do that, I'll be fine. >> A lot of talk from Germaine. They want to get pads on and come at you guys. What scares you when you line up across from someone? >> Scares. Um, no. Germaine is a he's a great player. Um, actually happy we brought Germaine in. He's he's going to give us some great work. He's going to get us better. Um, in terms of competition, obviously the Dline, they they they talk stuff. Um, so it's it's good team competition, right? Um, and yeah, we'll find out a lot when the pads come on. >> Know what hit you when the pads go. >> We'll see. >> You're saying you don't get scared when you line up across from anyone? >> No. >> Do you see? Go ahead. On that note, Salah said before the Pats come on, defensive line has an advantage. Offensive line has a clear disadvantage. Do you feel that way? And how important are these first days before the Pats come on? >> I hear people saying that about the disadvantages. Um I won't say disadvantage. I think that uh we're all protecting each other in certain ways. So those disadvantages by offensive linemen um not being able to use as much um grip, no pads and things like that, more feet, technique and stuff like that. But also they're not allowed to really bull rush, get into our chest. So the physicality is definitely brought down without pads. It's definitely forcing you to just use more technique as opposed to willpower. >> Did you see a difference in Cam from last year this year already? Yeah, he's more aware of just different things going on around him. Um, and you have to be that way as a quarterback. Uh, you got to know um where everybody is, where everybody's supposed to be. You got to know where your O line's protecting, where you're hot from. Um, just a lot of different things that obviously as a rookie quarterback you're not going to have. Um, I think Dave is doing a good job of helping him with that awareness and kind of toning some of that fearlessness we talked about earlier down a little bit and just controlling it. >> What's the feeling in in that room just as a group seeing how things kind of metriculate through camp? Because there a couple of open spots that haven't been given out yet and just how do you approach how that's going to work out >> in the O line room? >> Um, I mean that's that's kind of not a I I don't really know how to answer that question. And I feel like that's more so for a coach, I guess. Um, if you're I you asking me who's going to >> start? I was just kind of asking you about how it's going to be an evolution during camp and ultimately a decision will be made. I'm just curious as to as a unit. I mean, and you guys will see it as you go along, like what works best and who works best with who. What What's it like going through that process? >> Um, I think for one, it's creating depth for us regardless of who's out there. Um, I think it's given us trust in everybody who gets in front of him. Um, yeah. >> What's the biggest difference you've seen in Brandon Crrenshaw Dixon as he comes in in year two fighting for swing tackle spot? >> He's just more confident, man. He's got some reps. Uh, he's got a year under his belt. Um, he kind of knows who he is as a player. Um, some things that works for him. He's adding some tools to his game. Um, as offensive lineman, I I say it all the time that if your confidence isn't there, then you're not going to be playing well. And I just I just feel like his confidence is much higher than where he came in at. >> All right. Thanks, man. Appreciate it. >> Position changes in two years. >> Two position changes in two years. >> Part of the game. Got to be versatile. Uh, football's football though. You only got so many things you can do. Just got to keep learning. Learning from my vets. So, yeah. >> How much you learned last year? How much better you feel heading into year two? >> Uh, I learned a lot last year. Just the importance of the details, taking care of your body obviously, uh, learning from your vets, watching film, learning your opponent, and perfecting your craft. >> You got even bigger last year, >> maybe. >> Was that by design or did you try to do anything different? >> Stuck the same program. Just ate well, stayed in the weight room, hot yoga, took care of my body, and just got bigger. >> Jermaine Johnson, he had talked about keep it simple process for a guy like you >> being able to just attack and go get it and not have to read as much like you did before. How much does that help you be able to transition into your position? >> Uh it's incredible. It helps tremendously. Uh >> I think when I moved to edge in college at UCLA, that's what it was just going straight. So to be an assistant that's similar where I can just go straight and not think is where money's made. >> How much do you like the intensity that White Cotton and Tanzel Smart like the way that they have you guys in individual period. >> No, that's incredible. That's that's how you compete. That's how you get better. He gets the best out of us. He pushes us and he helps us know that it's all love at the end of the day. It's no hard feelings. It's no tension. Nothing like that. >> We keep saying we keep saying year two. Does this feel like year two or does this feel like year one part two? With how much time you were in and out last >> Still feel like year two. Obviously, I was in the building the whole time and I only played what, five or six games, but you learn from it. you move on and you uh take it as a lesson and not a loss. >> How hard was it back in the spring to not be out here and learning with the teammates? I know you had the stuff in the film room, but just how tough was that period for you? >> Yeah, it was tough. Uh kind of like what I just said, you you learn from it. You take it as a lesson and uh you you take it as an opportunity to take more care of your body and to stay on point. Coaching changes are difficult, you know, to understand where you're going to fit in. But Coach Salah made it known immediately that you were a guy they looked at in the draft process in San Francisco for this defense. How much did that show up when you first sat down? >> Uh, can you elaborate a little bit more? >> That he already had a plan for you. >> Oh, got you. >> Yeah, I don't think it's anything's free. You still got to earn your spot, earn your position, but uh obviously had a meetings with them in the draft process, but got to still play and get better and learn the system and compete. >> Who in this group is maybe taking you under their wing early on? One of the vets that already knows solid system is maybe giving you pointers and saying, "Do it this way." >> Yeah, I learned a lot from a lot of the guys, JFM, uh Jake Martin, Germaine Johnson, Solomon Thomas, uh Ernest Brown, all of them. All of them. They've all been great, great vets. helped me a lot to learn the system and to learn how to be under the system. >> Robert talked about how how different this is for guys who haven't played it that some of them almost fall or attempted to fall out of their face come coming out of their stance with the adjustment. Have you kind of felt that different gravity and and what's the difference actually feeling? >> Yeah, you just four-point stance, hands in the dirt. Uh you just want to get off the ball and stay ready. you felt that feel at the at the beginning when you were out there? >> You can say so. Yeah. Like >> how you like your head coach and maybe what has he told you about how good he thinks you can be? >> Uh course is great. Uh great defensive minded coach. Uh great overall energy guy and I think I can fit well in the system and make plays and help the team win. >> When's the last time before this that you played with your hand in the dirt or or is it the first time? >> Uh did it a little bit last year. Uh so I'm familiar with it. Um, now it's just more being more consistent. >> Being away from the game for so long, what were some of the things that that you missed the most about not being able to be out there? >> Being on the field, being with your teammates, uh, the hotel nights for the game, playing on Sunday, things like that, >> keeping your mind right through that process and what were some of the things you did to make sure that that didn't go straight? >> Say it started my faith. Uh, prayer, reading, talking to family, friends, teammates, support crew is great. So, yeah. Sol said the one thing he's never doubted about you is the effort. Was there any point during this process where the effort or the I don't want to say hope, but where it started to fade a little bit where you doubted that this was going to come back for you or were you always pretty confident this would work out? >> In terms of effort, >> just in terms of play style in general, did did it ever dull for you while you were slowed down or No, >> I wouldn't say so. Just got to trust the process, trust your your crew. The training staff was great. Like I said, my support crew was great. So, just stayed focused. uh didn't get too distracted and trusted, like I said, the process. >> Where are you on a confident scale scheme wise as far as exactly what you need to do? >> Yeah, this I mean with this system, you put your hand in the dirt, you go straight, you can't really lose as long as you're coming off the ball. So, I'm I'm pretty confident. Uh still a lot to learn technique-wise, but like I said, if you come off the rock, you got a great shot. >> Do you have a goal in the offseason when you were training? And what's going to be different about the product you put on the field this year? Report that question, please. >> Did you have any goals when you were training in the offseason? Something you were focused on specifically, whether it's skill or physical and and what's going to be different for what you put out on the field this year? >> Yeah, just my pass identity. Just continue to learn that and put my best foot forward when it comes to being a three down player. >> All right. Thanks, man. >> Appreciate you. And he want to be the best tandem in the league uh this year. What do you make of those thoughts? And what is it going to take for you guys to be able to do that? Definitely this is going to take hard work every day. Um that's our mindset. That's our goal to come out here, get better 1% each and every day. Uh be hard on each other and just continue to keep that goal in mind. >> Yeah. Just following off that like how do you guys think you guys complement each other's games in terms of again living up to what we did? >> I love real physical his press game. Every day I learn from him and memes from out here on the field. So I pick his brain. He picked my brain. You know I like to play off, be technical. um you know knows certain concepts and stuff like that. So he picked my brain, I pick his and we go off of that. >> What have you noticed in camp specifically that has kind of gave you that mindset head into the season that you guys can be that type of duo? >> Just who we are, just how we play and um just focus on that. >> What do you think about the group of receivers on this team, the guys you're competing against every day? And what's it going to be like in camp? >> They fast, they physical, and they explosive. They getting us better on the back end, too. They know what they doing. Cam got a good, you know, camaraderie with them as they out here practicing. So, it's just folks, it's making the Olives compete. So, that's what we got to keep doing. >> They put a real emphasis on height and and length with you, Alante, Josh. >> Uh, outside of the obvious benefits of that, how much do you think that that helps with your identity and and what will it do for you? >> It helps a lot being long and physical like that because you can play off and you can press. So, it creates this defense to be physical, which we got a great front and hand. So the ball have to come out quick with the front we have and we got to make plays. >> You've obviously got the the length but not necessarily the weight. How does that how are you a physical player? >> Yeah, that don't ne necessarily mean nothing. It ain't showed up in all the years I have been playing too. So I'm not really worried about that. >> With Carell being the fourth pick of the draft, how much do you look for those one-on-one matchups on the practice? >> He competitive. I'm competitive uh throughout each and every rep. You know, we compete whether he win or I win. We talk about it after like what did you do here to win that rep or what do you do here to get that edge on me to catch the ball or vice versa and we continue to compete. So how >> how did you say your offseason win here and how you feel heading into your first first camp here? >> It went great. >> Building that brotherhood with the team, building that brotherhood with Lante as well off the field, you know, doing recovery, you know, uh training together. So building that camaraderie, that brotherhood in the locker room. It's been good. But I'm excited to be a part of the fans and this Nashville community. >> What does this environment mean to you? And how does it show itself even in a a practice out here where you guys can't hit anybody? >> Solid got a good way of saying it of putting your face in the fan, not slowing down when you coming up to hit or make a tackle. So that's what I, you know, lay my hat to. Uh being the size I am, so that's what I'm going to do. >> From a DB's perspective, what is it about Carnell that makes him so effective so early? >> He very smooth. He's very smooth. He's very poised in his routes. Um, you can never tell when he's going to break down, snap down, or even track the ball. So, I feel like that makes him a great player and elite player, too. >> How excited are you about what's in front of you, you know, with Jeff, Jonathan, and >> Oh, man. >> I just know the ball got to come out quick. I know the old linemen, you know, going to have a hard time with those guys. So, we got to do our job on the back end and make plays. >> More. >> How do you How do you like being in Nashville? Are you closer to family? I know you're >> Yeah, I'm closer to family. Mobile is like about 5 to 7 hours away with my wife family. So, they come up, visit us, spend time with us. It's going to be good to come to the games and have my family around. For once, >> what's what's your vantage point about how the offense is kind of picking up the speed? >> Uh, I've been with Day before. Uh, is you talking about defensive wise, offensive wise? >> Yeah. How what's your perspective from the defense about how the offense is picking up the speed? >> Yeah, I've been with Day before. He's an explosive guy. Uh, you got to always have your eyes right with Dayball. um he find ways to get you off of the spot and make plays and be explosive. So >> he likes to speaking of D ball like it's a lot of quick passing and quick decisions. How does that change you or impact you as a corner having to cover that? >> Like I say, you got to keep your eyes right. Uh you got to focus on your keys. You got to be disciplined and detailed in what you do because it expose it if you don't. >> Last one. >> You good? >> Yeah. You guys play you guys play the Giants this year and again you were in New York going against Elite and Barny's healthy. What are you kind of looking forward to within that matchup and yeah, what are you looking forward to? >> Compete with all the guys that I compete with at camp and all throughout the four season I was there. It's going to be a fun game. It's going to be a competitive game and an allaround game cuz that's you know that's why I started it. So I'm excited to do that. >> Excellent. Thanks. I appreciate you. Appreciate

title: Broderick Jones & Darnell Washington Press Conference (July 30) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: How you feeling? >> Good. Good. Glad to be back with the team. You know, knocking the rust off. It's been a long time since I've been out there on the field with the guys. So, you know, I'm just glad to be back with them. >> What was the biggest hurdle for you? >> The biggest hurdle? >> Of getting back here and healthy. >> Probably just the conditioning part. Like, on the back end of like rehab and stuff. Like, trying to get clear. Knowing we're coming back to camp. Knowing it's going to be hot. You know, just trying to because I wasn't doing nothing for like I would say like 3 months, 3 4 months. So, you know, just trying to get back in shape. Hitting the gym hard. You know, just enjoying enjoying the time out here with the team. So. >> Brodrick, were you ever concerned Were you ever concerned this was going to be a career-ending injury? >> Um Yes and no. At first when it first happened just because of how serious it was. That was That was my first like serious injury ever. Like, so it was it was kind of an eye-opener for me. Um But, you know, now I know talking with the team docs and talking with Dr. O. Um he did a great job. He said the MRIs and stuff were coming back great. So, you know, I'm just trying to continue to get better. No, I didn't. No, like yeah, it was after the MRI. Like, they made me go the following morning. Like, after after the game I felt fine. I told like I went in the next day and I was telling Gabe like this is the best I've ever felt after a game. And he was like, "I don't I don't know how because >> you were dying." >> I'm like, "What?" But, you know, that's how that conversation went. Um But, you know, for the most part it it wasn't It It was a shock, but you know, God always has plans for us. So, you know, it's it's nothing that I can't overcome. I just got to continue to battle through it. No. Hold. Hold. Hold. >> When you saw the replay of it, were you I mean, it looked kind of like a freakish injury almost on the way you landed on it or what? >> It It did, but it didn't at the same time. You know, we're all out there playing football at the end of the day. I'm I'm not saying it was a dirty player or anything. You know, I I just feel like he went to make a football play and you know, it was just wrong place at wrong time type type scenario. Um So, you know, I just I I got to be better, you know, having my hands up, not not shooting for, you know, leaning and stuff like that to prevent things like that, but you know, it's football. It's a physical game, so those things are bound to happen. That That That's my biggest focus. Uh that's my biggest focus on my technique and my strength. Um because at the end of the day, that's all it comes down to. Uh no, you know, it's a business. As you just said, uh you know, they it's it's new players. You know, I was in the same situation when I came in and Dan was here. So, it it was the same way. You know, it wasn't it wasn't really a shock for me because I was hurt. You know, um you never know what the future holds, so you know, it's a business decision on their part. You know, I just got to continue what I can do for the team and then just show uh continue to show up and get better. Uh just just continue to get healthy. You know, that's that's the first thing. That's the main goal. Um because if I'm not healthy, you know, I'm not going to be out there. So, uh but that that was like the main focus for them. You know, just talking to me like, "No don't try and rush it, you know, because anything can happen." So, you know, just taking your time and and actually like listening to the the the points that they they're giving you and and just implementing them into your day-to-day. Uh I believe so, yes. Uh it felt like a stinger. It just felt like a stinger. Honestly, um down both arms and then that was that was honestly about it. Uh it went away probably It took a little longer to go away than usual. I think like the stingers didn't go away until we got in the tent. And then it was kind of like uh that's why they took me to get an x-ray and then they pulled me so >> Right side or left side? >> You played both right and left tackle as a starter >> I've been doing that since I've been here so >> Right. And so what is what is your focus right now? Is it just getting overall technique back >> Yeah, just wherever the team needs me, you know, um uh as as I I just got back. It's only my second day. You know, I'm not trying to rush trying to get back into the starting lineup cuz you know it's it's it's things in and plans in place for that. So you know, I'm just trying to stay the course and you know >> care what side you work on? And you going to be primarily on the right or the left, you know? >> Not not really. So you know, at the end of the day I got to work both. I got to be able to play both because you never know. Troy can go down. I can go down. Max can go down. Anybody can go down. So you know, we all have to be prepared to play both sides. >> What will the offense miss Kenny Gainwell and how do you think the running backs that have been brought in will offset that? >> I mean, I miss him but I I feel like yes and no. Well, I'm not going to say no but yes. Everybody know KG, you know, he he he he was you know, a stud last year and he's going to continue to be that but then we brought in new talent. Um not going to compare those two kind of guys but you know we brought in new talent so >> You know, you've been through some injury stuff. What's it been like to see Broderick come back? What have you guys been there for him during this? >> Uh me personally, you know, I go way back with Brod. Uh you know, just just just just being in in his corner uh I know his injury a lot more different than mine. Uh you know, just just just really try to be in his corner and just be by his side through it all. So emotional and all that. So if he needs somebody to vent to, he know he he he can come to me and talk about it. >> Do you like the fact that you guys have an offensive minded head coach this year? I mean, nothing against Mike Tomlin but it seems like a lot of the offensive guys are pretty excited about it. >> Yeah, I feel like me for sure. This this first time ever in football. Even go back to Georgia, Kirby Smart, everybody knows he's a defensive mind. You know, Mike T defensive mind. So, so this is my first time ever experiencing it, you know, in football. So, it's a lot different. I enjoy it, you know, just cuz like the head coach is like you know, like he he's he's cool, but you know, like when you mess up he he's also getting on you, you know, get out there with I mean, all he doing is coaching. So, all all all we can do is to get better and just take it in, soak it in, and you know, just >> Was that one of the reasons or did it play into the fact that if you signed that extension, you wanted to be here? >> I mean, I for sure wanted to be here, but I mean, I can't tell you what they think from upstairs, so. >> I thought that was a really impressive two-minute drive that the offense Just what did you see from that? How do you guys feel like you move the ball now? >> Just just some things I picked up on it, you know, just seeing one of our brothers make a play and then it's just like get you excited, you know, just for just make make me want to play make the next play next. So, I feel like just feeding off each other's energy and just just continue to drive down the field. >> Does it feel like things are moving quicker for you like already a couple days in? Or >> Uh to me it's same page, you know, I I I kind of just like to take it day by day, just just be where my feet is and yeah. >> I know we're early in the process, but do you feel like there are a ton of changes on offense? Do you feel comfortable? >> Uh for me, yes. Just you know, it kind of just go back on our you know, head coach being an offensive mind guy. So, just seeing the head coach in the office of of unit meeting, it that that's that's a lot different for me. So, yeah. >> Probably the most important question, how was the wedding? >> Uh it was fun, you know, that that was actually my first wedding obviously besides mine, but my first wedding that I attended as a guest ever in my life and you know, Pat Pat money man. So, just seeing just seeing everything set up like that, you know, it was amazing. First wedding and you know, I I enjoyed it a lot.

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (July 30) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Hey, I you said the other day Mike about about your feelings about tackling at camp. You know, I know you do you weigh it with a veteran team and how do you think about it maybe installing physicality if you don't tackle in camp or the games they play? >> Yeah, I think there's so much to football. I think when you have a definition of having a physical camp, I feel I have great confidence of just let's just get to the end of camp and you can you can grade my camp. Um so, you know, I've I've tackled before in camp. It's it's a risk assessment decision. Um the fundamentals of tackling we work every day, so I have confidence in that. I mean the option of tackling and goal line, it's it's it's always a conversation. You know, there's years I've done it, there's years I haven't done it. Um it's it's a hard drill to do. I think it's more part of it yesterday. Um so, that's that's part of it. But there's there's so much more um that we can do in that area to emphasize that. You know, the long stride, short stride, the specifics of how the fundamentals are being taught to the you know, the approach, the strike, the wrap, the finish. Uh so, these are constants that are taught, you know, throughout you know, our whole our whole our whole team. You know, defense, obviously special teams, and our offensive players who play special teams. So, it's a it's a primary fundamental. We call it the Steelers six. You know, we have six fundamentals of Steelers football that we emphasize. Obviously tackling and breaking tackles is is one of those six. So, those six fundamentals are emphasized daily. We have a period just for team fundamentals to emphasize that. So, um you know, doing it for a long time, I have great confidence. And and frankly, evaluating the team last year, you know, that I think that's definitely I would say is an asset, you know, moving forward. So, it is a veteran team. Um but you have preseason games, too. You know, so that's that's always part of it. Who plays in pre-season, who doesn't. So I mean all those things are discussed and I think that's why I'll continue to say there's a systematic approach to everything we do. You know, we have a plan but the plan has proactive adjustments that that gives us in a systematic mindset. >> Can you share the other five? Can you share the other five things? >> Yeah, ball security. Obviously taking care of it, extracting it. Ball security is number one. Blocking, obviously sustaining and obviously getting off blocks. Already hit tackling. About big plays is the fundamentals. You can't win in the National Football League without big plays. There's you know, each game you look at the league average and it averages about 36 a game. So you get you got to you got to emphasize it. The finish, the pursuit and finish is clearly a big part of that too. But in one day we you know, spend a lot of time and particularly because the way we have to train more than ever in the off season is the mannerisms. Mannerisms and disguises are a big part of pro football. I think it's particularly coming from the quarterback position. You know, my history you spend time there but you know, the game's evolved that way. We're both sides of the of the ball are doing a lot more hearing and seeing it more in special teams. So those are the six, you know, fundamentals of stellar football. >> Is it on the on the tackling end? >> Yes. >> Was any part of evaluating the team in last season and what you saw and any missed tackles that showed up that went into your decision to not have live tackling this year? Like any concern about rust opening up? >> anything anything from the this end of season evaluation that affected the way we trained in the team today. You know, it's a it's a clean slate for everybody, coaches and players. You know, the the teaching environment that you want to create, I feel good about it. We're off to a good start. I think I think we hit the target in the spring. We're doing some things here in camp that you know, we have we have the you know, a a talk through, a walk-through type thing in the gymnasium. So, uh that's been very productive last today. So, the teaching environments is is clearly there. Um and then the you know, the competitive nature of the practice environment will only improve. You know, obviously we're still in we're in shells and protective shirts again today. You know, we're on the clock. Uh we emphasize two-minute again today. You'll see you know, that you'll see the two-minute team go today. Um we're still we're still hitting the end of the game. Uh talked on that yesterday. We got some end-of-the-game things we're looking at. Uh just cuz you know, finishing the install coming out of spring. And we'll you know, always have our fundamental sections and so forth. So, you know, and we're working in accordance uh to the you know, the CBA with like everybody, you know, and I think practicing uh helmets and shirts, you can emphasize things more on the perimeter, you know, ball and space and those types of things. And that's what we're doing. >> Mike, with that two-minute emphasis at the end of practice yesterday, the period was you know, you got 4 seconds, different down and distances, starting points. Just what's kind of your mythology methodology behind that? And what do you guys kind of gain out of some of that chaoticness and and going through those plays? >> Well, big a big part of uh the game of football is, you know, the understanding of time clocks, you know, and you know, and particularly when you talk about the two-minute situation. I mean, if you look at a 17-game season, and the really numbers haven't moved a whole lot in in my time in the league, you know, on an average of you know, with 17 games, eight games a year on an average will come down to the last series. You look at playing a football almost it's probably even closer to 90, 95% of the games come down to the last series. So, um those those are the things I look at. So, when I'm when I'm putting together a training regimen. So, that the opportunity to win games, we're the Pittsburgh Steelers. You know, we're going to get everybody's best shot. So, uh so, maybe ours will be 10, 11. So, that's how I evaluate it. That's how I when I look at the training, how I'm going to set up the practices, the reps, the quarterback school. Obviously, I think we all start somewhere as coaches. You know, my starting point was you know, the quarterback [snorts] room. So, uh that's I I train the team in a lot of ways how I I learned learned, you know, the training of the quarterback position. And I think it, you know, then you take it down and and either further into the science of what every play represents. Like today, one of the emphasis in the team meeting today was the anatomy of a play, you know. And uh the pre-snap is the first part of a play. So, everything that goes on in the pre-snap up until the ball snap, you know, the specifics, the mannerisms, the disguise, that's why that's why it's it's a fundamental. Uh the cadence, the substitution patterns, you know, the ability to get the ball get this up uh personnel in quickly in the red zone. So, you have to practice all those little things now cuz it's going to show up in preseason games. It's going to show up when you get out there for the first time with a 90-man roster. So, so you got the pre-snap, but then if you go if you watch as you watch film, you study the film, you'll see in the first 2.3 seconds, that's really the that's the execution battleground. That's where really the play gets established in the first 2.3. So, that's another time block. So, and then above 2.3, 2.5, now you're getting into extended play. Okay, so now we're talking about extended plays, which is what? Big plays, big play opportunities, which is another Steeler fundamental. So, that's that's the way my brain works. That's the way I've learned it through the eyes of a quarterback in my time in this league, and that's the way we train our team. So, all our situational emphasis, you know, really is broken down every specific play and how we can train in those in those little uh segments and and and our and hopefully as I uh express this, you know, hopefully hopefully you see that in our practice structure. >> It seems like you got a pretty aggressive It seems like you got a pretty aggressive cadence in terms of how the plays get called at practice. How did you come to that? And and can you push that too far where going too fast loses some things in some other areas. >> Well, everything's calculated, everything's regulated. So, you know, there's obviously science behind it. You know, we're we're in tune with the conditioning of our players. The commitment the players made in the spring was was evident. title: BAD news for Ricky Pearsall and the 49ers...
text: Big update on this off day for the 49ers. They've already decided to sign at least one player, a local tight end, Josiah Deguara. And of course, much worse news on the Ricky Pearsall front. But some key questions to be answered including a very simple one that many have asked me, why didn't Pearsall and the 49ers opt for surgery to begin this past off season? Because all options are on the table now, he is dealing with an injury to the same knee that compromised his 2025 season. It's a PCL injury that the 49ers and Pearsall obviously hoped would heal itself with rehab over the course of this past off season, but now that his knee is swelling again, uh the healing obviously has not completed itself in full. So, with all options on the table, surgery obviously is a possibility now. For that, hear from Treasure Island and we'll take a look at Treasure Island in a little bit. Beautiful reconstruction going on here, old and new, San Francisco skyline. But for that, we should check in with Nirav Pandya, doctor on social media that does a really good job explaining these situations. And take a look at his tweet yesterday about Ricky Pearsall and PCL injuries. In general, the vast majority of PCL injuries are managed non-operatively, so without surgery, especially if they are isolated. If patients become symptomatic with swelling, pain, or instability, and we know that Pearsall after Monday's practice became symptomatic with swelling, then surgery can be performed. Sometimes the symptoms won't creep up until players really start doing intensive activities, which explains why this happened in this timing for Ricky Pearsall because intensive activity didn't really start until training camp. You can't really simulate what 11 on 11 football is like until you actually have to perform in 11 on 11 context. The reason to try and delay PCL surgery is that reconstruction is a long recovery process, 9 to 12 months, and results are mixed, especially at an agility position like wide receiver. So, that 9 to 12 month timeline is really, really important to keep in mind because if Pearsall had undergone surgery to begin last off-season, probably would have missed time, might have missed the entire 2026 season anyway, and there would have been no guarantee that he'd be back to his original pre-injury self. So, you can see why the 49ers and Ricky Pearsall opted against the surgery because it was such a risky path. That being said, if the conservative path does not yield results, and if it hasn't yielded results for what, nearly a year at this point, and you have to start considering the riskier path because the riskier path actually ends up being less risky than staying put, and I think that's where the 49ers and Ricky Pearsall are at right now. It's all tremendously unfortunate because as we've said many times before, Ricky Pearsall did not miss a single game in his college career, not a single game. And the only injury that's caused him to miss game time in the NFL has been this one PCL injury. Obviously not counting the the shooting in San Francisco in 2024. That was not a football injury for Ricky Pearsall, but he came back from that shooting, finished that 2024 rookie season exceptionally well. So I just know the importance of uh passing that information. Um there's gaining the trust of the quarterbacks that's extremely important and it's creating certain habits that allow you to be successful at this level to create a consistency that allow you to excel and continue to get better and have a long career. So, um, you know, it's great to have a group of young guys who are super hungry, looking for their opportunity. And anytime that I can help them out, I'm going to do that. And I learned something from them as well, you know, uh, whether that's just getting a mental get getting a mental rep when they're in there or, uh, you know, certain things that they do that, you know, I kind of like witnessing as well. So, um, I just think that's a big part of being a leader. You know what I mean? When you're part of this entire camp, you kind of get to see things from start to finish, see guys grow, see yourself grow, and uh help build it from the ground up. >> Just my view from afar. Tell me if I'm wrong, but it seems like sometimes in camp that defense can come a come ahead early in camp. At what point in camp do you feel like you can get a really good assessment of where the offense is at? >> Uh yeah. Uh they had a really good day. I don't you know, I'm not afraid to say that, but um you know, that that's camp. There's going to be back and forth. Um there's also series of camps, you know, I mean, we're building things up. We're in the red zone. It's a little tighter, you know, things like that. But I mean, they they're they're making plays out there. And for us, it's about um not um recreating the same mistakes. So, you know, I'm my preaching to the the receivers is just making the tough plays and everything's not going to be perfect. You're not going to always be the most open or sometimes you are going to be the most open and you just got to make the plays when they come your way. And uh uh that's just part of camp when pass come on. That's a different aspect of camp. You know what I mean? So we're just trying to take this day by day. DQ's done a good job of just explaining what's expected of these first few days. But uh the point of the matter is you want to come out here and win the day. You know what I mean? I don't think we did that today. Um but this is day two. Tomorrow's a completely new day. And that's why we go in there and watch film and uh discuss the things that we could get better at so we can come out and have a better day. But I've always been a big believer of, you know, receivers to a certain degree kind of drive the practice in the sense that when receivers are making plays, it brings just a certain energy to the offense. Um, makes the quarterbacks feel a little bit more comfortable because it doesn't they don't feel like they have to be perfect. And then there's times where they make up for our mistakes. So, it's a it's a collective effort. Um, but, you know, I'm not worried about where we're at right now. It's just day two. It's good to have guys out there flying around. The juice is is what I'm super excited about. the competitiveness like you know we shake up with guys after after practice I didn't really want to shake up with nobody because we got beat you know what I mean that's just kind of that's how I am but at the end of the day we're still brothers you know what I mean and um you know we're going back and forth but we still have commanders across our chest so uh that's the main thing but that's what I like the competitive juices are here early >> going back to the young guys it seems like you you've done a lot of work with with Jaden Bradley >> what do you see in him what what kind of intrigues you about his potential >> um you know I think he has a unique skill set where He's a bigger receiver, but he moves very uh smoothly. Um his releases are very smooth. Uh he's sudden in his releases. He has really good feet at the top. He kind of has a pro like feel. Um for him, it's just going to be about detailing it. Splits, um timing, when you're running down the field, keeping your shoulder close so you can track the ball over your shoulder. Red zone, you know, there's not as much space. So you got to hold that hold that defender off so you could give the the quarterback more space to throw in that back corner of the end zone. Just little tidbits like that I try to pass along with him. But he's he's a sponge, man. He's been asking questions since he first got here. And um obviously he's undrafted. Uh you know, I haven't really had a guy who's undrafted who's like just followed every single thing that not only I do, but Deami does. And you see him working out in the offseason. He was out with us in LA. So he's just super hungry. And guys who tend to care that much about their craft tend to have success. So, uh, he knows that he has the opportunity to try to earn a spot on this team and I'm going to do whatever I can to try to help him because, uh, he has a really good skill set. >> Terry, what have been your early impressions of rookie Antonio Williams and just his progression since OTAAS? >> Yeah, I think Antonio, uh, he's he's a quiet guy, but, um, I think his play speaks for a lot of who he is. Uh, he's very smooth and he's uh, he's twitchy, you know what I mean? He's uh when he's running routes um he's very sudden and you don't quite know when he's breaking until he breaks and then he has the explosiveness to get out of his cuts and he has really good hands as well. So he has a good feel for the receiver position and I think he has a chance to really help us especially in uh Blau's offense where guys will be able to move around. Um, so you know, he has some good reps and OTAAS, but these reps are extremely critical for him. Um, whether he's running with the ones, twos, or even get into preseason, like this day-to-day repetition is extremely key so he can uh try to, you know, really help us this year. But, um, he's just done everything that we've asked him to do. Uh, you know, he's on snack duty, so he better have them he better have them snacks this afternoon. But, uh, he's a great guy, man. He he asked so many great questions, and I think he has a bright future. So, um, just this camp is going to be great for him to get day-to-day reps, building on. I just told him now it's about stacking days and being consistent, but he just has a great feel for the position already as a rookie. >> For him, he's a guy his last season in college at least, he spent a lot of time in the slot. What goes into making that transition from spending a lot of time there to moving more outside? >> Yeah, I mean, I think in the slot, you have more space to move. Um, you know, not a whole lot of press coverage, working on, you know, linebackers and safety. Sometimes you'll get nickel where you're going against a corner, but uh you have more spatial awareness, which I think that's naturally why he has a good feel. You know, to be a good slot receiver, you have to be quick and sudden, but you also have that good feel for zone timing of of the routes, timing of the concepts, and being on the same time as a quarterback when he's ready to throw you the ball. When you go on the outside, you know, I mean, it's it's more physical. It's more press man. Um you're going to get bigger corners. So, with that, you got to be good with uh you know, press releases, being physical at the line of scrimmage. when you got a quickness at the line like he has, it's going to uh definitely help him get into free releases. Then it's just about uh getting hands off and and getting vertical. He has really good speed, so uh I think he'll be able to show up in the vertical game as well. Um but, you know, I think he really excels in the slot and I know he's going to have a chance to move around, but um I think it's just really important, especially when you're a young guy, gaining that confidence. I think they're doing a great job easing him in um putting him in a space where he's comfortable that accentuates his skill set. He ran a really good like choice route against the middle linebacker and he killed him. Like killed him, you know what I mean? And it wasn't just the route, it was the sudd it was the uh savviness he had, the patience, the timing that allowed him to be so open. So um when he gets the chance to play outside receiver, I'll be able to help with that as well. Um but he has the releases to be able to win out there. Then it's just about being able to get hands off, getting your route, and make contested catches as well. Um, can you speak about your conversations with um, Jaden and about learning the new offense and how you can help as a receiver, him learning the playbook and vice versa? >> Yeah. Um, I there you go. [laughter] I just think our communication's just grown just as quarterback and receiver, you know, I mean, uh, third year playing with one another, having a full off season together to get some really good work in. Um, you know, I just love to see the way he's grown as a player, as a leader. Um, and we just communicate on and off the field a whole lot. You know what I mean? Whether it's sending clips, whether it's talking to Blau about what we like, long as we're on the same page. We've had plays like that over the last few years where when you are on the same page with the quarterback, you can make any play right. And I think that was the biggest thing for us is getting these reps in and being on the same page. Now, as we start incorporating this new offense, um, you know, we're both just trying to learn our assignment. So, we take care of our job first and then we talk about the little nuances. Like we had a play yesterday where um you know my split being a little too tight maybe may throw off his timing just a little bit. So we completed the play that's great but like to get it a catch and run versus a a catch and tackle that could be the difference in plusing out the split just a little bit more. So little details like that being able to work on that so early on top of the work we put in over the last few years is going to help us you know have a have a good season together. Terry, playing off it a little bit. When you're a vet learning another system, a new system. >> Yeah. >> How much do you pay attention to the verbiage and how much do you just pay attention to getting the concepts down? >> Yeah, I think that's a good question. I think uh I've been in uh quite a few offenses and um the great the great thing about it is you get to learn football from a a broadside view. And I think just coming out of college, I was really taught to learn uh offense conceptually because not only does that help you as a receiver to be able to move around and be versatile, the more you can do like you don't want to be receiver, I just play X, I just play Z, I just play slot, you know, like that just pig pigeon holes yourself. So your ability to be able to learn things conceptually allows you to understand the spacing. Like if I have a if we're running a a uh a corner flat read and I'm a little too flat and that that corner could possibly play if he's playing cover two, he could play me and Chig. You know what I mean? But if I don't know what he has because I'm not learning thing conceptually, then I don't know that detail and I can mess up the whole play, not only for myself but for him. So I think learning conceptually is extremely important and I think Bobby does a great job of just expressing that to us in the room. But, uh, I encourage all the guys to try to learn all the positions. And with this offense specifically, I think Blouse just done a great job of making things marry together. So, there's kind of, uh, little tidbits in the play calling that'll kind of remind you of what you may have. Um, so if you can learn, not only conceptually, okay, this is what we're trying to get done, but then you're hearing the play call, getting used to hearing the plays in the huddle, and it reminds you of what you studied the night before, then you're going to have success. And then it's about just detailing. Make sure you're on your splits, your your depths are correct, and then making the play. So, um, that's why we're out here and and and doing that. But, you know, Blau's done a really good job cuz sometimes you could get so many words where it's just like it's it could be a lot, but I think he's just he's done a really good job of just making it easy for us to digest and now it's on us to go execute it. >> Talk two more. >> Terry, um, you've been double digit practices with Chig by now. Like, what do you think he can add to an offense? >> Oh, man. He's very dynamic. He runs routes similar to like a a big receiver. Uh he has really good feet at the top of his routes. Uh he has the ability to win after the catch. Um and he's a big target. You know, I think Jaden has done a great job over the last few years of finding our tight ends over the middle. And when you got to have a guy a guy like that who's dynamic, who if you uh put him over the middle, he could get run after catch. But even when you have a guy who has great feet like that, who can win similar to a receiver, we may put him out at number one, and that's a mismatch. You put a linebacker on him, you put a corner on him, it's a mismatch. So, I think that's what he could bring to our offense where he could be a matchup nightmare whether he's in the slot or he's in the outside. And, you know, I don't know his background was at Tennessee, but he's going to get a lot of opportunities here to really help us and I know he's going to do that. He has a great attitude. Uh he's fun to be around and uh I'm glad he's on our team. >> Talk about communication with you, Jaden, and Blau. How important is that that he's open to that kind of communication when you're learning a new offense that you guys go to him what you like, what you don't like? >> Yeah, I think it's really huge. You know, I think um in football obviously from coaches to players, we respect the coach's scheme and their uh understanding of the game of football and the film, the time that they put in, but also there's a part of us being on the field as players and the things that we're seeing in real time that I feel like when there's a collaborative effort, it can really make the entire offense or defense better. Um, so the coaches I've been around who are open to those suggestions, who are open to the open communication back and forth, uh, are the ones that not only players tend to enjoy, but the coaches get to get an insight of what's going on in our brains. And I just feel like you grow quicker instead of like, hey, run my system, run these routes. At the end of the day, we're going to do that because we're players, but I think just collaboratively, you know, I mean, I think it's a lot better. So Blau, understanding that from being a player and now being a coach, um, I think that only helps. And um you know at the end of the day like we respect the coaches and we're going to suggest things that's going to help. Like I'm not being like hey run this route cuz I just you know but I'm trying to think of things that could help us all and I think when you have that type of collaborative effort it makes everything a lot better. >> Can I just Sure. Go ahead. >> Just going back to the when you were talking about the split things off. >> Do you know that immediately as a receiver is that you go back and watch it? >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean I think the great thing about it is like me and Jaden talk a lot after the reps happen about, you know, not only from when the twos are going, but when him and I are going and he was like, you know, I felt like uh [snorts] on that route like we're trying to catch that on the run. I was a little bit like having to what throttle, you know, you're kind of like moving slightly with the ball. Um, and so we want to hit that that play on the run. So, we were trying to figure out, okay, was his maybe his eyes were a little late or maybe I didn't get all my steps. He thought I maybe didn't get all my steps, which is also important, getting a a good stride length, so it times up. But I had this recollection. I was like, uh, because it's like a nasty split, so you're kind of more condensed. Well, nasty split could kind of be a variation where you're maybe four yards away from the tackle or you could be closer to two yards inside the numbers. Those two yards could make a difference. I think that was the difference because not only uh the defense was running a type of defense where I could get chucked. So if I'm too close to that guy on the end line of scrimmage, he could chuck me off my route and that can kind of mess up the timing as well. But me being in a more minus two minus three split even would not only give me space to move but will time up better because I have a a wider angle of departure and then when I'm coming in on the break like the timing will be more on the run. We want to hit things on the run and with Jaden's timing and and our ability to run after catch, like those will be huge plays and those are the difference between catching tackles and catching runs. So, we want catching runs. >> I appreciate you guys.

title: HC Dan Quinn Speaks To The Media Before Day 2 Of Training Camp | Washington Commanders
text: that we're not looking at as a long-term one. Um, some things I liked from yesterday as we got going onto the first day. Um, the red zone work right off the bat, I liked how that felt right off the space to get into a competition. We did a two-point play competition. Came back, hit some more end of the game or end of the half moments. Um, I thought the conditioning um was key for these guys coming in to say when we left to say we're not playing our way into shape. it has to be already there to keep working your skills hard. So, um, today's a big red zone day. In practice, you're going to see almost the entirety of the day there. Decision making happens quicker, decisiveness to go, the throws are quicker, the matches are quicker, and so, um, I'll look forward to doing that. That'll be the big emphasis yesterday and today. And then, um, as we get into next week, there'll be days that we'll be down in the red zone, other days not. So, glad to get it rocking with you guys today. with some of the early stuff you hear from offensive guys maybe more that the defense tends to be a little bit further ahead at this point in camp. So, how if that's the case, how do you then measure both sides of the ball um knowing that? >> Yeah, definitely like um some KPIs for practice that we're trying to find um every day. And so, some of it might just be as small as like um you know, ball security to speeds that we're trying to work to the execution of plays. Sometimes, John, it might even go down to, you know, against zone, what's the completion versus man and how are things going into that space, knowing that like in zone defense, there's going to be more completions in front, but so offensively, those should generally be higher on those kind of days. So, it goes back and forth for sure for about I don't know, a good 10 days or so where this can be an emphasis, that could be an emphasis, but timing over and over, that's what we're going through. And uh so, new set of plays, new installs, but it definitely goes back and forth. That's why I like kind of having the competition's good where you can keep score, see where you're at. >> Back to the GoPro stuff, why did you guys decide to do that this year? >> Just honestly, it came through the spring to say, is there an, you know, an advantage we can find doing it? And so, um, we knew some other clubs had tried it and so we thought this would be something to explore and see where it goes. And we liked it. So, the first the team, the individual work, it was, you know, not quite enough. And way back in the off seasonason, we tried even like some meta glasses to see what that would look like to turn them on and off. So I think if you want to just dig in and try and say what part of practice is it good, why wouldn't we use it? And then one of the hidden benefits we found was the communication piece with it. And that was like one of those things like an unintended good consequence came from that. And so I wouldn't say it's not like as the top of the list in terms of where we do the film, but we try to edit those into the same practice cuts. So this view, the second view, the third view, and then just for the QBs, they can add that part >> with Jaden. Logistically, like after practice, does he go back and watch each play and evaluate? Is it that detailed and self-critical? How does that, how does that >> Yeah. And that's true for the entire group. Yeah. And so you want to, you know, what was the intent of the play? You know, did we make the right check? Did we go to the right location? And so that could be at any of the number of spots. So yeah, you want to evaluate what specific things you want to nail for tomorrow. So I loved yesterday our quarterbacks being outside the pocket remaining passers knowing that like that's one of our emphasis to have explosive plays down the field. So we were intentional about that when we're getting outside, you know, scramble drills and down the field throws. So that would been like one small example of from the quarterback room of something we were trying to emphasize and like saw it come to life day one. And you are sometimes right in the middle of the play if if it's a skeleton situation. Like what do you get out of being, you know, the defense is on one sideline, the offense is on the other sideline. You're the head dude like kind of right in the middle. >> Yeah. Sometimes I want to see um the eyes of the defense if it's zone to see where they're looking. So if they have, you know, vision of the quarterback, I want to make sure I am seeing where their eyes are from another standpoint. Sometimes I want to see it from the offensive perspective to say where I'm the center, I'm the quarterback, I'm seeing spacing, I'm seeing timing, and that's really where I can also see the accuracy, you know, like balls thrown on the right side in a zone to extend plays. So, just small cues that I'm trying to find that I may have not seen from a sideline perspective. Hey Dan. Um, with regards to Chig, just curious like what your thoughts were at the time you were presented. Hey, maybe we could bring this guy in and now that you've had him for a few months, what have you learned or what's maybe changed in that? Uh, >> thinking. >> I loved um the urgency and the competitiveness. That's what jumped out on tape, Ben. So, he's not the biggest guy, but beating him to the punch and having the quickness to go. So, I thought that was, you know, one of the things that I really liked about his game. If we add those type of players, you know what generally happens that manifests itself into like absolutely battling for it. And so to see him in a system at a tight end from play actions and down the field throws, we thought that would be like a good mesh for him. It was also what he was looking for, too. So, um, when we showed clips from there and showed clips of what we were going to do, we intercut them together to like paint a clear picture. I think anytime a person's a free agent coming here, you want to say like this is how we plan on featuring you here. So they have a clear vision to say, you know what, this is a good spot for me, you know, like relative to the dollars and cents to say, okay, this is why I should choose, you know, this place. >> What I guess what did you present him to say, hey, this is may we saw how you were maybe used here. We can do something different here. the long play action passing, you know, over routes, pylon routes, things that were uh down the field, and even some, you know, crossing routes that are catching run to use some of his speed. So, we just wanted to, you know, highlight, hey, this is what we think you can do. >> Overall yesterday, first day intensitywise, were you pleased with uh where you guys were? >> Yeah, I thought first part of practice what I wanted to see was, you know, just not waiting and, you know, easing into it. And so the reason we do sometimes competition so quickly is just to jump start it and get it to go. So I liked the attitude of where we're at the first day on the first day of camp is sometimes waiting to see, but they did not. And so I was pleased to see that on day one and go through the corrections. We do some more walkthroughs and such last night. And so we'll go after it again today. >> With uh Matt and Julian now having to, you know, basically step in with uh Nick being out. Uh do you guys change anything as far as preparation for practice or just keep it going? Nope, we just keep it going. And those are the ones you move it around some, but even within a practice, there's going to be times where you'll see a guy maybe go up to the first group to go. It's just to like what are you going to do? And so, like, every player deserves his chance to go perform. And so, as coaches, I want to see this third player with the first group. What's he going to do? How's he going to react? All right, I'm in the huddle now with Jaden and here where I am. So, I wanted to find that out. But, um, because we're putting it all in together, no change of that. just we have about four guys that can snap and go through that and so we rotate that through. >> Hey coach, uh yesterday in the red zone, did you see the execution that you were looking for? >> On some plays we did. I wouldn't say overall blanketwise, not um but that's kind of part of why we practice. I want us to be right on the edge, but also like not quite nail it every time. And what's the coaching point? How do we get better? And but I want us to be right on that edge, you know, really push it. have to run and play it at full speed and when you're putting in a play, okay, this is the pace, this is the jog through, but man, now you go get it. Defensively, I liked, you know, the spacing of where they're at, forcing the QBs to get outside the pocket. So, um, each day kind of goes back and forth a little bit, but different than a bust, you know, like ran the wrong route, ran the wrong, you know, coverage. That part was fine. Is now it's the the details of finding, you know, how we level it up. Speaking about the defense, the defensive line yesterday, what were you what did you see there uh yesterday in the red zone and overall? >> Yeah, I think just a lot of versatility. So, in the early um not early, but throughout practice, Dante used a different mix of packages and so that'll be an ongoing, you know, experiment. How do we feature him? Where is Amen? He's inside, outside to pay over here, Newton over here, OA off, Casey on. You know, how do we manipulate the defense to have multiple roles? It doesn't mean that's what they're going to do, Donna, but this is the time to try and say while we're here at practice and say, "Okay, let's add him to that. Let's not let's blitz this person, see where it's at." And that'll be a good bit of the next three to four weeks. So, that that process is ongoing for sure. >> Hey, good morning, coach. Um, so when you're looking at your um pass rush and safety group is two questions. on >> um your so your pass rush and your safety group. What are you seeing from them currently and what's your expectations now in the you know next couple weeks here? >> Yeah, it'll take a while um to find the right balance of people and where we're going to go. Some will be one-on ones or five on four or group sessions to go. We're starting into our two-minute today. So, it's so much of it is the coordination to go. Every good defense that plays zone, you better have a pass rush, you know, in order to do that because there's not the leverage. So, the quarterback has to feel like he's getting affected. And so, I'm looking forward to seeing the different groups, the different combinations of people that can do that. And, uh, it's a good offensive line, you know, to work against. And so, if you really want to get right, how do you match up against LT and Josh out on the edges and, you know, certainly inside? So, um, it's a, like I said, it's a fun battle. And then I won this one, you won the next one, and just kind of keeps on going. >> Yeah. And safeties were working through a number of different groups. sometimes three safeties, sometimes two, who's down in the box, who plays back high. So, um, on the first day, you know, I'm pleased with what I saw. >> Along the lines of the energy that you're talking about, what are some of the things you look for when they come back from the break as far as like retention and things like that? And did you see it yesterday >> out on the field? First things you want, like from the defensive standpoint, you want to hear communication. Sometimes that's before the snap, sometimes that's after the snap, but that's when you can, you know, relay the information back and forth to one another. offensively. Um, am I at the right target? I'm at the right depth in a route. So, those are the things that you want to see. And so, to see that come to life early on. That's a good step. It gets progressively harder as you go. Practice get a little more more plays into it. So, for the first day, I thought, you know, just about everybody hit the marks that we were wanting to hit and then leveled up, leveled up. And so, over the next three weeks, you know, just keeps get progressively harder. We challenge them more and we try to put them into as many stressful scenarios as we can out at the practice field. So we create it to make it really hard on them. So um they know it's coming but you know not all the way everything on the first day. >> Take three more. >> Morning Dan. Can we just get a little clarification on the roster move putting Tres on the NFI please? >> Yes. So, um, Tres's injury, um, you know, hope, you know, short-term space, but, uh, it happened prior to training camp. And so, um, that's the designation between NFIs and PUPS to go. But, um, he's doing well and, uh, we're expecting, you know, him to make great progress, you know, over the next days ahead. >> Hey, Dan, only 10 forced turnovers last year, which I'm sure is a number you didn't like. What do you think the upgrades and the changes in terms of personnel and scheme are going to help get that number up to a number you'd like? >> Yeah, it's uh it's everything for us and so it's the way that we do it. You might have saw it even at the beginning of practice of you know every skilled player onto the jugs, the intentionality of it and so it's a big part of it. It's honestly like it's our philosophy, you know, the way we take care of it on offense, great decisions, and that's one of Jaden's superpowers, his accuracy of putting the ball in the right location, in the zone, in demand to go. And so, defensively, it's the mindset to go after it. So, we do things like how many times are we taking shots at the ball, having opportunities, and converting on those chances. So, um it's something that's an everyday discussion for us. >> Morning, coach. >> Good morning. >> Uh yesterday you were asked about Bill being a three down back. Where do you kind of see Kron Allen fitting into that mold and how have you seen him develop as training camp goes on? >> Yeah, the thing that you're wanting to see, he's got good running instincts for sure and uh that was demonstrated from his time through college tape. In the spring, you're getting to see not as much in the running game. Um it's heavier geared toward the passing game. So over the next three weeks and especially on the days that's padded, you know, we'll get a sense of that. as a running back, you're not seeing things like yards after contact and breaking tackles in a practice that has no contact. And so getting the skills down for that, getting the system knowledge that, you know, okay, done good job of that, of knowing it. So, we're excited to see what that development will look like ahead.
